Place pasta in bowl. Pour hot consommé over. Garnish with chive oil and cracked pepper.
notes: Ensure the stock is completely cold before starting the clarification process
Do not let the consommé boil once the raft has formed to maintain clarity
Chicken stock must reach a minimum internal temperature of 75°C during the initial simmer

recipes.recipe_name: Rigatoni with Vegetarian Italian Sausage and Tomato Ragù
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Rigatoni served in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The pasta is evenly coated in a rich, textured tomato sauce with a vibrant red hue. Visible 2cm chunks of browned plant-based sausage are distributed naturally among the tubes of pasta. Fresh, bright green basil leaves are torn and scattered across the top. A light, even dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese covers the dish. The setting is a modern bistro with a light oak wooden table. A folded white cotton napkin and a heavy stainless steel fork sit to the right. Natural, soft window lighting highlights the glossy sauce and the rustic texture of the sausage chunks. The arrangement is organic, showing the entire plate with clean edges and moderate negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm focaccia or crusty Italian bread
Pair with a glass of Chianti or Sangiovese
Present in a shallow pasta bowl (piatto fondo)
instructions: Boil 4 liters of water in a large pot.
Add 10g salt and Rigatoni to boiling water.
Cook pasta until al dente, approximately 10 minutes.
Cut plant-based sausage into 2cm thick chunks.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Brown sausage chunks for 5 minutes until crisp.
Add minced garlic and chili flakes to the skillet.
Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and simmer for 10 minutes.
Reserve 120ml of pasta cooking water.
Drain pasta and add to the skillet with the sauce.
Add reserved pasta water and half of the Parmesan.
Toss pasta over heat for 2 minutes to emulsify.
Tear basil leaves and stir into the pasta.
Serve immediately in warm bowls.
notes: Do not rinse the pasta after draining to preserve starch for the sauce
If the sauce is too thick, add more pasta water 15ml at a time
Use a high-quality aged Parmesan for best flavor profile

recipes.recipe_name: Argentinian-Style Beef Chunks with Oregano and Charred Peppers
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of seared beef sirloin is presented as thick 4cm cubes with a deep mahogany crust. The beef is arranged in a natural pile at the center of a clean white porcelain plate. Interspersed among the meat are vibrant 4cm squares of charred red bell pepper and thick wedges of caramelized red onion showing distinct grill marks. A bright green herb oil flecked with dried oregano and minced garlic is drizzled over the components. The arrangement is organic, leaving ample negative space. The setting is a modern bistro with a dark wooden table, a folded white cotton napkin, and simple flatware. Natural light highlights the glistening textures of the meat and softened vegetables.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm crusty bread to soak up the juices
Pair with a robust Argentinian Malbec
Provide extra chimichurri sauce on the side
instructions: Whisk 40ml olive oil, vinegar, garlic, oregano, salt, and pepper in a large bowl.
Toss the beef cubes in the marinade until well coated.
Marinate at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Heat the remaining 20ml oil in a heavy skillet over high heat.
Sear the beef cubes for 3 minutes per side until a dark crust forms.
Remove the beef from the skillet and let rest on a warm plate.
Add the peppers and onions to the same skillet.
Sauté for 5 minutes over high heat until the edges are charred.
Return the beef and any resting juices to the skillet.
Toss briefly to combine and serve immediately.
notes: Ensure the skillet is smoking hot before adding beef for a proper crust
Do not overcrowd the pan; sear in batches if necessary
Use fresh oregano for garnish if available for extra brightness

recipes.recipe_name: Mexican Arroz con Leche
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy Arroz con Leche served in a traditional hand-painted Mexican terracotta cazuela. The rice pudding is thick and luscious, with distinct soft grains visible through the milky white sauce. The texture is fluid rather than stiff. A light, even dusting of reddish-brown ground cinnamon covers the surface. One whole cinnamon stick is placed at a slight angle on top as a functional garnish. The bowl sits on a rustic dark wood table with a colorful woven textile napkin tucked underneath. Warm, soft kitchen lighting highlights the creamy sheen of the milk and the textured surface of the rice.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in traditional clay cazuelas
Enjoy warm for breakfast or chilled for dessert
Pair with a piece of pan dulce
instructions: Rinse rice under cold water until water runs clear.
Combine rice, water, and cinnamon stick in a medium pot.
Bring to a boil over medium-high heat.
Reduce heat to low and cover.
Simmer for 15 minutes until water is mostly absorbed.
Remove and discard the cinnamon stick.
Stir in whole milk, evaporated milk, and condensed milk.
Cook uncovered on low heat for 20 minutes.
Stir frequently to prevent the bottom from burning.
Remove from heat when the mixture is thick and creamy.
Stir in vanilla extract.
Serve warm or chilled in small bowls.
notes: Stir constantly during the milk phase to release rice starches.
The pudding will thicken significantly as it cools.
Adjust sweetness by adding more condensed milk if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Potato and Green Pea Risotto with Charred Broccoli
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a wide, matte-white porcelain plate. The potato and pea risotto forms a fluid, vibrant base, spreading naturally across the center without being contained. It features small 5mm cubes of pale gold potato and bright green whole peas. Resting atop the risotto are three large, charred broccoli florets, their edges deeply browned and crispy from the skillet. A light drizzle of extra virgin olive oil circles the perimeter of the creamy starch. Small shavings of Parmesan cheese and a few pea shoots are scattered over the top for height. The colors are a harmony of spring green and earthy cream. Natural lighting highlights the velvety texture and charred florets.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately on warmed plates.
Accompany with crusty sourdough bread.
Pair with a crisp Italian white wine.
instructions: Dice potatoes into uniform 5mm cubes.
Finely mince onion and garlic.
Heat chicken stock to a simmer in a saucepan.
Sauté onion and garlic in olive oil until soft.
Add potato cubes and toast for 2 minutes.
Add stock in 200ml increments while stirring.
Cook until potatoes are tender but hold their shape.
Toss broccoli florets with oil and salt.
Char broccoli in a hot cast-iron skillet until blackened.
Stir green peas into the potato mixture.
Remove from heat and add butter and cheese.
Stir vigorously to create a fluid creamy emulsion.
Thin with extra stock until the mixture flows freely.
Season with salt and pepper.
notes: Ensure potatoes are diced uniformly for even cooking.
The risotto should achieve an 'all'onda' or wave-like fluid consistency.

recipes.recipe_name: Annatto Braised Chicken and Savory Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Arroz con Pollo is presented on a clean white porcelain plate. Two whole, un-sliced chicken thighs with vibrant orange-red crispy skin serve as the focal point. They rest on a bed of moist, golden-hued rice flecked with small red pepper cubes and translucent onions. The rice has a slight sheen from the melted parmesan. A scattering of bright green cilantro leaves provides color contrast. The plate is set on a rustic dark wood table. A folded white cotton napkin and a polished silver fork sit to the side. Natural light highlights the textures of the crispy chicken skin and the fluid, savory rice.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of fried sweet plantains
Include a fresh lime wedge for acidity
Pair with a crisp lager or a dry white wine
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Add annatto seeds. Steep for 5 minutes until oil turns deep red.
Strain and discard seeds. Return oil to the pan.
Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Sear chicken skin-side down in the oil until golden. Flip and sear 2 minutes.
Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Sauté onion, bell pepper, and garlic in the same oil until soft.
Add rice. Stir to coat in oil for 2 minutes.
Pour in chicken stock. Return chicken to the pan.
Cover and simmer for 20 minutes.
Check chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove from heat. Stir parmesan cheese into the rice.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh cilantro.
notes: Do not boil the annatto seeds or the oil will turn bitter.
Ensure the parmesan is finely grated to melt smoothly into the rice.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Vegetable and Mozzarella Frittata
recipes.visual_description: A thick, golden-brown wedge of vegetable frittata sits on a clean white porcelain plate. Visible 1cm cubes of melted mozzarella and 1cm diced red bell peppers are embedded in the eggs. The frittata edges are crisp and browned. Beside the wedge, a neat dollop of thick Greek yogurt sauce is topped with grated cucumber and lemon zest. A small cluster of whole red grapes, two halved strawberries, and three thin apple batons provide a fresh side element. The plate is presented on a light oak table in a modern bistro setting with a white cotton napkin. Natural light highlights the textures of the melted cheese and sautéed vegetables. The composition is balanced with moderate negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm crusty bread to soak up the yogurt sauce.
Pair with a light herbal tea or fresh orange juice.
Present the frittata in the original cast-iron skillet for a rustic family-style presentation.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Grate cucumber and squeeze out excess moisture using a clean cloth.
Mix Greek yogurt, grated cucumber, lemon juice, and half the lemon zest in a small bowl.
Whisk eggs, milk, salt, and pepper in a large mixing bowl until combined.
Melt butter in an oven-proof skillet over medium heat.
Sauté diced bell peppers and grated carrots for 5 minutes until softened.
Pour egg mixture into the skillet over the vegetables.
Distribute mozzarella cubes evenly across the surface of the eggs.
Bake for 15 minutes until the center is set and the top is lightly golden.
Rest the frittata for 5 minutes before slicing into 4 wedges.
Serve each wedge with a dollop of yogurt sauce and a side of fresh fruit.
notes: Squeeze the cucumber thoroughly to prevent the yogurt sauce from becoming watery.
Use a non-stick oven-proof skillet to ensure the frittata releases easily.
Do not overcook the eggs to maintain a soft and creamy interior texture.

Enjoy warm for breakfast or chilled for dessert

recipes.recipe_name: Tarragon Chicken on Pommes Fondant
recipes.visual_description: Twelve golden-brown pommes fondant cylinders are arranged with consistent spacing on a clean white porcelain platter. Each 3cm potato cylinder is perfectly flat and caramelized on top and bottom. A single 2cm seared chicken cube sits centered atop each potato base, showing a crisp, savory exterior. A glossy, pale green tarragon cream sauce is draped neatly over the chicken, pooling slightly on the potato surface. A single bright green tarragon leaf provides a delicate garnish. The setting is a modern French bistro with a light oak table and soft natural side lighting. The composition uses moderate negative space to emphasize the architectural height of each bite-sized canapé.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve on a pre-warmed porcelain platter
Pair with a chilled dry white wine such as Chablis
Present as a passed hors d'oeuvre in a formal bistro setting
instructions: Peel potatoes. Cut into 3 cm thick cylinders using a round cutter.
Heat oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Sear potato ends until golden brown.
Add 40 g butter, garlic, and thyme to the pan. Baste potatoes.
Pour in chicken stock until halfway up the potatoes. Simmer until tender, about 15 minutes. Drain and keep warm.
Cut chicken breast into 2 cm cubes. Season with salt and white pepper.
Sauté chicken in remaining butter until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken.
In the same pan, sauté shallots until translucent. Deglaze with a splash of stock.
Stir in crème fraîche and chopped tarragon. Simmer until thickened.
Place one potato cylinder on a platter. Top with one chicken cube.
Spoon tarragon sauce over the chicken. Garnish with a fresh tarragon leaf.
notes: Ensure the potato cylinders are uniform in height for even cooking
Use a digital thermometer to verify chicken reaches exactly 75°C
Keep the sauce thick enough to coat the back of a spoon so it stays on the chicken

recipes.recipe_name: Garlic-Roasted Chicken with Cheesy Brown Rice and Peas
recipes.visual_description: A single portion served on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The base is a fluid, creamy bed of brown rice, its grains distinct yet bound by melted Parmesan. Bright green, round peas are scattered throughout the rice. A single whole, skin-on chicken thigh sits centered on the rice, featuring a deeply caramelized, golden-brown crispy skin. The chicken is left whole, not sliced. Fine flecks of emerald green parsley are sprinkled over the entire dish. The lighting is natural and even, highlighting the textures of the crispy skin and the moist rice. The background is a simple dark wood bistro table with a folded white cotton napkin and a silver fork.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve on a pre-warmed ceramic plate
Accompany with a crisp dry white wine
Provide extra grated Parmesan at the table
instructions: Simmer brown rice in chicken stock for 35 minutes until tender and liquid is mostly absorbed.
Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Place chicken skin-side down. Sear for 6 minutes until skin is golden and crispy.
Flip chicken. Add half the minced garlic to the pan.
Transfer skillet to a 200°C oven. Roast until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
In a separate pot, melt butter over medium heat. Sauté remaining garlic for 1 minute.
Stir cooked rice and green peas into the garlic butter. Heat for 2 minutes.
Remove rice from heat. Fold in grated Parmesan cheese until creamy.
Plate the rice. Place one whole chicken thigh on top. Garnish with parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken skin is very dry before searing for maximum crispness.
If rice becomes too dry, add a splash of warm stock before folding in the cheese.
Use a meat thermometer to confirm the chicken reaches 75°C.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo alla Cacciatora
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pollo alla Cacciatora is presented on a wide, matte white porcelain plate. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs are stacked slightly in the center, featuring deeply browned, caramelized skin. A thick, rustic sauce covers the base of the plate, filled with visible small cubes of orange carrots, green celery, and translucent onions. Whole, dark purple kalamata olives are nestled within the vibrant red tomato sauce. A light dusting of bright green chopped parsley and a single fresh rosemary sprig garnish the top. Two thick batons of grilled sourdough bread lean against the side of the chicken. The lighting is natural and soft, emphasizing the glossy texture of the braised sauce and the crispness of the chicken skin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with toasted sourdough bread to soak up the sauce
Accompany with a glass of medium-bodied Italian red wine
Place on a bed of soft, buttery polenta
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide braising pan over medium-high heat.
Place chicken skin-side down in the pan.
Sear for 6 minutes until the skin is deep golden and crisp.
Flip chicken and cook for 2 minutes.
Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Add onion, carrot, and celery to the remaining fat.
Sauté vegetables for 8 minutes until softened.
Stir in garlic, rosemary, and sage. Cook for 1 minute.
Pour in red wine. Scrape the bottom of the pan to deglaze.
Simmer wine for 3 minutes until reduced by half.
Add crushed tomatoes and stir to combine.
Place chicken thighs back into the sauce.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 25 minutes.
Check internal temperature of chicken reaches 75°C.
Stir in olives and simmer uncovered for 5 minutes.
Remove rosemary sprigs before serving.
Garnish with chopped parsley.
notes: Always use a meat thermometer to ensure chicken reaches the safe internal temperature of 75°C
Browning the skin thoroughly at the start is essential for the final texture
The sauce should be thick and chunky, not watery

recipes.recipe_name: Vegetable Risotto with Bell Peppers and Carrots
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy risotto served in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The rice has a fluid 'all'onda' consistency, spreading naturally toward the edges without being liquid. The dish features a vibrant mix of 5mm diced bright red bell peppers and orange carrots folded throughout the pale, ivory-colored rice. A concentrated mound of the reserved sautéed vegetable brunoise sits at the center for texture. Micro-thyme leaves are scattered across the top. The setting is a dark oak bistro table with a crisp white cotton napkin and a heavy silver fork. Natural side lighting highlights the glossy, velvety sheen of the mantecatura technique and the individual grains of rice.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in a pre-heated shallow bowl or 'piatto piano'
Pair with a crisp Italian white wine like Gavi or Pinot Grigio
Offer additional freshly grated Parmesan on the side
instructions: Sauté diced carrots and bell peppers in 10ml olive oil until tender-crisp.
Remove half of the vegetables and set aside for garnish.
Heat remaining oil and 20g butter in a wide pan.
Add onion and cook until translucent.
Add rice and toast for 2 minutes until edges are transparent.
Pour in white wine and stir until evaporated.
Add hot stock one ladle at a time, stirring constantly.
Wait for stock to be absorbed before adding more.
Continue for 18 minutes until rice is al dente.
Remove from heat.
Stir in remaining butter and parmesan cheese vigorously.
Fold in the sautéed vegetables and thyme.
Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Cover and rest for 2 minutes before serving.
notes: Ensure the stock is simmering before adding to the rice to maintain cooking temperature
Stirring is essential to release the rice starch for a creamy texture
The risotto should be fluid enough to move when the plate is tapped

recipes.recipe_name: Poulet à la Provençale with Garlic Roasted Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion served on a clean white porcelain plate. The dish features large, golden-brown seared chicken chunks nestled in a rich, vibrant red tomato sauce. Visible within the sauce are softened red and yellow bell pepper squares and earthy, browned mushroom quarters. Beside the chicken, a neat pile of crispy, golden-brown roasted potato cubes is arranged, showing flecks of toasted garlic. The plate has moderate negative space. A sprinkle of fresh green parsley provides a color contrast. The setting is a modern bistro with a light oak table, a folded white cotton napkin, and a stainless steel fork and knife. Lighting is natural and even, highlighting the textures of the crispy potatoes and the glossy sauce.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a crusty baguette to soak up the sauce
Pair with a dry Provençal rosé wine

ingredients.name: red and yellow bell peppers, 2cm squares

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Toss potato cubes with 15ml olive oil, half the garlic, and salt.
Roast potatoes on a tray for 25-30 minutes until golden and crisp.
Season chicken chunks with salt and pepper.
Heat remaining oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until skin is golden and meat reaches 75°C. Remove chicken.
Sauté mushrooms and bell peppers in the same pan for 5 minutes.
Add remaining garlic and herbs. Cook for 1 minute.
Stir in tomatoes and chicken stock. Simmer for 10 minutes to reduce.
Return chicken to the pan. Toss to coat in sauce.
Plate chicken and sauce alongside roasted potatoes. Garnish with parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C
Use waxy potatoes like Yukon Gold for the best roasting results
Keep chicken skin-on for maximum flavor and texture

recipes.recipe_name: Beef Fillet with Soubise and King Oyster Mushrooms
recipes.visual_description: A single whole beef fillet sits off-center on a large, matte grey designer plate. The beef is seared dark brown with a glossy red wine reduction glaze. Beside it, two large king oyster mushroom halves are roasted to a deep golden hue, placed in a natural, overlapping arrangement. Three precise mounds of ivory-white onion soubise create a fluid path across the plate. Tiny pickled pearl onion petals and roasted garlic cloves are tucked between the mushrooms. Vibrant green herb oil droplets provide contrast against the dark sauce. The setting is a dark grey veined marble table with a single silver fork and knife. Lighting is dramatic, casting soft shadows across the textured surfaces.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of silk-textured pommes purée in a copper pot
Pair with a full-bodied Bordeaux or Cabernet Sauvignon
Use warmed bone china plates to maintain temperature
instructions: Simmer pearl onions in vinegar and water for 5 minutes. Drain and cool.
Sweat sliced white onions in 20g butter over low heat. Do not brown.
Add cream to onions. Simmer 10 minutes.
Puree onion mixture until smooth. Pass through a fine sieve.
Halve king oyster mushrooms lengthwise. Score the flat side in a diamond pattern.
Sear king oyster mushrooms in butter until golden brown. Set aside.
Reduce red wine and beef broth in a saucepan by half.
Whisk 20g cold butter into the reduction to thicken. Keep warm.
Season beef fillets with salt and pepper.
Sear beef in a hot pan with remaining butter, garlic, and thyme.
Baste beef with foaming butter for 4 minutes. Target medium-rare.
Rest beef for 6 minutes before plating.
Place a spoonful of soubise on the plate. Position the whole beef fillet beside it.
Arrange king oyster mushrooms and pearl onion petals organically. Finish with red wine glaze.
notes: Ensure the beef is at room temperature before searing
Strain the soubise twice for maximum silkiness
Resting the meat is critical for juice retention

recipes.recipe_name: Cottage Cheese Gnudi with Roasted Tomato Sauce
recipes.visual_description: The dish features ten hand-formed, oval cottage cheese gnudi served in a wide white porcelain pasta bowl. The dumplings are ivory-white with a soft, pillowy texture. They are tossed in a vibrant, chunky sauce made from roasted cherry tomatoes and smashed garlic cloves. The sauce displays a rich orange-red hue with visible charred tomato skins. Three whole blistered tomatoes are arranged on top for height. A garnish of finely julienned fresh basil adds a bright green contrast. The bowl is placed on a rustic oak table. A white linen napkin and a polished silver fork sit to the left. The lighting is soft and natural, emphasizing the matte finish of the dumplings.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm crusty ciabatta bread
Pair with a crisp Vermentino or Pinot Grigio
Offer extra grated parmesan at the table
instructions: Strain cottage cheese through a fine-mesh sieve for 2 hours to remove all moisture.
Preheat oven to 200°C.
Place cherry tomatoes and 4 smashed garlic cloves on a tray with olive oil.
Roast tomatoes for 20 minutes until skins burst and char.
Mix the dry cottage cheese, eggs, 2 minced garlic cloves, and grated parmesan in a bowl.
Incorporate flour slowly until a soft, tacky dough forms.
Roll the dough into 3cm oval-shaped dumplings.
Boil a large pot of salted water.
Drop dumplings into water and cook until they float.
Remove dumplings with a slotted spoon one minute after they surface.
Mash the roasted tomatoes and garlic into a coarse sauce in a warm pan.
Toss the dumplings gently in the sauce to coat.
Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure the cottage cheese is extremely dry to prevent the dumplings from falling apart.
Handle the dough minimally to keep the gnudi light and airy.
Use high-quality olive oil for the roasting process to enhance the sauce flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Mushroom Pasta with Black Olives
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented as a single portion on a wide white porcelain plate. Wide ribbons of pappardelle are tossed in a shimmering, emulsified butter and mushroom sauce. Thick 3cm chunks of golden-seared chicken are distributed naturally across the pasta, showing a caramelized exterior. Sliced cremini mushrooms and halved dark olives are tucked into the pasta folds, providing earthy and salty accents. A light snowfall of finely grated Parmesan and a sprinkle of vibrant green flat-leaf parsley provide the finishing touch. The plate sits on a rustic wooden table with a folded linen napkin and a stainless steel fork. Soft natural light emphasizes the glossy sauce and the varied textures of the ingredients.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm crusty sourdough bread
Pair with a chilled Pinot Grigio
Offer extra grated Parmesan at the table
instructions: Boil 4 liters of salted water. Cook pasta until al dente. Reserve 100ml of pasta water. Drain pasta.
Cut chicken into 3cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks until browned. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken.
Slice mushrooms. Add to the same skillet. Sauté until golden brown.
Mince garlic. Halve olives. Add both to the skillet. Cook for 1 minute.
Pour in chicken stock. Simmer for 3 minutes to reduce slightly.
Stir in butter and 30g of grated cheese. Mix until a glossy sauce forms.
Return chicken to the skillet. Add cooked pasta and reserved water. Toss to coat evenly.
Chop parsley. Fold into the pasta. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
notes: Do not overcook the pasta as it will soften further in the sauce.
Ensure the skillet is hot before adding chicken to achieve a deep brown sear.

recipes.recipe_name: Poulet à la Provençale with Garlic Roasted Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion served on a clean white porcelain plate. The dish features large, golden-brown seared chicken chunks nestled in a rich, vibrant red tomato sauce. Visible within the sauce are softened red and yellow bell pepper squares and earthy, browned mushroom quarters. Beside the chicken, a neat pile of crispy, golden-brown roasted potato cubes is arranged, showing flecks of toasted garlic. The plate has moderate negative space. recipes.recipe_name: Poached Chicken with Pea Puree and Steamed Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, modern presentation on a clean white porcelain plate. The base is a smooth, bright green pea puree, spread in a clean circular motion. A whole, moist poached chicken breast sits centered on the puree. Beside the chicken are three whole steamed baby potatoes with their skins intact. The dish is garnished with small fresh mint leaves and a light dusting of lemon zest. The colors are high-contrast: vivid green, pale white chicken, and earthy yellow potatoes. The plate is set on a light oak table with a folded white cotton napkin. Natural daylight illuminates the scene from the side, highlighting the textures of the smooth puree and the tender chicken.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of lemon wedges
Pair with sparkling water and fresh mint
instructions: Wash baby potatoes thoroughly.
Steam potatoes over boiling water for 15-20 minutes until tender.
Keep potatoes warm.
Bring fat-free chicken stock and garlic to a gentle simmer in a wide pan.
Place chicken breasts into the simmering stock.
Poach chicken for 12-15 minutes.
Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove chicken and keep warm.
Boil peas in a separate pot of water for 3 minutes.
Drain peas immediately.
Blend peas with mint, lemon juice, and 60ml of poaching liquid.
Process until the puree is smooth.
Season puree with salt and pepper.
notes: Do not boil the poaching liquid; a gentle simmer keeps the meat tender.
Use frozen peas for a brighter green color in the puree.
Ensure the chicken stock is completely fat-free to meet dietary requirements.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo alla Romana
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pollo alla Romana served on a clean white porcelain plate. The dish features two whole pieces of golden-brown seared chicken—a thigh and a drumstick—nestled atop a vibrant bed of red and yellow bell pepper batons. The peppers are glossy and tender, coated in a rich, rustic tomato sauce that pools slightly at the base. Diced onions and smashed garlic cloves are visible within the sauce texture. The chicken skin is crisp and seasoned with cracked black pepper. A scattering of bright green chopped flat-leaf parsley provides a fresh contrast. The plate is set on a dark wood bistro table with a white linen napkin and a side of crusty Italian bread.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with thick slices of toasted sourdough or pane casereccio to mop up the sauce.
Accompany with a crisp white wine from the Lazio region.

ingredients.name: Chicken thighs and drumsticks, bone-in, skin-on
Red and yellow bell peppers, cut into 1cm batons
Peeled plum tomatoes, crushed by hand

instructions: Season chicken generously with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden brown and crisp.
Flip chicken and sear the other side for 2 minutes.
Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Add onion and bell pepper batons to the same pan.
Sauté 8 minutes until vegetables soften and edges brown.
Add garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze the pan with white wine, scraping the bottom.
Reduce wine by half.
Stir in crushed tomatoes.
Return chicken to the pan, nestling it into the vegetables.
Lower heat, cover, and simmer for 25 minutes.
Check chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove lid and simmer 5 minutes to thicken sauce.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Do not remove the chicken skin as it provides essential flavor to the braising liquid.
Ensure peppers are cut into uniform batons for even cooking and professional appearance.
Verify chicken reaches the safe internal temperature of 75°C using a probe thermometer.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Arroz con Pollo presented on a clean white porcelain plate. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs with deeply browned, crispy skin sit atop a bed of golden, saffron-stained rice. The rice grains are plump and distinct, interspersed with fine bits of softened onion and concentrated red tomato. The dish shows vibrant yellow and orange hues from the saffron and paprika. A generous sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped parsley is scattered over the top. A single lemon wedge is placed neatly on the side. The plate sits on a light oak wooden table with a folded white cotton napkin. Lighting is bright, natural, and even, highlighting the textures of the crispy skin and the moist rice grains.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Alioli (garlic mayonnaise)
Accompany with crusty bread and a glass of chilled white wine
Present in a traditional terracotta cazuela for family-style dining
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide shallow pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden and crispy.
Flip and brown the other side. Remove chicken from pan.
Add onion to the same pan. Sauté until translucent.
Stir in garlic and grated tomato. Cook until liquid evaporates and mixture darkens.
Add smoked paprika and rice. Stir to coat rice in oil for 2 minutes.
Pour in white wine. Deglaze the pan. Simmer until wine reduces by half.
Add hot stock and saffron. Stir once to distribute.
Place chicken thighs back into the pan on top of the rice.
Simmer undisturbed over medium-low heat for 18-20 minutes.
Ensure chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove from heat. Cover with a clean cloth. Rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Do not stir the rice once the stock is added to allow a crust to form on the bottom.
Use a wide pan to ensure even rice cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Lebanese Chicken with Vermicelli Rice and Sautéed Peppers
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Lebanese Vermicelli Rice is presented on a clean white porcelain plate. The base consists of fluffy long-grain rice mixed with deeply toasted, golden-brown vermicelli pasta strands. Two whole pan-seared chicken thighs are positioned centrally, showing a rich caramelized exterior seasoned with dark spices. To the side, a vibrant heap of sautéed red and yellow bell pepper strips and thick onion wedges provides a colorful contrast. The vegetables exhibit soft textures and charred edges. A light sprinkle of fresh green parsley garnishes the top. The arrangement is organic and spacious on a rustic wooden table. A small side bowl of thick white yogurt and a linen napkin complete the authentic setting under soft, natural lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of plain whole-milk yogurt
Accompany with fresh pita bread and pickled turnips
instructions: Rinse 300g rice in cold water until the starch clears.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat.
Break 50g vermicelli into small pieces and add to the pot.
Fry vermicelli while stirring until it turns a deep golden brown.
Add the rinsed rice and 5g salt to the pot.
Pour in 600ml chicken stock and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low and cover tightly.
Steam rice for 15 minutes then turn off heat.
Season 600g chicken thighs with 10g Baharat.
Heat remaining 15ml oil in a large skillet.
Sear chicken for 6 minutes per side.
Confirm the internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken and set aside to rest.
Slice 1 onion into thick wedges and 2 peppers into strips.
Sauté vegetables in the same skillet for 5 minutes until tender.
Serve chicken whole over a bed of vermicelli rice with peppers on the side.
notes: Toast the vermicelli carefully as it browns quickly.
Let the rice rest for 5 minutes before fluffing with a fork.

recipes.recipe_name: Poulet Basquaise with Sautéed Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Poulet Basquaise is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The focal point is a whole, golden-brown seared chicken thigh, skin side up, resting on a vibrant bed of Piperade. The sauce consists of softened 1cm strips of red and green bell peppers and translucent onions in a rich, glossy orange-red tomato reduction. Beside the chicken, a neat cluster of 2cm cubed potatoes, sautéed to a crisp golden-yellow finish, provides a clean textural contrast. The plate is garnished with a fresh thyme sprig and a light dusting of red Piment d'Espelette. The background is a modern bistro setting with a dark wood table and natural light.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm crusty baguette to soak up the Piperade sauce
Pair with a glass of chilled Irouléguy Rosé or a light-bodied red wine
Present in the center of the table in a traditional earthenware cassole for family-style service

ingredients.name: Red bell peppers, sliced into 1cm strips
Green bell peppers, sliced into 1cm strips
Waxy potatoes (such as Yukon Gold), 2cm cubes

instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt, pepper, and half of the Piment d'Espelette.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes until golden and crisp.
Flip chicken and sear for 2 minutes. Remove from pan and set aside.
Add sliced onions and peppers to the same pan. Sauté for 8 minutes until softened.
Stir in minced garlic and remaining Piment d'Espelette. Cook for 1 minute.
Deglaze pan with white wine. Scrape brown bits from the bottom. Reduce by half.
Add tomatoes, chicken stock, thyme, and bay leaf. Stir to combine.
Place chicken thighs back into the pan on top of the vegetables.
Cover and simmer over low heat for 25 minutes.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Boil potato cubes in salted water for 8 minutes. Drain and pat dry.
Heat remaining olive oil in a separate skillet. Sauté potatoes until golden and crispy.
Serve one whole chicken thigh over a generous portion of the pepper sauce with potatoes on the side.
notes: Piment d'Espelette is a traditional Basque chili powder; substitute with smoked paprika if unavailable.
Do not remove the chicken skin as it provides essential flavor to the braising liquid.
Ensure potatoes are completely dry before sautéing to achieve maximum crispness.

recipes.recipe_name: Zero-Waste Mediterranean Chicken and Fermented Tomato Rice Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of soup is presented in a handcrafted, matte cream ceramic bowl on a reclaimed wood surface. The broth is a warm, translucent orange-red with small beads of golden olive oil. Large, rustic chunks of moist poached chicken sit in the center, surrounded by visible grains of plump rice and small cubes of softened onion. Specks of deep red tomato pulp are distributed throughout. The dish is finished with a cluster of fresh, vibrant green basil leaves. Natural sunlight from the side creates soft shadows, highlighting the steam and the organic textures of the ceramic and wood. An undyed linen napkin and a heavy silver spoon rest beside the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty sourdough bread to utilize leftover grains.
Accompany with a small bowl of salt-cured olives.
Provide a cruet of high-quality extra virgin olive oil for drizzling.
instructions: Sear chicken thighs in a large pot until skin is golden.
Add onion skins and 1.5L water to the pot.
Simmer until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove chicken and set aside. Strain broth and discard skins.
Sauté diced onions and minced garlic in olive oil until translucent.
Add rice and toast for 2 minutes while stirring.
Pour in the strained broth and chopped tomatoes.
Simmer for 15 minutes or until rice is tender.
Break chicken into large chunks, removing bones.
Return chicken chunks to the soup.
Stir in finely chopped basil stems and season with salt and pepper.
Garnish with fresh basil leaves before serving.
notes: Use overripe tomatoes to maximize sweetness and reduce food waste.
Save chicken bones for a future secondary stock to ensure zero-waste.
Dehydrate tomato skins in a low oven to create a concentrated flavor powder garnish.

recipes.recipe_name: Beef Bourguignon
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Beef Bourguignon is served in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The centerpiece features four to five large, succulent chunks of braised beef chuck, glistening with a deep, mahogany-colored glossy sauce. Interspersed among the meat are whole, tender pearl onions and golden-brown sautéed button mushroom halves. Bright orange carrot rounds provide a pop of color. The stew is finished with a sprinkle of finely chopped fresh parsley. The sauce has a rich, velvety consistency, pooling slightly around the base. The dish sits on a dark wood bistro table. A side of crusty baguette slices and a simple silver spoon rest on a white cotton napkin nearby.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty French baguette
Pair with a glass of Pinot Noir or red Burgundy
Traditionally served with buttery mashed potatoes or boiled potatoes
instructions: Pat beef chunks dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Sauté bacon lardons in a heavy pot until crisp. Remove and set aside.
Sear beef chunks in the bacon fat over high heat until browned on all sides. Remove beef.
Add sliced carrots and onions to the pot. Sauté for 5 minutes.
Stir in tomato paste and flour. Cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in red wine. Scrape the bottom of the pot to release browned bits.
Return beef and bacon to the pot. Add beef stock and bouquet garni.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 2.5 hours until meat is tender.
Sauté mushrooms and pearl onions in butter in a separate pan until golden.
Add mushrooms and pearl onions to the stew. Simmer for 15 minutes.
Remove bouquet garni. Season to taste.
Garnish with chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Ensure the beef is patted dry before searing to achieve a deep crust.
Use a high-quality dry red wine for the most authentic flavor profile.
The sauce should be thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish-Style Arroz con Pollo
recipes.visual_description: A single portion served in a shallow white porcelain bowl. Two whole, golden-brown seared chicken thighs sit atop a bed of saffron-infused rice. The rice is a vibrant yellow, punctuated by 1cm squares of soft red bell pepper and bright green peas. The chicken skin is visibly crisp and textured. The rice is moist and separate, not mushy. Freshly chopped parsley is scattered over the dish for a vibrant green finish. The plate is set on a light oak wood table. A folded white cotton napkin and a polished silver fork sit to the right. The background is a softly blurred modern bistro interior with natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of authentic garlic alioli
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed in sherry vinaigrette
Present in a traditional terracotta cazuela for family-style service

ingredients.name: Red bell pepper, diced into 1cm squares

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels.
Season chicken generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide, shallow pan over medium-high heat.
Place chicken skin-side down in the pan.
Sear for 6 minutes until the skin is golden and crisp.
Flip chicken and sear for 3 minutes.
Remove chicken from the pan and set aside.
Add diced onion and red pepper to the same pan.
Sauté for 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the rice and smoked paprika.
Toast the rice for 2 minutes while stirring.
Pour in the chicken stock and add the saffron.
Bring the liquid to a boil.
Place the chicken thighs back into the pan on top of the rice.
Reduce heat to low and cover the pan.
Simmer for 20 minutes without stirring.
Check chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Scatter peas over the top and cover for 2 minutes.
Remove from heat and let rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Do not stir the rice once the stock is added to allow for a slight crust to form.
Ensure the saffron is high quality for the best aroma and color.
Use a wide pan to ensure even heat distribution for the rice.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Roasted Chicken with Västerbottensost Sauce and Glazed Carrots
recipes.visual_description: The dish features a single golden, pan-roasted skin-on chicken breast placed centrally on a white porcelain plate. The skin is crisp and deep amber. Beside the chicken, three whole glazed carrots are arranged naturally, showing a glossy orange sheen. A rich, pale ivory sauce made with Västerbottensost cheese and flecked with bright green dill is pooled elegantly around the base of the chicken. The arrangement uses moderate negative space typical of modern Nordic bistros. The setting includes a light oak wood table, a grey linen napkin, and a simple silver fork and knife. Lighting is soft and natural, highlighting the textures of the crispy skin and the smooth, emulsified sauce.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with boiled new potatoes.
Accompany with a side of lingonberry jam.
Pair with a crisp Scandinavian lager or aquavit.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Season chicken with salt and white pepper.
Heat oil in an oven-proof pan.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 5 minutes.
Flip chicken.
Add 20g butter and 2 garlic cloves.
Roast in oven until internal temperature is 75°C.
Boil carrots in salted water for 6 minutes.
Drain carrots.
Sauté carrots in 30g butter and remaining garlic.
Simmer cream and stock in a saucepan.
Reduce liquid by half.
Remove from heat.
Whisk in grated cheese and dill until smooth.
Rest chicken for 5 minutes.
Place whole chicken breast on plate with carrots and sauce.
notes: Whisk cheese into the sauce off the heat to prevent graininess.
Use white pepper to maintain the traditional Swedish flavor profile.
Ensure chicken skin is thoroughly dried before searing for maximum crispness.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Chicken and Mushroom Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spanish Chicken and Mushroom Rice is served in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The base consists of short-grain rice, cooked to a tender yet distinct texture, colored a rich amber from the tomato sofrito. Quartered cremini mushrooms and finely diced onions are evenly distributed throughout the grains. A single, whole bone-in chicken thigh with crispy, golden-brown skin rests on top as the focal point. The meat remains whole and unsliced. The arrangement is organic, with moderate negative space around the edges of the bowl. Finely chopped flat-leaf parsley provides a fresh green contrast. The scene is set on a light oak table with a neutral cotton napkin and a small glass of white wine in the soft-focus background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of garlic alioli
Accompany with crusty bread
Pair with a dry Spanish white wine like Albariño
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide, shallow pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes until golden.
Flip chicken and cook for 4 minutes. Remove from pan.
Add quartered mushrooms to the same pan. Sauté until browned.
Add diced onion. Cook until translucent and soft.
Stir in grated tomato and minced garlic. Reduce until the liquid evaporates.
Add rice and smoked paprika. Toast for 2 minutes while stirring.
Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a boil.
Nestle chicken thighs back into the rice mixture.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer uncovered for 18-20 minutes.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove from heat. Cover and rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Do not stir the rice once the stock is added to allow a crust to form
Ensure the tomato is reduced to a thick paste for maximum flavor

recipes.recipe_name: Tori Teriyaki
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Tori Teriyaki features four large 5cm chunks of succulent chicken thigh. The meat displays a deep, glossy mahogany glaze with subtle charred edges from the sauce reduction. The chicken sits slightly offset on a bed of fluffy white short-grain rice inside a shallow, dark matte-textured ceramic bowl. Finely sliced green scallion rounds and toasted white sesame seeds provide a sharp color contrast against the dark sauce. Beside the bowl, a pair of dark wooden chopsticks rests on a small ceramic holder. The setting includes a neutral linen napkin on a light oak table. Soft, natural side-lighting emphasizes the sticky texture of the glaze and the individual grains of rice.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of miso soup
Accompany with pickled daikon radish
Provide a small bowl of steamed edamame
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels.
Cut chicken into large 5cm chunks.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Place chicken skin-side down in the pan.
Sear for 5 minutes until skin is golden and crisp.
Flip chicken chunks and cook for 3 minutes.
Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Wipe excess fat from the pan with a paper towel.
Add soy sauce, mirin, sake, sugar, and ginger to the pan.
Simmer sauce over medium heat until it thickens into a glossy glaze.
Toss chicken chunks thoroughly to coat in the reduction.
Remove from heat immediately.
notes: Do not crowd the pan to ensure proper searing
Use high-quality Japanese soy sauce for authentic depth
The internal temperature must reach 75°C for safety

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Chicken Thighs with Glazed Carrots
recipes.visual_description: A single white porcelain plate sits on a light oak bistro table. At the center, two whole golden-brown seared chicken thighs rest in a shallow pool of glossy, translucent amber reduction. Surrounding the chicken are tender, glazed carrot batons and softened whole shallots. The carrots exhibit a vibrant orange hue with a subtle sheen from the butter glaze. Fresh thyme leaves are scattered naturally over the meat. The arrangement is organic and focused, with clean margins around the plate edge. Soft natural light highlights the crispy texture of the chicken skin and the smooth surface of the sauce. A folded white cotton napkin and polished silver fork lie to the left.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm crusty baguette slices
Pair with a glass of chilled Chardonnay
Present in a shallow wide-rimmed bowl

ingredients.name: Carrots, peeled and cut into 5cm batons

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels.
Season chicken generously with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a large heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes until golden and crisp.
Flip chicken and sear for 2 minutes.
Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Add carrot batons and shallots to the pan.
Sauté vegetables for 5 minutes until lightly browned.
Add garlic and thyme, cooking for 1 minute.
Deglaze the pan with white wine, scraping the bottom.
Reduce wine by half.
Pour in chicken stock and return chicken to the pan.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 25 minutes.
Confirm chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken and vegetables to a warm plate.
Whisk butter into the remaining liquid to create a glossy sauce.
Pour sauce over the chicken and carrots before serving.
notes: Use heirloom carrots for varied colors
Do not crowd the pan during searing to ensure crispy skin
Keep the braising liquid at a gentle simmer

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo alla Cacciatora
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pollo alla Cacciatora is presented on a wide, matte white porcelain plate. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs are stacked slightly in the center, featuring deeply browned, caramelized skin. A thick, rustic sauce covers the base of the plate, filled with visible small cubes of orange carrots, green celery, and translucent onions. Whole, dark purple kalamata olives are nestled within the vibrant red tomato sauce. A light dusting of bright green chopped parsley and a single fresh rosemary sprig garnish the top. Two thick batons of grilled sourdough bread lean against the side of the chicken. The lighting is natural and soft, emphasizing the glossy texture of the braised sauce and the crispness of the chicken skin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with toasted sourdough bread to soak up the sauce
Accompany with a glass of medium-bodied Italian red wine
Place on a bed of soft, buttery polenta
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide braising pan over medium-high heat.
Place chicken skin-side down in the pan.
Sear for 6 minutes until the skin is deep golden and crisp.
Flip chicken and cook for 2 minutes.
Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Add onion, carrot, and celery to the remaining fat.
Sauté vegetables for 8 minutes until softened.
Stir in garlic, rosemary, and sage. Cook for 1 minute.
Pour in red wine. Scrape the bottom of the pan to deglaze.
Simmer wine for 3 minutes until reduced by half.
Add crushed tomatoes and stir to combine.
Place chicken thighs back into the sauce.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 25 minutes.
Check internal temperature of chicken reaches 75°C.
Stir in olives and simmer uncovered for 5 minutes.
Remove rosemary sprigs before serving.
Garnish with chopped parsley.
notes: Always use a meat thermometer to ensure chicken reaches the safe internal temperature of 75°C
Browning the skin thoroughly at the start is essential for the final texture
The sauce should be thick and chunky, not watery

recipes.recipe_name: Orecchiette with Fennel, Bell Peppers, and Mushrooms
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of orecchiette served in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The pasta is tossed in a light, glossy sauce that coats each ear-shaped piece. Bright red diced bell peppers provide vibrant color contrast against the pale green, softened fennel batons and golden-brown quartered mushrooms. Translucent sautéed onions are scattered throughout. The dish is topped with a fine dusting of white Pecorino Romano and freshly chopped green parsley. The arrangement is natural and fluid, showing the textures of the vegetables. The bowl sits on a rustic light wood table next to a folded linen napkin and a stainless steel fork. Natural side lighting highlights the glisten of the olive oil sauce.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty sourdough bread
Pair with a dry Italian white wine like Vermentino
Offer extra grated Pecorino at the table
instructions: Boil 4 liters of salted water.
Heat 20ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sauté quartered mushrooms until golden brown.
Remove mushrooms from the pan and set aside.
Add remaining olive oil to the skillet.
Add diced onion, fennel batons, and diced bell peppers.
Cook 8 minutes until the vegetables soften.
Stir in minced garlic and chili flakes. Cook 1 minute.
Cook orecchiette in the boiling water until al dente.
Drain the pasta and reserve 150ml of the cooking water.
Add the pasta, sautéed mushrooms, and reserved water to the skillet.
Toss over medium heat for 2 minutes to emulsify the sauce.
Stir in chopped parsley and grated Pecorino Romano.
notes: Use the feathery fennel fronds as an additional garnish for aroma
Ensure the pasta water is well-salted to season the orecchiette internally
Adjust the sauce thickness with extra pasta water if needed

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Mushroom and Pepper Penne
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Italian-style pasta served on a clean white porcelain plate in a modern bistro setting. The base consists of penne pasta emulsified in a glossy butter and Parmesan sauce, mixed with sautéed red bell pepper dice, quartered cremini mushrooms, and sliced black olives. A whole pan-seared chicken breast with a deep golden-brown crust is positioned as the focal point on top of the pasta. Beside the pasta, several charred green broccoli florets provide height and color contrast. The dish is garnished with finely grated cheese and fresh parsley. The composition uses moderate negative space on a dark wood table. Natural light emphasizes the textures of the seared meat and vibrant vegetables.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty ciabatta bread
Pair with a crisp Pinot Grigio
Offer extra virgin olive oil for drizzling at the table
instructions: Boil a large pot of salted water.
Cook penne pasta until al dente. Reserve 100 ml of pasta water.
Season chicken breasts with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken for 6-8 minutes per side until the internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from pan and keep warm.
In the same pan, melt half the butter.
Sauté mushrooms and diced peppers for 5 minutes until softened.
Add garlic and broccoli florets. Cook for 3 minutes.
Stir in sliced olives.
Add cooked pasta, reserved water, remaining butter, and Parmesan to the pan.
Toss vigorously to create a creamy emulsion (mantecatura).
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Place pasta and vegetables on plates.
Top each serving with one whole chicken breast.
Garnish with fresh parsley.
notes: Always check chicken with a meat thermometer to ensure 75°C.
Do not overcook the broccoli to maintain a vibrant green color and firm texture.
The pasta water is essential for the sauce consistency.

recipes.recipe_name: French Bistro Beef and Mushroom Sauté
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of French Bistro Beef and Mushroom Sauté served on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The dish features large 4cm cubes of pan-seared beef, browned deeply on all sides, piled in the center. Interspersed are golden-roasted cremini mushroom quarters and softened garlic. A rich, glossy mahogany-colored red wine reduction coats the beef and mushrooms. Finely chopped flat-leaf parsley is scattered over the top. The plate sits on a dark oak bistro table next to a folded white cotton napkin and polished silver cutlery. Natural light from a window creates soft shadows. The entire plate is visible with ample negative space around the rim.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a crusty baguette to soak up the sauce
Pair with a glass of medium-bodied Bordeaux or Burgundy
Accompany with simple buttered haricots verts
instructions: Pat beef dry with paper towels.
Season beef generously with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a large skillet over high heat.
Sear beef cubes in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef.
Add mushrooms to the same pan. Sauté until golden brown.
Stir in shallots and garlic. Cook for 1 minute.
Pour in red wine. Scrape the bottom of the pan to release browned bits.
Reduce wine by half over medium-high heat.
Add beef stock and thyme. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Return beef to the pan. Toss to coat in sauce.
Remove from heat. Stir in cold butter until the sauce is thick and glossy.
Remove thyme sprigs. Garnish with parsley.
notes: Do not crowd the pan when searing beef to ensure a proper crust.
Use cold butter at the end to create a stable, emulsified sauce.
Ensure mushrooms are dry before sautéing to achieve maximum browning.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Sweet Potato and Pepper Stew
recipes.visual_description: The stew is presented in a wide, shallow ceramic bowl with a rustic, hand-thrown rim. Large 3cm cubes of softened, vibrant orange sweet potato are the focal point. These are surrounded by 2cm strips of sautéed red and green bell peppers. Dark green spinach leaves are folded into the thick, textured tomato base. The sauce shows visible bits of minced garlic and translucent onions. A fine dusting of dried oregano sits on the surface. A single individual portion fills the bowl. The bowl sits on a dark, well-used wooden table. A thick piece of crusty bread rests on a small ceramic side plate. Warm, natural lighting creates a cozy, home-cooked atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty sourdough bread
Accompany with a small bowl of Kalamata olives
Pair with a simple cucumber and tomato salad
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add diced onion and bell pepper strips.
Sauté for 5 minutes until vegetables soften.
Stir in minced garlic and dried oregano.
Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add sweet potato cubes to the pot.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and vegetable broth.
Bring the liquid to a boil.
Reduce heat to low and cover.
Simmer for 20 minutes until potatoes are tender.
Fold in fresh spinach leaves.
Stir until spinach is fully wilted.
Season with salt and black pepper.
Serve hot in deep bowls.
notes: Ensure sweet potato cubes are uniform for even cooking.
Add more broth if a thinner consistency is preferred.
Do not overcook the spinach to maintain its bright color.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Pork Ribs with Vinagrete Salsa
Moroccan Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Tagine
recipes.visual_description: The dish features thick carrot batons, roasted until tender and caramelized, nestled in a rich, amber-colored sauce. The carrots are piled naturally in a traditional terracotta tagine base, showcasing their vibrant orange hue. Plump chickpeas and translucent slices of preserved lemon are scattered throughout the arrangement. The sauce has a glossy, thick consistency from the reduction of vegetable stock and honey. Freshly chopped green cilantro and flat-leaf parsley provide a bright color contrast. Toasted flaked almonds are sprinkled over the top for texture. The setting is a rustic wooden table with a side of fluffy couscous in a small ceramic bowl and a polished silver spoon. Natural, soft lighting highlights the steam rising from the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed couscous
Accompany with a side of harissa paste for heat
Serve with warm khobz or crusty bread
Pair with traditional Moroccan mint tea

ingredients.name: Carrots, peeled and cut into 6cm batons
Preserved lemon, skin only, finely chopped

instructions: Heat olive oil in a heavy-based pot or tagine over medium heat.
Add onion and cook 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in garlic, ginger, Ras el Hanout, and cumin. Toast for 1 minute.
Add carrot batons and chickpeas. Stir to coat in spices.
Pour in vegetable stock and honey. Season with salt and pepper.
Bring to a simmer. Cover and cook for 25 minutes until carrots are tender.
Remove lid. Simmer 5 minutes more to thicken the sauce.
Stir in preserved lemon and half of the fresh herbs.
Garnish with remaining herbs and toasted almonds before serving.
notes: Use multi-colored heirloom carrots for added visual appeal.
Ensure the preserved lemon is rinsed before chopping to control salt levels.
The sauce should be thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Caramelized Onion Croquettes
recipes.visual_description: Four golden-brown chicken croquettes sit on a clean, white porcelain plate. The croquettes are shaped into uniform 3cm cylinders. They feature a crisp, jagged panko breadcrumb texture. A small, elegant pool of smooth Dijon aioli rests off-center. The plate shows ample negative space. A small sprig of fresh green thyme garnishes the top of the central croquette. The chicken inside is finely diced and bound with a creamy mustard sauce. The setting is a light oak bistro table. A folded white cotton napkin lies to the left. Natural afternoon light creates soft shadows. The entire plate is visible from a 45-degree angle. The arrangement is professional and uncluttered.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as an apéritif snack.
Pair with a crisp dry white wine.
Present on a shared wooden board for casual dining.
instructions: Dice 400g chicken into 5mm cubes.
Finely dice 1 onion.
Melt 30g butter in a skillet.
Sauté onion until deep brown.
Add chicken cubes to the skillet.
Cook chicken until the internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Stir in 40g flour.
Cook for 2 minutes.
Gradually whisk in 150ml milk.
Stir until the mixture is thick.
Fold in 20g Dijon mustard and thyme.
Season with salt and pepper.
Spread mixture onto a flat tray.
Chill for 2 hours until firm.
Shape into twelve 3cm cylinders.
Coat cylinders in 100g flour.
Dip in 2 beaten eggs.
Roll in 150g panko breadcrumbs.
Heat oil to 180°C in a deep pot.
Fry until golden brown.
Mix 50g mayonnaise with 15g wholegrain mustard.
notes: Ensure the chicken mixture is completely cold before shaping.
Keep the oil temperature consistent at 180°C for a non-greasy finish.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Beef Chunks with Charred Corn and Pickled Onions
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Mexican-inspired seared beef is presented on a clean white porcelain plate. The focal point is a cluster of thick, golden-brown seared beef sirloin chunks, showing a deep caramelized crust. These rest alongside a vibrant heap of charred yellow corn kernels mixed with finely diced white onions. Bright pink quick-pickled red onion rings are layered over the beef. The dish is garnished with crumbled white cotija cheese and fresh green cilantro leaves. A single lime wedge sits on the rim. The plate is set on a light oak wood table with a folded grey linen napkin and a simple glass of water. Natural side lighting highlights the textures of the meat and corn.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Warm corn tortillas
Spicy salsa verde
Fresh radish slices
instructions: Slice red onion into thin rings.
Combine lime juice and 5g salt in a bowl.
Soak onion rings in the mixture for 20 minutes.
Cut beef into 3cm chunks.
Rub beef with cumin, paprika, and remaining salt.
Heat 15ml oil in a heavy skillet over high heat.
Sear beef chunks for 2 minutes per side.
Transfer beef to a plate to rest.
Add remaining oil, corn, and diced white onion to the skillet.
Sauté until corn is tender and deeply charred.
Spoon corn onto a white plate.
Place beef chunks on top of the corn.
Garnish with pickled onions, cheese, and cilantro.
notes: Ensure the skillet is very hot for a good sear.
Resting the beef for 5 minutes keeps it juicy.
Use fresh corn for the best charring results.

recipes.recipe_name: Chili and Chocolate Braised Beef with Shrimp and Cheesy Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion served on a wide, matte white ceramic plate. The center features three thick, tender chunks of braised beef coated in a glossy, dark mahogany chocolate-chili sauce. Three large, pink seared shrimp rest directly on the beef, garnished with fine lemon zest and fresh cilantro. To the side, a cluster of four golden-brown potato wedges shows a textured crust of toasted breadcrumbs and melted cheddar. The setting is a modern bistro with a dark wood table and a neutral cotton napkin. Natural side lighting emphasizes the rich, velvety sauce and the crisp edges of the potatoes. The arrangement is clean with ample negative space around the rim.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas
Accompany with a side of pickled red onions
Pair with a bold red wine or a dark Mexican lager
instructions: Cut beef into 4cm thick chunks.
Heat oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat.
Sear beef chunks until browned on all sides. Remove beef.
Sauté diced onion and garlic in the same pot for 5 minutes.
Toast dried chilies in a dry pan, rehydrate in hot water, then blend with 100ml of beef stock.
Add chili paste, remaining stock, and chocolate to the pot.
Return beef to the pot. Cover and simmer on low for 90 minutes.
Cut potatoes into thick wedges. Boil in salted water for 8 minutes. Drain.
Toss potato wedges with breadcrumbs and grated cheddar.
Roast potatoes at 200°C for 20 minutes until crispy.
Sear shrimp in a separate pan with lemon juice for 3 minutes until pink.
Plate three beef chunks per person. Top with shrimp and lemon zest.
Serve with potato wedges on the side.
notes: Ensure the beef is simmered until fork-tender but still holds its chunk shape.
Use high-quality dark chocolate to avoid excessive sweetness.
The breadcrumbs on the potatoes provide a necessary texture contrast to the soft beef.

recipes.recipe_name: Pork Picadinho
recipes.visual_description: The dish features 2cm cubes of tender, browned pork shoulder nestled in a rich, mahogany-colored gravy. Bright orange carrot rounds and pale yellow potato cubes are scattered throughout the stew. The pork is served in a deep ceramic bowl alongside a mound of fluffy white long-grain rice and a portion of creamy black beans. A small pile of golden, toasted cassava farofa sits on the edge of the plate. Thinly shredded, sautéed dark green collard greens add a vibrant color contrast. The arrangement is casual and hearty, presented on a simple blue-patterned ceramic plate. The lighting is warm, suggesting a cozy family kitchen setting with a wooden table and a traditional spoon.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with white rice and black beans
Include toasted farofa (cassava flour) on the side
Accompany with 'Couve a Mineira' (thinly sliced sautéed collard greens)
Provide a small bowl of hot malagueta pepper oil
instructions: Season pork cubes with salt, pepper, cumin, and paprika.
Heat oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Brown pork cubes in batches until golden.
Remove meat and set aside.
Sauté onion and garlic in the same pot until soft.
Add tomatoes and bell pepper.
Cook for 3 minutes until softened.
Return pork to the pot.
Add stock and bay leaf.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 20 minutes.
Add potatoes and carrots.
Simmer for another 20 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Stir in fresh parsley.
Serve hot with traditional sides.
notes: This dish is a staple of the 'Prato Feito', the traditional Brazilian executive lunch.
Ensure the pork shoulder has some fat for a more flavorful gravy.
Do not overcook the potatoes to maintain their cube shape.

recipes.recipe_name: Murgh Do Pyaza
recipes.visual_description: The dish features large, succulent chunks of bone-in chicken thighs nestled in a thick, vibrant reddish-brown gravy. The sauce is textured with finely melted onions and studded with large, tender-crisp translucent onion petals. Bright green fresh cilantro leaves are scattered across the top. The chicken is cooked to a moist, tender finish with a visible spice coating. The meal is served in a polished copper kadai placed on a clean white porcelain plate, providing a modern yet authentic touch. Beside the plate sits a stack of warm, charred garlic naan and a small bowl of cool cucumber raita. Natural lighting highlights the glossy sheen of the aromatic gravy and the rustic texture of the bread.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with hot garlic naan
Accompany with cucumber raita
Include a side of pickled red onions

ingredients.name: chicken thighs, bone-in, skinless, cut into large chunks

instructions: Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pot.
Add cumin seeds, cardamom pods, and cinnamon stick.
Toast spices until fragrant.
Add diced onions.
Sauté until deep golden brown.
Stir in ginger-garlic paste.
Cook for 2 minutes.
Add turmeric, chili powder, and coriander powder.
Add chicken chunks.
Sear until browned on all sides.
Stir in tomato puree and whisked yogurt.
Cover the pot.
Simmer for 20 minutes.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Add onion petals.
Simmer 5 minutes until petals are tender-crisp.
Garnish with fresh cilantro.
notes: The name 'Do Pyaza' refers to onions being added at two different stages of the cooking process.
Use Kashmiri chili powder to achieve a vibrant red color without excessive heat.

recipes.recipe_name: Lomo Saltado
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Lomo Saltado presented on a clean white porcelain plate. The dish features 3cm chunks of seared beef sirloin with a deep brown crust. These are mixed with thick, glossy wedges of purple red onion and bright red Roma tomatoes. Golden, thick-cut potato batons are scattered through the beef mixture, all coated in a dark, shimmering sauce. A neat, molded dome of fluffy white rice sits on the side of the plate. Fresh green cilantro leaves garnish the top. The scene is set on a light wooden bistro table with a white cotton napkin and a small side bowl of spicy green aji sauce. The lighting is natural and even.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Aji Verde (green chili sauce)
Accompany with Inca Kola or a glass of red wine
Traditionally eaten with both rice and potatoes in the same meal

ingredients.name: Red onions, cut into thick wedges
Roma tomatoes, cut into thick wedges

instructions: Season beef chunks with salt and pepper.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a wok over high heat until smoking.
Sear beef in batches until browned and medium-rare.
Remove beef from wok and set aside.
Add remaining oil to the wok.
Stir-fry onion wedges for 2 minutes until slightly charred but crisp.
Add garlic and aji amarillo paste. Stir for 30 seconds.
Return beef to the wok.
Pour in soy sauce and red wine vinegar. Toss quickly.
Add tomato wedges. Stir for 30 seconds to warm through.
Fold in the cooked potato fries and half the cilantro.
Remove from heat immediately.
Serve with white rice.
notes: Ensure the wok is extremely hot before adding beef to achieve a smoky flavor.
Do not overcook the tomatoes; they should be warm but hold their shape.
The potatoes should be added at the very last second to maintain some crispness.

recipes.recipe_name: Green Banana Salad with Mustard and Smoked Duck
recipes.visual_description: Green Banana Salad with Mustard and Smoked Duck is presented on a matte charcoal designer plate. The green banana slices are cut into uniform 5mm discs, arranged in a fluid, organic curve across the plate. Three 1cm cubes of seared smoked duck are nestled among the bananas. The dish is drizzled with a vibrant yellow mustard seed and curry leaf dressing. Pickled yellow mustard seeds provide textural contrast. Thinly sliced green chilies and micro-cilantro add pops of bright green. The arrangement utilizes significant negative space. Lighting is dramatic and directional, highlighting the matte texture of the bananas and the rendered fat on the duck cubes. A pristine white linen napkin sits nearby on a dark slate surface.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with thin, crispy cumin-spiced papadums.
Accompany with a chilled glass of dry Riesling.
instructions: Peel 600g green bananas.
Slice bananas into uniform 5mm discs.
Blanch banana slices in boiling salted water for 6 minutes until tender.
Drain and cool completely.
Dice 150g smoked duck into 1cm cubes.
Sear duck cubes in a dry pan over medium heat for 3 minutes until fat renders.
Internal temperature must reach 75°C.
Heat 40ml mustard oil in a small pan.
Add 10g black mustard seeds and 15 curry leaves until they pop.
Remove from heat and cool.
Whisk tempered oil with 30ml lime juice and 10ml honey.
Combine bananas, 30g shallots, and 5g sliced chilies in a bowl.
Toss gently with the dressing and 20g pickled mustard seeds.
Arrange banana mixture in a fluid curve on four plates.
Place 3 duck cubes per plate among the bananas.
Garnish with micro-cilantro.
notes: Use very green, firm bananas to ensure they hold their shape after blanching.
Mustard oil provides the characteristic pungent aroma essential for authenticity.

recipes.recipe_name: Mujadara with Seared Halloumi and Crispy Onions
recipes.visual_description: The dish features a generous portion of Mujadara, a traditional blend of tender brown lentils and aromatic basmati rice, presented in a clean white porcelain bowl. The rice mixture has a deep, earthy hue from toasted cumin and caramelized onions. Atop the grain bed sit three thick, rectangular blocks of seared halloumi cheese, showing distinct golden-brown grill marks and a soft, warm texture. A vibrant mound of mahogany-colored crispy fried onion rings is piled high over the cheese. Fine-chopped flat-leaf parsley provides a bright green contrast. The setting includes a rustic wooden table with a side of thick Greek yogurt and warm flatbread, captured under soft, natural light that emphasizes the varied textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Labneh or thick Greek yogurt
Accompany with a fresh Salata Arabieh (tomato and cucumber salad)
Provide warm pita bread for scooping
instructions: Rinse lentils thoroughly in cold water.
Place lentils and vegetable stock in a large pot.
Boil for 15 minutes until lentils are partially tender.
Slice two onions into thin rings.
Heat 40ml olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat.
Fry onion rings until dark mahogany brown and crispy.
Drain crispy onions on paper towels and set aside.
Finely dice the remaining onion.
Sauté diced onion in the remaining oil until soft.
Stir cumin, coriander, and cinnamon into the diced onions for 1 minute.
Add rinsed rice and par-cooked lentils with their stock to the pot.
Simmer covered on low heat for 18 minutes until liquid is absorbed.
Cut halloumi into 2cm thick rectangular blocks.
Sear halloumi in a non-stick pan until golden brown on both sides.
Fluff the rice and lentils with a fork.
Plate the rice mixture and top with whole halloumi blocks and crispy onions.
Garnish with chopped parsley.
notes: Do not overcook the lentils in the first step or they will turn to mush.
The onions should be very dark brown but not burnt to provide the signature Mujadara flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Authentic Sichuan Mapo Tofu
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Mapo Tofu served in a shallow, dark-glazed stoneware bowl. The dish features uniform 2cm cubes of silken tofu submerged in a glossy, vibrant red chili oil sauce. Small crumbles of browned pork are distributed throughout the sauce. The tofu appears soft and white against the deep crimson liquid. A generous dusting of fine, reddish-brown Sichuan peppercorn powder coats the surface. Bright green scallion rounds are scattered unevenly over the top for contrast. The bowl sits on a dark wood table next to a small white porcelain bowl of steamed jasmine rice. A traditional ceramic Chinese soup spoon rests beside the bowl. Natural side lighting highlights the oily sheen and silky texture of the tofu.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice to balance the spice
Eat using a wide porcelain soup spoon to capture tofu and sauce together
Pair with a side of cold smashed cucumber salad

ingredients.name: Douchi (fermented black beans), rinsed and minced

instructions: Cut tofu into 2cm cubes.
Blanch tofu in boiling salted water for 2 minutes. Drain carefully.
Toast Sichuan peppercorns in a dry wok until fragrant. Grind into a fine powder.
Heat vegetable oil in wok over medium heat. Brown the ground pork until crispy.
Add doubanjiang and douchi. Stir-fry until the oil turns bright red.
Incorporate minced ginger and garlic. Cook for 30 seconds.
Pour in beef stock. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Slide tofu cubes into the wok. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Mix cornstarch and water to create a slurry. Stir into the sauce to thicken.
Drizzle with chili oil and half of the scallions.
Transfer to a bowl. Top with remaining scallions and ground peppercorn powder.
notes: Blanching the tofu prevents it from breaking during the final simmering process.
Ensure the doubanjiang is fried until the oil is red to release maximum umami.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Sun-Dried Tomato Penne
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of penne pasta is served in a wide, shallow white ceramic bowl with subtle rustic imperfections. The pasta is coated in a light, glossy, pale orange cream sauce. Generous 3cm chunks of seared, golden-brown chicken are distributed throughout the dish, never sliced or fanned. Strips of deep red sun-dried tomatoes provide intense color contrast against the pasta. The arrangement is natural and asymmetrical, filling the bowl comfortably. A light garnish of torn bright green basil leaves and a fine dusting of parmesan cheese are scattered on top. The bowl sits on a dark, textured wooden table next to a simple linen napkin and a silver fork. Warm, soft kitchen lighting creates a cozy, authentic home-dining atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to soak up the sauce
Pair with a simple arugula salad with lemon vinaigrette
Serve family-style in a large ceramic platter

ingredients.name: sun-dried tomatoes in oil, drained and sliced

instructions: Boil 5 liters of salted water in a large pot.
Cook penne until al dente according to package directions.
Reserve 100ml of pasta water and drain the rest.
Season chicken chunks with salt and pepper.
Heat 30ml of sun-dried tomato oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Brown chicken chunks for 6-8 minutes until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.
Add remaining oil and shallots to the same skillet.
Sauté shallots for 3 minutes until translucent.
Stir in sun-dried tomatoes and red pepper flakes.
Pour in chicken stock and simmer for 5 minutes to reduce slightly.
Lower heat and stir in heavy cream.
Add chicken, pasta, and reserved pasta water to the skillet.
