Toss ingredients over low heat for 2 minutes until sauce coats the pasta.
Remove from heat and stir in basil and parmesan cheese.
notes: Using the oil from the sun-dried tomato jar adds significant depth of flavor.
Shallots provide a delicate sweetness that compensates for the absence of garlic.
Ensure the chicken reaches exactly 75°C to maintain juiciness while ensuring safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Poulet Fermier with Sweetcorn Velouté, Heirloom Carrots, and Tomato Essence
recipes.visual_description: A single whole pan-seared chicken supreme sits as the focal point on an off-white designer bone china plate. The skin is deep golden-brown and crisp. Surrounding the chicken are three whole heirloom baby carrots, glazed to a high shine and positioned in a natural, flowing arrangement. A silky, pale yellow sweetcorn velouté is pooled at the base, showing a fluid, non-static consistency. Droplets of clear, vibrant tomato essence are dotted into the velouté, creating a sophisticated contrast. The plating is minimalist with significant negative space. The scene is set on a grey-veined white marble surface under soft, professional directional lighting, accompanied by a polished silver sauce spoon and a pristine white linen napkin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a chilled glass of Chablis or dry Chardonnay.
Present with artisanal sourdough and cultured butter on the side.
instructions: Blend tomatoes and strain through a coffee filter for 4 hours to collect clear tomato essence.
Simmer corn kernels in cream and 100 ml stock until soft. Blend and pass through a chinois.
Peel carrots. Simmer in water, 20 g butter, and salt until glazed and tender.
Season chicken. Vacuum seal with thyme. Cook in water bath at 65°C for 1 hour.
Remove chicken from bag. Pat skin dry.
Heat remaining butter in a pan. Sear chicken skin-side down until golden and crisp.
Baste chicken with foaming butter (arroser) until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Warm corn velouté and tomato essence separately.
Place chicken supreme whole on the plate. Arrange carrots organically around it.
Pour corn velouté at the base. Dot with tomato essence and serve immediately.
notes: Ensure the tomato essence is completely clear for the highest aesthetic impact.
The corn velouté must be passed through a fine-mesh chinois to achieve a professional texture.
Check chicken temperature with a digital probe to ensure exactly 75°C.

recipes.recipe_name: Mushroom and Caramelized Onion Tart
recipes.visual_description: A rustic, circular savory tart sits centered on a clean white porcelain plate. The shortcrust pastry is golden-brown and flaky. A base layer of dark, jammy caramelized onions supports thick chunks of golden-seared cremini mushrooms. Pitted black olives are scattered across the top as deep purple accents. The tart is garnished with a generous sprinkle of bright green, coarsely chopped coriander. The setting is a light oak bistro table with a white cotton napkin and polished flatware. Natural window light creates soft shadows and highlights the textures of the roasted vegetables. The arrangement is organic and professional, showing a single individual portion with balanced negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm as a main course.
Accompany with a simple green salad and vinaigrette.
Pair with a dry white wine or sparkling water.
instructions: Mix flour and salt in a bowl.
Cut cold margarine into flour until crumbly.
Add ice water. Mix until dough forms.
Wrap dough. Chill for 30 minutes.
Thinly slice onions. Sauté in oil until caramelized.
Cut mushrooms into thick chunks. Sear in hot pan.
Pit and halve the olives.
Roll dough into a 30cm circle on parchment.
Spread onions onto dough. Top with mushrooms and olives.
Fold dough edges toward the center.
Bake at 200°C for 25 minutes until golden.
Garnish with chopped coriander.
notes: Ensure the margarine is very cold for a flaky pastry.
Do not overcrowd the pan when searing mushrooms to ensure browning.
The dough can be made a day in advance.

recipes.recipe_name: Beef and Tomato Ragu with Rigatoni
recipes.visual_description: The dish features a single portion of rigatoni pasta tossed in a thick, rich tomato ragu, served in a wide, shallow ceramic pasta bowl with a slightly irregular rim. The beef appears as tender, chunky 2cm cubes, not sliced, nestled among the tubes of pasta. The sauce is deep red, clinging to the ridges of the rigatoni, with visible small bits of softened carrot and onion. A light dusting of finely grated white parmesan cheese covers the center, topped with three whole, small green basil leaves. The bowl sits on a rustic dark wood table. A simple stainless steel fork rests on a folded white linen napkin. Natural window light creates soft shadows. The entire plate is visible against the warm, lived-in kitchen background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to scoop up remaining sauce.
Provide a small bowl of extra grated Parmesan on the table.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed in olive oil and vinegar.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat.
Brown beef cubes in batches until seared on all sides. Remove and set aside.
Lower heat to medium. Add onion, carrot, and celery to the pot.
Sauté vegetables for 6 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return beef to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes and beef stock.
Simmer on low heat for 90 minutes. Ensure beef is fork-tender.
Boil rigatoni in salted water until al dente. Drain pasta.
Toss pasta directly into the ragu. Mix to coat each tube.
Season with salt and pepper. Serve immediately with parmesan and basil.
notes: Choose beef chuck for the best fat-to-meat ratio during slow cooking.
Ensure the pasta is slightly undercooked before adding to the sauce to finish cooking.
If the sauce becomes too thick, add a splash of pasta cooking water.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo e Broccoli al Pomodoro
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of rigatoni pasta served on a wide, clean white porcelain plate. The dish features golden-brown seared chicken chunks scattered naturally throughout the pasta. Vibrant green blanched broccoli florets and blistered red cherry tomato halves provide a bright color contrast. The pasta is lightly coated in a translucent, shimmering garlic-tomato emulsion. A fine dusting of freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano and several whole small basil leaves garnish the top. The plate sits on a dark oak bistro table. A neutral cotton napkin and a simple fork are placed to the side. Natural, soft daylight illuminates the textures of the seared meat and fresh vegetables.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in a shallow pasta bowl
Accompany with crusty rustic bread
Offer additional red pepper flakes at the table
instructions: Boil a large pot of salted water.
Cook pasta until 2 minutes before al dente.
Add broccoli florets to the pasta water for the last 3 minutes of cooking.
Reserve 120ml of pasta water and drain the rest.
Heat 30ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Season chicken chunks with salt and pepper.
Sear chicken until golden and internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from the pan and set aside.
Add remaining olive oil to the same pan.
Sauté onion for 4 minutes until translucent.
Add garlic and red pepper flakes. Cook for 1 minute.
Add cherry tomatoes. Cook for 3 minutes until they soften and release juice.
Return chicken to the pan. Add pasta and broccoli.
Pour in reserved pasta water. Toss over high heat for 2 minutes.
Remove from heat. Stir in Parmigiano-Reggiano and torn basil.
notes: Ensure the pasta water is as salty as the sea for authentic flavor.
Do not overcook the broccoli; it should retain a slight bite.

recipes.recipe_name: Filipino Chicken Adobo
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Filipino Chicken Adobo sits in a shallow, rustic ceramic bowl. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs are the focal point, coated in a deep mahogany, glossy sauce that pools slightly at the base. The skin is dark and slightly tacky from the reduction. Scattered over the meat are softened, golden-brown crushed garlic cloves and a few whole black peppercorns. The chicken rests partly on a bed of fluffy, steamed white jasmine rice. The setting is a dark wooden table with a simple spoon and fork placed on a linen napkin. Warm, overhead kitchen lighting highlights the rich textures and the steam rising from the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of atchara (pickled green papaya)
Eat using a spoon and fork, the traditional Filipino way
Pour extra adobo sauce over the rice
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels.
Heat oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken pieces until skin is brown and crisp.
Remove chicken and set aside.
Sauté crushed garlic in the same pot for 1 minute.
Return chicken to the pot.
Add soy sauce, vinegar, water, peppercorns, and bay leaves.
Bring liquid to a boil.
Reduce heat to low and cover.
Simmer for 30 minutes.
Check chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove the lid and increase heat to medium-high.
Simmer until the sauce reduces and thickens into a glossy glaze.
Stir in sugar if using for balance.
Discard bay leaves before serving.
notes: Do not stir the sauce immediately after adding vinegar to allow the raw acidity to cook off.
Use cane vinegar for the most authentic flavor profile.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Mushroom Risotto
recipes.visual_description: Serve the risotto on a flat white porcelain dinner plate. The consistency is fluid and spreads naturally across the plate, appearing free-flowing rather than molded. The rice grains are distinct, coated in a glossy, creamy sauce. Large 3cm chunks of golden-brown seared chicken thighs are distributed throughout the rice. Sliced cremini and shiitake mushrooms show deep caramelization and earthy brown tones. The dish features a pale golden hue. Finely minced flat-leaf parsley provides a vibrant green contrast. A light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese covers the surface. The arrangement is organic. Beside the plate sits a heavy silver spoon and a folded white cotton napkin on a light oak table. Natural side lighting highlights the creamy texture.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately while the consistency remains fluid
Accompany with a crisp dry white wine such as Pinot Grigio
Provide extra grated Parmesan at the table
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3cm chunks.
Dice onion into 5mm pieces.
Mince garlic cloves.
Slice mushrooms into 5mm thick pieces.
Heat 20ml olive oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until browned and internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Add mushrooms to the same pan. Sauté until moisture evaporates and edges brown.
Remove mushrooms and set aside.
Melt 20g butter in the pan. Add onion and garlic.
Cook until softened but not browned.
Add rice. Stir 2 minutes to toast the grains until edges are translucent.
Pour in white wine. Stir until liquid is fully absorbed.
Add 200ml warm stock. Stir continuously until liquid is absorbed.
Repeat stock additions one ladle at a time, stirring constantly, until rice is tender but firm.
Return chicken and mushrooms to the pan.
Remove from heat.
Vigorously stir in remaining 30g butter and Parmesan cheese to create a creamy emulsion.
Season with salt and pepper. Fold in chopped parsley.
notes: Keep the chicken stock at a low simmer in a separate pot to maintain cooking temperature.
Stirring constantly is essential to release rice starches for a creamy texture.
Ensure chicken reaches the safety temperature of 75°C during the initial searing phase.

recipes.recipe_name: Tuscan-Style Pasta e Fagioli with Basil Oil
recipes.visual_description: A wide, shallow white porcelain bowl contains a vibrant Pasta e Fagioli. The broth is a rich, warm terracotta color from the tomato and beef stock. Small 1cm cubes of golden potato and whole, creamy-white borlotti beans are visible throughout the fluid, glossy sauce. Ditalini pasta tubes are perfectly al dente and evenly distributed. A bright green basil oil is drizzled in a natural, organic swirl across the surface. Tiny, torn fresh basil leaves and a few drops of red hot sauce provide contrasting color accents. The entire plate is visible, centered on a dark oak bistro table next to a folded white cotton napkin and a polished silver spoon. The lighting is soft and natural.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with toasted sourdough bread rubbed with garlic
Top with freshly grated Pecorino Romano cheese
Pair with a glass of Chianti Classico
instructions: Heat 30ml olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat.
Add diced onion and cook until translucent.
Add minced garlic and potato cubes.
Sauté for 5 minutes until potatoes start to soften.
Stir in tomato paste, sugar, and mustard.
Cook for 2 minutes to caramelize the paste.
Pour in chicken stock and beef stock.
Bring the liquid to a boil.
Add beans and pasta to the pot.
Simmer until pasta is al dente and potatoes are tender.
Ensure the consistency remains fluid and soup-like.
Stir in hot sauce and season with salt.
Remove from heat.
Blend remaining olive oil with half the basil to create oil.
Ladle into bowls and garnish with remaining fresh basil.
notes: If the stew becomes too thick, add a splash of warm chicken stock
Ensure the potatoes are cut into uniform 1cm cubes for even cooking
The mustard adds a subtle acidic depth that balances the starch

recipes.recipe_name: Mexican Arroz con Pollo
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a shallow, matte-finished ceramic bowl on a dark wood table. The base is a vibrant, reddish-orange long-grain rice, cooked to a moist, free-flowing consistency. Two whole, golden-brown seared chicken thighs with crispy skin rest atop the rice. The chicken is not sliced. Accompanying the chicken are charred tomato wedges and small cubes of sautéed onion mixed within the grains. Garnishes include fresh, bright green cilantro leaves and thin wedges of lime placed on the side. The lighting is natural and even, highlighting the textural contrast between the crispy chicken skin and the soft rice. A linen napkin and a heavy silver fork sit beside the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas
Provide extra lime wedges for acidity
Accompany with pickled red onions
instructions: Remove stems and seeds from guajillo and arbol chilies.
Toast chilies in a dry skillet over medium heat for 2 minutes.
Soak toasted chilies in 200ml hot water for 10 minutes.
Blend soaked chilies, tomatoes, half the onion, and garlic until smooth.
Pat chicken dry and season with salt.
Heat oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden and crispy.
Flip chicken and sear for 2 minutes then remove from pot.
Add rice and remaining onion to the pot.
Toast rice for 3 minutes until opaque and slightly golden.
Pour blended chili-tomato mixture into the rice.
Cook for 5 minutes while stirring until sauce thickens.
Add chicken stock and return chicken to the pot.
Reduce heat to low and cover with a tight lid.
Simmer for 20 minutes.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove from heat and let rest covered for 5 minutes.
Fluff rice gently before serving.
notes: Use bone-in thighs to ensure the meat remains juicy during simmering
Do not over-toast the dried chilies as they can turn bitter
The rice should be moist and flavorful, absorbing all the chili-tomato broth

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Pork and Potato Estofado
recipes.visual_description: A deep, rich mahogany-colored stew served in a traditional shallow terracotta cazuela. The dish features 3cm cubes of succulent pork shoulder and irregular, hand-cracked potato chunks, both coated in a thick, glossy sauce made from lard, red wine, and smoked paprika. The pork surfaces show a dark, caramelized sear. Tiny fragments of rehydrated dried chili are visible throughout the sauce. A light sprinkling of finely chopped fresh parsley adds a vibrant green contrast. The cazuela sits on a clean white plate on a dark wood table. Beside it lies a piece of crusty rustic bread and a simple cotton napkin. The lighting is natural and even, highlighting the velvety texture of the sauce.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty rustic bread to soak up the sauce
Pair with a glass of Tempranillo or Rioja wine
Present in a traditional clay cazuela

ingredients.name: Dried ancho or chorizo chilies, rehydrated and chopped
Potatoes, peeled and cracked into chunks

instructions: Melt 30g lard in a heavy pot over medium-high heat.
Sear pork cubes in batches until browned on all sides.
Remove pork and set aside.
Add remaining lard to the pot.
Sauté onions until translucent and soft.
Stir in garlic, smoked paprika, and chopped dried chilies for 1 minute.
Pour in red wine to deglaze the pot, scraping the bottom.
Reduce wine by half.
Return pork to the pot and add beef stock.
Simmer covered for 45 minutes.
Add potato chunks and continue simmering until pork is tender and potatoes are soft.
Ensure pork reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Season with salt and pepper.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Cracking the potatoes instead of slicing them releases more starch to thicken the sauce.
Use high-quality smoked pimentón for the most authentic flavor profile.

recipes.recipe_name: Pineapple and Paneer Curry
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant North Indian curry served in a clean white porcelain bowl. The dish features thick 2cm cubes of seared paneer and 2cm chunks of fresh pineapple. The sauce is a rich, glossy orange-yellow hue. Small bubbles of golden ghee appear on the surface. Fresh green cilantro leaves are scattered on top. The bowl sits on a dark wooden table. Beside it lies a piece of butter-brushed naan bread and a small bowl of steamed basmati rice. A silver spoon rests on a folded white cotton napkin. The lighting is soft and natural, highlighting the textures of the seared paneer and the fibrous pineapple chunks. The arrangement is balanced with ample negative space around the central bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Butter Naan
Steamed Basmati Rice
Pickled Onions (Lacha Pyaaz)
Mint Chutney
instructions: Cut paneer into 2cm cubes.
Dice pineapple into 2cm chunks.
Finely chop the onions.
Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pan.
Fry paneer cubes until golden brown on all sides.
Remove paneer and set aside.
Add cumin seeds to the remaining oil.
Sauté onions until they reach a deep golden brown.
Stir in ginger-garlic paste. Cook for 1 minute.
Add tomato puree, turmeric, chili powder, and salt.
Cook the mixture until oil separates from the masala.
Add pineapple chunks. Sauté for 3 minutes.
Fold in the fried paneer cubes.
Add 100ml water. Cover and simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir in heavy cream and garam masala.
Garnish with chopped cilantro.
notes: Use fresh pineapple for superior flavor and texture.
If using store-bought paneer, soak cubes in warm water for 10 minutes to soften.
Adjust the chili powder to reach your preferred heat level.

recipes.recipe_name: Kurzemes Strogonoffs
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Kurzemes Strogonoffs is presented on a clean white porcelain plate. The focal point consists of thick pork loin batons and julienned pickled cucumbers enveloped in a rich, creamy ivory sauce. The meat is tender and coated thoroughly, presented as a hearty pile rather than slices. To the side, three whole boiled potatoes are arranged, brushed with melted butter and garnished with a generous layer of finely chopped fresh dill. The plate has moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro with a light wooden table. A slice of dark Latvian rye bread rests on a small wooden board to the side. Natural light highlights the creamy texture of the sauce and the vibrant green herbs.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of fermented cabbage
Accompany with a thick slice of dark Latvian rye bread
Pair with a glass of cold kvass or a local lager
instructions: Cut pork into 1 cm thick batons.
Dice onions finely.
Slice pickles into thin batons.
Heat oil in a large pan over high heat.
Sear pork batons until browned. Remove from pan.
Melt butter in the same pan. Sauté onions until translucent.
Add flour to onions. Stir for 1 minute.
Slowly pour in stock while stirring constantly.
Add seared pork and pickles to the pan.
Simmer on low heat for 15 minutes.
Stir in sour cream. Heat through but do not boil.
Season with salt and pepper.
Serve immediately with boiled potatoes and fresh chopped dill.
notes: Use naturally fermented pickles in brine, not vinegar-based sweet pickles.
Do not let the sauce boil after adding sour cream to prevent curdling.
Ensure pork is cooked to an internal temperature of 71°C.

recipes.recipe_name: Lomo Saltado with Steamed Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Lomo Saltado presented on a clean white porcelain plate. The dish features thick, seared beef chunks tossed with vibrant purple red onion wedges and softened red tomato wedges. Golden-brown fried potato batons are interspersed throughout the stir-fry, coated in a dark, glossy soy-vinegar sauce. A neat, circular mound of fluffy white long-grain rice is positioned on the side of the plate. The beef shows a deep brown sear. Fresh green cilantro leaves are scattered over the top. The arrangement is organic and centered with moderate negative space. The setting is a light wood table with a linen napkin and a simple fork and spoon.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of spicy aji verde sauce
Pair with Inca Kola or a Pisco Sour
Traditional fork and spoon service
instructions: Rinse rice until water runs clear. Combine with 450ml water. Simmer covered until tender.
Peel potatoes. Cut into 1cm thick batons. Fry in oil until golden and crisp. Drain on paper towels.
Cut beef into 2cm thick chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 30ml oil in a wok over high heat. Sear beef chunks in batches until browned. Remove and set aside.
Add remaining oil to wok. Sauté red onion wedges for 2 minutes until slightly softened.
Stir in minced garlic and aji amarillo paste. Cook for 1 minute.
Add tomato wedges and return beef to the wok.
Pour in soy sauce and red wine vinegar. Toss rapidly for 1 minute to deglaze.
Fold in the fried potato batons and chopped cilantro. Remove from heat immediately.
Serve immediately with the steamed rice.
notes: Ensure the wok is smoking hot before adding beef to achieve authentic 'wok hei' flavor.
Do not overcook the tomatoes; they should be softened but hold their wedge shape.
Add potatoes at the very last second to maintain their crispness.

recipes.recipe_name: Risotto ai Funghi con Bocconcini di Manzo
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The risotto is fluid and creamy, spreading naturally across the plate. The rice is a pale, earthy tan color, interspersed with golden-brown sautéed cremini mushroom quarters and dark porcini fragments. Resting in the center are five thick, 3cm cubes of seared beef tenderloin with a dark, caramelized crust. The meat is presented as whole chunks, never sliced. A sprinkle of bright green chopped parsley and delicate shavings of Parmigiano-Reggiano garnish the top. The scene is set on a dark walnut table with a folded linen napkin and a polished silver spoon. Natural side lighting creates soft shadows and highlights the glossy, velvety texture of the rice.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of medium-bodied red wine like Barbera or Nebbiolo.
Offer extra grated Parmigiano-Reggiano at the table.
Use a flat-bottomed risotto spoon for serving.
instructions: Soak dried porcini in 200ml warm water for 20 minutes.
Strain porcini liquid into beef stock. Chop porcini finely.
Season beef chunks with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a pan over high heat.
Sear beef chunks until browned on all sides. Remove and set aside.
Heat remaining oil in a heavy-based pot over medium heat.
Sauté shallots and cremini mushrooms until golden.
Add rice to the pot. Toast for 2 minutes until translucent.
Deglaze with white wine. Stir until liquid evaporates.
Add simmering stock one ladle at a time, stirring constantly.
Incorporate chopped porcini halfway through cooking.
Cook rice for 18 minutes until al dente.
Remove from heat. Add butter and Parmigiano-Reggiano.
Stir vigorously to create a creamy emulsion.
Fold in beef chunks. Cover and rest for 2 minutes.
Adjust seasoning and serve immediately.
notes: Ensure the beef stock is kept at a constant simmer.
Stir the rice frequently to release starches for a creamier texture.
The risotto should be 'all'onda', meaning it flows like a wave when the plate is tilted.

recipes.recipe_name: Zero-Waste Spiced Chicken and Apple Tart
recipes.visual_description: A single rustic circular tart sits centered on a matte cream handcrafted ceramic plate. The crust is golden-brown and flaky, revealing the sourdough texture. In the center, tender wedges of roasted apple are piled naturally, glistening with a honey-schmaltz glaze. Small, caramelized chunks of spiced chicken are nestled between the apple wedges. The plate rests on a dark reclaimed oak table. A beige linen napkin lies folded to the left. A simple wooden fork is placed beside the plate. Soft natural light from a side window highlights the glistening fruit and the crisp edges of the pastry. The background is a blurred minimalist kitchen with a small green plant.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm with a dollop of fermented cream or labneh
Pair with a dry sparkling local cider
Garnish with fresh thyme sprigs
instructions: Render chicken skin and fat over low heat.
Strain and reserve liquid schmaltz.
Mince chicken thigh meat finely.
Sauté chicken in 20g schmaltz, honey, and cinnamon.
Cook chicken to 75°C internal temperature.
Combine flour, salt, sourdough discard, and 60g chilled schmaltz.
Add cold water until dough forms.
Chill dough 30 minutes.
Slice apples into 5mm wedges.
Toss apples with vinegar and honey.
Roll dough to 3mm thickness.
Arrange chicken chunks and apples in center.
Fold edges to form a rustic galette.
Bake at 180°C for 30 minutes.
notes: Use chicken skin saved from previous meal prep to maximize waste reduction
Windfall or slightly bruised apples are ideal for this preservation method
The sourdough discard adds a traditional fermented tang to the pastry

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo with Black Beans
recipes.visual_description: The dish features a vibrant Mexican Arroz con Pollo served in a shallow white porcelain bowl. The centerpiece consists of two whole seared chicken thighs, their skin a deep golden brown with visible charred edges. They rest atop a bed of fluffy, tomato-tinted orange rice interspersed with whole black beans and softened diced onions. Bright red cubes of fresh tomato are scattered throughout for color contrast. Crumbled white queso fresco is melted slightly over the hot chicken and rice. A garnish of fresh cilantro leaves and a lime wedge provides a pop of green. The plate sits on a dark wood table next to a folded cotton napkin and a silver fork. Natural side lighting highlights the textures of the grains and the moist chicken.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas
Accompany with fresh salsa roja or salsa verde
Provide extra lime wedges for acidity
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt, pepper, and cumin.
Heat oil in a large heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken for 5 minutes per side until golden brown.
Remove chicken from the pan and set aside.
Add diced onion to the same pan. Sauté for 3 minutes until translucent.
Stir in the rice. Toast for 2 minutes until lightly golden.
Add garlic and half of the diced tomatoes. Cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in chicken stock and add dried oregano. Bring to a boil.
Return chicken thighs to the pan. Cover and reduce heat to low.
Simmer for 18 minutes until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Stir in the black beans and remaining tomatoes.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Sprinkle crumbled queso fresco over the top. Cover for 2 minutes to soften.
Garnish with fresh cilantro before serving.
notes: Ensure the rice is toasted before adding liquid for better texture
Use bone-in thighs for maximum flavor and moisture
Always check chicken reaches the safe internal temperature of 75°C

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Arroz con Pollo presented on a clean white porcelain plate. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs with deeply browned, crispy skin sit atop a bed of golden, saffron-stained rice. The rice grains are plump and distinct, interspersed with fine bits of softened onion and concentrated red tomato. The dish shows vibrant yellow and orange hues from the saffron and paprika. A generous sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped parsley is scattered over the top. A single lemon wedge is placed neatly on the side. The plate sits on a light oak wooden table with a folded white cotton napkin. Lighting is bright, natural, and even, highlighting the textures of the crispy skin and the moist rice grains.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Alioli (garlic mayonnaise)
Accompany with crusty bread and a glass of chilled white wine
Present in a traditional terracotta cazuela for family-style dining
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide shallow pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden and crispy.
Flip and brown the other side. Remove chicken from pan.
Add onion to the same pan. Sauté until translucent.
Stir in garlic and grated tomato. Cook until liquid evaporates and mixture darkens.
Add smoked paprika and rice. Stir to coat rice in oil for 2 minutes.
Pour in white wine. Deglaze the pan. Simmer until wine reduces by half.
Add hot stock and saffron. Stir once to distribute.
Place chicken thighs back into the pan on top of the rice.
Simmer undisturbed over medium-low heat for 18-20 minutes.
Ensure chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove from heat. Cover with a clean cloth. Rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Do not stir the rice once the stock is added to allow a crust to form on the bottom.
Use a wide pan to ensure even rice cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish White Bean and Bell Pepper Braise
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of the braise is served in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The base consists of plump, creamy white beans nestled in a deep ochre-colored tomato broth. Thick, 2-centimeter chunks of seared pancetta are distributed naturally throughout the beans. Vibrant red bell pepper squares, cut into 1-centimeter dice and charred at the edges, provide a bright contrast across the surface. A swirl of vivid green herb oil and fresh torn parsley leaves garnish the top. The bowl rests on a rustic light wood table. A side of toasted sourdough batons sits on a small plate. Soft natural light emphasizes the glossy sheen of the sauce and the rustic textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty sourdough or pan con tomate
Accompany with a glass of Tempranillo
Present in a traditional clay cazuela for communal dining
instructions: Drain and rinse soaked beans.
Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat.
Add diced bell peppers. Sauté 8 minutes until edges char.
Remove half of the peppers and reserve for garnish.
Add pancetta chunks to the pot. Brown for 5 minutes.
Stir in garlic and smoked paprika. Toast for 1 minute.
Add grated tomatoes. Cook 5 minutes until the mixture thickens into a sofrito.
Add beans and stock. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer 90 minutes until beans are tender.
Season with salt and pepper.
Ladle into bowls. Top with reserved peppers and fresh parsley.
notes: Ensure beans are fully submerged during the entire simmering process
The sofrito is the flavor base; do not rush the tomato reduction
Adjust stock levels if a soupier consistency is desired

recipes.recipe_name: Thai Mustard and Tomato Chicken Stir-Fry
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Thai Mustard and Tomato Chicken Stir-Fry served on a clean white porcelain plate. The base features a mound of fluffy, steamed jasmine rice. On top, 3cm chunks of golden-seared chicken thigh are tossed with translucent 1cm onion wedges and softened, slightly charred cherry tomato halves. The sauce is a glossy, vibrant yellow-orange glaze that coats the ingredients without pooling. Garnish with fresh cilantro sprigs. The setting is a modern bistro with a dark wood table. A traditional Thai spoon and fork are placed on a folded white cotton napkin to the side. Natural light highlights the steam and the succulent texture of the meat. The entire plate is visible with moderate negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Prik Nam Pla (fish sauce with sliced chilies)
Use a spoon and fork, the traditional Thai way to eat rice dishes
Accompany with a cold Thai iced tea or lager
instructions: Rinse jasmine rice until water runs clear.
Combine rice and 450ml water in a pot.
Bring to boil, cover, and simmer 15 minutes.
Remove from heat and let stand 5 minutes.
Cut chicken into 3cm chunks.
Mix mustard, fish sauce, and sugar in a small bowl.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a wok over high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until golden and internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from wok and set aside.
Add remaining oil to wok.
Sauté garlic and onion wedges for 2 minutes.
Add halved cherry tomatoes and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Return chicken to the wok.
Pour mustard sauce over the ingredients.
Toss quickly for 30 seconds to glaze everything.
Garnish with fresh cilantro.
notes: Ensure the wok is very hot before adding chicken to achieve a proper sear.
Do not overcook the tomatoes; they should hold their shape while being soft.
Internal chicken temperature must reach 75°C for safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Matar Mushroom Masala
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Matar Mushroom Masala presented in a deep, matte-white porcelain bowl. The dish features plump, halved button mushrooms and vibrant green peas nestled in a thick, glossy, reddish-orange gravy. The sauce shows visible texture from the sautéed onions and spices, with a delicate swirl of white cream on top. Finely chopped green coriander and a pinch of crushed fenugreek leaves provide a fresh herbal garnish. The bowl sits on a rustic dark wood table alongside two thick, charred pieces of garlic naan stacked on a small wooden board. Natural window lighting creates soft highlights on the tender mushrooms and the rich, emulsified sauce base.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with hot garlic naan or tandoori roti
Accompany with a side of kachumber salad (cucumber, tomato, and onion)
Include a small bowl of thick Greek yogurt or raita
Serve with long-grain basmati rice or jeera rice
instructions: Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium heat.
Add cumin seeds and let them sizzle for 30 seconds.
Add diced onions. Sauté until deep golden brown.
Stir in ginger-garlic paste. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in tomato puree. Add turmeric, chili powder, and coriander powder.
Cook the masala, stirring frequently, until oil separates from the edges.
Add halved mushrooms and green peas. Toss to coat in the spice base.
Pour in 150ml warm water. Season with salt.
Cover with a tight lid. Simmer on low heat for 10 minutes.
Crush kasuri methi between palms and add to the pan.
Stir in garam masala and heavy cream. Simmer for 2 minutes.
Garnish with fresh coriander before serving.
notes: Ensure onions are properly browned for a deep, authentic flavor base.
Do not overcook mushrooms to maintain their plump, meaty texture.
Kashmiri chili powder provides a vibrant red color without excessive heat.

recipes.recipe_name: Vietnamese Shaking Beef (Bo Luc Lac)
recipes.special_requests: beef protein full meal without much carbs but with veggies cuisine
recipes.visual_description: The dish features seared 2.5cm beef sirloin cubes, glistening with a dark soy glaze and showing deep caramelized edges from the high-heat wok sear. The beef is piled naturally in the center of a clean white porcelain plate, mixed with softened red onion wedges. It rests atop a vibrant bed of fresh, bright green watercress and halved ruby-red cherry tomatoes. The arrangement is organic and uncrowded, leaving white space around the perimeter. Beside the plate sits a small ceramic ramekin containing a clear lime juice and coarse black pepper dipping sauce. The setting is a modern bistro with a dark wood table, a folded white cotton napkin, and dark wooden chopsticks. Natural side lighting highlights the succulent meat and crisp greens.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with Muoi Tieu Chanh (salt, pepper, and lime dipping sauce)
Use chopsticks for dining
Can be accompanied by pickled daikon and carrots

ingredients.name: Red onion, cut into thin wedges

instructions: Pat beef cubes dry with paper towels.
Marinate beef with garlic, soy sauce, fish sauce, oyster sauce, and sugar for 30 minutes.
Whisk lime juice and black pepper in a small bowl for the dipping sauce.
Arrange watercress and cherry tomatoes on a large platter or individual plates.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat until smoking.
Add beef cubes in a single layer to ensure a hard sear.
Sear without moving for 2 minutes until a dark crust forms.
Add red onion wedges to the wok.
Shake the wok vigorously to sear all sides of the beef for 2 minutes.
Remove from heat immediately to keep the beef medium-rare.
Tumble the beef and onions directly onto the bed of watercress and tomatoes.
notes: Ensure the wok is smoking hot before adding meat to achieve authentic wok hei flavor.
Do not overcrowd the pan; cook in batches if necessary to maintain high heat.
The residual heat from the beef will slightly wilt the watercress, creating a warm salad effect.

recipes.recipe_name: Orecchiette with Italian Sausage and Herb Ricotta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of orecchiette served in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The pasta is coated in a smooth, creamy off-white ricotta sauce with visible flecks of vibrant green basil chiffonade. Large, 2cm rustic golden-brown seared Italian sausage chunks are nestled throughout the pasta, never sliced. The arrangement is organic and centered, leaving a clean white rim. A light dusting of finely grated Pecorino Romano and three small, whole basil leaves garnish the top. The dish sits on a light oak bistro table with a folded white linen napkin and a polished silver fork. Natural, soft daylight highlights the creamy sauce texture and the charred edges of the sausage.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread
Pair with a dry white wine like Vermentino
Present in shallow bowls
instructions: Boil 4 liters of salted water.
Cook orecchiette until al dente.
Reserve 200ml of pasta cooking water.
Brown sausage chunks in a large skillet over medium-high heat until golden.
Remove sausage from skillet and set aside.
Wipe skillet and heat olive oil over medium heat.
Sauté garlic for 1 minute until fragrant.
Whisk ricotta and blended cottage cheese in a bowl.
Slowly whisk 100ml warm pasta water into the cheese mixture to temper.
Add cooked pasta and sausage chunks back to the skillet.
Fold in cheese mixture and half the basil.
Toss over low heat until sauce reaches a creamy consistency.
Season with salt, pepper, and Pecorino Romano.
notes: Blending the cottage cheese ensures a smooth, professional sauce texture.
Do not boil the sauce once the cheese is added to prevent curdling.

recipes.recipe_name: Mushroom Ragù with Pappardelle
recipes.visual_description: The dish features a generous mound of wide, flat pappardelle ribbons coated in a rich, dark brown mushroom ragù. The mushrooms are cut into uniform 1cm cubes, showing a distinct caramelized sear and meaty texture. The glossy sauce clings to the pasta, interspersed with vibrant green flecks of fresh oregano. Plated in a clean, wide-rimmed white porcelain bowl, the arrangement is natural and fluid with moderate negative space. The lighting is soft and natural, emphasizing the matte texture of the pasta against the glistening sauce. A rustic wooden table provides the background, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and a small carafe of olive oil.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty sourdough bread to mop up the extra ragù.
Pair with a glass of robust red wine like Chianti.
Use a large shallow pasta bowl for presentation.
instructions: Boil 5 liters of water with 50g salt in a large pot.
Heat 40ml olive oil in a wide skillet over medium-high heat.
Add diced mushrooms and sear until deep brown and liquid evaporates, about 10 minutes.
Lower heat to medium. Add remaining oil, diced onion, and minced garlic.
Sauté 5 minutes until onions are translucent.
Stir in tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes until darkened.
Pour in vegetable stock and add chopped oregano.
Simmer ragù for 15 minutes until sauce thickens and coats the back of a spoon.
Cook pappardelle in boiling water until al dente.
Transfer pasta directly to the skillet using tongs.
Toss pasta with the ragù, adding 60ml of pasta water to emulsify.
Season with salt and pepper. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure mushrooms are well-browned before adding liquids to maximize umami flavor.
Reserve extra pasta water to adjust sauce consistency if needed.

recipes.recipe_name: Rum-Glazed Pork Belly with Pineapple-Guava Chutney
Risotto ai Funghi e Manzo
Hungarian Beef Pörkölt
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Hungarian Beef Pörkölt is presented on a clean white porcelain plate. The dish features 3cm chunks of tender, slow-braised beef coated in a thick, glossy, deep-crimson sauce. The beef chunks are arranged in a natural, rustic cluster in the center. Small droplets of vibrant red oil glisten on the surface of the rich gravy. Beside the meat, a small portion of hand-torn Nokedli dumplings provides a pale contrast. A garnish of fresh, finely chopped flat-leaf parsley is scattered over the top. The setting is a dark wooden bistro table with a linen napkin and a small side bowl of traditional pickled cucumbers. Natural side lighting emphasizes the succulent texture of the beef.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with Nokedli (Hungarian dumplings)
Accompany with Savanyúság (pickled vegetables)
Pair with a dry Hungarian red wine like Egri Bikavér
instructions: Heat olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat.
Add diced onions and sauté until soft and translucent.
Remove pot from heat and stir in paprika.
Add beef chunks and return pot to heat.
Sear beef until browned on all sides.
Add diced tomatoes, minced garlic, caraway seeds, salt, and pepper.
Pour in water and stir to combine.
Cover the pot and reduce heat to low.
Simmer for 2 hours until beef is fork-tender.
Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper before serving.
notes: Do not brown the onions too much; they should be soft to create a thick sauce.
Always remove the pot from heat before adding paprika to prevent burning.
The sauce should be thick and reduced, not watery like a soup.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Veal Blanquette with Pearl Onions
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a deep, wide-rimmed white porcelain bowl on a light oak bistro table. At the center, four large 4cm cubes of tender, pale-simmered veal shoulder are stacked naturally, coated in a glossy, ivory-colored sauce made from evaporated milk. Five whole, lightly caramelized pearl onions are tucked between the veal chunks. The sauce has a velvety, fluid consistency, pooling slightly at the base. A scattering of 2cm fresh chive batons provides a vibrant green contrast. The lighting is soft and natural from the side, highlighting the silky texture of the sauce and the matte finish of the meat. A crisp white cotton napkin and polished silver flatware rest beside the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed white rice
Pair with buttered tagliatelle
Serve with a dry white wine like Chenin Blanc
instructions: Place 4cm veal cubes in pot.
Cover with cold water.
Boil for 2 minutes.
Drain and rinse meat.
Return meat to clean pot.
Add stock, halved onion, carrot batons, celery batons, and bouquet garni.
Simmer 90 minutes until meat is tender.
Sauté pearl onions in butter until golden.
Strain cooking liquid.
Reserve 500ml liquid.
Discard boiled aromatics.
Melt 30g butter in saucepan.
Whisk in 30g flour.
Cook 2 minutes on medium heat.
Gradually whisk in reserved stock.
Simmer until sauce thickens.
Mix 250ml evaporated milk and 2 egg yolks.
Stir milk mixture into sauce.
Heat gently without boiling.
Add veal and pearl onions to sauce.
Season with salt, white pepper, and lemon juice.
notes: Rinsing the meat after the first boil ensures a clean, white sauce.
Do not let the sauce boil after adding the egg liaison to prevent curdling.

recipes.recipe_name: Tuscan Beef and Cannellini Bean Stew
recipes.visual_description: The dish features a deep, rustic red braise served in a wide white porcelain bowl. Large, tender 4cm beef chunks are the centerpiece, glistening with a rich tomato reduction. Creamy white cannellini beans are nestled between the meat, maintaining their shape. The sauce is thick and savory, showing visible bits of softened diced onion. A single sprig of fresh rosemary and a drizzle of extra virgin olive oil garnish the top. The bowl sits on a dark wood bistro table next to a piece of toasted ciabatta bread. A linen napkin and a silver spoon rest beside the plate. Natural side lighting highlights the succulent texture of the seared beef and the smooth beans.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with toasted ciabatta bread rubbed with garlic
Pair with a glass of Chianti or other Sangiovese-based wine
Finish with a generous dusting of grated Pecorino Romano
instructions: Pat beef cubes dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Brown beef chunks in batches until deep brown on all sides. Remove and set aside.
Add diced onions to the pot. Sauté until soft and translucent.
Stir in minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return beef to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes, beef stock, rosemary, and oregano.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 90 minutes until beef is tender.
Stir in cannellini beans. Simmer uncovered for 10 minutes to thicken the sauce.
Remove rosemary sprig before serving.
notes: Ensure the beef is patted very dry before searing to achieve a proper crust
Do not boil the stew; a low simmer ensures the meat remains succulent
The flavor improves if made one day in advance

recipes.recipe_name: Poulet Basquaise
recipes.visual_description: The dish features two whole bone-in chicken thighs with crisp, golden-brown skin. The chicken sits atop a vibrant, thick Piperade sauce made of softened julienne-cut red peppers and onions. The sauce is a rich, deep red color from the tomatoes and Piment d'Espelette. The chicken is presented whole, never sliced. The plating uses a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl with moderate negative space. A glossy sheen coats the vegetables. Freshly chopped green parsley is scattered over the top. The setting includes a dark wood table, a neutral cotton napkin, and a side plate of crusty baguette. Natural, soft side lighting highlights the textures of the seared skin and tender peppers.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty baguette to soak up the sauce
Accompany with steamed white rice or boiled potatoes
Pair with a crisp French rosé or a light-bodied red wine
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large deep skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden brown. Flip and sear 2 minutes.
Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Slice onions into thin wedges. Cut red peppers into long julienne strips.
Add onions and peppers to the skillet. Sauté 8 minutes until softened.
Stir in minced garlic and Piment d'Espelette. Cook for 1 minute.
Pour in white wine. Scrape the bottom of the pan. Reduce liquid by half.
Add tomatoes, chicken stock, thyme, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken to the skillet, skin-side up. Do not submerge the skin.
Cover and simmer for 20 minutes.
Uncover. Continue cooking until chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove thyme sprigs and bay leaf. Season sauce with salt.
Garnish with chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Ensure the chicken skin remains above the liquid level to stay crisp during braising
If Piment d'Espelette is unavailable, substitute with mild smoked paprika and a pinch of cayenne

recipes.recipe_name: Gai Tod Kratiem Prik Thai
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Gai Tod Kratiem Prik Thai served on a traditional blue and white Thai ceramic plate. The dish features golden-brown, seared chicken chunks piled naturally next to a neat mound of steamed jasmine rice. The chicken is generously topped with a heap of crispy, deep-fried golden garlic bits. Three thick cucumber rounds are placed on the side for contrast. The plate sits on a dark wood table in a modern bistro setting. A Thai-style stainless steel spoon and fork lie on a folded white cotton napkin. Natural light highlights the glistening oil on the chicken and the airy texture of the rice. A small side bowl of chili fish sauce completes the arrangement.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Prik Nam Pla (fish sauce with sliced bird's eye chilies)
Eat using a large spoon in the right hand and a fork in the left hand to push food onto the spoon
Pair with a clear cucumber soup to balance the savory garlic flavor

ingredients.name: boneless skin-on chicken thighs, cut into 3cm chunks

instructions: Pound coriander roots, white peppercorns, and 20g of garlic in a mortar until a smooth paste forms.
Mix the paste with chicken, oyster sauce, soy sauce, fish sauce, and palm sugar in a bowl.
Marinate chicken for 30 minutes at room temperature.
Heat oil in a wok over medium-low heat.
Add remaining 80g of minced garlic to the oil.
Fry garlic until golden brown and crisp.
Remove fried garlic with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
Increase wok heat to medium-high.
Add chicken chunks to the garlic-infused oil.
Sear chicken until deeply browned and the internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from the wok and drain excess oil.
Toss chicken with half of the fried garlic.
Serve immediately over jasmine rice.
notes: Do not burn the garlic or it will become bitter.
Ensure the chicken skin remains attached to the chunks for maximum crispness.
The 'Thai Trinity' of coriander root, garlic, and pepper is essential for the authentic aroma.
traditional_techniques: pounding aromatics in a mortar and pestle

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Cacciatore
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of rustic chicken cacciatore served in a shallow, cream-colored ceramic bowl with minor surface imperfections. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs are the centerpiece, their skin appearing dark golden and tender from braising. The chicken is partially submerged in a thick, chunky tomato sauce featuring visible pieces of softened translucent onions and whole black olives. A single fresh rosemary sprig is placed casually on top. The bowl sits on a weathered dark wood kitchen table. Beside the bowl is a thick piece of torn crusty bread. The scene is illuminated by warm, soft overhead kitchen lighting, creating a cozy, authentic Italian home-dining atmosphere. A simple linen napkin and a stainless steel fork are placed to the left of the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty sourdough bread to soak up the tomato sauce
Pair with a side of simple polenta or rustic mashed potatoes
Traditional family-style dining involves placing the skillet in the center of the table
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper on all sides.
Heat olive oil in a large deep skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes until golden brown.
Flip chicken and sear for 4 minutes. Remove chicken from skillet.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Sauté for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add crushed tomatoes, oregano, and the rosemary sprig.
Place chicken back into the skillet, nestled into the sauce.
Simmer on low heat for 30 minutes until chicken reaches 75°C internally.
Stir in the olives 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Use bone-in thighs for maximum flavor and protein content
Ensure the sauce reduces until thick to concentrate the savory tomato profile
Always check the thickest part of the chicken for a safe internal temperature of 75°C

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Stuffed Onions
recipes.visual_description: A single, large white onion sits centrally on a clean white porcelain plate. The onion is braised to a translucent, golden-amber hue, revealing a savory stuffing of browned ground beef and pork mixed with vibrant red peppers. A glossy, deep mahogany reduction sauce coats the base of the plate, pooling slightly around the onion. Fine flecks of bright green flat-leaf parsley are scattered over the top. Beside the plate lies a piece of crusty rustic bread and a traditional Spanish wine glass. The lighting is soft and natural, highlighting the silky texture of the onion layers and the rich sheen of the sauce. The background is a dark wood bistro table, providing a warm, professional atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Crusty rustic bread
Asturian cider
Tempranillo wine
instructions: Peel onions and remove the tops.
Scoop out onion centers using a spoon.
Leave two outer layers to form a shell.
Finely chop the removed onion centers.
Heat olive oil in a large pan.
Sauté chopped onions and garlic until soft.
Add beef and pork to the pan.
Brown the meat over medium heat.
Stir in tomato paste and pimentón.
Add diced roasted peppers.
Pour in white wine.
Simmer until liquid evaporates.
Season with salt and pepper.
Stuff onion shells tightly with meat mixture.
Place stuffed onions in a deep pot.
Add beef stock to the pot.
Cover and simmer on low for 45 minutes.
Transfer onions to a serving plate.
Boil remaining liquid until it thickens into a glaze.
Spoon glaze over the onions.
Garnish with chopped parsley.
notes: Select onions of uniform size for even cooking.
Ensure the onion shells are not punctured during scooping.

recipes.recipe_name: Thai Basil Chicken with Jasmine Rice
recipes.visual_description: A steaming mound of fluffy jasmine rice occupies half of a clean white porcelain plate. Beside it, glossy 2cm chunks of golden-brown seared chicken thighs are coated in a dark, savory sauce. Vibrant green Thai basil leaves are wilted throughout the stir-fry. A single fried egg with a lacy, golden-crisp edge and a bright runny yolk rests atop the chicken. The dish is presented on a dark teak wood table with a small side dish of fish sauce containing sliced red chilies. Soft natural lighting highlights the textures of the crispy egg and tender chicken. A traditional Thai stainless steel spoon and fork lie on a white cotton napkin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with Prik Nam Pla (fish sauce with chilies)
Eat with a spoon in the right hand and fork in the left
Provide cucumber slices to cool the palate
instructions: Rinse rice until water runs clear.
Cook rice in 600ml water until fluffy.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a pan over high heat.
Fry eggs until edges are crispy and brown.
Remove eggs and set aside.
Heat remaining oil in a wok.
Sauté garlic and chilies until fragrant.
Add chicken chunks to the wok.
Stir-fry chicken until browned and internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Stir in oyster sauce, soy sauces, and sugar.
Add basil leaves and toss until wilted.
Divide rice into four plates.
Top rice with chicken and a fried egg.
notes: Use Holy Basil for the most authentic flavor if available.
Adjust chili count based on heat preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Baingan Bharta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Baingan Bharta is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl, centered on a dark rustic wooden table. The dish is a thick, textured mash of fire-roasted eggplant, showing charred flecks and a rich brown hue, interspersed with diced sautéed red tomatoes and translucent caramelized onions. The mash is topped with a vibrant garnish of coarsely chopped fresh coriander. To the side of the bowl, two warm, charred whole-wheat rotis are stacked neatly. The arrangement leaves ample negative space on the clean white surface of the bowl. A simple cotton napkin and a polished spoon lie beside the plate. The scene is captured in natural light, emphasizing the rustic, savory textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm tandoori roti or naan
Accompany with a side of cooling cucumber raita
Include sliced raw red onions and lemon wedges on the side
instructions: Wash and dry eggplants. Rub surfaces with oil.
Roast eggplants over an open gas flame until skin is charred and flesh is soft.
Cool eggplants. Peel off charred skin and mash the flesh.
Finely dice onions and tomatoes. Mince the green chilies.
Heat remaining oil in a large pan. Add cumin seeds.
Add diced onions. Sauté until golden brown.
Stir in ginger-garlic paste and chilies. Cook for 1 minute.
Add tomatoes, turmeric, red chili powder, and salt. Cook until oil separates.
Add mashed eggplant. Mix well. Cook for 10 minutes on medium heat.
Stir in half of the chopped coriander. Remove from heat.
Garnish with remaining coriander.
notes: Ensure the eggplant is completely soft before peeling to ensure a smooth mash
If an open flame is unavailable, roast eggplants in a 220°C oven for 45 minutes

recipes.recipe_name: Gai Tod Kratiem Prik Thai
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Gai Tod Kratiem Prik Thai served on a traditional blue and white Thai ceramic plate. The dish features golden-brown, seared chicken chunks piled naturally next to a neat mound of steamed jasmine rice. The chicken is generously topped with a heap of crispy, deep-fried golden garlic bits. Three thick cucumber rounds are placed on the side for contrast. The plate sits on a dark wood table in a modern bistro setting. A Thai-style stainless steel spoon and fork lie on a folded white cotton napkin. Natural light highlights the glistening oil on the chicken and the airy texture of the rice. A small side bowl of chili fish sauce completes the arrangement.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Prik Nam Pla (fish sauce with sliced bird's eye chilies)
Eat using a large spoon in the right hand and a fork in the left hand to push food onto the spoon
Pair with a clear cucumber soup to balance the savory garlic flavor

Mix the paste with chicken, oyster sauce, soy sauce, fish sauce, and palm sugar in a bowl.
Marinate chicken for 30 minutes at room temperature.
Heat oil in a wok over medium-low heat.
Add remaining 80g of minced garlic to the oil.
Fry garlic until golden brown and crisp.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Arroz con Pollo
recipes.visual_description: A wide, shallow white porcelain bowl contains a vibrant mound of golden-hued short-grain rice. Two whole bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs rest atop the rice, featuring a deeply seared, crispy bronze skin. Evenly distributed through the rice are 1cm cubes of charred red bell pepper and finely diced translucent onions. The rice is moist and slightly glossy from the olive oil and tomato reduction. Sprigs of fresh, bright green flat-leaf parsley are scattered over the dish. The plate sits on a rustic light oak table next to a folded white cotton napkin and a polished silver fork. Natural side-lighting highlights the textures of the crispy skin and the individual grains of rice.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in a traditional shallow terracotta dish or paella pan
Accompany with a side of garlic aioli
Pair with a chilled glass of Spanish Albariño
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes until golden.
Flip chicken and sear for 3 minutes. Remove from pan.
Sauté onion and red pepper in the same pan for 5 minutes.
Add garlic and thyme. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in grated tomato. Cook for 4 minutes until liquid evaporates.
Add rice to the pan. Stir for 2 minutes to toast the grains.
Pour in white wine. Scrape the bottom of the pan to deglaze.
Add chicken stock. Bring to a simmer.
Place chicken thighs back into the pan on top of the rice.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 20 minutes.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove from heat. Let rest covered for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Do not stir the rice once the stock is added to allow a crust to form
Grate the tomatoes to remove skins easily while keeping the pulp

recipes.recipe_name: Basque Chicken with Peppers and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain plate in a modern bistro setting. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs are the centerpiece, featuring crispy, golden-brown skin glazed in a vibrant, deep red chilindrón sauce. The sauce is thick and rustic, filled with softened julienne strips of red and green bell peppers and translucent onions. To the side, a cluster of 3cm potato chunks provides a textural contrast with their craggy, golden-fried exterior. Coarsely chopped fresh parsley is scattered over the chicken. The plate sits on a light oak table next to a linen napkin and a small basket of crusty bread, illuminated by soft, natural window light.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty baguette or rustic sourdough to soak up the sauce
Pair with a glass of Rioja or a dry Spanish cider
Present in a traditional terracotta cazuela for family-style service

ingredients.name: Potatoes, peeled and cut into 3cm chunks

instructions: Soak dried chilies in hot water for 15 minutes. Scrape out the pulp and set aside.
Season chicken with salt and pepper. Heat 30ml olive oil in a wide pan.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden brown. Flip and sear 2 minutes. Remove chicken from pan.
Add onions and bell peppers to the same pan. Sauté over medium heat until softened.
Stir in garlic, chili pulp, and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute.
Add tomato purée and chicken stock. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken to the pan. Cover and simmer for 25 minutes until chicken reaches 75°C internally.
Boil potato chunks in salted water for 10 minutes. Drain well.
Heat remaining oil in a skillet. Fry potatoes until golden and crispy on all sides.
Plate two whole chicken thighs per person. Top with the pepper sauce. Serve potatoes on the side.
Garnish with fresh parsley.
notes: Ensure the chili pulp is smooth to integrate better into the sofrito
Do not crowd the pan when frying potatoes to maintain crispness
Use a meat thermometer to confirm the chicken reaches exactly 75°C

recipes.recipe_name: Pasta alla Norma
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of rigatoni pasta is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. Each tube of pasta is evenly coated in a vibrant, glossy tomato sauce. Large 2cm cubes of eggplant, fried to a rich golden-brown with visible caramelized edges, are distributed throughout the dish. A central mound of snow-white Ricotta Salata is coarsely grated over the top, providing a sharp textural contrast. Three fresh, deep green basil leaves are placed intentionally off-center. The bowl sits on a dark walnut wood table under soft, natural side lighting. A neutral grey cotton napkin and a polished silver fork rest beside the bowl. The arrangement is clean, focusing on the vivid red, white, and green colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of Nero d'Avola red wine
Present with extra Ricotta Salata on the side
Provide crusty bread to clean the sauce
instructions: Cut eggplant into 2cm cubes.
Sprinkle cubes with salt. Let sit for 30 minutes.
Rinse eggplant and pat dry with paper towels.
Heat 200ml olive oil in a pan. Fry eggplant cubes until golden brown.
Drain eggplant on paper towels. Set aside.
Mince garlic cloves.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large skillet. Sauté garlic for 1 minute.
Add tomato passata. Simmer on low heat for 15 minutes.
Boil 4 liters of salted water. Cook rigatoni until al dente.
Drain pasta. Reserve 50ml pasta water.
Add pasta and half the eggplant to the sauce.
Toss over heat for 1 minute. Add pasta water if dry.
Plate pasta. Top with remaining eggplant.
Grate ricotta salata over the top. Garnish with basil.
notes: Ensure eggplant is dried thoroughly before frying to achieve a crisp texture.
Use aged Ricotta Salata, not fresh ricotta, for the authentic salty flavor profile.
Do not overcook the pasta; it must maintain a firm bite.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo with Manchego
recipes.visual_description: The dish features two whole, golden-brown seared chicken thighs resting atop a bed of vibrant yellow saffron rice. The rice is textured with small diced red bell peppers and translucent onions. The chicken skin is crisp and deeply caramelized. Finely grated Manchego cheese is partially melted into the rice, with a light dusting of fresh cheese visible on top. Fresh green parsley is sprinkled evenly across the plate. The meal is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. The setting includes a rustic wooden table with natural side-lighting, a white cotton napkin, and a polished silver fork. No meat is sliced; chicken is served as whole pieces. The entire plate is visible with balanced negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with fresh lemon wedges for acidity
Accompany with a side of crusty bread
Pair with a glass of Spanish Tempranillo
instructions: Season chicken thighs generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide, heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat.
Place chicken skin-side down. Sear for 6 minutes until skin is crisp and golden.
Flip chicken. Sear for 4 minutes. Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Add onion and red bell pepper to the same pan. Sauté for 5 minutes until softened.
Stir in garlic and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add rice to the pan. Stir to coat in oil and toast for 2 minutes.
Pour in chicken stock and add saffron. Bring to a simmer.
Place chicken thighs back into the pan on top of the rice.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 20 minutes.
Verify chicken internal temperature has reached 75°C.
Remove from heat. Stir half of the Manchego cheese into the rice.
Cover and let rest for 5 minutes. Top with remaining cheese and parsley before serving.
notes: Do not stir the rice once the chicken is added to ensure a proper crust forms at the bottom.
Ensure the saffron is high quality for the best color and aroma.

recipes.recipe_name: Filipino Chicken Adobo
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Filipino Chicken Adobo sits in a shallow, rustic ceramic bowl. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs are the focal point, coated in a deep mahogany, glossy sauce that pools slightly at the base. The skin is dark and slightly tacky from the reduction. Scattered over the meat are softened, golden-brown crushed garlic cloves and a few whole black peppercorns. The chicken rests partly on a bed of fluffy, steamed white jasmine rice. The setting is a dark wooden table with a simple spoon and fork placed on a linen napkin. Warm, overhead kitchen lighting highlights the rich textures and the steam rising from the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of atchara (pickled green papaya)
Eat using a spoon and fork, the traditional Filipino way
Pour extra adobo sauce over the rice
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels.
Heat oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken pieces until skin is brown and crisp.
Remove chicken and set aside.
Sauté crushed garlic in the same pot for 1 minute.
Return chicken to the pot.
Add soy sauce, vinegar, water, peppercorns, and bay leaves.
Bring liquid to a boil.
Reduce heat to low and cover.
Simmer for 30 minutes.
Check chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove the lid and increase heat to medium-high.
Simmer until the sauce reduces and thickens into a glossy glaze.
Stir in sugar if using for balance.
Discard bay leaves before serving.
notes: Do not stir the sauce immediately after adding vinegar to allow the raw acidity to cook off.
Use cane vinegar for the most authentic flavor profile.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo alla Valdostana
recipes.visual_description: A single whole pan-seared chicken breast sits centered on a clean white porcelain plate. The chicken is topped with a draped slice of savory prosciutto and a generous layer of melted, bubbling pale-yellow Fontina cheese. A glossy, light-colored white wine and butter emulsion pools around the base of the chicken. Two crisp-fried dark green sage leaves rest on top of the melted cheese. The plate is set on a dark rustic wood bistro table. A folded white cotton napkin and polished silver fork are placed to the left. The lighting is natural and soft, highlighting the creamy textures of the cheese and the golden seared edges of the meat. Moderate negative space ensures a clean, professional restaurant presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with roasted rosemary potatoes
Accompany with sautéed spinach and garlic
Pair with a dry white wine from the Aosta Valley
instructions: Pound chicken breasts to 1.5 cm thickness.
Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Dredge chicken lightly in flour and shake off excess.
Heat oil and 15g butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken for 4 minutes per side.
Confirm internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Place one prosciutto slice on each chicken breast.
Top with sliced Fontina cheese.
Add wine and remaining butter to the skillet.
Cover skillet and simmer for 2 minutes until cheese melts.
Garnish with fresh sage leaves.
notes: Use authentic Fontina from Aosta Valley for a nutty flavor profile
Do not over-flour the chicken to keep the sauce translucent

recipes.recipe_name: Roast Chicken with Potatoes and Gruyère Broccoli
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents a whole pan-seared chicken breast with deeply browned, crispy skin as the focal point. It rests against a cluster of golden-brown roasted potato cubes, cut into uniform 3cm pieces with visible herb flecks. Beside the potatoes, bright green steamed broccoli florets provide a fresh color contrast. A smooth, glossy Gruyère Mornay sauce is poured elegantly over one side of the chicken, cascading onto the vegetables. The meal is served on a wide, matte white ceramic plate with ample negative space. A single sprig of fresh thyme adds a final touch. The background is a minimalist bistro setting with a light wood table, a folded linen napkin, and natural morning light.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of chilled Chardonnay or dry white wine
Accompany with fresh crusty baguette to soak up the Gruyère sauce
instructions: Heat oven to 200°C.
Toss potato cubes with olive oil, salt, and smashed garlic on a baking tray.
Roast potatoes for 25 minutes until golden and crisp.
Season chicken breasts with salt and pepper.
Sear chicken skin-side down in a hot oven-safe pan for 5 minutes until skin is crisp.
Flip chicken and transfer the pan to the oven.
Roast chicken until the internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Steam broccoli florets for 4 minutes until tender-crisp and vibrant green.
Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in flour for 2 minutes.
Gradually whisk in milk. Simmer until the sauce thickens and coats a spoon.
Whisk in grated Gruyère until completely melted and smooth. Season to taste.
Rest chicken for 5 minutes. Plate whole chicken breast with roasted potatoes and broccoli. Drizzle with cheese sauce.
notes: Ensure the chicken reaches a minimum internal temperature of 75°C for safety
Use high-quality aged Gruyère for a more complex and savory sauce flavor
Pat the chicken skin very dry before searing to ensure maximum crispness

recipes.recipe_name: French Chicken Fricassee
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of French Chicken Fricassee served on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Two whole, golden-brown seared chicken thighs sit at the center of the plate. The thighs are partially coated in a velvety, ivory-colored cream sauce. Small, translucent bits of softened diced onion and minced garlic are visible within the sauce. Freshly chopped bright green parsley is scattered over the top. Beside the chicken, three small boiled buttered potatoes are placed neatly. The plate is set on a dark wood bistro table. A white cotton napkin and polished silver fork and knife sit to the side. Natural light highlights the glossy texture of the sauce and the crisp skin of the chicken.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a crusty baguette to soak up the sauce
Pair with a dry Chablis or Sauvignon Blanc
Accompany with steamed green beans or buttered peas
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels.
Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Melt butter in a large heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat.
Place chicken skin-side down in the pan.
Sear for 6 minutes until skin is golden and crisp.
Flip chicken and sear for 3 minutes.
Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Add diced onions to the remaining fat.
Sauté onions for 5 minutes until translucent.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in flour and cook for 1 minute to form a roux.
Pour in white wine and scrape the bottom of the pan.
Add chicken stock, thyme, and bay leaf.
Return chicken thighs to the pan skin-side up.
Reduce heat to low and simmer for 20 minutes.
Check chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken thighs and set aside.
Stir heavy cream into the sauce.
Simmer sauce for 3 minutes until thickened.
Return chicken to the pan to coat.
Garnish with fresh parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches a safe internal temperature of 75°C
Use a high-quality dry white wine for the best sauce flavor
Do not cover the pan completely during simmering to keep the skin slightly crisp

recipes.recipe_name: Lemon and Garlic Braised Chicken with Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion served on a wide white porcelain plate. The base is a mound of fluffy long-grain rice with visible bits of softened onion. Two whole bone-in chicken thighs sit prominently on the rice, featuring a dark golden-brown, crispy seared skin. Two thick, slightly caramelized lemon wedges are positioned next to the meat. The dish is garnished with a precise sprinkle of vibrant green chopped parsley. The arrangement is natural and centered with clean margins. The setting is a modern bistro with a light oak table, a folded white linen napkin, and a stainless steel fork. Natural side lighting emphasizes the textures of the crispy skin and individual rice grains.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Greek yogurt or tzatziki
Accompany with crusty sourdough bread
Pair with a crisp Greek salad
instructions: Pat chicken dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes. Flip and sear for 3 minutes. Remove chicken.
Finely dice onion. Mince garlic.
Sauté onion in the same pan for 4 minutes. Add garlic. Cook for 1 minute.
Add rice. Stir for 2 minutes to toast the grains.
Add chicken stock, juice of one lemon, and lemon zest. Stir once.
Place chicken thighs on top of the rice. Add slices from the second lemon between chicken pieces.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 18 minutes.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Rest for 5 minutes. Garnish with finely chopped parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken skin is very dry before searing to achieve maximum crispness
Do not stir the rice while simmering to maintain distinct grains
Use a meat thermometer to guarantee the chicken reaches the safe 75°C internal temperature

recipes.recipe_name: Gambas al Ajillo with Roasted Peppers
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a traditional shallow terracotta cazuela resting on a clean white porcelain plate. The hero ingredient, large whole shrimp with tails intact, sits centrally, glistening in a vibrant, orange-tinted garlic oil. Interspersed among the shrimp are vibrant red bell pepper strips, softened and lightly charred at the edges. Thinly sliced golden-brown garlic chips and red chili flakes are scattered throughout the oil. The arrangement is organic and free-flowing. A sprinkle of bright green finely chopped parsley provides a fresh contrast. Beside the cazuela, two thick diagonal slices of toasted rustic sourdough bread are placed on the white plate. The scene is set on a light oak bistro table with a folded grey cotton napkin and a small side dish of sea salt. Natural side lighting highlights the glossy texture of the oil and the sear on the shrimp.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in a traditional terracotta cazuela to retain heat
Provide ample crusty bread to soak up the infused garlic oil
Pair with a chilled glass of dry Sherry or Albariño
instructions: Pat shrimp dry with paper towels. Season with salt.
Heat 20ml olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat.
Add bell pepper strips. Sauté 5 minutes until soft and charred. Remove and set aside.
Add remaining 80ml olive oil to a heavy skillet or clay cazuela.
Place sliced garlic and chili flakes into the cold oil.
Heat over medium-low. Cook until garlic turns golden brown. Do not burn.
Increase heat to medium-high. Add shrimp in a single layer.
Sear shrimp 2 minutes per side until opaque.
Fold in sautéed peppers and smoked paprika. Stir for 30 seconds.
Remove from heat. Stir in lemon juice and parsley.
Serve immediately with toasted bread.
notes: Ensure the oil is not too hot when adding garlic to prevent bitterness
Shrimp should be completely dry before cooking to achieve a proper sear

recipes.recipe_name: Thai Pineapple and Chili Chicken Stir-fry
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Thai stir-fry served on a clean white porcelain plate. The dish features 3cm chunks of golden-seared chicken breast and vibrant 2cm cubes of fresh yellow pineapple. Crisp 2cm diced red bell peppers and translucent onions are tossed in a glossy amber glaze. Bright green Thai basil leaves and whole roasted cashews provide textural contrast. A neat, steaming mound of white jasmine rice sits adjacent to the stir-fry. The entire plate is visible against a dark wood table. A blue cotton napkin and traditional Thai stainless steel spoon and fork are placed beside the plate. Natural even lighting highlights the juicy pineapple and seared meat textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Prik Nam Pla (fish sauce with sliced chilies)
Use a traditional Thai spoon and fork for dining
Accompany with a wedge of lime for added acidity
instructions: Rinse jasmine rice until water runs clear.
Cook rice in 450ml water until tender and fluffy.
Whisk fish sauce, soy sauce, oyster sauce, and palm sugar in a small bowl.
Heat vegetable oil in a wok over high heat until shimmering.
Add garlic and chilies. Stir-fry 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add chicken chunks. Sear 3-4 minutes until golden on all sides.
Toss in onion and bell pepper. Stir-fry 2 minutes.
Add pineapple cubes. Stir-fry 1 minute.
Pour in the sauce mixture. Toss to coat all ingredients.
Cook until chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove from heat. Fold in Thai basil and roasted cashews.
Serve immediately over warm jasmine rice.
