recipes.recipe_name: Yu Xiang Chicken and Eggplant
recipes.visual_description: A shallow white porcelain bowl holds the Yu Xiang Chicken and Eggplant. The chicken is cut into uniform 5cm batons, seared until opaque and tender. The eggplant batons retain a vibrant deep purple skin and a soft, translucent interior. Everything is coated in a glossy, reddish-brown translucent sauce speckled with minced garlic, ginger, and fermented chili bean paste. Bright green scallion rings are scattered across the top. The dish sits on a dark wood table next to a small bowl of steamed jasmine rice and a pair of dark wood chopsticks. The lighting is soft and natural, highlighting the silky texture of the eggplant and the sheen of the savory sauce.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice
Use dark wood chopsticks
Serve with a side of smashed cucumber salad
instructions: Cut chicken into 5cm batons.
Cut eggplant into 5cm batons.
Whisk soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, cornstarch, and water.
Heat 30ml oil in a wok.
Fry eggplant until tender.
Remove eggplant.
Heat 15ml oil.
Sear chicken until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken.
Sauté minced garlic, ginger, and chili paste for 30 seconds.
Return chicken and eggplant to wok.
Add sauce mixture.
Stir until sauce is thick and glossy.
Garnish with sliced scallions.
notes: Salt eggplant for 15 minutes to reduce oil absorption
Use Chinkiang vinegar for authentic flavor

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Thighs with Roquefort Cream Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of this modern French dish is presented on a clean white porcelain plate. Two whole bone-in chicken thighs with crispy, deep golden-brown seared skin are positioned centrally. A thick, velvety ivory-colored Roquefort cream sauce is draped elegantly over the lower half of the chicken, showing small blue cheese flecks. To the side, roasted golden fingerling potatoes cut into halves and bright green blanched haricots verts are arranged neatly. The plate features generous negative space for a professional look. The setting is a rustic wooden bistro table with a folded white cotton napkin and silver cutlery. Natural side lighting emphasizes the glossy texture of the sauce and the crispy chicken skin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty baguette slices to soak up the cream sauce
Pair with a dry white wine such as a French Chardonnay or Sauvignon Blanc
Follow with a simple green salad dressed in vinaigrette
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels.
Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil and butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Place chicken skin-side down in the pan.
Sear for 8 minutes until skin is golden and crisp.
Flip chicken and cook until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from pan and keep warm on a plate.
Drain excess fat, leaving 1 tablespoon in the skillet.
Sauté shallots and garlic for 2 minutes until translucent.
Pour in white wine to deglaze the pan, scraping up browned bits.
Reduce wine by half.
Stir in heavy cream and thyme sprigs.
Simmer for 5 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly.
Whisk in crumbled Roquefort cheese until melted and smooth.
Return chicken to the pan to coat with sauce.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Ensure the pan is not overcrowded to maintain skin crispness
Do not add extra salt to the sauce until tasting, as Roquefort is naturally salty
Use a meat thermometer to verify the 75°C internal temperature

recipes.recipe_name: Rajma Masala with Tofu and Basmati Rice
recipes.visual_description: A wide-rimmed white porcelain bowl contains a vibrant, thick tomato-based gravy. Large, un-sliced 2cm cubes of golden-seared tofu and plump red kidney beans are the focal point. The gravy is deep reddish-orange, textured with finely diced onions and softened red bell pepper chunks. A neat mound of long-grain, snowy white basmati rice sits slightly off-center, partially submerged in the sauce. Fresh green cilantro leaves and two bright green slit chilies garnish the top. The dish is placed on a rustic dark wood table. Beside the bowl is a small steel katori of mango chutney and a folded cotton napkin. Natural side-lighting highlights the steam and the glossy surface of the sauce.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with Lacha Piaz (sliced onions with lemon and salt)
Accompany with mango chutney or lime pickle
Serve with a side of plain yogurt or raita

ingredients.name: Red kidney beans, canned and drained
Red bell pepper, diced into 1cm squares

instructions: Rinse rice until water runs clear. Soak for 20 minutes.
Boil 600ml water. Add rice and salt. Simmer 12 minutes until fluffy.
Cut tofu into 2cm cubes. Pat dry.
Heat 1 tbsp oil. Brown tofu cubes on all sides. Remove and set aside.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a deep pan. Add cumin seeds. Let them sizzle.
Add onions and green chilies. Sauté until deep golden brown.
Stir in garlic and ginger paste. Cook for 1 minute.
Add bell peppers. Sauté for 3 minutes.
Pour in tomato puree. Add turmeric, chili powder, and salt.
Cook masala until oil separates from the edges.
Add kidney beans and 200ml water. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Gently fold in browned tofu cubes. Simmer for 2 minutes.
Stir in garam masala. Garnish with cilantro.
notes: Ensure the onions are well-browned for a deep, authentic gravy flavor.
Do not over-stir the tofu once added to the gravy to prevent breaking.
Use Kashmiri chili powder for the signature red color without excessive heat.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Katsu Curry Udon
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a deep, textured charcoal ceramic bowl. Thick, ivory-white udon noodles are partially submerged in a rich, mahogany-colored curry sauce that has a silky, reflective sheen. Three to four large, irregularly shaped chunks of golden panko-crusted chicken are positioned prominently, their surfaces showing a distinct craggy crunch. Adjacent to the chicken, several perfectly toasted 2cm cubes of white bread offer a geometric contrast and golden hue. A vibrant nest of finely julienned scallions provides a pop of fresh green against the dark sauce. The entire bowl is captured in soft, natural side-lighting on a minimalist light-oak table. A pair of tapered wooden chopsticks and a ceramic soup spoon rest on a neutral cotton napkin beside the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Fukujinzuke (Japanese red pickled vegetables)
Provide a deep ceramic renge spoon for the curry broth
Pair with iced mugicha (barley tea)
instructions: Cut bread into 2cm cubes. Toast in a dry pan until golden and crisp. Set aside.
Cut chicken into 4cm large chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Dredge chicken in flour, dip in beaten egg, and coat thoroughly with panko breadcrumbs.
Heat oil to 175°C. Fry chicken chunks until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Drain on a wire rack.
Thinly slice onion. Sauté in a large pot with a little oil until translucent.
Add dashi stock, soy sauce, and mirin. Bring to a simmer.
Turn off heat. Add curry roux blocks. Stir until completely dissolved and sauce thickens.
Blanch udon noodles in boiling water for 2 minutes. Drain well.
Divide noodles into four deep bowls. Ladle the curry sauce over the noodles.
Place 3-4 whole fried chicken chunks on top of each bowl. Add bread croutons and sliced scallions.
notes: Ensure the curry roux is fully dissolved before adding noodles to avoid clumps.
Do not overcook the udon; it should maintain a chewy, 'mochi-mochi' texture.
The bread croutons add a unique textural element that mimics the crunch of the katsu.

recipes.recipe_name: Sun-Dried Tomato and Three-Cheese Grilled Sandwich
recipes.visual_description: A single portion features a thick-cut sourdough sandwich toasted to a deep golden-brown hue. The sandwich is sliced once diagonally and stacked slightly offset to reveal the interior. Molten white Swiss and sharp yellow cheddar cheese stretch between the halves. Bright red, oil-packed sun-dried tomatoes are visible within the melted cheese layers. The bread surface shows a crisp, buttery texture with visible flecks of garlic. It sits on a clean white porcelain plate. A small pile of fresh green arugula provides a color contrast. The background is a light oak bistro table with a folded white cotton napkin and a simple glass of water. Natural side lighting highlights the crispy bread crust.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of creamy tomato basil soup
Accompany with spicy pickled cucumbers
Pair with a crisp apple cider or light lager
instructions: Drain and finely chop the sun-dried tomatoes.
Grate the cheddar, Swiss, and mozzarella cheeses.
Combine all three cheeses in a medium bowl.
Mix the softened butter with garlic powder in a small dish.
Spread the garlic butter evenly on one side of each bread slice.
Place four slices of bread, butter-side down, in a large skillet over medium heat.
Distribute the cheese mixture evenly across the four slices in the pan.
Top the cheese with chopped sun-dried tomatoes and fresh basil.
Place the remaining bread slices on top with the butter-side facing up.
Grill the sandwiches for 4 minutes per side until the bread is golden brown.
Ensure the internal cheese is completely melted before removing from the heat.
Serve immediately while hot.
notes: Use high-quality aged cheddar for better flavor depth.
Ensure the skillet is not too hot to prevent burning the bread before the cheese melts.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Potato Gratin with Gruyère
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chicken and Potato Gratin served in a clean white porcelain bowl. The base features thinly sliced 3mm potato rounds, layered and baked in a creamy, nutmeg-infused sauce. The surface has a bubbly, golden-brown crust of melted Gruyère cheese with caramelized edges. Two whole, pan-seared chicken thighs with crispy, deep-brown skin sit centrally atop the gratin. Fresh thyme leaves are scattered over the dish. The setting is a modern bistro with a light oak table, a white linen napkin, and a silver fork. Natural lighting highlights the contrast between the creamy sauce and the roasted chicken skin. The entire plate is visible.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty French baguette to soak up the cream sauce
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed in a sharp dijon vinaigrette
Pair with a glass of chilled Chardonnay or a light Pinot Noir
instructions: Peel and slice potatoes into 3mm rounds.
Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat butter in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes until crispy.
Flip chicken and cook for 4 minutes.
Remove chicken from the pan and set aside.
Whisk heavy cream, chicken stock, garlic, and nutmeg in a bowl.
Arrange half the potato slices in a greased ceramic baking dish.
Sprinkle 75g of Gruyère over the potatoes.
Layer the remaining potatoes on top.
Pour the cream mixture evenly over the potatoes.
Place the whole chicken thighs on top of the potato layers.
Bake at 190°C for 45 minutes.
Ensure chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Sprinkle remaining cheese over the dish.
Broil for 3 minutes until the cheese is bubbly and golden.
Let the dish rest for 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh thyme leaves.
notes: Using a mandoline ensures even potato slices for consistent cooking.
Dry the chicken skin thoroughly before searing to ensure maximum crispiness.
Check the thickest part of the chicken thigh to confirm it reaches 75°C.

recipes.recipe_name: Beer-Braised Beef and Black Bean Stew
recipes.visual_description: A deep, white porcelain bowl contains a generous portion of thick stew. Large 4cm chunks of dark, tender braised beef are the centerpiece, surrounded by whole black beans and rings of green jalapeño. The sauce is a rich, glossy reddish-brown. The dish is garnished with fresh cilantro leaves and a small dollop of white crema in the center. A single lime wedge sits on the rim of the bowl. The bowl is placed on a dark wooden bistro table. To the side, three warm corn tortillas are neatly folded on a small clay plate. The lighting is natural and bright, highlighting the moist texture of the meat and the vibrant green of the herbs.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas
Provide fresh lime wedges for acidity
Accompany with a side of pickled red onions
instructions: Pat beef cubes dry with paper towels. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear beef chunks in batches until browned on all sides. Remove and set aside.
Add onions to the pot. Sauté for 5 minutes until translucent.
Stir in garlic, jalapeños, cumin, and paprika. Cook for 1 minute.
Pour in beer to deglaze the pot. Scrape the bottom to release browned bits.
Return beef to the pot. Add beef stock and hot sauce.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 90 minutes.
Add black beans. Simmer uncovered for 20 minutes until beef is tender and sauce thickens.
Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper before serving.
notes: Use a tough cut like chuck for best results after slow cooking
Ensure the beer is not overly bitter to avoid a sharp sauce

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Vegetable Pulao
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of steaming chicken pulao served on a rustic, hand-painted ceramic plate. The long-grain Basmati rice is fluffy and light yellow from turmeric. Large, golden-brown seared chicken chunks are scattered throughout the rice, not sliced. Vibrant orange carrot cubes and bright green peas provide pops of color. The arrangement is natural and mounded, filling the center of the plate with visible steam rising. The setting is a well-used wooden kitchen table with a simple steel spoon and a small side bowl of white yogurt raita. Warm, natural light illuminates the textures of the rice grains and the moist, tender chicken pieces.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of cucumber raita
Accompany with lime wedges and sliced raw red onions
Serve with mango pickle or papadums
instructions: Wash rice until water runs clear. Soak in cold water for 20 minutes. Drain.
Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add cumin seeds. Toast for 30 seconds.
Add sliced onions. Sauté until golden brown.
Stir in ginger and garlic pastes. Cook for 1 minute.
Add chicken chunks. Brown all sides for 5 minutes.
Add diced carrots, turmeric, garam masala, and salt. Stir to coat.
Add drained rice. Stir gently for 2 minutes to toast grains.
Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Cover with a tight lid. Simmer for 12 minutes.
Check chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Gently fold in green peas. Cover and rest off heat for 5 minutes.
Fluff with a fork before serving.
notes: Thigh meat stays moist during reheating for meal prep.
Do not over-stir the rice to prevent breaking the long grains.
Ensure the lid is tight to trap steam effectively.

recipes.recipe_name: Cabbage and Herb Thai Salad with Spiced Chicken Chunks
recipes.visual_description: This Thai-inspired salad is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl, showcasing a vibrant base of finely shredded napa and red cabbage mixed with bright orange julienned carrots. Scattered throughout are golden-brown seared chicken chunks, cooked to a perfect 75°C. Fresh green mint leaves, chopped cilantro, and torn Thai basil are distributed evenly, providing pops of emerald color. A light coating of lime and fish sauce dressing gives the vegetables a glistening sheen. The dish is finished with a dusting of coarse toasted rice powder and crushed roasted peanuts. It sits on a dark teak wood table with a neutral cotton napkin and traditional bamboo sticky rice basket nearby, lit by soft, natural window light.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of warm sticky rice in a bamboo basket
Provide extra lime wedges for individual seasoning
Pair with iced lemongrass tea
instructions: Whisk lime juice, fish sauce, palm sugar, and minced chili in a bowl.
Cut chicken into 2cm chunks.
Sear chicken in a hot pan until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Shred napa and red cabbage into thin strips.
Julienne carrots into fine matchsticks.
Thinly slice the red onion.
Tear mint and basil leaves by hand.
Combine cabbages, carrots, onion, and herbs in a large mixing bowl.
Toss vegetables with three-quarters of the dressing.
Add chicken chunks and toasted rice powder to the bowl.
Toss gently to coat all ingredients.
Plate immediately and garnish with crushed roasted peanuts.
notes: Toasted rice powder can be made by browning raw glutinous rice in a dry pan and grinding it.
Ensure chicken reaches the safety mark of 75°C before adding to the salad.
Adjust chili quantity to control heat levels.
traditional_techniques: balancing the four pillars of Thai flavor

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Braised Chicken with Eggplant and Peppers
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Mediterranean braised chicken is presented on a wide, clean white porcelain plate. One whole, bone-in chicken thigh with a deeply browned, crispy skin serves as the centerpiece. It rests on a mound of fluffy, steamed long-grain rice. Surrounding the chicken is a vibrant mixture of 3cm eggplant cubes, 1cm wide red bell pepper strips, and whole white cannellini beans. A light, savory pan sauce coats the vegetables. Fine slices of red chili and dried herbs are scattered across the dish. The plating is organized with clear negative space around the edges. Set on a light wood bistro table with natural side lighting, a white cotton napkin, and polished silverware.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty sourdough bread
Pair with a crisp dry white wine
Garnish with fresh flat-leaf parsley
instructions: Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes until golden.
Flip and sear for 3 minutes.
Remove chicken from the pan and set aside.
Add onion, garlic, and chili to the same pan.
Sauté for 3 minutes until softened.
Add eggplant cubes and bell pepper strips.
Cook for 5 minutes until eggplant begins to brown.
Stir in beans, stock, and oregano.
Return chicken to the pan, skin-side up.
Simmer for 20 minutes until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Boil rice in salted water until tender.
Drain rice and keep warm.
Plate rice first, then place chicken and vegetables on top.
notes: Always ensure chicken reaches 75°C at the bone.
Do not cover the pan completely during braising to keep the chicken skin crisp.
Salt the eggplant cubes 10 minutes before cooking to remove excess moisture.

recipes.recipe_name: Hungarian Mushroom and Potato Paprikash
recipes.visual_description: The dish is served in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The centerpiece features golden, 2cm cubed potatoes and thick, earthy-brown mushroom quarters coated in a rich, vibrant orange-red paprika sauce. Small 1cm dices of red bell pepper and softened tomatoes are interspersed throughout the stew, adding texture and color variation. A single, generous dollop of thick white sour cream sits slightly off-center, partially melting into the warm sauce. Finely chopped bright green parsley is scattered across the top. The bowl sits on a dark oak bistro table next to a folded white cotton napkin and a heavy stainless steel spoon. Natural side lighting highlights the glossy sheen of the sauce and the rustic textures of the vegetables.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with fresh crusty rye bread
Accompany with a side of cucumber salad (uborkasaláta)
Traditional Hungarian table setting with a small bowl of extra hot paprika on the side

ingredients.name: waxy potatoes, peeled and cut into 2cm cubes
cremini mushrooms, cleaned and cut into thick quarters
red bell pepper, seeded and cut into 1cm dice

instructions: Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat.
Sauté diced onions until translucent and golden, about 8 minutes.
Add diced bell peppers and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Remove pot from heat and stir in paprika to prevent burning.
Return to heat and add diced tomatoes and quartered mushrooms.
Cook for 5 minutes until mushrooms release moisture.
Add cubed potatoes and vegetable stock.
Season with salt and pepper.
Simmer covered for 25 minutes until potatoes are tender.
Whisk 1 tablespoon of hot liquid into the sour cream to temper.
Stir tempered sour cream into the pot and simmer for 2 minutes.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Ensure the paprika is authentic Hungarian sweet paprika for the correct flavor profile.
Do not boil the sauce after adding the sour cream to prevent curdling.
Waxy potatoes hold their shape better during the long simmering process.

recipes.recipe_name: Orecchiette with Italian Sausage and Sun-Dried Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of orecchiette served on a clean white porcelain plate. The ear-shaped pasta is naturally piled, coated in a glossy, translucent sauce. The dish features rustic 2 cm chunks of browned Italian sausage and vibrant green 3 cm broccolini batons. Strips of deep red julienned sun-dried tomatoes are scattered throughout. The arrangement is organic and flowing, leaving moderate negative space around the rim. A light dusting of finely grated Pecorino Romano sits on top. The setting is a modern bistro with a light oak wood table, a folded white cotton napkin, and a stainless steel fork. The lighting is natural and even, highlighting the textures of the seared meat and tender vegetables.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty focaccia
Pair with a crisp Primitivo wine
instructions: Boil a large pot of salted water.
Cook orecchiette until al dente.
Reserve 200 ml of pasta cooking water.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add sausage meat in 2 cm chunks.
Brown sausage chunks for 5 minutes until fully cooked to 75°C.
Add sliced garlic and chili flakes to the skillet.
Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in julienned sun-dried tomatoes and broccolini batons.
Add the cooked pasta and 100 ml of reserved pasta water to the skillet.
Toss vigorously over medium heat to emulsify the sauce.
Remove from heat and stir in Pecorino Romano.
Add more pasta water if needed for a fluid consistency.
notes: Ensure the pasta water is well-salted to season the orecchiette internally.
Do not drain the pasta completely; the residual starch helps bind the sauce.

recipes.recipe_name: Crispy Pasta Chips with Spicy Tomato Dip
recipes.visual_description: A rustic wooden board holds a generous pile of golden-brown, crispy farfalle pasta chips. The pasta shows slightly charred edges and a dusting of white parmesan cheese and green dried oregano. Next to the pile sits a small, hand-painted ceramic bowl filled with a thick, vibrant red tomato dip. Tiny flakes of red chili and small pieces of torn green basil are visible on the sauce surface. The arrangement is casual and asymmetrical. The setting is a sun-drenched Italian kitchen with a linen napkin nearby. The lighting is warm and natural, highlighting the crunchy texture of the fried pasta and the matte finish of the rustic table. The entire board is visible.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as an aperitivo snack before dinner
Pair with chilled sparkling water or a light Italian lager
Present in a communal bowl for family-style sharing
instructions: Boil pasta in salted water until al dente.
Drain pasta well and pat dry with a towel.
Preheat oven to 200°C.
Toss pasta in a bowl with 30ml olive oil, parmesan, oregano, and garlic powder.
Spread pasta in a single layer on a baking tray.
Bake for 15 minutes until golden and crunchy.
Stir pasta halfway through baking.
Combine crushed tomatoes, remaining olive oil, chili flakes, and salt in a pan.
Simmer sauce over medium heat for 8 minutes.
Stir chopped basil into the sauce.
Serve pasta chips on a platter with the dipping sauce.
notes: Ensure pasta is completely dry before baking to achieve a crisp texture.
Substitute farfalle with penne or fusilli if preferred.
Store leftovers in an airtight container to maintain crunch.

recipes.recipe_name: Beer-Braised Chicken with Savory Rice and Beans
recipes.visual_description: The dish features two whole, bone-in chicken thighs with deeply seared, golden-brown skin. The chicken sits atop a bed of fluffy long-grain rice mixed with whole black beans. Small translucent pieces of sautéed onion and minced garlic are visible throughout the rice. The rice has a light amber hue from the beer reduction. Thin, bright red chili rings and fresh green cilantro leaves garnish the top. The arrangement is centered on a clean white porcelain plate. A small pool of savory braising liquid surrounds the base of the rice. The setting is a light wood table with a folded cotton napkin and a simple fork. Natural side lighting highlights the textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with lime wedges for acidity
Accompany with fried plantains
Provide extra hot sauce on the side
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt, pepper, and cumin.
Heat oil in a large deep pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes until golden.
Flip chicken and sear for 4 minutes.
Remove chicken and set aside.
Sauté diced onions and minced garlic in the same pan for 3 minutes.
Add sliced chilies and rice. Stir for 2 minutes to toast.
Pour in beer to deglaze the pan. Scrape the bottom.
Add black beans and chicken stock. Stir to combine.
Place chicken back into the pan on top of the rice.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 20 minutes.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Use a crisp lager for the best flavor balance.
Do not remove the chicken skin as it provides essential fat for the rice.
Ensure the rice is not overcooked to maintain distinct grains.

recipes.recipe_name: Korean Braised Beef Short Ribs (Galbi Jjim)
recipes.visual_description: The dish features four large, bone-in beef short rib chunks, deeply glazed in a dark, glossy mahogany sauce. The meat is tender and intact, positioned centrally in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. Surrounding the beef are three rounded cylinders of Korean radish and three thick carrot batons, all softened and stained golden-brown from the braise. Four halved shiitake mushrooms are nestled between the meat and vegetables. A light sprinkle of bright green sliced scallions and toasted white sesame seeds provides a textural contrast. The sauce pools slightly at the base, reflecting the soft overhead light. Beside the bowl sit stainless steel chopsticks and a long-handled spoon on a dark wood table.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a bowl of multi-grain rice (Japgokbap)
Accompany with small dishes of Napa cabbage kimchi and pickled radish
Provide stainless steel chopsticks and a long-handled spoon
Present in a traditional ceramic or stone bowl to retain heat
instructions: Soak beef ribs in cold water for 30 minutes to remove excess blood.
Drain and rinse the ribs thoroughly.
Blanch ribs in boiling water for 5 minutes.
Drain and rinse again to remove impurities.
Combine soy sauce, water, pear juice, mirin, sugar, garlic, ginger, and sesame oil.
Place ribs in a heavy-bottomed pot and pour in the sauce mixture.
Simmer covered over low heat for 60 minutes.
Round the edges of radish and carrot chunks with a peeler to prevent breaking.
Add radish, carrots, and mushrooms to the pot.
Simmer for 40 minutes until meat is tender and sauce reduces to a glaze.
Skim excess fat from the surface of the sauce.
Garnish with green onions and sesame seeds before serving.
notes: Rounding the vegetable edges is a traditional technique called 'chamfering' to keep the sauce clear.
Pear juice contains enzymes that tenderize the beef naturally.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo al Ajillo
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pollo al Ajillo served on a clean white porcelain plate in a modern Spanish bistro setting. The dish features two whole chicken pieces—a thigh and a drumstick—with crispy, deep golden-brown skin. The chicken is surrounded by twenty whole, soft, golden-confit garlic cloves. A rich, translucent emulsion of olive oil and sherry glaze coats the meat. Bright green, finely chopped parsley is scattered over the top. The arrangement is organic and centered with moderate negative space. A side of thick-cut, toasted rustic baguette sits on the edge of the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the glistening textures of the oil and the sear on the chicken.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty rustic bread to soak up the garlic oil.
Accompany with a glass of chilled dry Fino sherry.
Present in a traditional terracotta cazuela for a rustic look.
instructions: Pat chicken dry with paper towels.
Season chicken generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide heavy-bottomed pan over medium heat.
Add whole garlic cloves to the oil.
Fry garlic until golden brown on all sides.
Remove garlic with a slotted spoon and set aside.
Increase heat to medium-high.
Place chicken pieces in the pan, skin-side down.
Sear chicken until deep golden brown on all sides, about 10 minutes.
Drain half of the rendered fat from the pan.
Add bay leaf and return fried garlic to the pan.
Pour in the dry sherry.
Scrape the bottom of the pan to release browned bits.
Lower heat to medium-low and cover with a lid.
Simmer for 15 minutes or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove lid and increase heat for 2 minutes to thicken the sauce.
Stir in chopped parsley and serve immediately.
notes: Ensure the garlic does not burn; it should be golden and sweet, not black and bitter.
Use high-quality extra virgin olive oil for the best flavor profile.
Always verify the thickest part of the chicken reaches 75°C for safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Pork with Cherry-Lemon Sauce and Creamy Mash
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of three thick, cylindrical pork medallions sits atop a smooth, snowy-white bed of creamy milk-mashed potatoes. The pork is seared to a deep golden-brown crust. A rich, glossy, dark burgundy cherry sauce is draped over the pork, with several visible halves of softened, deep-red cherries nestled around the meat. The sauce pools slightly into the white mash, creating a sharp color contrast. The dish is presented on a clean, wide-rimmed white porcelain plate. A light sprinkle of lemon zest and tiny rosemary bits adds a touch of green and yellow. The background features a rustic dark wood bistro table with a folded white cotton napkin and a simple silver fork.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of braised red cabbage
Pair with a dry Riesling or a light-bodied red wine

ingredients.name: Pork tenderloin, cut into 4cm thick medallions

instructions: Boil cubed potatoes in salted water for 15 minutes until soft.
Drain potatoes and return to the pot.
Mash potatoes while adding warm milk and 40g butter until smooth.
Season mash with salt and keep warm.
Pat pork medallions dry and season with salt, pepper, and rosemary.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear pork medallions for 4 minutes per side until they reach 63°C.
Remove pork from pan and let rest on a plate.
Add cherries, sugar, and lemon juice to the same skillet.
Pour in chicken stock and scrape the bottom of the pan.
Simmer sauce for 5 minutes until liquid reduces by half and thickens.
Whisk in remaining 20g butter and lemon zest.
Place a generous portion of mash on each plate.
Top with three pork medallions and spoon cherry sauce over the meat.
notes: Ensure the pan is very hot before adding pork to achieve a proper crust.
Resting the meat is essential to maintain juiciness.
If the sauce is too tart, add an extra pinch of sugar to balance the lemon.

recipes.recipe_name: Beef and Bean Chili with Dark Beer
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of beef and bean chili served in a deep, matte charcoal stoneware bowl. The dish features 3cm chunks of tender, dark-brown seared beef and plump red kidney beans submerged in a thick, glossy, mahogany-colored sauce. Vibrant green jalapeño rounds and fresh cilantro sprigs garnish the top. The bowl sits on a rustic light oak table next to a folded white cotton napkin and a small stack of warm, charred flour tortillas. Natural side lighting highlights the fibrous texture of the beef chunks and the steam rising from the bowl. The background is a soft-focus modern bistro interior with clean lines.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm flour tortillas
Garnish with lime wedges
Accompany with pickled red onions
instructions: Pat beef dry and season with salt.
Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over high heat.
Sear beef chunks until browned on all sides. Remove beef.
Reduce heat to medium. Sauté onions and garlic until soft.
Stir in tomato paste, chili powder, and cumin. Cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in beer. Scrape the bottom of the pot to release browned bits.
Return beef to the pot. Add stock and hot sauce.
Simmer on low heat for 90 minutes until beef is tender.
Stir in kidney beans. Cook for 20 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
notes: Use a stout or porter for a deeper flavor profile.
Ensure beef is cut into uniform cubes for even cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Red Wine Braised Beef with Mushrooms
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of rich beef stew served in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. Four to five large, 4cm cubes of seared beef sit prominently in the center, coated in a glossy, dark burgundy-colored sauce. The beef chunks are tender and intact, not sliced. Interspersed among the meat are whole, glazed pearl onions and golden-brown sautéed cremini mushroom halves. Small bits of softened tomato are visible in the thick reduction. The dish is garnished with a single fresh thyme sprig. The bowl is placed on a dark oak bistro table next to a folded white cotton napkin and a heavy silver spoon. Natural side-lighting highlights the textures of the meat and the sheen of the sauce.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty baguette slices
Pair with a glass of Pinot Noir or Burgundy
Traditional accompaniment of buttery mashed potatoes or wide egg noodles

ingredients.name: beef chuck roast, cut into 4cm cubes

instructions: Pat beef cubes dry with paper towels.
Season beef generously with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot over high heat.
Sear beef in batches until deeply browned on all sides.
Remove beef and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium.
Add pearl onions to the pot and cook until lightly browned.
Stir in garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add tomato paste and diced tomatoes.
Cook for 2 minutes while stirring.
Sprinkle flour over the vegetables and stir for 1 minute.
Pour in red wine and scrape the bottom of the pot to release brown bits.
Return beef and accumulated juices to the pot.
Add beef stock, thyme, and bay leaf.
Bring to a simmer, then cover and reduce heat to low.
Braise for 2 hours or until beef is fork-tender.
Sauté mushrooms in butter in a separate pan until golden brown.
Stir mushrooms into the stew 10 minutes before serving.
Remove thyme sprigs and bay leaf.
Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
notes: Do not crowd the pan when searing beef to ensure a dark crust.
Use a wine you would enjoy drinking for the best sauce flavor.
Ensure the sauce is thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.

recipes.recipe_name: Beef Medallions with Fondant Potatoes and Garlic Mushrooms
recipes.visual_description: A single, thick pan-seared beef medallion sits as the centerpiece on a clean white porcelain plate. The beef has a deep brown crust from butter-basting. Beside it stands a golden-brown fondant potato cylinder, glistening with herb-infused butter. Earthy cremini mushrooms, halved and sautéed to a rich mahogany, are clustered near the beef. A glossy, dark brown pan reduction lightly coats the mushrooms. Fresh thyme sprigs are placed naturally over the meat. The arrangement is clean with ample negative space. The setting features a dark wood bistro table, a folded white linen napkin, and polished silver flatware. Natural side-lighting highlights the textures of the seared meat and soft potato. The entire plate is visible.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of red Bordeaux wine
Accompany with fresh crusty baguette
Provide a sharp steak knife and traditional European flatware
instructions: Peel potatoes. Cut into 4cm cylinders with flat ends.
Heat oil in a pan. Sear potato ends until golden brown.
Add 20g butter, 2 thyme sprigs, and 100ml stock. Cover and simmer until tender.
Season beef medallions with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a separate heavy pan. Sear beef 4 minutes per side.
Add 20g butter, 2 smashed garlic cloves, and 4 thyme sprigs to the beef pan.
Baste beef with foaming butter for 2 minutes using a spoon.
Remove beef from pan. Rest for 5 minutes.
Sauté halved mushrooms in the same pan with remaining garlic and butter.
Add remaining stock. Reduce over high heat until a thick glaze forms.
Plate the whole beef medallion with the potatoes and mushrooms.
notes: Ensure the beef rests to maintain internal juices
Use a high-smoke point oil for the initial sear
Check potato tenderness with a paring knife; it should slide in easily

recipes.recipe_name: Kung Pao Tofu with Jasmine Rice
recipes.visual_description: The dish features golden-brown, seared tofu cubes tossed in a glossy, dark soy-based sauce. The tofu cubes are arranged in a heap over a bed of fluffy, steamed white jasmine rice. Whole toasted cashews and bright green scallion batons are scattered throughout the tofu. Dried red chilies add pops of deep crimson. The meal is presented in a clean, white ceramic bowl on a dark wood bistro table. Beside the bowl, a pair of dark wood chopsticks rests on a small porcelain holder. A linen napkin is folded neatly to the side. The lighting is natural and even, highlighting the textures of the crispy tofu and the individual grains of rice.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in individual ceramic bowls.
Provide dark wood chopsticks and porcelain rests.
Accompany with a side of lightly pickled cucumber strips.
instructions: Rinse jasmine rice in cold water.
Combine rice with 450ml water.
Boil over high heat.
Simmer 15 minutes on low.
Rest 10 minutes.
Press tofu to remove water.
Cut tofu into 2cm cubes.
Whisk soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, and 5g cornstarch.
Dust tofu with 15g cornstarch.
Heat oil in wok.
Fry tofu until golden.
Remove and drain tofu.
Fry peppercorns and chilies for 30 seconds.
Stir in minced ginger and garlic.
Return tofu to wok.
Add sauce and stir until thick.
Toss in cashews and scallions.
Serve immediately over rice.
notes: Use extra-firm tofu to maintain shape during stir-frying.
Adjust the number of dried chilies to control spice levels.

recipes.recipe_name: Mustard-Braised Beef with Roasted Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single portion served on a wide, matte white porcelain plate. Three large, 5cm chunks of beef chuck sit centrally, glistening with a thick, deep-umber mustard and tomato reduction. The meat shows a rich, caramelized exterior. Arranged around the beef are three 6cm carrot batons, vibrant orange and tender. Beside them are 3cm squares of red bell pepper, lightly charred at the edges. Four bright green broccoli florets provide a crisp textural contrast. The plating is clean with moderate negative space. The background features a dark oak bistro table, a folded grey linen napkin, and polished stainless steel cutlery. Natural side lighting highlights the glossy sauce and the fibrous texture of the beef chunks.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty baguette to soak up the sauce.
Pair with a medium-bodied French red wine like Merlot.
instructions: Cut beef into 5cm chunks.
Season beef with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat.
Sear beef chunks until browned on all sides.
Remove beef from pot.
Add onion wedges and carrot batons.
Cook 5 minutes until slightly softened.
Stir in minced garlic and bell pepper squares.
Add diced tomatoes and mustard.
Return beef to pot and add stock.
Simmer covered for 90 minutes until beef is tender.
Steam broccoli florets separately for 4 minutes.
Plate beef chunks with vegetables and spoon sauce over meat.
notes: Ensure the beef is cooked until fork-tender.
The sauce should be thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.

recipes.recipe_name: Mexican-Style Arroz con Pollo
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Arroz con Pollo is presented on a clean white porcelain plate. The base is a mound of savory rice, tinted orange from hot sauce and spices. The rice features charred golden corn kernels and small diced white onions. Large 3cm chunks of seared chicken thighs are nestled into the rice, showing a deep caramelized crust. A layer of melted white cheese covers the center, appearing glossy and fluid. The dish is garnished with finely chopped green cilantro and a fresh lime wedge. The plate sits on a dark wooden table in a modern bistro setting with natural light. The arrangement is organic and centered, highlighting the textures of the grains and succulent chicken.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas
Provide extra hot sauce on the side
Accompany with pickled jalapeños
instructions: Cut chicken into 3cm chunks.
Mix chicken with cumin, paprika, and 30ml hot sauce.
Heat oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Brown chicken chunks. Remove from pan.
Sauté diced onion until soft.
Add corn. Char for 2 minutes.
Add rice. Toast for 2 minutes.
Stir in stock and remaining hot sauce.
Simmer covered on low heat for 15 minutes.
Return chicken to pan. Cook until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Top with shredded cheese. Cover until melted.
Garnish with chopped cilantro.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C for safety.
Rinse rice before cooking to remove excess starch.
Use a heavy-bottomed pan to prevent the rice from sticking.

recipes.recipe_name: Spezzatino di Manzo alla Birra e Senape con Risotto Bianco
recipes.visual_description: A single portion served on a clean, white porcelain flat plate. The base is a fluid, creamy white risotto spread naturally across the plate, demonstrating a glossy 'all'onda' consistency. In the center, a cluster of four large, 3cm chunks of tender, braised beef is neatly piled. The beef is coated in a thick, rich mahogany-colored sauce flecked with fine mustard seeds and bits of softened onion. The meat appears succulent and moist, not sliced. A single small sprig of fresh rosemary is placed atop the beef. The lighting is soft and natural, emphasizing the textural contrast between the pale, velvety rice and the dark, glazed beef. A silver fork and a folded linen napkin sit on a light wood bistro table.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of the same amber beer used in the recipe or a structured red wine like Nebbiolo.
Provide extra grated Grana Padano at the table.
Follow the meal with a simple espresso.
instructions: Pat beef chunks dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 30ml olive oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat. Brown beef in batches. Remove and set aside.
Add diced onion to the same pot. Sauté 5 minutes until translucent. Add minced garlic and rosemary. Cook 1 minute.
Deglaze pot with beer. Scrape browned bits from the bottom. Reduce liquid by half.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and mustard. Return beef to the pot.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 90 minutes until beef is tender. Remove lid for final 15 minutes to thicken sauce.
Start risotto 20 minutes before beef is finished. Toast rice in remaining oil for 2 minutes.
Add stock one ladle at a time. Stir constantly. Wait for liquid to absorb before adding more.
Once rice is al dente, remove from heat. Perform mantecatura by vigorously stirring in butter and Grana Padano.
Adjust risotto consistency with a splash of stock until it flows freely (all'onda).
Serve risotto on flat plates. Top with beef chunks and sauce.
notes: Ensure the risotto remains fluid; it should move when the plate is tilted.
The mustard provides acidity to balance the richness of the beef and beer reduction.
Do not overcook the rice; it must retain a firm 'al dente' bite.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo con Cipolle e Basilico
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pollo con Cipolle e Basilico served in a wide, shallow white porcelain pasta bowl. The base consists of rigatoni pasta coated in a glossy, golden-brown onion sauce. One whole, golden-brown seared chicken thigh sits prominently atop the pasta. The skin is crispy and textured. Scattered across the dish are hand-torn fresh basil leaves and a light dusting of finely grated parmesan cheese. Caramelized onion strands are visible throughout the pasta. The plate sits on a dark oak wooden table next to a folded white cotton napkin and a polished silver fork. The lighting is soft and natural, coming from the side. The background is a blurred, warm bistro interior.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty ciabatta bread
Pair with a crisp Italian white wine like Pinot Grigio
Present on a pre-warmed ceramic plate
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and black pepper.
Heat 30ml olive oil in a wide skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes until golden and crispy.
Flip chicken and cook for 4 minutes. Remove chicken from skillet.
Add sliced onions to the remaining fat in the skillet.
Sauté onions for 10 minutes over medium heat until soft and caramelized.
Stir in garlic and dried oregano. Cook for 2 minutes.
Return chicken to the skillet. Add 100ml water. Cover and simmer for 15 minutes.
Check chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet.
Boil 4 liters of salted water. Cook rigatoni until al dente.
Reserve 60ml pasta water. Drain pasta.
Toss pasta into the onion mixture with reserved water and remaining olive oil.
Stir in half of the parmesan and hand-torn basil leaves.
Serve pasta topped with a whole chicken thigh.
notes: Ensure the onions reach a deep golden color for maximum flavor.
The pasta water is essential for creating a silky sauce that clings to the rigatoni.
Do not slice the chicken; serve it whole to retain juices.

recipes.recipe_name: Thai Panang Pork Curry
recipes.visual_description: A wide, shallow white porcelain bowl contains a rich, thick orange-red Panang curry. The focal point is several large 3cm chunks of tender, braised pork shoulder emerging from the glossy sauce. The sauce shows a visible cracked coconut oil sheen on the surface. Finely julienned dark green makrut lime leaves and bright red diagonal slices of spur chili are scattered over the pork chunks. A sprinkle of golden crushed peanuts adds texture to the center. Beside the bowl sits a separate small ceramic bowl of fluffy white steamed jasmine rice and a traditional stainless steel Thai soup spoon. The setting is a matte dark wood table with a folded grey cotton napkin. Natural side lighting highlights the creamy curry texture and the clean edges of the pork.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice in a separate bowl
Provide a flat-bottomed Thai soup spoon and a fork
Accompany with fresh cucumber slices to balance the heat
instructions: Heat 100ml of coconut milk in a wok over medium heat.
Stir constantly until the oil separates from the cream.
Add the curry paste to the wok.
Fry the paste for 3 minutes until fragrant.
Add pork chunks to the wok.
Sear the pork until all sides are browned.
Pour in the remaining coconut milk.
Reduce heat and simmer for 20 minutes until pork is tender.
Add palm sugar and fish sauce to the sauce.
Stir in half of the julienned lime leaves.
Cook for an additional 2 minutes.
Remove from heat.
notes: Do not shake the coconut milk tin before opening to easily access the thick cream at the top
Adjust the amount of palm sugar to balance the saltiness of the fish sauce

recipes.recipe_name: Kung Pao Tofu with Jasmine Rice
recipes.visual_description: The dish features golden-brown, seared tofu cubes tossed in a glossy, dark soy-based sauce. The tofu cubes are arranged in a heap over a bed of fluffy, steamed white jasmine rice. Whole toasted cashews and bright green scallion batons are scattered throughout the tofu. Dried red chilies add pops of deep crimson. The meal is presented in a clean, white ceramic bowl on a dark wood bistro table. Beside the bowl, a pair of dark wood chopsticks rests on a small porcelain holder. A linen napkin is folded neatly to the side. The lighting is natural and even, highlighting the textures of the crispy tofu and the individual grains of rice.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in individual ceramic bowls.
Provide dark wood chopsticks and porcelain rests.
Accompany with a side of lightly pickled cucumber strips.
instructions: Rinse jasmine rice in cold water.
Combine rice with 450ml water.
Boil over high heat.
Simmer 15 minutes on low.
Rest 10 minutes.
Press tofu to remove water.
Cut tofu into 2cm cubes.
Whisk soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, and 5g cornstarch.
Dust tofu with 15g cornstarch.
Heat oil in wok.
Fry tofu until golden.
Remove and drain tofu.
Fry peppercorns and chilies for 30 seconds.
Stir in minced ginger and garlic.
Return tofu to wok.
Add sauce and stir until thick.
Toss in cashews and scallions.
Serve immediately over rice.
notes: Use extra-firm tofu to maintain shape during stir-frying.
Adjust the number of dried chilies to control spice levels.

recipes.recipe_name: Indian Chicken Biryani
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Indian Chicken Biryani served on a clean white porcelain plate. The dish features a mound of fluffy, long-grain Basmati rice with distinct white and saffron-orange tinted grains. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs are nestled into the rice, displaying a rich, spice-rubbed golden exterior. The rice is topped with a generous scatter of dark, caramelized onion strips and vibrant green mint leaves. A small ceramic bowl of white cucumber raita sits to the side. The arrangement is placed on a dark wood bistro table under natural light. A folded white cotton napkin and a polished silver spoon complete the setting. Proportions show moderate negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with cooling cucumber and cumin raita
Accompany with spicy lime or mango pickle
Present with a side of sliced raw red onions and lemon wedges
instructions: Slice onions into thin uniform strips.
Heat ghee in a heavy pot.
Fry onions until dark brown and crisp.
Remove half the onions for garnish.
Whisk yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, turmeric, and garam masala.
Coat chicken thighs thoroughly in yogurt mixture.
Marinate chicken for 30 minutes.
Boil 2 liters of salted water with cinnamon and cardamom.
Add rice to boiling water.
Cook rice until 70% tender.
Drain rice completely.
Layer marinated chicken in the bottom of the pot.
Spread par-boiled rice over the chicken.
Top with fried onions, mint, and cilantro.
Seal pot with a tight lid.
Cook on very low heat for 25 minutes.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Rest for 10 minutes before serving.
notes: Use aged long-grain basmati rice for the best texture
Do not stir the rice while boiling to avoid breaking grains
Ensure the pot lid is heavy or sealed with dough to trap steam effectively

recipes.recipe_name: Orecchiette with Italian Sausage and Sun-Dried Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of orecchiette served on a clean white porcelain plate. The ear-shaped pasta is naturally piled, coated in a glossy, translucent sauce. The dish features rustic 2 cm chunks of browned Italian sausage and vibrant green 3 cm broccolini batons. Strips of deep red julienned sun-dried tomatoes are scattered throughout. The arrangement is organic and flowing, leaving moderate negative space around the rim. A light dusting of finely grated Pecorino Romano sits on top. The setting is a modern bistro with a light oak wood table, a folded white cotton napkin, and a stainless steel fork. The lighting is natural and even, highlighting the textures of the seared meat and tender vegetables.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty focaccia
Pair with a crisp Primitivo wine
instructions: Boil a large pot of salted water.
Cook orecchiette until al dente.
Reserve 200 ml of pasta cooking water.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add sausage meat in 2 cm chunks.
Brown sausage chunks for 5 minutes until fully cooked to 75°C.
Add sliced garlic and chili flakes to the skillet.
Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in julienned sun-dried tomatoes and broccolini batons.
Add the cooked pasta and 100 ml of reserved pasta water to the skillet.
Toss vigorously over medium heat to emulsify the sauce.
Remove from heat and stir in Pecorino Romano.
Add more pasta water if needed for a fluid consistency.
notes: Ensure the pasta water is well-salted to season the orecchiette internally.
Do not drain the pasta completely; the residual starch helps bind the sauce.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Arroz con Pollo presented on a clean white porcelain plate. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs with deeply browned, crispy skin sit atop a bed of golden, saffron-stained rice. The rice grains are plump and distinct, interspersed with fine bits of softened onion and concentrated red tomato. The dish shows vibrant yellow and orange hues from the saffron and paprika. A generous sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped parsley is scattered over the top. A single lemon wedge is placed neatly on the side. The plate sits on a light oak wooden table with a folded white cotton napkin. Lighting is bright, natural, and even, highlighting the textures of the crispy skin and the moist rice grains.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Alioli (garlic mayonnaise)
Accompany with crusty bread and a glass of chilled white wine
Present in a traditional terracotta cazuela for family-style dining
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide shallow pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden and crispy.
Flip and brown the other side. Remove chicken from pan.
Add onion to the same pan. Sauté until translucent.
Stir in garlic and grated tomato. Cook until liquid evaporates and mixture darkens.
Add smoked paprika and rice. Stir to coat rice in oil for 2 minutes.
Pour in white wine. Deglaze the pan. Simmer until wine reduces by half.
Add hot stock and saffron. Stir once to distribute.
Place chicken thighs back into the pan on top of the rice.
Simmer undisturbed over medium-low heat for 18-20 minutes.
Ensure chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove from heat. Cover with a clean cloth. Rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Do not stir the rice once the stock is added to allow a crust to form on the bottom.
Use a wide pan to ensure even rice cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Arroz con Pollo presented on a clean white porcelain plate. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs with deeply browned, crispy skin sit atop a bed of golden, saffron-stained rice. The rice grains are plump and distinct, interspersed with fine bits of softened onion and concentrated red tomato. The dish shows vibrant yellow and orange hues from the saffron and paprika. A generous sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped parsley is scattered over the top. A single lemon wedge is placed neatly on the side. recipes.recipe_name: Poulet aux Champignons
recipes.visual_description: A shallow white porcelain bowl features two golden-brown, skin-on chicken thighs nestled in a rich, velvety cream sauce. The sauce is studded with halved, deeply browned button mushrooms and translucent, softened large-diced onions. The chicken remains whole, not sliced, positioned centrally to show the crispy skin. A garnish of finely chopped fresh parsley and a single thyme sprig adds vibrant green contrast against the ivory-colored sauce. The arrangement is clean and professional with visible negative space around the bowl's rim. The setting is a modern bistro with a light oak table, a folded white cotton napkin, and polished silverware. Soft natural light emphasizes the textures of the seared poultry and sautéed fungi.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty French baguette to soak up the sauce
Accompany with buttery mashed potatoes or steamed green beans
Pair with a chilled dry white wine like Chardonnay
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat oil and butter in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden brown. Flip and sear the other side.
Remove chicken from the pan and set aside.
Add onions and mushrooms to the same pan. Sauté until browned.
Add garlic and thyme sprigs. Cook for 1 minute.
Deglaze the pan with white wine. Scrape up browned bits.
Pour in chicken stock. Return chicken to the pan.
Simmer covered for 20 minutes until chicken reaches 75°C internally.
Remove chicken. Stir in heavy cream. Reduce sauce by half over high heat.
Return chicken to the pan to coat with sauce.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Ensure the chicken skin is dried with paper towels before searing for maximum crispness
Use a wide pan to avoid overcrowding the mushrooms while browning

recipes.recipe_name: Sweet Ravioli with Tomato Jam and Roasted Garlic Mascarpone
recipes.visual_description: Three large, circular hand-crimped ravioli are positioned centrally on a matte white porcelain plate. The pasta is silky and translucent, dusted lightly with superfine sugar. The vibrant ruby-red tomato jam is visible through the thin dough. A small, precise quenelle of the remaining garlic mascarpone sits atop the center ravioli. A thin drizzle of the golden tomato syrup circles the pasta. The arrangement uses moderate negative space for a clean, professional look. The plate rests on a light-colored wooden bistro table. A silver dessert spoon and a small glass of sweet Vin Santo are placed nearby. Natural side lighting emphasizes the smooth textures and deep red colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small glass of Vin Santo or Moscato d'Asti
Accompany with a strong espresso
Present on white ceramic to highlight the red tomato tones
instructions: Roast garlic cloves at 180°C for 20 minutes until soft. Squeeze paste from skins.
Mix mascarpone, roasted garlic paste, icing sugar, and lemon zest. Chill.
Dice tomatoes into small cubes. Combine with 100g granulated sugar and lemon juice in a pan.
Simmer tomato mixture over low heat for 25 minutes until jam consistency. Cool.
Mix flour, eggs, and 20g sugar. Knead for 10 minutes. Rest dough for 30 minutes.
Roll pasta dough into thin sheets using a machine or rolling pin.
Cut pasta into 8cm circles. Place 1 teaspoon garlic mascarpone in the center.
Top mascarpone with 1/2 teaspoon tomato jam. Fold and seal edges with water.
Boil ravioli in lightly sweetened water for 3 minutes. Drain.
Toss gently in melted butter. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure garlic is fully roasted to remove sharp pungency.
Seed the tomatoes thoroughly to prevent the jam from becoming watery.
Dust with extra lemon zest just before serving for aroma.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Chicken Adobo
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents two whole bone-in chicken thighs, braised to a deep mahogany hue with a high-gloss glaze. The chicken rests on a centered bed of pristine, steamed white jasmine rice. The dark, savory sauce is drizzled generously over the meat, flowing naturally onto the rice. Garnishes include a sprinkle of golden, crispy fried garlic slivers and fresh green scallions cut into thin diagonal batons. The composition uses a clean white porcelain plate, providing a sharp contrast to the dark sauce. The background features a rustic dark wood surface with a folded linen napkin and a side of pickled papaya. Lighting is soft and natural, highlighting the succulent texture of the chicken skin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice
Provide a side of atchara (pickled green papaya)
Traditional Filipino dining uses a spoon and fork
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels.
Heat oil in a large heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden brown, about 5-7 minutes.
Flip chicken and sear for 3 minutes.
Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Add smashed garlic to the pan and sauté until fragrant and lightly golden.
Return chicken to the pan.
Add soy sauce, cane vinegar, water, brown sugar, peppercorns, and bay leaves.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low.
Cover and simmer for 25 minutes.
Uncover the pan and increase heat to medium.
Simmer until the sauce reduces to a thick, glossy glaze and chicken reaches 75°C.
Turn chicken occasionally to coat evenly in the sauce reduction.
notes: Use cane vinegar for authentic flavor profile
Do not stir the vinegar immediately after adding to avoid a raw taste
Adjust sugar for desired sweetness balance

recipes.recipe_name: French Style Beef and Mushroom Stew
recipes.visual_description: The dish features a single portion of rich beef stew served in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The focal point consists of four to five large, 4cm cubes of braised beef, glistening with a dark, glossy mahogany sauce. Interspersed among the beef are golden-brown halved button mushrooms and translucent, softened onion ribbons. The arrangement is organic and centered, leaving a clean white rim around the edges. A single sprig of fresh green thyme rests on the meat. The bowl sits on a light oak bistro table next to a folded white cotton napkin and polished silver cutlery. Two thick, rustic baguette slices rest on a small side plate, completing the authentic French presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty French baguette
Pair with a medium-bodied red wine
Present in a shallow wide bowl
instructions: Pat beef cubes dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear beef chunks in batches until deep brown on all sides. Remove meat.
Add onions to the pot. Sauté 5 minutes until translucent.
Add mushrooms. Cook 4 minutes until browned.
Stir in flour. Cook 1 minute while stirring.
Pour in red wine. Scrape the bottom of the pot to release brown bits.
Add chicken stock, garlic, and thyme sprigs.
Return beef to the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook on low heat for 90 minutes until beef is tender.
Remove thyme sprigs. Season to taste.
notes: Ensure beef is patted very dry before searing for a better crust
Do not crowd the pan during searing to maintain high heat

recipes.recipe_name: Bucatini all'Amatriciana
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Bucatini all'Amatriciana is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. Thick pasta strands are twirled into a central mound, coated in a glossy red tomato sauce. Distinct 1cm cubes of golden-brown, crispy rendered bacon are scattered naturally across the top and within the pasta folds. A generous dusting of finely grated white Pecorino Romano cheese covers the center, contrasted by a sprinkle of finely chopped emerald-green parsley. Coarsely cracked black pepper grains are visible throughout the sauce. The bowl sits on a dark oak bistro table next to a folded white linen napkin and a silver fork. Soft natural lighting highlights the rich textures of the sauce and the rustic meat chunks.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in a warmed pasta bowl
Accompany with a glass of medium-bodied red wine
Provide extra grated Pecorino Romano on the side
instructions: Boil 4 liters of water with 10g salt.
Dice bacon into 1cm cubes.
Finely dice the onion.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add bacon cubes. Fry until fat renders and edges are crispy.
Add onion to the skillet. Sauté until translucent.
Stir in black pepper and crushed tomatoes.
Simmer sauce on low heat for 15 minutes.
Cook bucatini in boiling water until al dente.
Reserve 100ml of pasta cooking water. Drain pasta.
Add pasta to the skillet with the sauce.
Pour in reserved pasta water. Toss vigorously to emulsify.
Remove from heat. Stir in 50g of grated Pecorino Romano.
Garnish with remaining cheese and chopped parsley.
notes: Ensure the sauce is fluid and coats the pasta entirely.
Do not rinse the pasta after draining to preserve starch.
Use high-quality Pecorino Romano for authentic sharp flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Tomato Essence and Onion Soubise
recipes.visual_description: A single, golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast sits whole and off-center on a pristine white bone china plate. A silky, ivory-white onion soubise is swiped elegantly across the base in a natural curve. Three whole glazed pearl onions and three red confit cherry tomatoes are arranged in an organic cluster near the meat. A crystal-clear, concentrated tomato essence is poured into the plate, creating a vibrant, translucent pool around the components. The dish is presented on a grey-veined Carrara marble surface with a polished silver setting and a white linen napkin. Dramatic professional lighting creates soft shadows, highlighting the crispy skin texture and the architectural arrangement. Abundant negative space focuses attention on the central elements.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of chilled Chardonnay
Accompany with crusty baguette to soak up the tomato essence
instructions: Pulse chopped tomatoes in a blender. Strain through a cheesecloth-lined sieve for 2 hours to collect clear liquid.
Simmer clear tomato liquid in a small saucepan until reduced by half. Season with salt.
Sauté sliced white onions in 50g butter over low heat until translucent. Do not brown.
Add heavy cream to onions. Simmer 10 minutes. Blend until smooth and pass through a fine-mesh sieve.
Place pearl onions in a pan with chicken stock and 20g butter. Simmer until liquid evaporates and onions are glazed.
Submerge cherry tomatoes in olive oil with thyme. Cook at 90°C for 30 minutes until soft.
Season chicken breasts. Place skin-side down in a cold pan with remaining butter. Increase heat to medium.
Sear chicken until skin is crisp and golden. Flip and cook to an internal temperature of 75°C.
Rest chicken for 5 minutes before plating.
notes: Ensure the tomato essence is completely clear for a high-end presentation
The chicken skin must be perfectly rendered and audible when tapped

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Braised Beef Ragù with Pappardelle
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of wide, golden pappardelle ribbons coiled in a shallow white porcelain bowl. The pasta is coated in a glossy, deep mahogany-colored ragù. Large 3cm chunks of braised beef are nestled naturally among the pasta folds, appearing tender and succulent. The sauce shows visible bits of finely diced carrots and celery. A delicate snow-like dusting of finely grated Parmigiano-Reggiano covers the center. A single small, fresh rosemary sprig is placed off-center as a garnish. The bowl sits on a rustic dark oak table with a folded grey linen napkin and a heavy silver fork. Natural window light creates soft shadows and highlights the rich textures of the meat and pasta.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of toasted ciabatta rubbed with raw garlic
Pair with a full-bodied Italian red wine like Chianti Classico
Present in a wide-rimmed pasta bowl
instructions: Season beef cubes generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a heavy-based pot over medium-high heat.
Sear beef in batches until deeply browned on all sides. Remove beef.
Add onion, carrot, and celery to the pot. Sauté for 6 minutes.
Stir in garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Deglaze the pot with red wine. Scrape the bottom to release browned bits.
Add crushed tomatoes, beef stock, rosemary, and thyme.
Return beef to the pot. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a low simmer.
Cover and cook for 2.5 hours until beef is fork-tender.
Boil pappardelle in salted water until al dente. Reserve 60ml pasta water.
Discard herb stems. Gently break up some beef chunks with a spoon.
Toss pasta with the sauce and reserved water over low heat for 1 minute.
Serve immediately topped with grated cheese.
notes: Do not over-shred the beef; keep the cubes mostly whole for a premium texture.
Ensure the sauce is reduced until it coats the pasta without pooling.
Use a high-quality bronze-cut pasta for better sauce adhesion.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo y Brócoli
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented as a single portion in a shallow, hand-painted ceramic bowl. A base of fluffy, tomato-infused rice is studded with diced red bell peppers and translucent onions. Five to six large, whole chunks of pan-seared chicken thighs are arranged centrally, showing a deep golden-brown crust. Vibrant green broccoli florets, cut into bite-sized pieces, are tucked between the chicken chunks. The arrangement is organic and uncrowded, leaving a clean margin around the bowl's edge. A side of lime wedges and a small bowl of fresh salsa sit on the dark wood tabletop. The lighting is soft and natural, emphasizing the textures of the seared poultry and the individual grains of rice.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with fresh lime wedges for acidity
Accompany with warm corn tortillas
Provide a side of fresh salsa verde or pico de gallo

ingredients.name: Chicken thighs, boneless and skinless, cut into 4cm chunks
Red bell pepper, diced into 1cm cubes

instructions: Heat 15ml oil in a wide, heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat.
Season chicken chunks with salt and pepper.
Sear chicken until browned on all sides. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add remaining oil to the same pan.
Sauté onion and bell pepper for 4 minutes until softened.
Stir in garlic and chili. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add rice to the pan. Toast for 2 minutes, stirring constantly until opaque.
Add tomatoes and cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in chicken stock and return chicken chunks to the pan.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low.
Cover and simmer for 15 minutes.
Place broccoli florets on top of the rice. Cover again.
Cook for 7 minutes until rice is tender and chicken reaches 75°C.
Remove from heat. Let rest, covered, for 5 minutes.
Fluff rice gently with a fork before serving.
notes: Toasting the rice in oil before adding liquid prevents it from becoming mushy.
Ensure the chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C for safety.
The broccoli is steamed on top to maintain its bright color and crunch.

Add bacon cubes. Fry until fat renders and edges are crispy.
Add onion to the skillet. Sauté until translucent.

Simmer sauce on low heat for 15 minutes.
Cook bucatini in boiling water until al dente.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Mahi Mahi with Avocado Lime Salsa
recipes.visual_description: A single, thick 150g Mahi Mahi fillet sits at the center of a clean white porcelain plate. The fish is pan-seared to a golden-brown crust with visible specks of cracked black pepper and lime zest. Atop the whole fillet, a vibrant salsa features 1cm avocado cubes, finely diced red onion, and minced green jalapeño, all tossed in fresh lime juice. A few whole cilantro leaves garnish the top. Beside the fish, a neat mound of fluffy white rice provides contrast. The entire plate is visible, set on a light wooden table next to a folded cotton napkin and a small bowl of extra lime wedges. Natural side-lighting highlights the flaky texture of the unsliced fish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas
Accompany with a side of black beans
Provide extra lime wedges for squeezing
instructions: Pat mahi mahi fillets dry with paper towels.
Season fillets with salt, pepper, and lime zest.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Place fillets in the pan.
Sear for 4 minutes until a golden-brown crust forms.
Flip fillets once.
Cook for 3 minutes until internal temperature reaches 63°C.
Remove fillets from pan and rest for 2 minutes.
Dice avocado into 1cm cubes.
Finely dice the red onion and mince the jalapeño.
Combine avocado, onion, jalapeño, chopped cilantro, and lime juice in a bowl.
Toss gently to maintain avocado shape.
Place one whole fillet on each plate.
Top with a generous portion of the avocado salsa.
notes: Use firm but ripe avocados to ensure the cubes hold their shape.
Ensure the pan is very hot before adding the fish to get a proper sear.
Do not over-mix the salsa to prevent it from becoming mushy.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Black Pudding with Sweet Corn Puree and Spiced Cherries
recipes.visual_description: A single portion presented on a wide white porcelain plate. The foundation is a vibrant, smooth yellow sweet corn puree spread in a thick, organic circle. Two thick, whole medallions of pan-seared black pudding rest in the center. The pudding displays a dark, crispy, and crumbly crust. A glossy, deep crimson sauce containing halved cherries is spooned over the pudding, creating a stark color contrast. Scattered charred corn kernels and fresh thyme leaves garnish the dish. The scene is set on a dark oak bistro table with a grey linen napkin and a polished silver fork. Soft natural light emphasizes the rich textures of the seared crust and the silkiness of the puree.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of robust red wine
Accompany with crusty sourdough bread to mop up the puree
instructions: Simmer corn kernels in milk and 25g butter for 10 minutes.
Blend corn mixture until smooth. Season with salt.
Sauté shallots in remaining butter for 2 minutes.
Add cherries, balsamic vinegar, and thyme to the shallots.
Simmer sauce for 5 minutes until syrupy and thick.
Heat olive oil in a heavy skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear black pudding medallions for 3 minutes per side until crispy.
Spread a thick circle of corn puree on each plate.
Place two whole pudding medallions in the center of the puree.
Spoon the cherry reduction and halved cherries over the pudding.
notes: Ensure the black pudding is at room temperature before searing for an even crust
Pass the corn puree through a fine-mesh sieve for a professional restaurant finish

recipes.recipe_name: Plant-Based Chicken in Dark Beer and Chili Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of plant-based chicken chunks is served in the center of a clean white porcelain plate. The protein is coated in a thick, glossy mahogany-colored sauce made from dark beer and toasted chilies. The chunks are arranged naturally, not sliced or fanned. Interspersed are vibrant, charred thick-cut wedges of red bell pepper and soft, translucent white onion petals. The sauce has a rich, velvety texture that pools slightly at the base. A light scatter of fresh chopped cilantro adds a bright green contrast. The dish is presented on a rustic dark wood table with a side of warm corn tortillas in a cloth basket and a glass of dark beer. Natural side lighting highlights the glisten of the braising liquid.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas
Accompany with Mexican red rice
Provide fresh lime wedges for acidity

ingredients.name: dried guajillo chilies, stemmed and seeded
bell peppers, cut into thick wedges
white onion, cut into thick petals

instructions: Toast dried chilies in a dry pan over medium heat for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Soak toasted chilies in hot water for 10 minutes.
Blend soaked chilies, garlic, and 100 ml of dark beer until smooth.
Heat oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear plant-based chicken chunks for 5 minutes until browned on all sides.
Remove protein from pan and set aside.
Sauté onion petals and bell pepper wedges for 4 minutes until edges char.
Return protein to the pan and stir in cumin.
Pour in the blended chili mixture and the remaining dark beer.
Simmer uncovered for 12 minutes until the sauce thickens into a glossy glaze.
Verify internal temperature of plant-based chicken reaches 75°C.
Season with salt to taste.
notes: Ensure the pan is very hot before searing the plant-based chicken to achieve a crust.
Strain the chili sauce through a fine-mesh sieve for a smoother texture if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Estofado Criollo de Pollo y Carne
recipes.visual_description: A deep white porcelain bowl contains a hearty Argentinian Estofado. The dish features large 3cm cubes of tender braised beef and whole bone-in chicken thighs with golden skin. Large, irregular hand-cut potato wedges are submerged in a rich, vibrant rust-colored tomato and pimentón broth. The sauce is glossy and thick, showing bits of softened diced onion and minced garlic. The arrangement is rustic yet clean, centered in the bowl with ample broth. A garnish of coarsely chopped fresh parsley adds a bright green contrast. The bowl sits on a dark rustic wooden table accompanied by a side of crusty baguette and a small ceramic dish of green chimichurri. Natural light emphasizes the succulent texture of the unsliced meats.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty white bread to soak up the braising liquid
Accompany with a side of fresh chimichurri
Pair with a glass of Argentinian Malbec
Present in a traditional clay pot or deep ceramic vessel

ingredients.name: Potatoes, peeled and cut into large wedges

instructions: Heat oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Season beef cubes and chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Sear beef and chicken until browned on all sides.
Remove meat from the pot and set aside.
Add onion and garlic to the same pot. Sauté until translucent.
Stir in tomato paste, pimentón, and oregano. Cook for 2 minutes.
Return the beef and chicken to the pot.
Pour in beef stock until meat is nearly covered.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 45 minutes.
Add potato wedges to the pot. Continue simmering for 25 minutes.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Check potatoes for tenderness and adjust seasoning.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C
The stew is often better the next day as flavors develop
Use waxy potatoes to ensure they hold their shape during braising

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Pork Tenderloin with Garlic-Parmesan Polenta and White Truffle
recipes.visual_description: A whole roasted pork tenderloin rests on a bed of creamy garlic-Parmesan polenta. The pork features a dark, caramelized crust with flecks of black pepper and rosemary. The polenta is a soft, pale yellow with a fluid, velvety texture that spreads naturally across a white porcelain plate. Delicate, paper-thin shavings of white truffle are draped over the pork, showcasing their intricate internal marbled patterns. The plating is minimalist and centered, leaving clean space at the rim. The scene is set on a light gray stone tabletop with a single silver fork and a folded white cotton napkin. Soft, natural light from a window creates gentle highlights on the truffle shavings and the glossy surface of the polenta.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of Barolo or Nebbiolo wine
Present with a truffle shaver at the table
Follow with a simple green salad
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Season pork with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in an oven-proof pan.
Sear pork on all sides until browned.
Add rosemary and half the garlic to the pan.
Transfer pan to oven.
Roast pork for 15 minutes.
Remove pork and rest for 10 minutes.
Boil water in a large pot with salt.
Whisk in polenta slowly.
Reduce heat to low.
Cook polenta for 20 minutes while stirring.
