recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Mole Poblano
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chicken Mole Poblano served on a clean white porcelain plate. The centerpiece is a whole, bone-in chicken thigh completely coated in a thick, velvety, dark reddish-brown mole sauce. The sauce appears glossy and rich with visible texture from ground seeds and spices. Toasted white sesame seeds are sprinkled evenly over the chicken. Three small sprigs of fresh cilantro and four thin rings of raw red onion provide a vibrant color contrast. Beside the chicken, a neat mound of fluffy Mexican red rice is positioned. The background features a rustic wooden table with a small basket of warm corn tortillas wrapped in a colorful woven cloth and a simple cotton napkin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Warm corn tortillas served in a traditional cloth-lined basket
Mexican red rice (arroz rojo)
Refried beans topped with crumbled queso fresco
instructions: Remove stems and seeds from all dried chilies.
Toast chilies in a dry pan over medium heat for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Place toasted chilies in a bowl of hot water and soak for 20 minutes.
Toast almonds, 15g of sesame seeds, and the cinnamon stick in a dry pan until golden.
Char the tomatoes, onion, and garlic in a dry pan until blackened in spots.
Drain chilies and place in a blender with toasted nuts, spices, and charred vegetables.
Add 100ml of chicken stock and blend until a smooth paste forms.
Heat oil in a large pot. Add the mole paste and fry for 5 minutes, stirring constantly.
Stir in the remaining chicken stock and chopped dark chocolate. Simmer on low heat.
Season chicken thighs with salt. Sear in a separate pan until the skin is golden brown.
Transfer chicken to the mole sauce. Simmer until the internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Adjust seasoning with salt if necessary.
notes: Do not burn the chilies during toasting or the sauce will become bitter.
The mole sauce should be thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.
Ensure chicken reaches the safety temperature of 75°C at the bone.

recipes.recipe_name: Szechuan Peppercorn Cacio e Pepe
recipes.visual_description: The spaghetti is presented as a single portion in a shallow, wide-rimmed white porcelain bowl. The pasta is expertly tossed in a glossy, pale-cream sauce, showing a fluid and silken consistency. Coarsely crushed Szechuan peppercorns are scattered across the dish, their reddish-brown husks providing a sharp visual contrast against the ivory cheese sauce. The pasta is arranged in a loose, organic mound, allowing the sauce to pool slightly at the bottom. A light garnish of finely grated Pecorino Romano sits atop the nest. The scene is set on a light-colored wooden bistro table with a crisp white cotton napkin and a silver fork. Natural daylight highlights the creamy texture and the speckled spices.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in warmed porcelain bowls
Pair with a crisp Frascati or a dry Riesling
Consume immediately to maintain the emulsion
instructions: Grate the Pecorino Romano finely using a microplane.
Place grated cheese in a bowl. Add 60 ml of warm water. Whisk into a thick, smooth paste.
Toast Szechuan peppercorns in a dry skillet over medium heat for 2 minutes.
Crush the toasted peppercorns coarsely using a mortar and pestle.
Boil 3 liters of water in a large pot. Add 15 g of salt.
Cook spaghetti until 2 minutes before al dente consistency.
Reserve 250 ml of starchy pasta water. Drain the pasta.
Place the crushed peppercorns in the large skillet. Add 125 ml of reserved pasta water. Bring to a simmer.
Add the pasta to the skillet. Toss continuously until the water is mostly absorbed.
Remove the skillet from the heat. Add the cheese paste.
Stir vigorously and toss the pasta to emulsify the sauce. Add more pasta water if needed for a fluid consistency.
Serve immediately.
notes: The numbing effect of the peppercorns replaces the heat of traditional black pepper
Ensure the pan is off the heat before adding cheese to prevent clumping
Use high-quality Pecorino Romano for the best emulsification

recipes.recipe_name: Turkish Style Tomato and Egg Scramble
recipes.visual_description: The dish features a vibrant, moist scramble of eggs and softened tomatoes served in a traditional small cast-iron skillet. The tomatoes are cut into small cubes, cooked down into a thick, rustic sauce that mingles with the creamy, soft-set eggs. Strands of melted cheddar cheese stretch throughout the mixture. The surface is speckled with red pepper flakes and freshly chopped flat-leaf parsley. Beside the skillet sits a thick wedge of crusty bread and a small bowl of olives. The setting is a rustic wooden table under warm, natural light. The arrangement is casual and unpretentious, capturing a hearty home-cooked breakfast. The entire skillet is visible, showcasing the textured, colorful meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty white bread or simit
Accompany with black olives and sliced cucumbers
Serve with Turkish black tea in a tulip glass

ingredients.name: ripe tomatoes, diced into small cubes

instructions: Heat olive oil in a medium skillet over medium heat.
Add diced green pepper. Sauté for 3 minutes until softened.
Add diced tomatoes to the skillet. Cook for 8 minutes until juicy and soft.
Whisk eggs in a small bowl with salt.
Pour eggs into the tomato mixture.
Add grated cheddar cheese immediately.
Stir gently with a wooden spoon for 2 minutes. Keep eggs moist and soft.
Remove from heat before eggs fully dry out.
Sprinkle with red pepper flakes.
notes: Do not overcook the eggs; they should remain slightly saucy.
Use very ripe tomatoes for the best flavor and juice consistency.

recipes.recipe_name: Rigatoni with Chicken and Tomato Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of rigatoni is presented in a wide, rustic ceramic bowl with a cream-colored glaze. The pasta is coated in a thick, vibrant red tomato sauce that clings to the ridges of the noodles. Large 3cm chunks of seared chicken thighs are distributed naturally throughout the dish, showing visible golden-brown caramelization. The arrangement is casual and home-style, with ingredients overlapping. Finely grated parmesan cheese is dusted over the center, and hand-torn green basil leaves provide a fresh contrast. The bowl sits on a dark, well-worn wooden table. A simple stainless steel fork and a folded linen napkin are placed to the side under warm, soft kitchen lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm crusty bread to scoop up remaining sauce
Pair with a glass of Chianti or similar medium-bodied red wine
Present in a large communal bowl for family-style dining
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3cm chunks.
Finely dice the onion and mince the garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large deep pan over medium-high heat.
Brown chicken chunks for 6 minutes until golden. Season with salt and pepper.
Remove chicken from the pan and set aside.
Add onion and garlic to the same pan. Sauté for 4 minutes until soft.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and dried oregano. Simmer on low heat for 15 minutes.
Boil 4 liters of water with 10g salt. Cook rigatoni until al dente.
Return chicken to the sauce. Simmer until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Drain pasta and reserve 60ml of the cooking water.
Toss pasta with the sauce and reserved water over low heat for 1 minute.
Tear basil leaves and stir into the pasta. Serve with grated parmesan.
notes: Ensure the chicken reaches 75°C for safety
Cook pasta one minute less than package directions for perfect al dente texture
Use pasta water to create a silky sauce consistency

recipes.recipe_name: Polish Żurek with White Sausage
recipes.visual_description: A deep white porcelain bowl sits centered on a dark wooden bistro table. The soup is a creamy, opaque pale-grey with a velvety consistency. Visible in the broth are thick chunks of poached white sausage and a single hard-boiled egg half, yolk facing upward. Small flecks of green marjoram and golden fat droplets from the bacon shimmer on the surface. To the side, two thick wedges of toasted dark rye bread are stacked neatly on a small bread plate. A heavy silver spoon rests on a folded grey linen napkin. The lighting is soft and natural, emphasizing the steam and the rustic textures of the bread crust.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in a hollowed-out bread bowl for festive occasions
Accompany with a small glass of chilled potato vodka
Garnish with fresh dill or parsley
instructions: Dice bacon into 1cm cubes.
Fry bacon in a large pot over medium heat until crispy.
Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until translucent.
Pour in vegetable stock and add whole white sausages.
Simmer gently for 20 minutes.
Remove sausages from pot. Cut into 2cm thick chunks. Return to pot.
Shake the rye starter well and pour into the soup while stirring.
Add minced garlic and marjoram. Simmer for 5 minutes until thickened.
Whisk sour cream in a bowl. Add a ladle of hot soup to temper.
Stir tempered cream and horseradish into the pot. Do not boil.
Toast rye bread slices until golden.
Ladle soup into bowls. Top with half a hard-boiled egg. Serve with rye bread.
notes: Ensure the rye starter is at room temperature before adding to prevent clumping.
Use high-quality marjoram as it provides the signature aroma of the dish.
Do not boil the soup after adding sour cream to avoid curdling.

recipes.recipe_name: Thai Garlic Chicken Rice Noodles
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Thai garlic chicken noodles is presented on a clean, off-white ceramic plate. The wide rice noodles are glossy with a dark soy glaze, showing distinct charred edges from the high-heat wok. Generous 3cm chunks of golden-seared chicken thighs are piled at the center, thoroughly coated in a savory sauce. A thick layer of crispy, deep-fried golden garlic bits covers the chicken. Fresh, cool cucumber rounds are arranged on the side with vibrant green cilantro sprigs. The plate sits on a dark teak wood table in a modern bistro. A small porcelain dish of chili fish sauce and a pair of dark wood chopsticks complete the authentic Thai setting under soft, natural light.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Prik Nam Pla (fish sauce with sliced bird's eye chilies)
Provide a wedge of lime for acidity
Traditionally eaten with a fork in the left hand and a spoon in the right
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3cm chunks.
Mince all garlic cloves finely.
Heat oil in a wok over medium heat.
Fry minced garlic until golden and crispy.
Remove half of the fried garlic and set aside.
Increase heat to high and add chicken chunks.
Sear chicken until the internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Add wide rice noodles to the wok.
Pour in oyster sauce, light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, and sugar.
Toss ingredients rapidly over high heat for 2 minutes until noodles develop char marks.
Season with ground white pepper.
Transfer to a plate and top with reserved crispy garlic.
Garnish with cucumber rounds and cilantro sprigs.
notes: Ensure the wok is smoking hot before adding noodles to achieve authentic wok hei flavor
If using dried noodles, soak in warm water until pliable but firm before stir-frying
The dark soy sauce is primarily for color; do not over-add

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Arroz con Pollo presented on a clean white porcelain plate. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs with deeply browned, crispy skin sit atop a bed of golden, saffron-stained rice. The rice grains are plump and distinct, interspersed with fine bits of softened onion and concentrated red tomato. The dish shows vibrant yellow and orange hues from the saffron and paprika. A generous sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped parsley is scattered over the top. A single lemon wedge is placed neatly on the side. The plate sits on a light oak wooden table with a folded white cotton napkin. Lighting is bright, natural, and even, highlighting the textures of the crispy skin and the moist rice grains.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Alioli (garlic mayonnaise)
Accompany with crusty bread and a glass of chilled white wine
Present in a traditional terracotta cazuela for family-style dining
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide shallow pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden and crispy.
Flip and brown the other side. Remove chicken from pan.
Add onion to the same pan. Sauté until translucent.
Stir in garlic and grated tomato. Cook until liquid evaporates and mixture darkens.
Add smoked paprika and rice. Stir to coat rice in oil for 2 minutes.
Pour in white wine. Deglaze the pan. Simmer until wine reduces by half.
Add hot stock and saffron. Stir once to distribute.
Place chicken thighs back into the pan on top of the rice.
Simmer undisturbed over medium-low heat for 18-20 minutes.
Ensure chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove from heat. Cover with a clean cloth. Rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Do not stir the rice once the stock is added to allow a crust to form on the bottom.
Use a wide pan to ensure even rice cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Foie Gras with Granny Smith Apple and Calvados
recipes.visual_description: A single, whole seared foie gras medallion sits atop a thick 4cm golden-brown toasted brioche cube on a matte white porcelain plate. The foie gras features a deep mahogany crust with precise crosshatch scoring. Beside the brioche, three 1cm cubes of dark caramelized Granny Smith apple and three 5mm batons of translucent compressed apple are arranged in a fluid, organic composition. Five vibrant green dots of apple gel are placed with architectural precision. Two delicate micro-sorrel leaves provide herbal contrast. The plate rests on a dark grey veined marble surface with significant negative space. Sharp, dramatic professional lighting emphasizes the textures of the seared protein and the glassy fruit gel.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a chilled glass of Sauternes or a late-harvest Chenin Blanc
Present as an opening course for a formal French-style tasting menu
Provide a small dessert spoon alongside the fork to capture the apple reduction
instructions: Peel and dice one apple into 1cm cubes.
Sauté cubes in butter and sugar until caramelized and golden.
Deglaze the pan with Calvados and reduce until a thick syrup forms.
Whisk agar-agar into apple juice and bring to a boil for 1 minute.
Pour juice into a tray and refrigerate until firmly set.
Blend the set apple jelly until a smooth, glossy gel forms.
Cut the second apple into precise 5mm batons.
Place batons in a vacuum bag with 20ml apple juice and compress at 100%.
Score the foie gras medallions in a shallow 2mm crosshatch pattern.
Sear foie gras in a dry, hot stainless steel pan for 2 minutes per side.
Ensure internal temperature reaches a safe level for consumption.
Toast the brioche cubes in the rendered foie gras fat until golden.
Place one brioche cube in the center of each plate.
Position one whole foie gras medallion on top of the brioche.
Arrange caramelized cubes, compressed batons, and gel dots around the base.
notes: Ensure the pan is extremely hot before adding foie gras to achieve a crust without melting the interior
The apple gel can be made 24 hours in advance and stored in a squeeze bottle
Acidulated water can prevent the apple batons from browning before compression

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo con Calabacitas and Cumin
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a wide, matte white porcelain plate. Two whole, golden-brown seared chicken thighs sit off-center, their skin crisp and glistening. Surrounding the chicken are 2cm cubes of bright green and pale yellow squash, lightly softened but holding their shape. A vibrant green sauce made from the reduced stock, minced green chilies, and flecks of fresh coriander pools slightly around the base. The arrangement is organic and clean, with moderate negative space. Small sprigs of fresh coriander are scattered over the squash. Beside the plate sits a small stack of warm, folded corn tortillas in a cloth-lined basket and a side of lime wedges. Lighting is natural and even, highlighting the textures of the seared skin and succulent squash.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas
Provide fresh lime wedges for acidity
Accompany with a side of Mexican red rice
instructions: Season chicken with salt and half the cumin.
Heat oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden and crisp.
Flip chicken and cook until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from pan and keep warm.
Sauté onion and green chili in the same pan for 4 minutes.
Add garlic and remaining cumin. Cook 1 minute.
Add squash cubes. Sauté 3 minutes.
Pour in chicken stock. Simmer until squash is tender-crisp.
Stir in fresh coriander.
Place chicken back in the pan briefly to coat.
Serve immediately.
notes: Use skin-on thighs for better texture and flavor.
Ensure squash is not overcooked to maintain its structure.
Adjust chili count based on desired heat level.

recipes.recipe_name: Hainanese Chicken Rice
recipes.visual_description: The dish features large, succulent chunks of bone-in poached chicken with glossy, pale skin. The chicken rests on a bed of fragrant, light-yellow Jasmine rice infused with ginger and pandan. Slices of fresh, cool cucumber are arranged neatly to the side. The chicken is lightly drizzled with a mixture of soy sauce and sesame oil. Three small ceramic dipping bowls contain bright red chili sauce, dark soy sauce, and a vibrant green ginger-scallion oil. The meal is served on a clean white porcelain plate on a light wood table. A pair of dark wood chopsticks and a traditional ceramic soup spoon sit to the right. Natural light highlights the moist texture of the meat and the individual grains of rice.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side bowl of hot chicken broth
Include chili sauce, ginger-garlic sauce, and dark soy sauce
Serve at room temperature as per tradition
instructions: Rub chicken with salt to remove impurities.
Rinse chicken under cold water.
Boil 3 liters of water with 30g crushed ginger and scallions.
Submerge chicken in boiling water.
Simmer for 20 minutes.
Turn off heat and cover pot.
Steep chicken for 30 minutes.
Confirm internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Submerge chicken in ice water for 5 minutes.
Drain chicken and rub skin with sesame oil.
Sauté 20g minced ginger and minced garlic in chicken fat.
Add rice and toast for 2 minutes.
Add 600ml poaching liquid and pandan leaves.
Cook rice until liquid is absorbed.
Cut chicken into large chunks.
notes: Save the remaining poaching liquid for a light soup
Rubbing the chicken with salt ensures a smooth skin texture
Using rendered chicken fat for the rice is essential for authenticity

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Lyonnaise Potatoes and Caramelized Onions
recipes.visual_description: A single portion served on a clean white porcelain plate. The base consists of a rustic pile of golden-brown potato rounds, 5mm thick, intermingled with dark, jammy caramelized onion strands and flecks of bright green parsley. Centered on top is one whole, bone-in chicken thigh with a deeply browned, crispy skin. The chicken remains whole and is not sliced. Small droplets of shimmering pan glaze surround the base of the potatoes. The lighting is natural and soft, highlighting the textures of the crispy skin and tender potatoes. The setting is a dark wood bistro table with a folded grey cotton napkin and polished silver cutlery.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Dijon mustard
Pair with a crisp glass of Chablis or dry white wine
Provide crusty baguette to soak up the pan juices

ingredients.name: Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and sliced into 5mm rounds
Sea salt and cracked black pepper

instructions: Boil potato rounds in salted water for 5 minutes until parboiled. Drain and air dry.
Melt 20g butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add onions.
Cook onions for 20 minutes, stirring frequently until deep golden brown. Remove from pan.
Season chicken thighs generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in the same skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken skin-side down.
Sear chicken for 8-10 minutes until skin is dark gold and crispy.
Flip chicken and cook until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove and rest.
Add remaining butter to the pan. Fry potato rounds until golden and crisp on both sides.
Stir in garlic and caramelized onions. Cook for 2 minutes.
Deglaze pan with vinegar and chicken stock. Simmer until liquid reduces to a light glaze.
Fold in chopped parsley.
Place the potato and onion mixture on plates. Top with one whole chicken thigh per serving.
notes: Ensure potatoes are completely dry before frying to achieve maximum crispness.
Do not rush the onions; low and slow heat is essential for deep flavor development.
Rest the chicken for 5 minutes before plating to retain juices.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Tikka Masala
recipes.visual_description: The dish features large, charred chunks of succulent chicken submerged in a glossy, vibrant orange-red tomato gravy. The sauce has a thick, velvety texture with visible flecks of ground spices. The chicken chunks show dark, caramelized edges from the high-heat roasting. Plating is in a clean, white porcelain bowl set on a dark wooden table. A single portion is shown with a light swirl of heavy cream on top and a scattering of bright green chopped cilantro. To the side sits a stack of warm, charred garlic naan bread and a small bowl of steamed long-grain basmati rice. Lighting is natural and even, highlighting the rich colors and creamy consistency of the sauce while maintaining professional negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm garlic naan or buttered roti
Accompany with steamed basmati rice
Side of mint-yogurt raita and kachumber salad
Serve in a traditional hammered copper karahi
instructions: Combine yogurt, 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 1 tsp garam masala, 1/2 tsp turmeric, and 1 tsp chili powder.
Toss chicken chunks in marinade. Cover and refrigerate for 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 220°C. Place chicken on a wire rack over a baking sheet.
Roast chicken 15 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Set aside.
Heat oil in a large pan over medium heat. Sauté onions until golden brown.
Add remaining ginger-garlic paste. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in remaining garam masala, turmeric, and chili powder. Toast for 30 seconds.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Simmer 10 minutes until sauce thickens and oil separates.
Stir in butter and heavy cream. Season with salt.
Add roasted chicken chunks to the sauce. Simmer 2 minutes to combine flavors.
Garnish with fresh cilantro.
notes: Kashmiri chili powder provides color without excessive heat.
Ensure the chicken is well-charred for authentic smoky flavor.
Let the sauce simmer until the oil separates to ensure spices are fully cooked.

recipes.recipe_name: Authentic Hainanese Chicken Rice
Roasted Corn and Poblano Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of fluid, creamy risotto is presented in a wide-rimmed white porcelain bowl. The rice flows naturally across the center, showing a glossy, rich texture. Bright yellow charred corn kernels and 1cm dark green roasted poblano squares are evenly distributed throughout the pale rice. The dish is finished with crumbled white cotija cheese and a light dusting of red smoked paprika for color contrast. Fresh, roughly torn cilantro leaves are scattered on top. The bowl sits on a dark wood bistro table with a neutral cotton napkin and a polished silver spoon. Lighting is soft and natural, highlighting the creamy sheen of the rice.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with extra lime wedges on the side
Pair with a crisp Mexican lager or chilled hibiscus tea
instructions: Brush corn ears with oil. Char over an open flame or in a hot cast-iron pan until kernels are blackened in spots.
Cut kernels from the cob and set aside.
Char poblano peppers until skin blisters. Place in a bowl and cover for 10 minutes.
Peel, seed, and dice poblanos into 1cm squares.
Heat stock in a medium saucepan. Keep at a low simmer.
In a heavy-bottomed pot, sauté onion in oil until translucent.
Add rice to the pot. Toast for 2 minutes while stirring.
Add garlic and cook for 30 seconds.
Add one ladle of hot stock. Stir constantly until liquid is absorbed.
Continue adding stock one ladle at a time. Stir frequently to release starches.
Fold in corn kernels and diced poblanos when rice is al dente.
Remove from heat. Stir in butter, lime juice, and half of the cotija cheese.
Season with salt and smoked paprika. Ensure consistency is fluid and creamy.
notes: Ensure the stock is hot when added to the rice to maintain a steady cooking temperature
The risotto should move like lava when the plate is tilted; add more stock if it becomes too thick

recipes.recipe_name: Mexican Arroz con Pollo
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a shallow, matte-finished ceramic bowl on a dark wood table. The base is a vibrant, reddish-orange long-grain rice, cooked to a moist, free-flowing consistency. Two whole, golden-brown seared chicken thighs with crispy skin rest atop the rice. The chicken is not sliced. Accompanying the chicken are charred tomato wedges and small cubes of sautéed onion mixed within the grains. Garnishes include fresh, bright green cilantro leaves and thin wedges of lime placed on the side. The lighting is natural and even, highlighting the textural contrast between the crispy chicken skin and the soft rice. A linen napkin and a heavy silver fork sit beside the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas
Provide extra lime wedges for acidity
Accompany with pickled red onions
instructions: Remove stems and seeds from guajillo and arbol chilies.
Toast chilies in a dry skillet over medium heat for 2 minutes.
Soak toasted chilies in 200ml hot water for 10 minutes.
Blend soaked chilies, tomatoes, half the onion, and garlic until smooth.
Pat chicken dry and season with salt.
Heat oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden and crispy.
Flip chicken and sear for 2 minutes then remove from pot.
Add rice and remaining onion to the pot.
Toast rice for 3 minutes until opaque and slightly golden.
Pour blended chili-tomato mixture into the rice.
Cook for 5 minutes while stirring until sauce thickens.
Add chicken stock and return chicken to the pot.
Reduce heat to low and cover with a tight lid.
Simmer for 20 minutes.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove from heat and let rest covered for 5 minutes.
Fluff rice gently before serving.
notes: Use bone-in thighs to ensure the meat remains juicy during simmering
Do not over-toast the dried chilies as they can turn bitter
The rice should be moist and flavorful, absorbing all the chili-tomato broth

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo al Ajillo
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pollo al Ajillo served on a clean white porcelain plate in a modern Spanish bistro setting. The dish features two whole chicken pieces—a thigh and a drumstick—with crispy, deep golden-brown skin. The chicken is surrounded by twenty whole, soft, golden-confit garlic cloves. A rich, translucent emulsion of olive oil and sherry glaze coats the meat. Bright green, finely chopped parsley is scattered over the top. The arrangement is organic and centered with moderate negative space. A side of thick-cut, toasted rustic baguette sits on the edge of the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the glistening textures of the oil and the sear on the chicken.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty rustic bread to soak up the garlic oil.
Accompany with a glass of chilled dry Fino sherry.
Present in a traditional terracotta cazuela for a rustic look.
instructions: Pat chicken dry with paper towels.
Season chicken generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide heavy-bottomed pan over medium heat.
Add whole garlic cloves to the oil.
Fry garlic until golden brown on all sides.
Remove garlic with a slotted spoon and set aside.
Increase heat to medium-high.
Place chicken pieces in the pan, skin-side down.
Sear chicken until deep golden brown on all sides, about 10 minutes.
Drain half of the rendered fat from the pan.
Add bay leaf and return fried garlic to the pan.
Pour in the dry sherry.
Scrape the bottom of the pan to release browned bits.
Lower heat to medium-low and cover with a lid.
Simmer for 15 minutes or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove lid and increase heat for 2 minutes to thicken the sauce.
Stir in chopped parsley and serve immediately.
notes: Ensure the garlic does not burn; it should be golden and sweet, not black and bitter.
Use high-quality extra virgin olive oil for the best flavor profile.
Always verify the thickest part of the chicken reaches 75°C for safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Rajma Chawal with Brown Rice
recipes.visual_description: The dish features a vibrant mound of steamed brown rice positioned on a clean white porcelain plate. Beside the rice, a generous serving of thick, savory kidney bean curry displays a deep reddish-brown hue. The beans remain whole and tender, coated in a rich tomato-based gravy. Fresh green cilantro leaves are scattered over the beans. Fine julienne strips of ginger provide a sharp visual contrast. On the side of the plate, three thin wedges of lime and a small pile of pickled red onion rings add height and color. The arrangement is organic and clean, utilizing moderate negative space. The setting includes a rustic wooden table, a stainless steel spoon, and a small side bowl of plain yogurt.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of lachha pyaz (pickled onion rings)
Accompany with plain whole milk yogurt
Provide a fresh lime wedge for acidity
instructions: Soak kidney beans in water for 8 hours.
Drain beans and boil in fresh salted water until tender. Drain.
Rinse brown rice thoroughly.
Boil rice in 600ml water until soft. Drain excess liquid.
Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pot.
Add cumin seeds until they sizzle.
Add diced onions. Sauté until dark golden brown.
Stir in ginger-garlic paste. Cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in tomato puree and salt. Cook until oil separates from the masala.
Add turmeric, coriander, and chili powder. Stir well.
Mix in cooked kidney beans and 250ml water.
Simmer on low heat for 20 minutes.
Mash a few beans with a spoon to thicken the gravy.
Stir in garam masala. Garnish with fresh cilantro.
notes: Ensure onions are deeply caramelized for authentic flavor.
Use Kashmiri chili powder for a vibrant red color without excessive heat.
If using canned beans, rinse thoroughly before simmering in the masala.

recipes.recipe_name: Red-Braised Beef with Carrots
Mujadara with Caramelized Onions
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Mujadara is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The base is a natural, fluffy mound of basmati rice mixed with tender whole brown lentils. The rice grains are distinct and lightly tinted golden from the cumin and onions. A generous heap of deeply caramelized, glossy dark brown onion strands is piled in the center. Fresh, coarsely chopped flat-leaf parsley provides a vibrant green contrast. A side of thick, white labneh is served in a small separate ceramic dish. The background features a clean wooden table with a folded linen napkin and a small plate of pink pickled turnips. Natural, soft lighting emphasizes the textures of the grains and the crispy onion garnish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of plain yogurt or labneh
Accompany with a fresh tomato and cucumber salad
Include pickled vegetables or olives as a side
instructions: Rinse lentils under cold water.
Place lentils in a pot with 1 liter of water. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes until partially tender. Drain.
Slice onions into thin half-moons.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed skillet.
Add onions to the skillet. Cook over medium heat for 20 minutes.
Stir frequently until onions are dark brown and sweet.
Remove half of the caramelized onions and set aside for garnish.
Add rice, par-cooked lentils, and cumin to the remaining onions in the skillet.
Stir to coat rice in oil for 2 minutes.
Add boiling water and salt. Cover tightly.
Simmer on low heat for 15-18 minutes until water is absorbed.
Remove from heat. Let rest covered for 10 minutes.
Fluff rice with a fork.
Serve topped with reserved crispy onions and chopped parsley.
notes: Do not rush the onions; deep caramelization provides the main flavor.
Ensure the rice is fluffed gently to keep the grains separate.
Brown lentils hold their shape better than red lentils for this dish.

recipes.recipe_name: Hazelnut Praline Entremet with Burnt Butter Financier and Espresso Gel
recipes.visual_description: The dessert centers on a perfect spherical hazelnut mousse entremet coated in a matte, pale beige praline glaze. It sits off-center on an oversized matte white designer porcelain plate. Three small, precise cubes of golden-brown burnt butter financier are placed in a natural, organic curve beside the sphere. Tiny, sharp dots of dark espresso gel and droplets of translucent hazelnut oil provide sophisticated color contrast. Two thin shards of caramelized hazelnut praline are leaned against the mousse for architectural height. The arrangement utilizes abundant negative space with Michelin-starred precision. The setting features a grey-veined white marble surface, a silver dessert spoon, and a crisp white linen napkin under dramatic, directional professional lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small glass of Frangelico or a late-harvest dessert wine
Present on a chilled porcelain plate to maintain mousse integrity
Pair with a high-quality double espresso
instructions: Toast hazelnuts at 160°C for 12 minutes. Rub off skins. Reserve 20 g for garnish.
Make praline: Caramelize 60 g sugar. Add 100 g hazelnuts. Cool on silicone mat. Process into a smooth paste.
Prepare dacquoise: Whisk 80 g egg whites with 40 g sugar to stiff peaks. Fold in 80 g hazelnut flour and 80 g icing sugar. Bake at 170°C for 15 minutes. Cut into 6 cm circles.
Create crunch layer: Melt 30 g praline paste with 20 g butter. Fold in feuilletine. Spread over dacquoise circles. Chill.
Make financier: Brown 100 g butter until dark gold. Mix with 70 g egg whites, 20 g hazelnut flour, and 20 g icing sugar. Bake in a flat sheet at 180°C for 10 minutes. Cut into 1 cm cubes.

Prepare mousse: Bloom gelatin in cold water. Heat 100 ml cream with 100 g praline paste. Dissolve gelatin. Fold in 300 ml whipped cream. Pour into sphere molds. Insert dacquoise/crunch discs. Freeze 4 hours.
Make espresso gel: Boil espresso with agar-agar for 1 minute. Chill until set. Blend into a smooth gel. Transfer to a squeeze bottle.
Unmold entremets. Glaze with remaining melted praline or neutral glaze.
notes: Ensure the praline paste is processed until completely smooth for the best mousse texture
The beurre noisette must be strained through a fine-mesh sieve to remove burnt solids
Allow entremets to temper at room temperature for 15 minutes before serving

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Beef and Shells Skillet Snack
recipes.visual_description: Four small, mismatched ceramic bowls sit on a worn wooden kitchen table. Each bowl is filled with a hearty mixture of small pasta shells and browned ground beef crumbles. The shells are coated in a glossy, savory tomato-based sauce that appears rich and deep red. Melted orange cheddar cheese is draped over the pasta, creating soft, gooey textures. Small pieces of translucent diced onion are visible throughout the mix. The arrangement is unpretentious and overflowing, suggesting a generous home-cooked snack. The lighting is warm and domestic, coming from a nearby window. A single folded paper towel lies casually on the table next to the bowls. The entire scene feels lived-in and comfortable.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in small individual bowls for casual snacking
Eat with a spoon for a homestyle experience
Accompany with a cold beverage
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add ground beef to the skillet.
Brown beef for 5 minutes.
Break meat into small crumbles with a spatula.
Add diced onion to the beef.
Sauté 3 minutes until onion is soft.
Stir in minced garlic and tomato paste.
Cook for 1 minute.
Add dry pasta shells and beef broth.
Bring the mixture to a boil.
Reduce heat to low.
Cover the skillet with a lid.
Simmer for 10-12 minutes.
Stir occasionally until pasta is tender.
Remove from heat when liquid is absorbed.
Stir in shredded cheese and oregano.
Season with salt and pepper.
Serve immediately in small bowls.
notes: Use lean ground beef to prevent excess grease in the snack
Ensure the skillet lid fits tightly to cook the pasta evenly

recipes.recipe_name: Charred Cabbage with Fermented Chili Vinaigrette
recipes.visual_description: A single thick triangular wedge of charred green cabbage sits centered on a handcrafted cream ceramic plate with a matte finish. The cabbage displays deep black char marks on the outer leaves, contrasting with the vibrant emerald green interior layers. A dark mahogany-colored vinaigrette made from chili bean paste is drizzled precisely over the wedge, pooling slightly at the base. Small, thin white discs of pickled cabbage stems and bright green spring onion rounds are scattered across the top for texture. The arrangement is minimalistic, utilizing the negative space of the earthy-toned plate. The scene is set on a reclaimed dark wood table with bamboo chopsticks and a neutral linen napkin under soft, natural side lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with bamboo chopsticks
Accompany with hot jasmine tea to cleanse the palate
Present as a communal starter course
instructions: Cut cabbage into four thick wedges through the core.
Finely slice the tough cabbage stems into thin discs.
Toss stem discs with 5ml vinegar and a pinch of salt. Set aside to pickle.
Whisk chili bean paste, remaining vinegar, soy sauce, sugar, and oil into a smooth vinaigrette.
Heat a dry cast iron pan over high heat until smoking.
Place cabbage wedges in the pan. Char each side for 3 minutes until blackened edges appear.
Add 20ml water to the pan. Cover immediately and steam for 2 minutes.
Remove cabbage and place one wedge on each plate.
Drizzle vinaigrette over the charred leaves.
Garnish with pickled stem discs, sliced spring onions, and sesame seeds.
notes: Ensure the core remains attached to keep the wedge intact during charring.
Use the outer leaves to make a fermented cabbage broth for zero-waste practice.
The Doubanjiang provides the primary salt and umami profile.

recipes.recipe_name: Nigerian Jollof Rice with Fried Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of vibrant, orange-red Jollof rice is served on a clean white porcelain plate. The rice is fluffy and free-flowing, showing small cubes of orange carrots and thin strips of red bell peppers throughout. Two whole, golden-brown fried chicken thighs rest prominently beside the rice, skin crispy and intact. The arrangement is organic, leaving moderate negative space on the plate. Beside the plate sits a small bowl of dark-fried plantain slices. The setting is a modern bistro with a dark wood table and a white cotton napkin. Lighting is natural and soft, highlighting the textures of the grain and the glossy finish of the chicken.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Fried plantains (Dodo)
Nigerian salad or coleslaw
Moin moin (steamed bean pudding)
Chilled malt drink
instructions: Season chicken with salt, half the curry powder, and thyme.
Boil chicken in a small amount of water until tender. Drain and reserve stock.
Heat oil in a large pan. Fry chicken until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken.
Blend bell peppers, scotch bonnets, and one onion into a smooth purée.
In the same oil, sauté one sliced onion and tomato paste for 5 minutes.
Add blended pepper purée. Cook over medium heat until oil separates from the sauce.
Stir in chicken stock, bouillon cubes, bay leaves, and remaining curry powder.
Wash rice thoroughly until water runs clear. Add rice to the pot.
Cover the pot tightly with foil and a lid. Simmer on low heat for 30 minutes.
Dice carrots into small cubes. Add to the rice and steam for 5 minutes.
Remove bay leaves. Mix the rice gently with a large fork.
Serve hot with the fried chicken pieces.
notes: Using foil under the lid is essential to trap steam for even cooking.
Do not stir the rice too often to avoid breaking the grains.
The 'bottom pot' or slightly burnt rice at the base adds authentic smoky flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Beer-Braised Pork and Mushroom Stew
Pollo en Salsa Roja
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pollo en Salsa Roja served in a shallow matte-gray ceramic bowl. Two whole, skin-on chicken thighs sit at the center, coated in a thick, vibrant deep-red tomato and guajillo sauce. Large wedges of softened white onion and blistered serrano chilies are nestled around the meat. The sauce has a glossy finish with visible specks of charred vegetable skin. Fresh cilantro leaves are scattered on top. The dish is set on a light oak table next to a small basket of warm corn tortillas and a lime wedge. Natural side-lighting highlights the texture of the sauce and the crispy chicken skin. The background is a blurred modern bistro with white porcelain accents.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas
Accompany with Mexican red rice
Provide fresh lime wedges for acidity

ingredients.name: White onions, cut into thick wedges

instructions: Heat a dry skillet over high heat.
Char tomatoes, half of the onion wedges, and serrano chilies until skins are blackened.
Toast guajillo chilies in the same skillet for 30 seconds.
Soak toasted guajillos in hot water for 10 minutes until soft.
Blend charred vegetables, soaked chilies, and garlic into a smooth sauce.
Season chicken thighs with salt.
Heat oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden brown.
Flip chicken and sear for 2 minutes.
Remove chicken from pot.
Sauté remaining onion wedges in the pot until softened.
Pour blended sauce and chicken stock into the pot.
Return chicken to the pot.
Simmer for 20 minutes over medium-low heat.
Ensure chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C.
Garnish with fresh cilantro.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches 75°C at the bone
Charring vegetables is essential for authentic smoky flavor
Strain the sauce after blending for a smoother texture if desired

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Chicken Thighs with White Beans and Rosemary
recipes.visual_description: A single portion features two whole bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs with deeply seared, golden-brown crispy skin. The chicken sits atop a bed of ivory-colored cannellini beans and vibrant green shredded kale. The beans are bathed in a light, savory broth with visible flecks of minced garlic and diced shallots. A single sprig of fresh rosemary and a lemon wedge garnish the side. The arrangement is clean and centered on a matte white porcelain plate, leaving balanced negative space. The setting is a modern bistro with a dark wood table, a folded linen napkin, and stainless steel flatware. Natural light highlights the textures of the crispy skin and tender beans.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty sourdough bread to soak up the bean broth
Pair with a crisp dry white wine like Sauvignon Blanc
instructions: Pat chicken dry and season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes until crispy.
Flip and sear for 2 minutes, then remove from pan.
Sauté diced shallots and minced garlic for 3 minutes.
Stir in beans, rosemary sprigs, and thyme sprigs.
Pour in chicken stock and bring to a simmer.
Return chicken to the pan skin-side up.
Simmer for 20 minutes until chicken reaches 75°C.
Stir in shredded kale and lemon juice until wilted.
notes: Ensure chicken skin remains above the liquid level to maintain crispness
Use high-quality chicken stock for a deeper savory flavor

recipes.recipe_name: Kadai Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant individual portion of Kadai Chicken is presented in a deep, rustic cast-iron kadai, or a similar deep white porcelain bowl, centered on a simple wooden table. The dish features generous 3-4cm chunks of succulent chicken, seared to a golden-brown, bathed in a rich, reddish-brown, thick tomato-onion gravy. Interspersed throughout are bright green and red bell pepper squares (2cm) and translucent onion petals, adding color and textural contrast. The surface glistens with a subtle sheen of oil, indicative of proper cooking. A generous sprinkle of fresh, chopped cilantro and a few strands of julienned ginger adorn the top. The scene is set with a clean white cotton napkin and traditional Indian flatware beside the bowl. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's warmth and texture. A small, neatly piled portion of basmati rice or a warm piece of naan bread rests subtly nearby, completing the authentic Punjabi dining experience. The background is simple and uncluttered.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with fresh, warm naan bread or fluffy basmati rice.
Offer sliced red onions and lemon wedges on the side for a fresh accompaniment.
Pair with a cooling raita (yogurt dip with cucumber or boondi).
instructions: Cut chicken into 3-4 cm chunks. Season chicken with 1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp turmeric. Set aside.
Dry roast coriander seeds, cumin seeds, and dried red chilies in a dry pan over medium heat for 2-3 minutes. Toast until fragrant. Let cool. Grind into a coarse powder. This is your Kadai masala.
Finely chop one onion. Cut the remaining onion into 2 cm petals. Cut bell peppers into 2 cm squares. Mince ginger and garlic.
Heat oil or ghee in a large kadai or heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat. Add chopped onion. Sauté until golden brown, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced ginger and garlic. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add chicken chunks. Sear chicken until lightly browned on all sides, about 5-7 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Add crushed tomatoes and the prepared Kadai masala. Stir well. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 8-10 minutes until the oil begins to separate from the gravy. This is the 'bhunao' stage.
Add bell pepper squares and onion petals. Stir to combine. Cook for 3-4 minutes until vegetables are slightly tender-crisp.
Crush kasoori methi between your palms. Add to the kadai. Stir in garam masala.
Cook for 2 more minutes. Taste and adjust salt if needed.
Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro before serving.
notes: The 'bhunao' step is crucial for developing deep flavors in the curry. Cook until the oil separates from the masala.
Adjust the dried red chilies or chili powder to your preferred spice level.
traditional_techniques: Dry roasting and grinding whole spices to create fresh masala.
Bhunao (sautéing the masala until oil separates and flavors are concentrated).

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Beef Tenderloin with Onion Soubise and Charred Petals
recipes.visual_description: A single thick, whole roasted beef tenderloin medallion sits off-center on a large, matte white bone china plate. The beef has a dark, mahogany-seared crust. A smooth, ivory-colored onion soubise is swiped in an organic, flowing motion across the plate. Five charred pearl onion petals, kept as hollow concave cups, are nestled into the soubise. A deep, glossy brown beef jus is drizzled with architectural precision around the base of the beef. The plate sits on a grey-veined Carrara marble surface. Natural side-lighting creates soft shadows, highlighting the fibrous texture of the seared beef and the silky sheen of the puree. A polished silver steak knife and fork are placed to the side.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of aged Bordeaux
Provide warm crusty baguette to finish the soubise
Use a heated ceramic plate to maintain beef temperature
instructions: Sweat sliced white onions in 50g butter over low heat for 20 minutes without browning.
Add heavy cream to onions and simmer for 5 minutes.
Blend onion mixture until completely smooth and pass through a fine-mesh chinois.
Season with salt and keep warm.
Sear halved pearl onions in a dry pan until faces are charred black.
Separate charred onion layers into individual petals.
Season beef tenderloin with salt.
Heat oil in a heavy skillet until smoking.
Sear beef on all sides to develop a dark crust.
Add remaining butter, thyme, and garlic to the pan.
Baste beef with foaming butter until internal temperature reaches 52°C.
Rest beef for 10 minutes on a warm rack.
Reduce bone broth until it coats the back of a spoon.
Carve beef into four thick, whole cylindrical medallions.
notes: Ensure the soubise is passed through a chinois for a professional texture.
Resting the meat is critical for juice retention.
The jus should be reduced until it reaches a syrupy consistency.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Cooked Beef and Bean Chili with Dark Chocolate and Beer
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of dark beef stew is served in a wide white porcelain bowl. Three 3cm beef cubes sit prominently in the center. The sauce is thick, glossy, and dark mahogany brown. Whole black beans and small pieces of crushed tomato are visible throughout the sauce. One fresh lime wedge rests on the side of the bowl. A small dollop of white crema and three fresh cilantro leaves garnish the top. The bowl sits on a dark oak wooden table. A small stack of warm corn tortillas is placed nearby on a small plate. Natural light illuminates the textures of the braised meat and the rich sauce. The background is a clean, modern bistro setting with minimal distractions.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm hand-pressed corn tortillas
Accompany with fresh lime wedges for acidity
Garnish with Mexican crema or crumbled cotija cheese
instructions: Pat beef cubes dry with paper towels.
Season beef with salt.
Heat oil in a heavy-based pot over medium-high heat.
Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides.
Remove beef and set aside.
Add onion to the same pot.
Sauté 5 minutes until translucent.
Add garlic, chilis, and cumin.
Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in beer to deglaze the pot.
Scrape the bottom of the pot to release browned bits.
Add tomatoes, beans, and the seared beef.
Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low and cover.
Cook for 90 minutes or until beef is tender.
Stir in grated chocolate until melted.
Add lime juice.
Season with additional salt if needed.
notes: Use a high-quality dark stout for maximum depth of flavor
Ensure the beef is seared in batches to prevent steaming
The chocolate should be added at the very end to preserve its aroma

recipes.recipe_name: Hyderabadi Chicken Biryani
recipes.visual_description: The entire plate is captured in a professional shot. The dish is presented in a traditional wide-rimmed white porcelain bowl. Steamed long-grain Basmati rice displays a mix of snow-white and saffron-infused yellow grains. Large, moist chunks of marinated and steamed bone-in chicken thighs are buried partially in the rice, coated in a dark, aromatic masala. The top is scattered with crispy, deep-brown fried onions and vibrant green chopped mint and coriander. A small copper bowl of chilled cucumber raita sits to the left. The setting includes a dark wood surface, a silver spoon, and a crisp white cotton napkin. Natural light emphasizes the fluffy rice texture and the steam rising from the center. No meat is sliced.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Chilled cucumber and onion raita
Mirchi ka Salan
Fresh lime wedges and sliced red onions
instructions: Mix chicken chunks, yogurt, biryani masala, ginger-garlic paste, and 10g salt.
Marinate for 60 minutes.
Rinse rice until water runs clear.
Soak rice in water for 30 minutes.
Boil 2 liters water with cloves and cardamom.
Add rice and cook until 70% tender.
Drain rice immediately.
Place marinated chicken chunks in a heavy-bottomed pot.
Spread 50g fried onions, chopped mint, and coriander over chicken.
Layer rice over the herbs and onions.
Drizzle saffron-infused milk and ghee over rice.
Seal pot lid tightly with aluminum foil.
Cook on low heat for 30 minutes.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Rest for 10 minutes before fluffing with a fork.
notes: Use high-quality aged Basmati rice for long, separate grains.
Do not stir the rice during the dum process to prevent breakage.

recipes.recipe_name: Beef Ragù alla Bolognese with Pappardelle
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of wide, golden pappardelle ribbons served in a shallow white porcelain pasta bowl. The pasta is coated in a rich, thick, brick-red sauce featuring visible small cubes of braised beef and finely diced vegetables. The noodles are arranged in a natural, flowing pile with moderate negative space around the edges. A generous dusting of finely grated white Parmigiano-Reggiano covers the center. The dish is set on a dark walnut wood table. Beside the bowl lies a folded white linen napkin and a heavy silver fork. The lighting is soft and natural, highlighting the glossy texture of the sauce and the rustic chunks of beef. Background elements include a half-filled glass of red wine.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of Sangiovese or Lambrusco
Provide extra Parmigiano-Reggiano on the side
Accompany with crusty sourdough bread to clean the plate

ingredients.name: Beef chuck, finely hand-chopped into small 1cm cubes

instructions: Heat olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat.
Add diced pancetta. Cook until the fat renders and meat browns.
Add onion, carrot, and celery. Sauté until vegetables soften.
Increase heat to medium-high. Add beef cubes.
Brown the beef thoroughly on all sides.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in white wine. Scrape the bottom of the pot to release browned bits.
Simmer until the wine evaporates completely.
Add milk and beef stock. Season with salt and pepper.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 2 hours until beef is tender.
Boil a large pot of salted water. Cook pappardelle until al dente.
Drain pasta. Reserve 60ml of pasta cooking water.
Toss pasta directly into the ragù pot.
Add reserved pasta water. Stir until the sauce coats the noodles evenly.
Remove from heat. Stir in half of the Parmigiano-Reggiano.
notes: Hand-chopping the beef instead of using mince provides a superior texture.
Adding milk is traditional for Bolognese to tenderize the meat and balance acidity.
Ensure the sauce is fluid and coats the pasta completely before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Venison and Beef Ragù with Pappardelle
Pressed Chicken and Squash Terrine with Pickled Cherries
recipes.visual_description: A single rectangular block of pressed chicken and golden squash cubes sits centrally on a matte cream ceramic plate. The terrine shows a rustic texture of shredded chicken and vibrant orange squash. A bold line of black squash skin ash is dusted across the top of the block. Three whole, glossy pickled cherries are placed in a cluster at the base. Small, precise dots of ivory almond reduction decorate the negative space. One irregular, translucent rice crisp is propped vertically against the chicken block. The lighting is soft and natural, emphasizing the contrast between the dark ash and the pale almond cream on the handcrafted stoneware.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve on handcrafted pottery to honor artisanal traditions
Pair with a dry sparkling cider to complement the fermented cherries
Provide a small appetizer fork and knife
instructions: Combine vinegar, 5g salt, and cherries in a jar. Let ferment at room temperature for 2 hours.
Peel the squash. Reserve all skins. Dice flesh into 1 cm cubes.
Roast squash cubes at 200°C for 15 minutes until tender.
Place squash skins on a tray. Bake at 120°C until brittle and charred. Grind into a fine black ash.
Poach chicken in salted water until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Shred chicken while hot. Mix with roasted squash and thyme leaves.
Line a small mold with parchment. Pack chicken mixture tightly. Weight it down and chill for 4 hours.
Boil rice in 300ml water until mushy. Blend into a paste. Spread thinly on silicone and dry at 80°C. Fry briefly in hot oil to puff.
Toast almonds. Blend with 100ml water. Strain and simmer liquid until reduced by half into a thick cream.
Turn out terrine. Cut into 4 thick rectangular blocks.
notes: Use the chicken poaching liquid as a base for a future soup to ensure zero waste.
The squash skin ash provides a deep smoky flavor and prevents waste of the nutrient-dense peel.
Ensure the terrine is fully chilled before slicing to maintain structural integrity.

recipes.recipe_name: Tomato and Beef Stir-Fry
Pressed Chicken and Squash Terrine with Pickled Cherries

recipes.recipe_name: Oregano Roasted Chicken with Garlic Swiss Chard Pasta
recipes.visual_description: The dish features two golden-brown, skin-on roasted chicken thighs resting on a bed of glossy orecchiette pasta. The pasta is mixed with vibrant dark green shredded swiss chard leaves and small 5mm cubes of sautéed chard stems. Thinly sliced garlic cloves are interspersed within the pasta. The chicken skin is perfectly crisp, showing a textured surface seasoned with dried oregano. A light, translucent sauce coats the pasta, reflecting natural light. The meal is served on a clean white porcelain plate with ample negative space. A single sprig of fresh oregano is placed on the side. The setting is a modern bistro with a light wood table and a neutral cotton napkin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty sourdough bread
Accompany with a crisp dry white wine
Garnish with a drizzle of high-quality finishing olive oil
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt, pepper, and dried oregano.
Place chicken skin-side down in a cold skillet.
Turn heat to medium-high and sear for 8 minutes until skin is crisp and golden.
Flip chicken and transfer skillet to oven preheated to 200°C.
Roast chicken until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Boil orecchiette in salted water until al dente.
Separate chard leaves from stems. Dice stems into 5mm cubes and shred leaves.
Sauté garlic and chard stems in olive oil for 4 minutes in a large pan.
Add chard leaves and cook until wilted.
Deglaze pan with chicken stock and lemon juice. Simmer for 2 minutes.
Toss drained pasta and fresh oregano into the pan to coat with sauce.
Serve chicken whole on top of the pasta.
notes: Ensure chard stems are diced small to cook at the same rate as the garlic.
Starting chicken in a cold pan helps render the fat for a crispier skin.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken with Beet Purée and Crab-Corn Salsa
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, modern plate features a deep purple beet purée spread in a smooth, thick circle at the center. A whole roasted chicken thigh with crisp, golden-brown skin sits atop the purée. The chicken is crowned with a textured salsa of charred yellow corn kernels, finely diced red bell peppers, and large lumps of white crab meat. Fresh, bright green coriander leaves are scattered over the top. The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain plate with ample negative space. The setting is a modern bistro with a light oak wooden table and a soft cotton napkin. Natural light highlights the glossy skin of the chicken and the earthy texture of the beet purée.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a crisp dry white wine
Accompany with crusty sourdough bread
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wrap beets in foil. Roast 45 minutes until tender.
Peel beets. Blend with lemon juice and salt until smooth.
Season chicken with salt and black pepper.
Sear chicken skin-side down in a pan for 5 minutes.
Transfer chicken to oven. Roast until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Sauté corn and diced bell peppers with garlic in butter for 4 minutes.
Remove from heat. Fold in crab meat and coriander gently.
Spread beet purée in a circle on four plates.
Place one whole chicken thigh on the purée. Top with crab-corn salsa.
notes: Ensure the beet purée is completely smooth for the best mouthfeel.
Do not overmix the crab to keep the lumps intact.

recipes.recipe_name: Homestyle Indian Chicken Curry
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of chicken curry served in a traditional stainless steel bowl on a circular metal thali tray. The dish features large, tender chunks of bone-in chicken submerged in a thick, textured reddish-brown gravy. The sauce shows visible bits of softened onions and tomatoes. A generous handful of bright green chopped coriander is scattered over the top. Beside the bowl on the tray is a small mound of fluffy white basmati rice and two folded, charred whole wheat rotis. A side of raw red onion rings and a single green chili sit at the edge. The setting is a dark wooden table with warm, natural kitchen lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm roti or naan
Accompany with steamed basmati rice
Provide raw onion rings and lemon wedges on the side
Eat traditionally using the bread as a scoop for the chicken and gravy

ingredients.name: chicken thighs, bone-in, cut into large chunks

instructions: Heat oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat.
Add cumin seeds and let them sizzle for 30 seconds.
Add onions. Sauté until deep golden brown.
Stir in ginger-garlic paste. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add turmeric, chili powder, and coriander powder. Stir for 30 seconds.
Add tomato puree. Cook until oil separates from the spice mixture.
Add chicken chunks. Stir to coat thoroughly with the masala.
Pour in water and add salt. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 25 minutes.
Check chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Stir in garam masala. Turn off heat.
Garnish with chopped coriander before serving.
notes: For a spicier curry, add 2 slit green chilies with the ginger-garlic paste.
Ensure the onions are well-browned for a deep, authentic flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Caramelized Onion Pasta with Parmesan
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of rigatoni pasta served in a wide white porcelain bowl on a rustic wooden bistro table. The pasta is coated in a deep amber, glossy sauce made from melted onions. Large 3cm chunks of seared chicken are distributed naturally throughout the dish. The chicken shows golden-brown caramelized edges. Fine wisps of freshly grated Parmesan cheese and a light sprinkle of chopped green parsley are scattered over the top. The arrangement is organic and free-flowing. A silver fork sits on a white cotton napkin beside the plate. The lighting is soft and natural, emphasizing the silky texture of the onion sauce and the rustic grain of the wood background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of dry Italian white wine such as Gavi or Soave
Provide extra grated Parmesan in a small side bowl
Serve with crusty ciabatta bread to mop up the onion sauce

ingredients.name: Chicken thigh fillets, cut into 3cm chunks

instructions: Heat olive oil and 20g butter in a large heavy-based pan over medium-low heat.
Add sliced onions and a pinch of salt.
Cook onions slowly for 35 minutes, stirring occasionally until deep golden brown.
Increase heat to medium and add chicken chunks to the pan.
Sear chicken until browned on all sides and internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Stir in minced garlic and cook for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Boil rigatoni in salted water until 2 minutes before al dente.
Reserve 200ml of pasta cooking water, then drain pasta.
Add pasta and reserved water to the onion and chicken mixture.
Simmer for 2 minutes while stirring to emulsify the sauce.
Remove from heat. Add remaining butter and Parmesan cheese.
Stir vigorously to create a glossy coating. Season with black pepper.
Garnish with chopped parsley and serve immediately.
notes: Slow cooking the onions is essential for the deep savory base of this sauce.
Always remove the pan from heat before adding the cheese to prevent clumping.
Ensure the chicken reaches 75°C for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo en Crema de Elote
recipes.visual_description: A single, golden-brown seared bone-in chicken thigh sits at the center of a matte charcoal ceramic plate. The chicken is partially submerged in a thick, vibrant pale-yellow corn cream sauce. Whole charred corn kernels and small 5mm cubes of dark green poblano pepper are scattered throughout the sauce. The chicken skin is visibly crispy and textured. A light sprinkle of finely chopped bright green cilantro and a few small dollops of crema provide contrast. The plate sits on a dark walnut wood table next to a small basket of warm, folded corn tortillas and a wedge of lime. Natural side lighting highlights the creamy texture of the sauce and the roasted edges of the corn.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Warm corn tortillas
Mexican red rice
Lime wedges
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes until golden and crisp.
Flip chicken and cook for 4 minutes.
Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Add butter to the same pan.
Sauté 400 g of corn kernels, onion, and poblano pepper for 5 minutes.
Add garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Transfer the sautéed mixture to a blender with cream and stock.
Blend until smooth and return to the pan.
Add the remaining 100 g of corn kernels to the sauce.
Place chicken back into the sauce.
Simmer for 10 minutes until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Garnish with fresh cilantro.
notes: Use fresh corn for the best sweetness and texture.
Ensure the sauce is thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.
Do not slice the chicken; serve the thigh whole to maintain juiciness.
