A thick, rustic sauce covers the base of the plate, filled with visible small cubes of orange carrots, green celery, and translucent onions. Whole, dark purple kalamata olives are nestled within the vibrant red tomato sauce. A light dusting of bright green chopped parsley and a single fresh rosemary sprig garnish the top. Two thick batons of grilled sourdough bread lean against the side of the chicken. The lighting is natural and soft, emphasizing the glossy texture of the braised sauce and the crispness of the chicken skin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with toasted sourdough bread to soak up the sauce
Accompany with a glass of medium-bodied Italian red wine
Place on a bed of soft, buttery polenta
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide braising pan over medium-high heat.
Place chicken skin-side down in the pan.
Sear for 6 minutes until the skin is deep golden and crisp.
Flip chicken and cook for 2 minutes.
Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Add onion, carrot, and celery to the remaining fat.
Sauté vegetables for 8 minutes until softened.
Stir in garlic, rosemary, and sage. Cook for 1 minute.
Pour in red wine. Scrape the bottom of the pan to deglaze.
Simmer wine for 3 minutes until reduced by half.
Add crushed tomatoes and stir to combine.
Place chicken thighs back into the sauce.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 25 minutes.
Check internal temperature of chicken reaches 75°C.
Stir in olives and simmer uncovered for 5 minutes.
Remove rosemary sprigs before serving.
Garnish with chopped parsley.
notes: Always use a meat thermometer to ensure chicken reaches the safe internal temperature of 75°C
Browning the skin thoroughly at the start is essential for the final texture
The sauce should be thick and chunky, not watery

recipes.recipe_name: Aloo Do Pyaza
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Aloo Do Pyaza is presented in a deep white porcelain bowl on a dark wood bistro table. The dish consists of 3cm fried potato cubes and large, sautéed translucent red onion petals coated in a thick, savory reddish-brown slow-cooked masala gravy. The sauce displays a rich, glossy texture from the traditional bhuna technique. The dish is topped with 2cm ginger julienne and freshly chopped cilantro. Two pieces of warm, charred garlic naan are folded neatly on a white cotton napkin to the side. A small white ramekin of cucumber raita provides a color contrast. Natural light from the side emphasizes the steam and the textures of the spices.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm garlic naan or tandoori roti
Accompany with a side of cooling cucumber raita
Provide a fresh lime wedge for bright acidity
instructions: Peel and cut potatoes into 3cm cubes.
Heat 30ml oil in a heavy-bottomed pan.
Fry potato cubes until golden and crisp. Remove and drain.
Sauté onion petals in the same oil for 2 minutes. Remove while still firm.
Add remaining oil to the pan and add cumin seeds.
Sauté sliced onions until deep golden brown.
Stir in ginger-garlic paste and green chilies. Cook for 1 minute.
Add tomato puree, turmeric, chili powder, and coriander powder.
Cook the mixture until oil separates from the masala base.
Return fried potatoes to the pan with 200ml water and salt.
Cover and simmer for 8 minutes until potatoes are tender.
Fold in sautéed onion petals and garam masala. Heat through for 2 minutes.
Garnish with fresh cilantro and ginger julienne.
notes: Do not overcook the onion petals to maintain a slight crunch
Ensure potatoes are fried until golden to prevent them from breaking in the gravy
Adjust the number of green chilies to control the heat level

recipes.recipe_name: Sun-Dried Tomato and Cheese Stuffed Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A single, golden-brown roasted chicken breast sits centrally on a white porcelain plate. The chicken is plump and intact, showing a slight melt of white cheese and deep red sun-dried tomato peeking from the side. Scattered around the base are thick, rustic chunks of toasted sourdough bread, crisped and golden from roasting in natural juices. Beside the bread are whole, charred spring onions, glistening with olive oil. Vibrant green sprigs of fresh oregano are scattered over the dish. The background is a clean, light wood bistro table with a white cotton napkin and a simple silver fork. The lighting is soft and natural, highlighting the textures of the seared poultry skin and the porous bread chunks.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of crisp white wine
Accompany with a simple side of dressed arugula
Present on warmed ceramic plates
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Chop sun-dried tomatoes and cube mozzarella into 1cm pieces.
Finely slice four spring onions and chop half the oregano.
Mix tomatoes, cheese, sliced onions, and chopped oregano in a bowl.
Cut a deep pocket into the side of each chicken breast.
Stuff each breast with the cheese mixture and secure with toothpicks.
Season the outside with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in an oven-proof pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken for 3 minutes per side until golden brown.
Tear bread into 3cm chunks and trim remaining whole spring onions.
Scatter bread chunks and whole spring onions around the chicken.
Pour chicken stock into the pan.
Transfer pan to the oven and roast for 12-15 minutes.
Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Garnish with remaining fresh oregano leaves.
notes: Use oil-packed sun-dried tomatoes for better moisture
Remove toothpicks before serving to guests
Rest the chicken for 5 minutes after roasting to retain juices

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Tagine with Preserved Lemon and Olives
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Moroccan chicken tagine presented on a wide, white porcelain plate. Two whole, golden-brown braised chicken thighs sit at the center, coated in a glossy, vibrant yellow-orange sauce. The sauce contains translucent diced onions, thin yellow strips of preserved lemon rind, and whole green olives. A scattering of bright green chopped cilantro and flat-leaf parsley provides contrast. Beside the chicken, a neat mound of fluffy, steamed couscous absorbs the sauce. The background features a modern bistro table with a small bowl of harissa and a piece of crusty bread. Natural side lighting highlights the succulent texture of the skin and the steam rising from the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed couscous
Accompany with spicy harissa paste
Provide fresh crusty bread for dipping
Serve in a traditional clay tagine vessel

ingredients.name: Preserved lemon, rind only, cut into thin strips

instructions: Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide pan or tagine over medium-high heat.
Brown chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes.
Flip chicken and brown for 3 minutes.
Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Sauté diced onions in the same pan until soft.
Add garlic, ginger, turmeric, cumin, and cinnamon.
Stir spices for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return chicken to the pan.
Add saffron with its soaking liquid and chicken stock.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 30 minutes.
Add preserved lemon strips and green olives.
Simmer uncovered for 10 minutes to thicken sauce.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Stir in chopped cilantro and parsley before serving.
notes: Rinse preserved lemon thoroughly to remove excess salt
Use a heavy-bottomed Dutch oven if a clay tagine is unavailable
Soak saffron in warm water for 10 minutes before use

recipes.recipe_name: Uzbek Beef Plov
recipes.visual_description: A wide, shallow ceramic platter holds a mountain of glistening, golden-hued long-grain rice. Large, tender 3cm chunks of seared beef are nestled on top and throughout the rice, never sliced. Vibrant orange julienned carrots and translucent caramelized onions are evenly distributed among the grains. A whole head of roasted garlic with charred skin sits prominently in the center. The rice appears fluffy and separate, lightly coated in aromatic oil. The platter rests on a traditional Ikat-patterned textile over a rustic wooden table. A small side dish of thinly sliced tomatoes and onions sits nearby. Soft, natural side-lighting highlights the succulent texture of the beef and the distinct individual grains of rice.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with Achichuk (tomato and onion salad)
Accompany with hot green tea
Serve with fresh Uzbek non bread
Present on a communal 'Lagan' ceramic platter
instructions: Rinse rice in cold water until the water runs clear.
Soak rice in warm salted water for 30 minutes.
Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed cast iron pot over high heat.
Brown beef chunks in batches until a dark crust forms.
Add onions to the pot. Fry until dark golden brown.
Stir in carrots. Cook 10 minutes until softened.
Pour in 500ml boiling water. Add cumin and salt.
Simmer uncovered for 30 minutes to create the zirvak base.
Drain rice. Spread rice in an even layer over the meat and vegetables.
Pour boiling water over a slotted spoon to cover rice by 1.5cm.
Boil on high heat until water disappears from the surface.
Push the whole garlic head into the center of the rice.
Poke five holes through the rice to the bottom using a spoon handle.
Cover pot with a tight lid. Reduce heat to the lowest setting.
Steam for 20 minutes.
Remove garlic. Mix rice and meat gently. Serve immediately.
notes: Do not stir the rice into the meat until the final steaming is complete.
The color of the plov depends on how dark you fry the onions.
Ensure the beef chunks are at least 3cm to maintain juiciness during the long cook.

recipes.recipe_name: Pad Kra Pao Gai with Shiitake Mushrooms
recipes.visual_description: The dish features golden-brown chicken chunks and thick-sliced shiitake mushrooms coated in a glossy, dark savory glaze. Bright red chili flecks and vibrant wilted basil leaves are distributed throughout. It is served on a clean white porcelain plate alongside a small bowl of steamed jasmine rice. A crispy, golden-edged fried egg with a runny yolk sits atop the rice. The arrangement is organic and centered, showing moderate negative space. Beside the plate lies a traditional Thai stainless steel spoon and fork on a folded cotton napkin. The background is a warm, modern bistro setting with a natural wood table. Lighting is even and soft, highlighting the textures of the seared chicken and the silkiness of the sauce.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Steamed jasmine rice
Crispy fried egg (Kai Dao)
Prik Nam Pla condiment
instructions: Pound garlic and chilies into a coarse paste.
Cut chicken into 2cm chunks.
Slice mushrooms into thick pieces.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat until smoking.
Fry garlic-chili paste for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add chicken chunks. Sear until browned on all sides.
Add mushrooms. Stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Mix oyster sauce, soy sauces, fish sauce, and sugar in a small bowl.
Pour sauce into wok. Toss to coat ingredients thoroughly.
Cook chicken to an internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove from heat. Fold in basil leaves until just wilted.
notes: Use holy basil for authenticity.
Ensure wok is smoking hot before adding ingredients.
Adjust chili count for heat preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Homestyle Chicken and Potato Biryani
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Homestyle Chicken and Potato Biryani served in a shallow, rustic ceramic bowl on a dark wooden table. The long-grain Basmati rice is fluffy and variegated with shades of white and turmeric-yellow. Interspersed within the rice are three large, golden-brown seared chicken thigh chunks and two soft, roasted potato wedges. Thin strands of dark caramelized onions are scattered across the top alongside fresh green cilantro leaves. The lighting is warm and directional, highlighting the steam rising from the dish. Beside the bowl sits a small stainless steel spoon and a tiny side dish of plain white yogurt. The arrangement is casual and organic, filling the bowl naturally.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of cooling cucumber raita
Include a fresh lime wedge for acidity
Pair with a simple onion and tomato salad
instructions: Rinse rice until water runs clear.
Soak rice in water for 20 minutes.
Boil 500ml salted water.
Add rice and cook for 5 minutes until par-boiled.
Drain rice and set aside.
Heat oil in a small pot over medium heat.
Fry potato wedges until golden and tender. Remove and set aside.
Fry sliced onions until dark brown and crispy. Remove half for garnish.
Add chicken chunks to the pot. Sear until browned on all sides.
Stir in ginger-garlic paste, turmeric, and garam masala for 1 minute.
Add yogurt and salt. Mix well.
Return potatoes to the pot.
Layer the par-boiled rice over the chicken and potato mixture.
Cover with a tight lid. Reduce heat to low.
Steam for 10 minutes.
Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Garnish with fried onions and cilantro.
notes: Long-grain Basmati rice provides the most authentic texture
Do not overcook the rice during the initial boiling stage

recipes.recipe_name: Korean Spicy Chicken and Potato Stew (Dakdoritang)
recipes.visual_description: The dish features large, rustic chunks of braised chicken and softened potato wedges coated in a vibrant, glossy red sauce. The chicken pieces are whole and succulent. The potatoes have rounded edges from simmering, absorbing the deep crimson hue of the gochugaru. Thick wedges of translucent onion are interspersed throughout the stew. The stew is presented in a traditional dark stoneware bowl on a light wood surface. A separate small white porcelain bowl contains a pristine mound of fluffy, steamed short-grain rice. Garnish with a diagonal sprinkle of bright green sliced scallions and toasted sesame seeds. Natural lighting highlights the rich sauce texture. A pair of stainless steel chopsticks sits beside the bowl on a linen napkin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with cabbage kimchi
Include various banchan side dishes
Use stainless steel chopsticks and a flat spoon
Present rice in an individual covered stainless steel bowl

ingredients.name: Chicken thighs, bone-in, cut into large chunks
Potatoes, peeled and cut into large wedges

instructions: Wash rice until water runs clear.
Cook rice with 450ml water until fluffy.
Mix gochugaru, gochujang, soy sauce, sugar, garlic, and ginger in a bowl.
Place chicken chunks in a heavy-bottomed pot.
Add water and the prepared sauce mixture.
Bring to a boil over high heat.
Skim any foam from the surface.
Reduce heat to medium.
Cover and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add potato chunks and onion wedges to the pot.
Simmer covered for 20 minutes until potatoes are tender.
Check chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Uncover and boil for 5 minutes to thicken sauce.
Stir in sesame oil.
Serve in deep bowls with rice on the side.
Garnish with scallions and sesame seeds.
notes: Use waxy potatoes to ensure they hold their shape during braising
Adjust gochugaru quantity to control the spice level
The sauce should be thick enough to coat the back of a spoon

recipes.recipe_name: Casarecce with Slow-Roasted Cherry Tomatoes and Ricotta Salata
recipes.visual_description: The dish features golden casarecce pasta twists coated in a light, glossy tomato emulsion. Deep red, wrinkled, slow-roasted cherry tomato halves are distributed throughout the pasta. Small, irregular crumbles of snow-white ricotta salata are scattered on top, providing a sharp textural contrast. Bright green, hand-torn basil leaves add vibrant color and freshness. The pasta is served in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The arrangement is natural and fluid, showing moderate height in the center. The setting is a dark wooden bistro table with a crisp white cotton napkin. A small ceramic side dish of extra cheese sits in the soft-focus background. Natural morning side-lighting highlights the textures of the roasted tomato skins and the ridges of the pasta twists.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty ciabatta bread
Pair with a crisp Falanghina or Vermentino wine
Follow with a simple arugula salad
instructions: Preheat oven to 150°C.
Halve the cherry tomatoes.
Toss tomatoes with 30ml olive oil, salt, and smashed garlic.
Spread tomatoes on a lined baking sheet.
Roast for 45 minutes until shriveled and concentrated.
Boil 4 liters of salted water.
Cook casarecce pasta until al dente.
Reserve 100ml of pasta cooking water.
Drain the pasta.
Heat remaining 30ml oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Add chili flakes and the roasted tomatoes.
Add pasta and reserved water to the pan.
Toss over high heat for 1 minute to emulsify the sauce.
Fold in torn basil leaves.
Plate immediately and top with crumbled ricotta salata.
notes: Ensure the pasta is al dente for the best texture
Do not over-roast the tomatoes to keep some moisture
Use high-quality extra virgin olive oil for the finish

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Parmesan with Spaghetti al Pomodoro
recipes.visual_description: A whole, golden-brown breaded chicken breast sits on a clean white porcelain plate. Beside the chicken, a neat nest of spaghetti is thoroughly coated in a vibrant, glossy red tomato sauce. The chicken is topped with a concentrated layer of sauce and a crown of melted, toasted parmesan cheese. Fresh, bright green basil leaves provide a colorful garnish against the warm tones of the dish. The lighting is natural and soft, emphasizing the crispy texture of the breading and the silkiness of the pasta. The arrangement is clean with visible negative space. A simple linen napkin and polished silver fork sit on a light wood surface.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty Italian bread
Offer extra grated parmesan and red chili flakes at the table
Pair with a glass of Chianti
instructions: Butterfly chicken breasts to even thickness. Season with salt.
Mix breadcrumbs with 50g grated parmesan.
Dredge chicken in flour. Dip in beaten eggs. Coat in breadcrumb mixture.
Sauté diced onion and minced garlic in olive oil until translucent.
Add crushed tomatoes. Simmer for 20 minutes. Stir in torn basil.
Boil spaghetti in salted water until al dente. Drain.
Heat oil in skillet. Fry chicken until golden brown and 75°C internally.
Top chicken with sauce and remaining parmesan. Broil until cheese melts.
Toss pasta with remaining tomato sauce.
Plate pasta in a nest. Place whole chicken breast alongside.
notes: Ensure the oil is hot before frying to prevent the breading from becoming greasy
Use high-quality San Marzano tomatoes for the best sauce flavor
Always check chicken temperature with a probe thermometer for safety

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo al Chilindrón
recipes.visual_description: Two whole roasted chicken thighs are presented in a traditional shallow terracotta cazuela. The chicken skin is deep golden-brown and crisp. The thighs rest in a thick, rustic chilindrón sauce containing finely diced onions and red bell peppers. Visible 1cm cubes of seared Serrano ham are scattered throughout the sauce. The sauce is a rich, glossy red from the olive oil and crushed tomatoes. Fresh chopped parsley is sprinkled over the dish. The cazuela sits on a dark wood table next to a small wicker basket containing thick chunks of crusty sourdough bread. A single glass of Spanish red wine and a simple white cotton napkin complete the authentic bistro setting under soft natural lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in a terracotta cazuela
Accompany with crusty white bread for dipping
Pair with a Tempranillo-based red wine
instructions: Dice the onions and red peppers into 1cm pieces.
Cut the Serrano ham into 1cm cubes.
Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden and crisp. Flip and sear for 3 minutes.
Remove chicken from the pan and set aside.
Add ham cubes to the same pan. Sauté for 2 minutes until fat renders. Remove and set aside.
Add onions and peppers to the pan. Sauté for 10 minutes until soft.
Add minced garlic and smoked paprika. Stir for 1 minute.
Pour in white wine. Scrape the bottom of the pan to deglaze.
Add crushed tomatoes and chicken stock. Stir to combine.
Return chicken and ham to the pan. Submerge the meat in the sauce.
Simmer uncovered for 25-30 minutes.
Cook chicken to internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) - minimum safe temperature.
Garnish with chopped fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Use high-quality Pimentón de la Vera for the most authentic smoky flavor.
Do not remove the chicken skin as it provides essential fat and texture to the sauce.
The sauce should be thick enough to coat a spoon.

recipes.recipe_name: Vietnamese Shaking Beef (Bò Lúc Lắc)
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Shaking Beef served on a clean white porcelain plate. The focal point features 2.5cm cubes of seared beef with a dark, caramelized crust. These are tossed with charred 2cm red onion wedges and vibrant orange 5cm carrot batons. The beef and vegetables are piled naturally in the center, showing a glossy glaze. To the side, a fresh bed of green watercress and thick tomato slices provides color contrast. A small ceramic ramekin containing a clear lime and cracked black pepper dipping sauce sits on the plate. The setting is a modern bistro with a light wood table, a pair of dark wood chopsticks, and a side bowl of steamed jasmine rice. Natural side-lighting highlights the textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of steamed jasmine rice or tomato rice
Provide a Muối Tiêu Chanh (salt, pepper, and lime) dipping sauce
Eat with chopsticks and a flat-bottomed soup spoon
instructions: Cut beef into 2.5cm cubes.
Mince garlic finely.
Mix beef with garlic, 15ml soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar, and 5g black pepper.
Marinate beef for 30 minutes at room temperature.
Peel carrots and cut into 5cm batons.
Cut red onion into 2cm wedges.
Whisk lime juice, fish sauce, and remaining black pepper in a small bowl for dipping.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat until smoking.
Add beef in a single layer. Sear for 2 minutes without moving.
Add onion wedges and carrot batons to the wok.
Shake the wok vigorously for 3 minutes to sear all sides.
Add butter and toss for 30 seconds to glaze.
Place watercress on a plate. Top with the hot beef and vegetables.
notes: Ensure the wok is extremely hot before adding meat to achieve a proper sear.
Do not overcrowd the pan; cook in batches if necessary to maintain heat.
The butter at the end provides the signature French-influenced Vietnamese glossy finish.

recipes.recipe_name: Paneer Lababdar
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Paneer Lababdar is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl on a dark wood table. The dish features 2cm cubes of soft, un-seared paneer nestled in a thick, vibrant orange-red gravy. The sauce is glossy and smooth, showing visible specks of crushed tomatoes. A light swirl of fresh white cream and a pinch of crushed green fenugreek leaves garnish the center. The entire plate is visible, maintaining balanced negative space. To the side, two pieces of folded, charred garlic naan rest on a small copper plate. A small ceramic bowl of green mint chutney and a lemon wedge accompany the meal. Natural light creates soft highlights on the gravy's surface.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with hot garlic naan or tandoori roti
Accompany with sliced red onions and lemon wedges
Pair with a side of mint and coriander chutney
instructions: Cut paneer into 2cm cubes.
Heat oil and butter in a heavy pan.
Add cardamom and cinnamon. Sauté 30 seconds.
Add onions. Sauté until golden brown.
Stir in ginger-garlic paste. Cook 2 minutes.
Add tomato puree. Cook until oil separates from the sides.
Stir in cashew paste and Kashmiri chili powder.
Add water and salt. Simmer 10 minutes on low heat.
Gently fold in paneer cubes.
Sprinkle garam masala and crushed fenugreek leaves.
Stir in heavy cream. Simmer 2 minutes.
Remove from heat immediately.
notes: Toast fenugreek leaves slightly before crushing for maximum aroma
Ensure the cashew paste is ground very smooth to achieve the signature velvety texture
Do not overcook paneer to prevent it from becoming rubbery

recipes.recipe_name: Orange and Sugar Cane Grilled Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A single white porcelain plate features three thick sugar cane batons, each threaded with large, charred chunks of chicken thigh. The chicken appears glossy with a deep amber orange glaze, showing visible bits of orange zest and minced red chili. The meat is presented as whole chunks, not sliced. The sugar cane ends are slightly toasted and golden-brown. Beside the skewers sits a neat mound of steamed jasmine rice and a side of quick-pickled carrot and daikon batons. A small ceramic dipping bowl containing clear amber sauce sits on the side. The scene is set on a dark wood table with a neutral linen napkin and bamboo chopsticks. Natural side lighting emphasizes the sticky, caramelized texture of the glaze.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Nuoc Cham dipping sauce
Accompany with Do Chua (pickled carrots and daikon)
Provide fresh herbs like mint and cilantro for wrapping
instructions: Peel the sugar cane stalks with a sharp knife.
Cut the cane into batons 12cm long and 1cm thick.
Cut the chicken thighs into 4cm chunks.
Combine orange juice, zest, fish sauce, honey, garlic, shallots, and chili in a bowl.
Marinate the chicken chunks in half of the orange mixture for 1 hour.
Simmer the remaining mixture in a small saucepan over medium heat.
Reduce the liquid until it becomes a thick, syrupy glaze.
Thread 3 to 4 chicken chunks onto each sugar cane baton.
Heat oil in a heavy grill pan over medium-high heat.
Place skewers in the pan and grill for 5 minutes per side.
Brush the chicken generously with the orange glaze during the final 4 minutes.
Cook chicken until it reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove skewers from the heat and rest for 2 minutes.
notes: If fresh sugar cane is unavailable, use canned sugar cane rinsed thoroughly.
Ensure the grill pan is very hot before adding skewers to achieve a char.

recipes.recipe_name: Mexican Entomatado de Res
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Entomatado de Res served in a shallow, matte white porcelain bowl. The dish features 3-4 large, tender 3cm chunks of seared beef nestled in a thick, vibrant red tomato sauce. The sauce is textured with softened chunks of diced tomato and translucent onions. A bright green garnish of fresh chopped cilantro and fine rings of raw white onion sits on top. The bowl is placed on a dark wood bistro table. Beside the bowl, three warm corn tortillas are folded neatly in a small cloth-lined basket. A small wedge of lime rests on the edge of the plate. Lighting is natural and soft, highlighting the glossy sheen of the rich, savory sauce.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas
Side of Mexican red rice
Accompanied by pickled red onions

ingredients.name: Beef chuck roast, cut into 3cm chunks

instructions: Season beef chunks with salt.
Heat oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat.
Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef.
Add onions to the pot. Sauté 5 minutes until translucent.
Add garlic. Cook 1 minute.
Blend half of the tomatoes with chipotle peppers until smooth.
Roughly chop the remaining tomatoes.
Return beef to the pot. Add blended sauce and chopped tomatoes.
Pour in beef stock. Add oregano.
Simmer covered on low heat for 90 minutes until beef is tender.
Remove lid. Simmer 15 minutes to thicken sauce.
Adjust salt. Garnish with cilantro.
notes: Ensure beef is well-seared to develop deep umami flavor
Use Mexican oregano for an authentic citrusy floral note
Do not over-blend the sauce if a rustic texture is preferred

recipes.recipe_name: Mushroom and Bell Pepper Risotto
recipes.visual_description: The risotto is presented on a clean white porcelain plate, flowing naturally across the surface with a fluid, 'all'onda' consistency. The hero ingredient, thick chunks of golden-brown seared cremini and oyster mushrooms, sits prominently throughout the rice. Vibrant 1cm squares of red bell pepper provide bright color contrast against the creamy, pale ivory rice. Finely diced translucent onions and minced garlic are integrated into the glossy sauce. Fresh green basil leaves are torn and scattered across the top. The dish is served in a modern bistro setting on a light oak table. A silver spoon rests on a folded white cotton napkin. Natural side lighting highlights the velvety texture and steam rising from the plate.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately while fluid
Pair with a crisp Italian white wine
Provide extra Parmigiano-Reggiano at the table
instructions: Keep vegetable stock at a low simmer in a small pot.
Clean and cut mushrooms into thick chunks.
Dice onion finely and cut bell peppers into 1cm squares.
Mince garlic cloves.
Heat 15ml oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat.
Sauté mushrooms until browned and moisture evaporates. Remove from pan.
Add remaining oil to the pan. Sauté onion and bell peppers for 5 minutes.
Stir in garlic for 1 minute.
Add rice. Toast for 2 minutes until edges are translucent.
Deglaze with white wine. Stir until liquid is fully absorbed.
Add one ladle of hot stock. Stir constantly until liquid is absorbed.
Repeat stock additions for 18 minutes until rice is al dente.
Fold sautéed mushrooms back into the rice.
Remove from heat. Vigorously stir in chilled butter and grated cheese.
Fold in torn basil leaves. Season with salt and black pepper.
notes: Do not rinse the rice before cooking to preserve starch
Ensure butter is cold for a better emulsion during mantecatura
Adjust stock amount as needed for a free-flowing consistency

recipes.recipe_name: Potato Leek Soup with Roasted Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of velvety, pale-ivory potato leek soup served in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The soup has a fluid, silky consistency. In the center, three golden-brown roasted chicken thigh chunks are nestled together, skin-side up to show a crispy, seared texture. Vibrant green chive oil droplets circle the chicken, interspersed with finely minced fresh chives. A small sprig of fresh thyme rests on one chicken piece. The bowl sits on a light oak bistro table next to a folded white linen napkin and a polished silver spoon. The lighting is soft and natural, highlighting the contrast between the smooth soup and the rustic, textured chicken skin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm crusty baguette
Pair with a chilled dry white wine
Offer a side of salted French butter

ingredients.name: Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and diced
Leeks, white and light green parts, sliced

instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden.
Transfer chicken to a baking dish.
Roast at 200°C until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Melt butter in a large pot over medium heat.
Add leeks and garlic.
Sweat until soft but not browned.
Add potatoes and chicken stock.
Simmer until potatoes are tender, about 20 minutes.
Blend soup until smooth.
Stir in heavy cream and thyme.
Season with salt and pepper.
Remove chicken skin and bones.
Keep chicken meat in large chunks.
Ladle soup into bowls.
Top with chicken chunks and minced chives.
notes: Wash leeks thoroughly to remove all grit before cooking
Use a high-speed blender for the smoothest possible texture
Do not allow the leeks to brown to maintain the pale color of the soup

recipes.recipe_name: Baghalee Polow with Lamb Shanks
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Baghalee Polow served on a clean white porcelain plate. The central focus is a mountain of fluffy, long-grain Basmati rice, heavily speckled with bright green halved fava beans and fine dark green dill flecks. A vibrant layer of golden saffron-stained rice crowns the peak. Nestled against the rice is one whole, tender braised lamb shank, its surface a rich, glistening mahogany. Three jagged, golden-brown shards of crispy tahdig rice lean against the side of the rice mound. The dish is presented in a modern bistro setting on a light oak table. A small side bowl of Maast-o-Khiar and a polished silver spoon accompany the plate. Lighting is natural and soft.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with Maast-o-Khiar (yogurt and cucumber dip)
Accompany with Salad Shirazi (diced tomato, cucumber, and onion)
Provide Torshi (pickled vegetables) on the side
Serve with fresh Sabzi Khordan (herb platter)

ingredients.name: saffron threads, ground and bloomed in water

instructions: Season lamb shanks with salt and pepper.
Heat 30 ml oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Sear lamb shanks until browned on all sides. Remove and set aside.
Add onions to the same pot. Sauté until translucent.
Stir in garlic, turmeric, and cinnamon stick. Cook 1 minute.
Return lamb to pot. Add 500 ml water. Cover and simmer 2 hours.
Ensure lamb reaches internal temperature of 75°C.
Bring a large pot of salted water to boil. Add rice.
Parboil rice for 6 minutes. Add fava beans in the last 2 minutes.
Drain rice and beans. Rinse with lukewarm water.
In a bowl, toss rice and beans with chopped dill.
Melt butter with remaining oil in a clean pot.
Layer the rice mixture into the pot in a pyramid shape.
Wrap pot lid in a clean kitchen towel. Cover tightly.
Steam on low heat for 45 minutes to create tahdig.
Mix a small portion of rice with bloomed saffron for garnish.
notes: Use high-quality long-grain basmati rice for the best texture.
Do not overcook the rice during parboiling; it must remain firm.
The kitchen towel on the lid absorbs steam to keep rice grains separate.

recipes.recipe_name: Mexican Beef with Charred Corn and Onions
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of seared beef chunks sits centered on a clean white porcelain plate. The beef is cut into 3cm cubes, showing a deep brown crust from high-heat searing. Beside the beef, a vibrant heap of charred yellow corn kernels provides a golden contrast, with visible blackened edges from the pan. Translucent, sautéed white onion strips and minced garlic are folded through the corn. The dish is garnished with fresh, bright green cilantro leaves. The plate rests on a dark wooden bistro table. A small stack of warm corn tortillas wrapped in a cloth napkin sits to the side. Natural light highlights the glistening textures of the meat and vegetables.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas in a cloth basket
Accompany with fresh salsa verde or pico de gallo
Provide lime wedges for additional seasoning at the table
instructions: Pat the beef chunks dry with paper towels.
Season beef with salt and black pepper.
Heat 15ml oil in a large skillet over high heat.
Sear beef chunks for 2 minutes per side until browned.
Remove beef from the pan and set aside.
Add remaining 15ml oil to the same skillet.
Add corn kernels to the pan.
Cook undisturbed for 3 minutes to char the corn.
Add sliced onion and minced garlic.
Sauté for 4 minutes until onions are translucent.
Stir in the ground cumin.
Return the beef to the skillet.
Toss everything together for 1 minute.
Remove from heat and stir in lime juice.
Garnish with fresh cilantro.
notes: Ensure the pan is very hot before adding corn to achieve a proper char.
Do not overcrowd the pan when searing beef to maintain high heat.

recipes.recipe_name: Risotto al Pomodoro with Burrata
recipes.visual_description: The risotto is presented on a wide, flat white porcelain plate. It exhibits a fluid, all'onda consistency, spreading naturally across the plate surface. The Carnaroli rice grains are distinct, coated in a glossy, vibrant red San Marzano tomato sauce. At the center, a thick chunk of creamy white burrata cheese sits prominently, its soft stracciatella interior gently exposed. Small, whole basil leaves are scattered around the cheese. Fine droplets of extra virgin olive oil create a shimmering finish on the surface. The arrangement is organic and centered. Natural side-lighting emphasizes the creamy texture and rich color. A single portion is shown with a silver fork and a white cotton napkin on a light wooden bistro table.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately while the rice is hot to contrast with the cold burrata
Pair with a crisp Italian white wine like Vermentino or Pinot Grigio
Provide extra virgin olive oil at the table for drizzling
instructions: Simmer vegetable stock in a pot.
Blend canned tomatoes until smooth.
Finely dice the onion and mince the garlic.
Sauté onion in olive oil over medium heat until translucent.
Add garlic. Cook for 1 minute.
Add rice. Toast for 2 minutes until edges are translucent.
Pour in white wine. Stir until fully evaporated.
Add blended tomatoes. Stir constantly.
Add stock one ladle at a time. Stir until absorbed before adding more.
Cook rice until al dente. This takes 16 to 18 minutes.
Remove from heat.
Add chilled butter and grated Parmigiano Reggiano.
Stir vigorously to create a creamy emulsion.
Season with salt and pepper.
Divide risotto into four plates.
Place a chunk of burrata in the center of each serving.
Garnish with fresh basil leaves.
notes: Ensure the butter is very cold for the best mantecatura emulsion
Do not let the rice become dry; it should flow when the plate is tilted
Use high-quality Carnaroli or Arborio rice for proper starch release

recipes.recipe_name: Thai Pineapple and Coconut Chicken
recipes.visual_description: Present the dish in a shallow celadon ceramic bowl. The primary focus is the braised chicken thighs, kept as thick, succulent 3cm chunks, and golden-seared pineapple wedges. The sauce is a rich, creamy orange-red coconut reduction. Arrange chicken and pineapple in a natural, mounded pile in the center. Garnish with bright green torn cilantro leaves and thin diagonal slices of red chili. The lighting is bright and natural, reflecting off the glossy sauce. Place the bowl on a dark wood table. Include a side of jasmine rice in a small separate white bowl and a pair of dark wood chopsticks and a flat-bottomed soup spoon. The plate shows ample negative space around the edges.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice in a separate bowl
Provide a traditional Thai condiment set (prik nam pla) on the side
Use a flat-bottomed ceramic soup spoon and fork or chopsticks
instructions: Whisk egg whites and cornstarch in a large bowl until smooth.
Cut chicken into 3cm chunks and toss in the egg white mixture.
Marinate chicken for 20 minutes.
Heat oil in a wok or large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks in batches until golden on all sides. Remove from pan.
Add red curry paste to the pan and fry for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in coconut milk and stir in brown sugar.
Return chicken to the pan and add pineapple wedges.
Simmer for 10 minutes until chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C.
Stir in fish sauce and lime juice.
Serve hot topped with cilantro and sliced chili.
notes: Velveting the chicken with egg whites ensures a silkier restaurant-quality texture.
Do not boil the coconut milk too vigorously to prevent the oil from separating excessively.
Ensure the pineapple is fresh for the best balance of acidity and sweetness.

recipes.recipe_name: Rigatoni with Slow-Roasted Tomatoes and Fresh Oregano
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of rigatoni is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The pasta tubes are thoroughly coated in a glossy, vibrant red tomato emulsion. Whole, slow-roasted cherry tomatoes are nestled between the pasta, showing slight caramelization and shriveled skins. Small, bright green fresh oregano leaves are scattered across the top. A light, airy dusting of finely grated Pecorino Romano adds a delicate white texture. The bowl sits on a natural light-oak bistro table. A crisp, folded white cotton napkin and a modern stainless steel fork are placed neatly to the left. Natural side-lighting emphasizes the sauce's sheen and the rustic texture of the roasted fruit.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in a shallow pasta bowl
Accompany with crusty sourdough bread
Pair with a light-bodied Italian red wine like Chianti
instructions: Preheat oven to 150°C.
Halve the cherry tomatoes.
Place tomatoes on a baking sheet.
Drizzle with 30ml olive oil and season with salt.
Roast tomatoes for 45 minutes until slightly shriveled.
Boil a large pot of salted water.
Cook rigatoni until al dente.
Sauté garlic and chili flakes in remaining oil over medium heat.
Add roasted tomatoes and their juices to the pan.
Reserve 150ml of pasta water.
Drain pasta and add to the tomato mixture.
Pour in reserved pasta water.
Toss vigorously to emulsify the sauce.
Stir in fresh oregano and Pecorino Romano.
Season with black pepper and serve immediately.
notes: Ensure the pasta water is heavily salted to season the rigatoni from within.
Do not overcook the garlic; it should be translucent and soft, not brown.

recipes.recipe_name: Lomo Saltado with Garlic Pea Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Lomo Saltado presented on a clean white porcelain plate. The dish features thick 3cm chunks of seared beef tossed with vibrant purple red onion wedges and golden-brown potato batons. The beef displays a dark, glossy glaze from the soy sauce and vinegar reduction. Beside the stir-fry sits a neat, flowing mound of fluffy white rice studded with bright green peas and bits of golden minced garlic. Fresh cilantro leaves are scattered over the meat chunks. The arrangement is natural and organized, showing moderate negative space on a dark wooden bistro table. Natural side lighting highlights the textures of the crispy potatoes and tender meat. A simple stainless steel fork and cotton napkin rest beside the plate.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Aji Verde (green chili sauce)
Traditional Inca Kola beverage on the side
Casual family-style dining setting
instructions: Rinse rice until water runs clear.
Sauté half the garlic in 15ml oil. Add rice, peas, 450ml water, and salt. Simmer until cooked.
Peel potatoes. Cut into 1cm by 5cm batons.
Fry potato batons in 180°C oil until golden and crisp. Drain on paper towels.
Cut beef into 3cm thick chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Slice onions into thick wedges.
Heat a wok until smoking. Add 30ml oil. Sear beef chunks in batches until browned. Remove.
Add onions to the wok. Stir-fry for 1 minute until slightly softened but crisp.
Add remaining garlic and aji amarillo paste. Stir 30 seconds.
Return beef to wok. Add soy sauce and vinegar. Toss quickly over high heat.
Fold in the fried potatoes and cilantro. Remove from heat immediately.
Serve the stir-fry next to the garlic pea rice.
notes: Ensure the wok is extremely hot to achieve the traditional smoky 'wok hei' flavor.
Do not overcook the onions; they should retain a structural crunch.
Add the fried potatoes at the very last second to prevent them from becoming soggy.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Beef with Swiss Chard and Asadero Cheese
recipes.visual_description: The dish features 800g of beef cut into 4cm chunks, seared to a deep mahogany crust. These rest on a bed of sautéed Swiss chard. The chard leaves are a vibrant emerald green, while the stems are sliced into 1cm batons for texture. A rich, glossy brown reduction of Worcestershire sauce and chicken stock coats the base. Melted white asadero cheese drapes over the beef in thick, creamy ribbons. The presentation uses a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl with moderate negative space. Freshly cracked black pepper and a sprig of cilantro garnish the top. The setting includes a dark wood table, a white cotton napkin, and a side of warm corn tortillas.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Warm corn tortillas
Fresh lime wedges
Salsa verde
instructions: Cut beef into 4 cm chunks.
Season beef with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a heavy skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear beef chunks for 2 minutes per side until browned.
Remove beef from skillet.
Sauté diced onion and minced garlic in the skillet for 3 minutes.
Add Worcestershire sauce and chicken stock to the pan.
Boil liquid until reduced by half.
Separate Swiss chard stems from leaves.
Slice stems into 1 cm pieces and leaves into wide ribbons.
Add stems and beef back to the skillet.
Stir in leaves until wilted.
Sprinkle grated asadero cheese over the beef.
Cover pan for 1 minute to melt cheese.
Serve immediately.
notes: Use a cast-iron skillet for the best sear on the beef chunks.
Ensure the chicken stock is unsalted to control the saltiness from the Worcestershire sauce.

recipes.recipe_name: Mexican Entomatado de Res
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Entomatado de Res served in a shallow, matte white porcelain bowl. The dish features 3-4 large, tender 3cm chunks of seared beef nestled in a thick, vibrant red tomato sauce. The sauce is textured with softened chunks of diced tomato and translucent onions. A bright green garnish of fresh chopped cilantro and fine rings of raw white onion sits on top. The bowl is placed on a dark wood bistro table. Beside the bowl, three warm corn tortillas are folded neatly in a small cloth-lined basket. A small wedge of lime rests on the edge of the plate. Lighting is natural and soft, highlighting the glossy sheen of the rich, savory sauce.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas
Side of Mexican red rice
Accompanied by pickled red onions

ingredients.name: Beef chuck roast, cut into 3cm chunks

instructions: Season beef chunks with salt.
Heat oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat.
Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef.
Add onions to the pot. Sauté 5 minutes until translucent.
Add garlic. Cook 1 minute.
Blend half of the tomatoes with chipotle peppers until smooth.
Roughly chop the remaining tomatoes.
Return beef to the pot. Add blended sauce and chopped tomatoes.
Pour in beef stock. Add oregano.
Simmer covered on low heat for 90 minutes until beef is tender.
Remove lid. Simmer 15 minutes to thicken sauce.
Adjust salt. Garnish with cilantro.
notes: Ensure beef is well-seared to develop deep umami flavor
Use Mexican oregano for an authentic citrusy floral note
Do not over-blend the sauce if a rustic texture is preferred

recipes.recipe_name: Sichuan-style Braised Butterfish with Winter Melon
recipes.visual_description: A single thick, whole seared butterfish fillet sits at the center of a shallow white porcelain bowl. The fish has a crisp, golden-brown skin. Surrounding the fish are 3cm cubes of winter melon, which appear translucent and tender. A glossy, deep-red Sichuan sauce coats the fish and melon, pooling slightly at the base. Finely sliced green scallion rings and fresh coriander leaves are scattered over the top. The arrangement is clean with visible negative space. The dish is set on a dark wood table next to a small bowl of steamed jasmine rice and a pair of dark wood chopsticks on a ceramic rest. Natural, soft lighting highlights the silkiness of the sauce.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice to balance the salt and heat
Accompany with a side of lightly blanched bok choy
Provide chopsticks and a flat-bottomed porcelain soup spoon
instructions: Pat butterfish fillets dry with paper towels.
Peel winter melon and remove seeds. Cut into 3cm cubes.
Finely chop coriander roots. Mince garlic and ginger.
Heat oil in a large wok over medium-high heat.
Sear butterfish fillets for 3 minutes per side until golden. Remove and set aside.
Add coriander roots, ginger, and garlic to the wok. Sauté for 1 minute.
Add chili bean paste. Stir-fry for 30 seconds until the oil turns red.
Add winter melon cubes. Stir to coat with the paste.
Deglaze with Shaoxing wine. Add soy sauce, sugar, and chicken stock.
Bring to a simmer. Cover and cook for 8 minutes until melon is translucent.
Return fish to the wok. Simmer uncovered for 3 minutes to finish cooking.
Transfer fish and melon to serving plates.
Mix cornstarch with 15ml water. Stir into the remaining sauce until thickened.
Pour sauce over the fish. Garnish with sliced scallions.
notes: Ensure the chili bean paste is fried in oil first to release its full aroma and color
Butterfish is high in oil; do not overcook to maintain its delicate texture
Substitute Black Cod if butterfish is unavailable

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Corn Pasta with Mushrooms and Peppers
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Creamy Chicken and Corn Pasta is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl on a light oak table. The rigatoni pasta is thoroughly coated in a glossy, ivory-colored cream sauce. Golden-brown, 3cm seared chicken chunks are scattered naturally throughout the dish, never sliced or fanned. Vibrant 1cm diced red bell peppers and bright yellow corn kernels offer a sharp color contrast against the earthy, quartered cremini mushrooms. The arrangement is organic and free-flowing, showing moderate negative space around the rim. A dusting of finely grated parmesan and fresh chopped parsley adds texture. The scene is illuminated by soft, natural light, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and a polished silver fork.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty garlic bread
Pair with a crisp Pinot Grigio
Provide extra grated parmesan at the table
instructions: Boil pasta in salted water until al dente.
Drain pasta and reserve 100ml of cooking water.
Season chicken chunks with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken until golden and internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.
Sauté onion and bell pepper in the same skillet for 4 minutes.
Add mushrooms and corn to the skillet.
Cook for 5 minutes until mushrooms are browned.
Lower heat and pour in heavy cream.
Simmer for 2 minutes then stir in parmesan cheese.
Add pasta, chicken, and reserved water to the skillet.
Toss until the sauce is glossy and coats the pasta evenly.
Garnish with fresh parsley and serve.
notes: Ensure the chicken reaches exactly 75°C to maintain juiciness while ensuring safety.
Use the reserved pasta water to adjust sauce consistency if it becomes too thick.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Seitan with Red Wine and Mushrooms
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of braised seitan served in a wide, white porcelain shallow bowl. The dish features four large, rustic chunks of seitan, deeply browned and coated in a glossy, dark burgundy red wine sauce. Thick rounds of carrots, halved cremini mushrooms, and whole pearl onions are arranged naturally around the seitan. The sauce has a rich, velvety texture that pools slightly at the base. A single fresh thyme sprig rests on the central seitan piece. The bowl sits on a dark oak bistro table next to a folded gray linen napkin and a small side plate with two thick hand-torn pieces of baguette. Natural side lighting highlights the textures of the braised protein and vegetables.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty baguette slices for dipping
Pair with a glass of dry Pinot Noir
Traditional side of buttery mashed potatoes
instructions: Pat seitan dry. Cut into 4cm chunks.
Heat oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Brown seitan chunks on all sides. Remove and set aside.
Add butter to the same pan. Halve mushrooms and peel pearl onions.
Sauté mushrooms, pearl onions, and thick carrot rounds for 5 minutes.
Stir in tomato paste and minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute.
Sprinkle flour over vegetables. Stir to coat thoroughly.
Pour in red wine. Scrape the pan bottom to release browned bits.
Add vegetable stock and thyme sprigs. Return seitan to the pan.
Simmer over medium-low heat for 25 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
notes: Ensure seitan is well-browned for maximum savory depth
Use a high-quality dry red wine like Burgundy or Bordeaux for the best sauce flavor

recipes.recipe_name: Ginger-Soy Chicken and Broccoli
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a clean, wide white porcelain bowl on a dark mahogany wood table. On one side, a neat mound of steamed jasmine rice shows individual, fluffy grains. Beside the rice, 3cm chunks of chicken are piled naturally, coated in a glossy, dark amber ginger-soy glaze. Vibrant green broccoli florets and translucent, slightly charred onion wedges are interspersed among the chicken. The chicken exhibits golden-brown sear marks. Fine julienne strips of ginger are visible across the surface. A pair of dark bamboo chopsticks and a white ceramic spoon rest on a folded white cotton napkin. The lighting is soft and natural, emphasizing the glossy texture of the sauce and the fresh greens.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of chili oil or soy-marinated bird's eye chilies
Accompany with a small dish of pickled daikon radish
Provide a pot of hot jasmine or oolong tea
instructions: Rinse jasmine rice until water runs clear.
Combine rice and 450ml water in a pot. Bring to a boil.
Cover and reduce heat to low. Simmer for 15 minutes.
Toss chicken chunks with 5g cornstarch and 5ml soy sauce in a bowl.
Blanch broccoli florets in boiling water for 2 minutes. Drain and set aside.
Whisk remaining soy sauce, oyster sauce, and cornstarch with 50ml water.
Heat 30ml vegetable oil in a wok over high heat.
Add chicken chunks. Sear until golden and internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from wok. Wipe wok clean.
Heat remaining 15ml oil. Add onion wedges, ginger, and garlic. Stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Return chicken and broccoli to the wok.
Pour in the sauce mixture. Toss constantly until sauce thickens and coats ingredients.
Drizzle with sesame oil and serve immediately over the steamed rice.
notes: Ensure the wok is very hot before adding chicken to achieve wok hei flavor
Do not overcook broccoli during the blanching stage to maintain a crisp texture
Internal temperature of chicken must be verified with a probe thermometer

recipes.recipe_name: Sweet Cashew Mousse with Candied Chicken and Fermented Garlic
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy, pale ivory cashew mousse is centered on a handcrafted, matte-finished sand-colored ceramic plate. The mousse is presented as a smooth, rounded mound. Drizzled over the top is a dark, viscous fermented garlic honey syrup, creating deep amber streaks. Scattered across the surface are small, golden-brown shards of rendered chicken skin and fine fibers of candied chicken breast, adding complex textural contrast. Toasted whole cashews are nestled into the side. A few delicate sprigs of micro-cilantro provide a touch of green. The lighting is soft and natural, coming from the side to highlight the velvety texture of the mousse. The entire plate is visible, surrounded by a minimalist setting of raw linen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small cup of warm ginger tea to cleanse the palate.
Present on traditional celadon or handcrafted stoneware pottery.
Accompany with a side of lightly pickled green mango to balance the sweetness.
instructions: Soak raw cashews in filtered water for 4 hours then drain.
Poach chicken breast in simmering water until the internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Shred the cooked chicken breast into very fine fibers using two forks.
Sauté shredded chicken in a pan with 20g of palm sugar until caramelized and crisp.
Render the chicken skin in a dry pan over low heat until golden and crunchy.
Crumble the crispy skin into small bits.
Blend the soaked cashews, coconut cream, black garlic, and remaining palm sugar until completely smooth.
Chill the cashew mousse in the refrigerator for 1 hour.
Place a large dollop of mousse in the center of a plate.
Top with the candied chicken fibers and crumbled skin.
notes: Ensure chicken breast reaches exactly 75°C to maintain safety and texture.
Use the chicken poaching liquid as a base for a savory broth to ensure zero waste.
Stone grinding the cashews provides a more authentic, dense texture if a high-speed blender is unavailable.

recipes.recipe_name: Beer-Braised Corn and Roasted Tomato Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A wide, shallow white porcelain bowl presents a fluid, creamy risotto that spreads naturally. The Arborio rice grains are glossy and distinct. Scattered throughout are bright yellow, whole corn kernels and blistered, deep-red cherry tomatoes. The tomatoes are roasted whole until skins are slightly charred and split. The dish is topped with a fine cloud of grated parmesan cheese and a light dusting of red cayenne pepper. Three small, vibrant green basil leaves are placed near the center. The risotto is served on a light-colored wooden table with a silver spoon. The background features a clean, modern bistro setting with soft, natural side-lighting emphasizing the creamy texture and organic arrangement of the vegetables.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in wide, shallow bowls to allow the risotto to flow freely across the surface.
Pair with the same chilled lager used during the cooking process.
Provide extra aged parmesan and a small dish of chili flakes for individual seasoning.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Toss cherry tomatoes with olive oil and cayenne pepper on a baking tray.
Roast tomatoes for 15 minutes until skins blister and char slightly.
Heat vegetable stock in a medium pot and maintain a low simmer.
Melt 30g butter in a large heavy-bottomed pan over medium heat.
Sauté finely diced onion and minced garlic until translucent.
Add Arborio rice to the pan.
Toast rice grains for 2 minutes until edges are translucent.
Pour in the beer and stir until the liquid is fully absorbed.
Add warm stock one ladle at a time while stirring continuously.
Ensure each ladle of stock is absorbed before adding the next.
Fold in the corn kernels and roasted tomatoes after 10 minutes of cooking.
Continue adding stock until rice is tender but retains a firm bite.
Remove pan from heat.
Stir in grated parmesan and the remaining 20g butter vigorously.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve immediately in warm bowls.
notes: Use a light lager rather than an IPA to prevent excessive bitterness in the finished dish.
Keep the vegetable stock hot to ensure the rice cooks evenly without dropping in temperature.
Stir the rice vigorously during the mantecatura stage to create the characteristic creamy emulsion.

recipes.recipe_name: Herb-Crusted Chicken with Roasted Potatoes and Garlic Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single whole roasted chicken breast occupies the center of a clean white porcelain plate. The chicken features a thick, golden-brown crust of toasted breadcrumbs and herbs. To the left, a cluster of small roasted potato cubes shows caramelized edges and rosemary sprigs. On the right, a neat nest of glistening spaghetti is tossed with translucent garlic bits and bright green parsley. A thick, grilled sourdough bread wedge rests at the top edge. The plating is organized with moderate negative space on a light oak bistro table. Natural side-lighting highlights the textures of the crispy crust and the smooth pasta. A white cotton napkin and polished silver fork sit beside the plate.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of simple arugula salad with lemon vinaigrette
Provide a small bowl of extra grated Parmesan for the pasta
Accompany with a crisp Italian white wine like Pinot Grigio
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Toss potato cubes with 20ml olive oil, rosemary, salt, and pepper.
Spread potatoes on a baking sheet. Roast for 25 minutes until golden.
Mix breadcrumbs, parmesan, lemon zest, and 1 tbsp parsley in a bowl.
Season chicken breasts with salt and pepper.
Sear chicken in a hot pan with oil for 3 minutes per side.
Press the breadcrumb mixture onto the top of each chicken breast.
Transfer chicken to the oven. Roast until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Boil pasta in salted water until al dente. Drain and reserve 50ml water.
Sauté minced garlic in remaining olive oil until fragrant.
Toss pasta with garlic oil, reserved water, and remaining parsley.
Toast sourdough bread until crisp.
Plate the whole chicken breast alongside the potatoes and a nest of pasta.
notes: Ensure the breadcrumbs are pressed firmly onto the chicken to prevent shedding.
Use high-quality olive oil for the pasta to maximize flavor.
Do not overcook the garlic or it will become bitter.

recipes.recipe_name: Pappardelle with Wild Mushrooms, Asparagus, and Herbed Ricotta
recipes.visual_description: A wide white porcelain bowl features a swirling mound of wide, golden pappardelle ribbons coated in a glossy, light-reflecting sauce. Nestled within the pasta folds are thick, meaty chunks of seared brown mushrooms and vibrant green asparagus batons. Three large, rustic dollops of snowy white ricotta are positioned on top, garnished with bright green parsley and fine yellow lemon zest. The dish is finished with a delicate dusting of grated Parmigiano-Reggiano. The bowl sits on a dark walnut table next to a folded cream linen napkin and a polished silver fork. Natural daylight from a nearby window illuminates the textures of the pasta and the creamy cheese.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty ciabatta bread
Pair with a crisp white wine such as Pinot Grigio

ingredients.name: Mixed mushrooms (Cremini and Oyster), cut into thick chunks
Asparagus, woody ends removed, cut into 4cm batons

instructions: Boil 4 liters of heavily salted water.
Whisk ricotta with lemon zest, half the parsley, salt, and pepper in a small bowl.
Heat olive oil and butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add mushroom chunks in a single layer. Sear until deep brown.
Add garlic and asparagus batons. Sauté 3 minutes until asparagus is tender-crisp.
Cook pappardelle in boiling water until al dente.
Reserve 120ml of pasta water. Drain pasta.
Transfer pasta and reserved water to the skillet.
Toss pasta vigorously over low heat to emulsify the sauce.
Stir in lemon juice and remaining parsley. Season with salt and pepper.
Plate pasta immediately. Top with dollops of herbed ricotta and Parmigiano-Reggiano.
notes: Do not crowd the mushrooms in the pan to ensure proper browning.
Use high-quality whole milk ricotta for the best creamy texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Hainanese Chicken Rice
recipes.visual_description: The dish features large, succulent chunks of bone-in poached chicken with glossy, pale skin. The chicken rests on a bed of fragrant, light-yellow Jasmine rice infused with ginger and pandan. Slices of fresh, cool cucumber are arranged neatly to the side. The chicken is lightly drizzled with a mixture of soy sauce and sesame oil. Three small ceramic dipping bowls contain bright red chili sauce, dark soy sauce, and a vibrant green ginger-scallion oil. The meal is served on a clean white porcelain plate on a light wood table. A pair of dark wood chopsticks and a traditional ceramic soup spoon sit to the right. Natural light highlights the moist texture of the meat and the individual grains of rice.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side bowl of hot chicken broth
Include chili sauce, ginger-garlic sauce, and dark soy sauce
Serve at room temperature as per tradition
instructions: Rub chicken with salt to remove impurities.
Rinse chicken under cold water.
Boil 3 liters of water with 30g crushed ginger and scallions.
Submerge chicken in boiling water.
Simmer for 20 minutes.
Turn off heat and cover pot.
Steep chicken for 30 minutes.
Confirm internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Submerge chicken in ice water for 5 minutes.
Drain chicken and rub skin with sesame oil.
Sauté 20g minced ginger and minced garlic in chicken fat.
Add rice and toast for 2 minutes.
Add 600ml poaching liquid and pandan leaves.
Cook rice until liquid is absorbed.
Cut chicken into large chunks.
notes: Save the remaining poaching liquid for a light soup
Rubbing the chicken with salt ensures a smooth skin texture
Using rendered chicken fat for the rice is essential for authenticity

recipes.recipe_name: Lomo Saltado
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Lomo Saltado presented on a clean white porcelain plate. The dish features 3cm chunks of seared beef sirloin with a deep brown crust. These are mixed with thick, glossy wedges of purple red onion and bright red Roma tomatoes. Golden, thick-cut potato batons are scattered through the beef mixture, all coated in a dark, shimmering sauce. A neat, molded dome of fluffy white rice sits on the side of the plate. Fresh green cilantro leaves garnish the top. The scene is set on a light wooden bistro table with a white cotton napkin and a small side bowl of spicy green aji sauce. The lighting is natural and even.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Aji Verde (green chili sauce)
Accompany with Inca Kola or a glass of red wine
Traditionally eaten with both rice and potatoes in the same meal

ingredients.name: Red onions, cut into thick wedges
Roma tomatoes, cut into thick wedges

instructions: Season beef chunks with salt and pepper.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a wok over high heat until smoking.
Sear beef in batches until browned and medium-rare.
Remove beef from wok and set aside.
Add remaining oil to the wok.
Stir-fry onion wedges for 2 minutes until slightly charred but crisp.
Add garlic and aji amarillo paste. Stir for 30 seconds.
Return beef to the wok.
Pour in soy sauce and red wine vinegar. Toss quickly.
Add tomato wedges. Stir for 30 seconds to warm through.
Fold in the cooked potato fries and half the cilantro.
Remove from heat immediately.
Serve with white rice.
notes: Ensure the wok is extremely hot before adding beef to achieve a smoky flavor.
Do not overcook the tomatoes; they should be warm but hold their shape.
The potatoes should be added at the very last second to maintain some crispness.

recipes.recipe_name: Thai Chili Chicken Stir-fry (Gai Pad Prik)
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Gai Pad Prik served on a clean white porcelain plate. The dish features 3cm chunks of golden-brown seared chicken thigh tossed with vibrant red bird's eye chilies and translucent, charred onion wedges. The chicken is glossy with a dark savory sauce. Beside the stir-fry sits a neat mound of fluffy steamed jasmine rice. Garnish with fresh cilantro sprigs and a lime wedge. The plate sits on a dark wood table with a small ceramic bowl of prik nam pla and traditional Thai flatware. Natural side lighting highlights the textures of the seared meat and the steam from the rice. Clean composition with balanced negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with Prik Nam Pla (fish sauce with sliced chilies).
Eat using a large spoon in the right hand and a fork in the left hand.
Serve with a side of fresh cucumber slices to cool the palate.
instructions: Rinse jasmine rice until water runs clear.
Combine rice and 360ml water in a pot.
Bring to boil, reduce heat, and simmer covered for 15 minutes.
Cut chicken into 3cm chunks.
Mince garlic finely.
Slice chilies into thin rounds.
Cut onion into 2cm wedges.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat until smoking.
Add garlic and chilies to the wok.
Stir-fry 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add chicken chunks to the wok.
Sear chicken until golden brown on all sides.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Add onion wedges.
Stir-fry for 2 minutes until onions soften slightly.
Add fish sauce, oyster sauce, and sugar.
Toss rapidly for 1 minute to coat ingredients.
Serve stir-fry immediately with steamed rice.
notes: Use jasmine rice for authentic floral aroma.
Adjust chili count for preferred heat level.
Ensure the wok is smoking hot before adding ingredients to achieve wok hei.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Corn Pasta with Mushrooms and Peppers
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Creamy Chicken and Corn Pasta is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl on a light oak table. The rigatoni pasta is thoroughly coated in a glossy, ivory-colored cream sauce. Golden-brown, 3cm seared chicken chunks are scattered naturally throughout the dish, never sliced or fanned. Vibrant 1cm diced red bell peppers and bright yellow corn kernels offer a sharp color contrast against the earthy, quartered cremini mushrooms. The arrangement is organic and free-flowing, showing moderate negative space around the rim. A dusting of finely grated parmesan and fresh chopped parsley adds texture. The scene is illuminated by soft, natural light, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and a polished silver fork.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty garlic bread
Pair with a crisp Pinot Grigio
Provide extra grated parmesan at the table
instructions: Boil pasta in salted water until al dente.
Drain pasta and reserve 100ml of cooking water.
Season chicken chunks with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken until golden and internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.
Sauté onion and bell pepper in the same skillet for 4 minutes.
Add mushrooms and corn to the skillet.
Cook for 5 minutes until mushrooms are browned.
Lower heat and pour in heavy cream.
Simmer for 2 minutes then stir in parmesan cheese.
Add pasta, chicken, and reserved water to the skillet.
Toss until the sauce is glossy and coats the pasta evenly.
Garnish with fresh parsley and serve.
notes: Ensure the chicken reaches exactly 75°C to maintain juiciness while ensuring safety.
Use the reserved pasta water to adjust sauce consistency if it becomes too thick.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Broccoli Stir-Fry
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chicken and Broccoli Stir-Fry served in a wide, shallow ceramic bowl. The base is a bed of fluffy, steamed white Jasmine rice. On top, glossy 2cm chunks of golden-seared chicken are tossed with vibrant green, tender-crisp broccoli florets. The savory brown sauce coats every piece, creating a reflective, appetizing sheen. The chicken is presented as whole chunks, never sliced or fanned. The arrangement is natural and slightly asymmetrical. Beside the bowl sits a pair of dark wooden chopsticks and a small dish of pickled radish. The setting is a rustic wooden kitchen table with soft, warm overhead lighting. A simple linen napkin rests nearby to create a lived-in atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of chili oil
Accompany with hot jasmine tea
Provide a small dish of pickled ginger or radish
instructions: Rinse rice until water runs clear.
Boil rice in 600ml water. Cover and simmer 15 minutes.
Toss chicken chunks with cornstarch and 15ml soy sauce.
Blanch broccoli florets in boiling water for 2 minutes. Drain.
Heat vegetable oil in a wok over high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Add ginger and garlic. Stir for 30 seconds.
Add broccoli, remaining soy sauce, oyster sauce, and water.
Stir-fry 2 minutes until sauce thickens and coats ingredients.
Drizzle with sesame oil and remove from heat.
Serve immediately over the steamed rice.
notes: Ensure the wok is smoking hot for the best flavor
Do not crowd the pan to maintain the sear on the chicken
Use high-quality oyster sauce for a deeper umami profile

recipes.recipe_name: Rigatoni with Tomato and Fresh Oregano
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of rigatoni served in a wide, shallow white porcelain pasta bowl. The large tubes of pasta are thoroughly coated in a vibrant, glossy tomato sauce. The sauce shows visible bits of hand-crushed tomato pulp and golden garlic slices. Bright green, whole fresh oregano leaves are scattered naturally across the top. Fine shavings of Parmigiano-Reggiano are dusted lightly over the center. The bowl sits on a dark walnut wood table next to a folded white cotton napkin. A polished silver fork rests to the right. The lighting is soft and natural, coming from the side to highlight the texture of the pasta and the sheen of the emulsified sauce. The background is a blurred, warm bistro interior.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm ciabatta bread to soak up the sauce
Pair with a medium-bodied Italian red wine
Present in a shared family-style bowl if preferred
instructions: Bring 5 liters of water to a boil.
Add 10 grams of salt to the water.
Cook rigatoni until 2 minutes before al dente.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Sauté sliced garlic for 1 minute until fragrant.
Crush canned tomatoes by hand into the pan.
Add dried oregano and black pepper.
Simmer sauce for 15 minutes on low heat.
Reserve 120 ml of pasta cooking water.
Drain pasta and add to the sauce.
Add reserved water and half the fresh oregano.
Toss vigorously for 2 minutes to emulsify.
Remove from heat.
Stir in Parmigiano-Reggiano and remaining olive oil.
Garnish with remaining fresh oregano leaves.
notes: Use bronze-die pasta for better sauce adhesion
Ensure the sauce remains fluid before adding cheese
Fresh oregano is more floral than dried; do not skip it

recipes.recipe_name: Gruyère Gougères with Herbed Cheese Mousse
recipes.visual_description: Twelve golden-brown Gruyère gougères are arranged on a rectangular white porcelain platter. The puffs feature a crisp, craggy exterior with visible melted cheese shards on top. Each pastry is a uniform four-centimeter sphere. The puffs are spaced evenly in two rows of six. A subtle hint of the white herbed mousse is visible at the base of each puff. The platter sits on a light oak bistro table next to a folded white cotton napkin. Natural morning light creates soft shadows, highlighting the airy texture of the choux. The composition is clean, centered, and professional, emphasizing the contrast between the warm pastry and fresh herb filling.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as an apéritif
Pair with chilled white wine
Present on a silver tray
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Combine water, butter, and salt in a saucepan.
Bring to a boil.
Add flour all at once.
Stir vigorously until dough forms a ball.
Cook 2 minutes to dry dough.
Transfer to a bowl and cool 5 minutes.
Beat in eggs one at a time until smooth.
Fold in 75g of grated Gruyère.
Pipe 12 mounds onto a lined baking sheet.
Top with remaining cheese.
Bake 22 minutes until golden and puffed.
Whisk yogurt, mayonnaise, goat cheese, chives, and pepper.
Pierce bottom of cooled puffs.
Pipe filling into each puff.
notes: Ensure eggs are at room temperature
Do not open oven door during the first 15 minutes of baking

recipes.recipe_name: Garlic Roasted Portobello Mushrooms with Bacon and Fresh Cheese
recipes.visual_description: A single, large roasted Portobello mushroom cap sits centered on a clean white porcelain plate. The mushroom is thick and dark, topped with a bubbling, golden-brown crust of melted Gruyère and creamy goat cheese. Visible 1cm chunks of crispy, browned bacon are embedded within the cheese filling. Finely sliced green spring onion rounds and fresh thyme leaves are scattered across the top for color. A light drizzle of garlic-infused oil circles the base of the mushroom. The entire plate is visible, set on a dark oak bistro table with a folded white linen napkin and silver flatware. Natural side-lighting highlights the textures of the roasted fungi and the creamy, toasted cheese.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm crusty baguette slices
Pair with a glass of crisp Chablis or Sauvignon Blanc
Accompany with a simple dressed green salad
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wipe mushrooms clean with a damp cloth.
Remove stems and dice them finely.
Slice bacon into 1cm chunks.
Sauté bacon in a pan until crisp.
Add diced mushroom stems and minced garlic to the pan.
Cook for 3 minutes until softened.
Stir in half of the thyme and half of the sliced spring onions.
Remove from heat and cool for 5 minutes.
Combine goat cheese and grated Gruyère in a bowl.
Fold the bacon mixture into the cheese blend.
Brush mushroom caps with olive oil.
Season caps with salt and pepper.
Fill each cap generously with the cheese and bacon mixture.
Place mushrooms on a lined baking tray.
Roast for 15-18 minutes until the cheese is golden and bubbling.
Garnish with remaining spring onions and thyme.
notes: Do not wash mushrooms under water to avoid a soggy texture.
Use high-quality thick-cut bacon for better textural contrast.
Ensure the goat cheese is at room temperature for easier mixing.

recipes.recipe_name: Kung Pao Chicken
recipes.visual_description: The dish features 2cm cubes of seared chicken thigh coated in a glossy, dark mahogany sauce. The chicken cubes are clustered naturally in the center of a shallow white porcelain bowl, showing visible caramelized edges from the wok. Bright green 2cm scallion batons and whole roasted golden peanuts are interspersed throughout the chicken. Vibrant red dried chili halves and small Sichuan peppercorns provide color contrast against the dark glaze. The arrangement is organic and clean with moderate negative space around the rim. The lighting is natural and even, highlighting the reflective sheen of the sauce. A pair of dark wood chopsticks rests on a ceramic holder beside the bowl on a light wood table.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice
Provide dark wood chopsticks and a ceramic spoon
Accompany with a side of lightly pickled cucumbers

ingredients.name: boneless chicken thighs, cut into 2cm cubes
dried Sichuan chilies, deseeded and halved

instructions: Mix chicken cubes with 15ml soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, and cornstarch. Marinate for 20 minutes.
Whisk remaining soy sauce, black vinegar, sugar, and sesame oil in a small bowl to create the sauce.
Heat vegetable oil in a wok over high heat until smoking.
Add chicken cubes in a single layer. Sear without moving for 2 minutes to develop a crust.
Stir-fry chicken until the internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from wok.
Reduce heat to medium. Add dried chilies and Sichuan peppercorns to the remaining oil. Fry until fragrant and dark red.
Add garlic, ginger, and scallion batons. Stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Return chicken to the wok. Pour in the prepared sauce.
Toss rapidly over high heat until the sauce thickens and coats the chicken cubes evenly.
Stir in roasted peanuts and serve immediately.
notes: Ensure the wok is extremely hot before adding chicken to achieve wok hei flavor.
Deseed chilies to control heat levels while maintaining aroma.
Add peanuts at the very end to preserve their crunchy texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Chicken Bhuna
recipes.visual_description: The dish features thick 4cm chunks of succulent chicken coated in a concentrated, dark reddish-brown onion gravy. The chicken is presented as whole pieces, never sliced, piled naturally in the center of a clean white porcelain plate. Visible flecks of caramelized onion and whole roasted dried chilies add texture. Bright green, coarsely chopped fresh coriander leaves are scattered over the top. The plate sits on a light oak bistro table next to a small bowl of fluffy white basmati rice and a single, charred piece of folded naan bread. The lighting is soft and natural, highlighting the glossy sauce and the rustic textures of the spices.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed basmati rice
Accompany with warm garlic naan
Provide a side of cucumber raita to balance heat
instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium heat.
Add whole dried red chilies and fry for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add sliced onions to the pan.
Sauté onions for 15 minutes until deep golden brown.
Stir in minced garlic and cook for 2 minutes.
Add chicken chunks and sear until browned on all sides.
Stir in cayenne pepper, ground coriander, and salt.
Fry spices with the meat for 5 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in water and bring to a simmer.
