The color of the stew deepens the longer it simmers.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Filipino Chicken Adobo
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Filipino Chicken Adobo served on a clean white porcelain plate. Two whole bone-in chicken thighs are the centerpiece, featuring a deep mahogany, glossy glaze from the reduced soy-vinegar sauce. The chicken skin is slightly caramelized and tacky. Beside the chicken sits a neat mound of fluffy, white long-grain steamed rice. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of bright green sliced scallions and golden-brown crispy fried garlic bits. A small bowl of extra adobo sauce and a side of pickled papaya (atchara) sit nearby. The setting is a modern bistro with a dark wood table, a neutral cotton napkin, and a traditional spoon and fork set.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm jasmine rice
Pair with a side of Atchara (pickled papaya)
Traditional spoon and fork dining utensils
instructions: Pat chicken dry with paper towels.
Heat oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden brown. Flip and sear other side.
Remove chicken and set aside.
Sauté smashed garlic in the same pan until fragrant.
Add soy sauce, vinegar, water, peppercorns, sugar, and bay leaves.
Return chicken to the pan.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low.
Simmer covered for 30 minutes.
Remove lid and increase heat to medium-high.
Reduce sauce until thickened and glossy, coating the chicken.
Ensure chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Garnish with scallions and fried garlic.
notes: Do not stir the vinegar immediately after adding it; let it boil off the raw acidity first.
Use cane vinegar for the most authentic flavor profile.
Bone-in thighs provide the best moisture and flavor for this long simmer.

recipes.recipe_name: Ragù alla Napoletana with Ziti
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Ragù alla Napoletana served on a wide, white porcelain plate. The hand-broken ziti pasta is coated in a thick, glossy, deep mahogany-red tomato sauce. One large, tender chunk of seared beef and one whole, succulent pork rib sit prominently atop the pasta. The meat is unsliced and shows a rich, caramelized exterior. A single sprig of vibrant green basil is placed off-center. The plate rests on a dark walnut wood table in a modern bistro setting. A white cotton napkin and a glass of red wine sit nearby. Natural side lighting highlights the sauce's texture and the rustic, irregular shapes of the pasta.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of Aglianico or Taurasi red wine
Present with crusty pane di cafone to scoop the remaining sauce
Traditionally served as a single course where pasta and meat are eaten together in casual settings
instructions: Cut beef into 5cm chunks.
Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear beef chunks and pork ribs until deeply browned on all sides.
Remove meat and set aside.
Thinly slice onions and add to the same pot.
Cook onions on low heat for 15 minutes until soft.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in red wine to deglaze the pot.
Simmer until wine reduces by half.
Stir in tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes.
Crush canned tomatoes by hand and add to the pot.
Return meat to the sauce.
Simmer on the lowest heat setting for 5 hours.
Season with salt and pepper.
Break ziti pasta into 5cm pieces by hand.
Boil ziti in salted water until al dente.
Drain pasta and toss with a portion of the red sauce.
Internal meat temperature must reach 75°C.
notes: The secret is the 'pappuliando' technique, where the sauce barely bubbles for several hours.
Do not blend the sauce; the onions should melt into the tomatoes naturally.
Hand-breaking the ziti is a traditional Neapolitan ritual for this specific dish.

recipes.recipe_name: Dakdoritang (Korean Spicy Chicken Stew)
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Dakdoritang served in a shallow, dark matte ceramic bowl. The dish features three large, whole bone-in chicken thighs coated in a glossy, vibrant deep-red sauce. Beside the chicken are three large, rounded 4 cm chunks of potato, slightly softened at the edges, and thick wedges of translucent onion. The thick sauce pools at the bottom of the bowl. Garnish with a generous pinch of toasted sesame seeds and diagonal slices of bright green onion. The bowl sits on a light oak wood table. Next to it are polished stainless steel chopsticks and a flat spoon on a rest. A small white porcelain bowl of steamed white rice and a tiny dish of red cabbage kimchi are placed in the background. Natural window light highlights the sauce texture.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a bowl of steamed short-grain white rice
Accompany with traditional banchan side dishes like kimchi
Use stainless steel chopsticks and a long-handled spoon
Enjoy the sauce by mixing it directly into the rice
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into large, uniform pieces.
Peel potatoes and cut into 4 cm chunks.
Cut onions into 3 cm thick wedges.
Whisk gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce, sugar, garlic, and ginger in a small bowl.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken pieces until skin is golden brown.
Add potatoes and onions to the pot.
Pour the sauce mixture over the ingredients.
Add water and stir to combine.
Bring the liquid to a boil.
Reduce heat to medium and simmer for 25 minutes.
Increase heat to high and boil for 7 minutes to thicken the sauce.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Turn off heat and stir in sesame oil.
Garnish with green onions and sesame seeds.
notes: Round the edges of the potato chunks with a peeler to prevent them from breaking in the stew
Use bone-in chicken for a deeper flavor and juicier texture
Adjust the amount of gochugaru to control the spice level

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Mushroom Ragù with Potato Gnocchi
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of handmade potato gnocchi served in a shallow white porcelain bowl. The gnocchi are small, pillowy 2cm dumplings with soft ridges. They are coated in a glossy, light-brown savory sauce. The ragù features 2cm succulent chunks of seared chicken and quartered caramelized cremini mushrooms. Tiny orange specks of finely diced carrots are visible throughout the sauce. The dish is topped with a snowy dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese and a few fresh thyme leaves. The bowl sits on a dark oak wood table with a folded grey linen napkin and a polished silver fork. Natural side-lighting emphasizes the soft texture of the gnocchi and the sheen of the ragù.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a 'Primi Piatti' or a substantial main course.
Pair with a crisp Italian white wine like Gavi or Soave.
Accompany with crusty ciabatta bread to soak up the ragù.

ingredients.name: Chicken thighs, boneless and skinless, 2cm chunks

instructions: Boil potatoes in salted water until soft. Drain and mash while hot.
Spread mashed potatoes on a tray to cool slightly.
Mix potatoes with flour, egg, and a pinch of salt. Knead into a soft dough.
Roll dough into long ropes. Cut into 2cm batons.
Heat oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until golden. Remove from pan.
Sauté onion, carrot, and mushrooms in the same pan for 5 minutes.
Return chicken to the pan. Add chicken stock and thyme.
Simmer for 15 minutes until chicken reaches 75°C and sauce reduces.
Boil gnocchi in salted water until they float. Drain.
Toss gnocchi into the ragù. Stir in half of the parmesan.
Serve immediately topped with remaining parmesan.
notes: Ensure potatoes are dry before adding flour to prevent gummy gnocchi.
Do not overwork the gnocchi dough; mix just until combined.
Use a thermometer to ensure chicken chunks reach exactly 75°C.

recipes.recipe_name: Boeuf Bourguignon
recipes.visual_description: A deep white porcelain bowl holds a generous serving of Boeuf Bourguignon. The focal point is several 5cm chunks of braised beef coated in a glossy, dark mahogany red wine sauce. Thick-cut smoked bacon batons and 2cm carrot rounds are scattered throughout. Whole peeled pearl onions and halved cremini mushrooms rest on top, glistening with butter. The dish is garnished with a sprig of fresh flat-leaf parsley. The plate sits on a rustic dark wood table next to a cotton napkin. A glass of red wine and crusty baguette slices are visible in the background. Lighting is soft and natural, highlighting the rich textures of the braised meat and the velvety sauce.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in deep ceramic bowls to retain heat and sauce.
Accompany with crusty French baguette slices for dipping.
Pair with a medium-bodied red Burgundy wine.
Optionally serve over buttered egg noodles or mashed potatoes.

ingredients.name: smoked bacon, cut into thick batons

instructions: Pat beef chunks dry with paper towels.
Season meat with salt and black pepper.
Sauté bacon batons in a heavy pot until crisp.
Remove bacon and set aside.
Sear beef in bacon fat over high heat until browned on all sides.
Remove beef and sauté carrots and pearl onions for 5 minutes.
Stir in tomato paste and flour. Cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in red wine and deglaze the bottom of the pot.
Return beef and bacon to the pot.
Add beef stock and bouquet garni.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 2.5 hours.
Sauté mushrooms in butter in a separate pan.
Add mushrooms to the pot 15 minutes before serving.
Discard the bouquet garni before plating.
notes: Use a high-quality dry red wine for the best sauce flavor.
The stew tastes even better when reheated the next day.
Ensure the beef is fork-tender before finishing the dish.

recipes.recipe_name: Poached Quince with Yuzu Curd and Ginger Crumble
recipes.visual_description: A single portion served on a clean white porcelain plate. The focal point is four thick, tender wedges of poached quince, glowing with a deep rosy-pink hue. The wedges are placed upright on a smooth, vibrant yellow pool of yuzu curd. Golden-brown ginger crumble is scattered organically around the base of the fruit, providing a rustic texture contrast. The arrangement is clean and fluid, utilizing the plate's negative space. The setting is a modern bistro with a light wood table and a neutral cotton napkin. Lighting is natural and even, highlighting the silky curd and the matte, soft texture of the poached fruit. The entire plate is visible.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a cup of hot Sencha green tea.
Pair with a glass of late-harvest Riesling.
instructions: Peel and core quinces. Cut each into 8 thick wedges.
Combine water, 150g granulated sugar, star anise, and sliced ginger in a saucepan.
Bring to a simmer. Add quince wedges.
Cover with a cartouche. Poach on low heat for 90 minutes until quince turns deep pink and tender.
Whisk eggs, remaining 50g granulated sugar, yuzu juice, and zest in a heatproof bowl.
Place bowl over simmering water. Stir constantly until mixture coats the back of a spoon.
Remove from heat. Whisk in 50g cold butter cubes until smooth. Chill curd.
Mix flour, brown sugar, minced ginger, and remaining 50g butter until coarse crumbs form.
Spread on a tray. Bake at 180°C for 12 minutes until golden brown.
Spread a circle of yuzu curd on each plate. Place four quince wedges on the curd. Scatter crumble around the fruit.
notes: Quince requires long, slow poaching to achieve the characteristic pink color.
Ensure the yuzu curd does not boil to prevent the eggs from curdling.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Pollo al Ajillo with Crispy Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: The dish features golden-brown chicken thigh chunks and crispy 2cm potato cubes tossed together in a rustic white porcelain bowl. Slices of toasted garlic and vibrant green chopped parsley are scattered across the surface. The chicken displays a glistening, savory glaze from the reduced wine and olive oil emulsion. Beside the bowl sits a small side of crusty bread and a small dish of marinated olives. The setting includes a light wood table, a neutral cotton napkin, and a Spanish-style ceramic water jug. Lighting is natural and soft, highlighting the textures of the seared meat and the fluffy interior of the roasted potatoes. The entire plate is visible within a clean, modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the garlic oil
Accompany with a glass of chilled Sherry or dry white wine
Present in a traditional terracotta cazuela
instructions: Heat 60ml olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat.
Fry potato cubes until golden and tender. Remove and drain on paper towels. Season with salt.
Add remaining olive oil to the pan. Season chicken chunks with salt and pepper.
Sear chicken chunks until skin is crispy and meat is browned on all sides.
Add smashed garlic cloves. Cook until garlic is golden brown.
Add sliced garlic and smoked paprika. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Scrape the bottom of the pan to release browned bits.
Simmer until liquid reduces by half and chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C.
Fold potatoes and parsley into the pan. Toss to coat in the garlic sauce.
Serve immediately.
notes: Use a high-quality Spanish olive oil for the best flavor profile
Ensure the pan is not overcrowded to achieve a proper sear on the chicken

recipes.recipe_name: Red Wine Braised Beef with Mushrooms and Pearl Onions
recipes.visual_description: Four large, tender chunks of braised beef are placed in the center of a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The meat is coated in a glossy, dark mahogany red wine sauce. Whole, golden-caramelized pearl onions and halved, earthy-brown cremini mushrooms are arranged naturally around the beef. The sauce has a thick, velvety consistency that pools slightly at the bottom. A light sprinkle of fresh, chopped thyme leaves adds a vibrant green contrast. The dish is presented on a dark oak table with a side of sliced, crusty baguette. Natural window light creates a soft sheen on the sauce and highlights the fibrous texture of the slow-cooked beef chunks.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty baguette slices to soak up the sauce
Pair with a medium-bodied French red wine like Pinot Noir or Merlot
Traditionally served with buttery mashed potatoes or wide egg noodles
instructions: Pat beef dry with paper towels.
Season beef generously with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a heavy-based pot over medium-high heat.
Sear beef chunks in batches until deep brown on all sides.
Remove beef and set aside.
Add mushrooms to the same pot. Sauté until browned. Remove and set aside.
Add pearl onions. Cook until lightly caramelized. Remove and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add garlic and tomato paste. Stir for 1 minute.
Whisk in flour. Cook for 1 minute.
Pour in red wine. Scrape the bottom of the pot to release browned bits.
Return beef to the pot. Add stock, thyme, and bay leaf.
Bring to a simmer. Cover and cook on low heat for 90 minutes.
Add mushrooms and onions back to the pot.
Simmer uncovered for 20 minutes until sauce thickens and meat is tender.
Remove bay leaf and thyme stems before serving.
notes: Ensure the beef is completely dry before searing to achieve a dark crust.
Do not crowd the pan during searing to prevent the meat from steaming.
Use a wine you would enjoy drinking for the best flavor profile.

recipes.recipe_name: Mustard and Chili Chicken with Steamed Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Bengali-style mustard chicken served on a clean white porcelain plate. The dish features four large, succulent chunks of chicken coated in a vibrant, thick yellow mustard gravy. The chicken is placed beside a neat mound of fluffy, long-grain white basmati rice. Two bright green chilis, slit lengthwise, garnish the top of the chicken chunks. The sauce has a visible texture from the ground mustard seeds. The setting is a dark wood bistro table with a simple white cotton napkin and a small side bowl of pickled red onions. Lighting is soft and natural, highlighting the glossy sheen of the mustard oil. The entire plate is visible with moderate negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with fresh lime wedges
Accompany with raw red onion rings
Serve in a traditional stainless steel thali
instructions: Rinse rice until water runs clear.
Boil rice in 2 liters of salted water for 12 minutes.
Drain rice and keep warm.
Blend mustard seeds, two green chilis, and 30ml water into a smooth paste.
Toss chicken chunks with turmeric and salt.
Heat mustard oil in a large pan until it smokes slightly.
Fry onions in oil until dark golden.
Add garlic and sauté for 30 seconds.
Add chicken chunks.
Brown all sides for 5 minutes.
Stir in mustard paste and 250ml water.
Simmer on medium heat for 12 minutes.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Stir in remaining slit chilis and remove from heat.
notes: High-quality mustard oil is essential for authentic flavor
Do not overcook the mustard paste to avoid bitterness
Check chicken temperature at the thickest part of the chunks

recipes.recipe_name: Venison Loin with Blackberry Liqueur Gastrique
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of roasted venison loin sits as a whole, unsliced piece atop a smooth, ivory-colored parsnip puree. The puree is spread in a clean circle on a matte white porcelain plate. A deep purple, glossy blackberry liqueur gastrique is drizzled precisely over the meat, pooling slightly at the base. Three fresh, plump blackberries and a small sprig of green thyme are placed naturally beside the meat. The venison has a dark, caramelized outer crust. The setting is a dark oak bistro table with a crisp white cotton napkin and polished silver cutlery. Natural side-lighting highlights the velvety texture of the sauce and the matte finish of the puree.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of full-bodied Syrah or Saint-Émilion.
Present on pre-heated porcelain plates to maintain meat temperature.
instructions: Boil parsnips in salted water until tender. Drain well.
Blend parsnips with milk and 20g butter until smooth. Season with salt.
Season venison loin generously with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a heavy pan over high heat. Sear venison on all sides until browned.
Add 20g butter and thyme to the pan. Baste venison for 2 minutes.
Remove venison when internal temperature reaches 52°C for medium-rare. Rest 10 minutes.
In a small saucepan, simmer shallot and vinegar until reduced by half.
Add blackberry liqueur and stock. Reduce by two-thirds until syrupy.
Whisk in remaining 20g cold butter. Strain the sauce through a fine mesh sieve.
Warm the parsnip puree. Place a large spoonful on each plate.
Place the whole rested venison piece on the puree. Do not slice.
Spoon sauce over the meat and garnish with fresh blackberries.
notes: Ensure the gastrique is reduced sufficiently to coat the back of a spoon.
Venison is lean; do not overcook or it will become tough.
Resting the meat is essential for juice retention.

recipes.recipe_name: Sichuan Twice-Cooked Pork with Steamed Rice
recipes.visual_description: The dish features thick, square chunks of twice-cooked pork belly, glossy with a vibrant red chili bean sauce. The pork edges are slightly curled and caramelized from the wok. Large wedges of softened white onion and bright red chili slices are interspersed with the meat. The pork is piled naturally in a shallow celadon ceramic bowl, showing charred surfaces and rendered fat. A side of fluffy, steaming white jasmine rice is served in a separate small porcelain bowl. The setting includes dark wood chopsticks resting on a ceramic holder and a simple cotton napkin. Lighting is natural and bright, highlighting the oily sheen of the sauce and the texture of the pork skin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small dish of pickled mustard greens to cut through the richness
Provide individual rice bowls for each guest
Pair with a light green tea such as Tieguanyin
Eat using traditional bamboo or wood chopsticks
instructions: Rinse rice until water runs clear. Combine with 600ml water in a pot. Bring to boil, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes. Let stand for 5 minutes.
Place whole pork belly in a pot of cold water with sliced ginger. Bring to a boil. Simmer for 20 minutes until just cooked through.
Remove pork from water. Pat dry and let cool completely. Cut into 5mm thick square chunks.
Peel and cut onion into 2cm wedges. Thinly slice garlic and chilies.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat. Add pork chunks. Stir-fry until fat renders and edges begin to curl and brown.
Push pork to the side of the wok. Add doubanjiang to the center. Fry for 30 seconds until the oil turns red.
Incorporate garlic, chilies, and onions. Stir-fry for 2 minutes until onions soften slightly.
Add soy sauce, sugar, and Shaoxing wine. Toss everything together for 1 minute to glaze.
Check pork internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove from heat immediately.
Serve the pork in a communal bowl with individual bowls of steamed rice.
notes: Ensure the pork is cooled before cutting to maintain clean square chunk shapes
The doubanjiang provides significant salt, so add extra soy sauce sparingly
Render the pork fat until the skin is slightly crispy but not tough

recipes.recipe_name: Jalapeño and Aged Cheddar Scones
recipes.visual_description: Four tall, golden-brown scones are arranged organically on a light oak serving board. Each scone is a thick, 5cm high cylinder with a craggy, matte exterior showing visible pockets of melted orange cheddar. Vibrant green 5mm diced jalapeños are speckled throughout the pale crumb. The scones exhibit distinct horizontal cracks along the sides from the lamination technique. A small white porcelain ramekin of salted butter and a folded grey linen napkin sit beside the board. The scene is set on a clean wooden bistro table under soft, natural side lighting. The background is a minimalist restaurant interior. The composition uses moderate negative space to highlight the texture of the scones.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm with salted farmhouse butter
Pair with a strong black tea or a dry savory cider
Traditional afternoon savory snack service
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Line a baking tray with parchment paper.
Sift flour, baking powder, and salt into a large bowl.
Rub chilled butter cubes into flour using fingertips until it resembles coarse breadcrumbs.
Fold in cheddar cubes and diced jalapeños evenly.
Make a well in the center and pour in the milk.
Mix quickly with a knife until a soft dough forms.
Turn dough onto a floured surface and pat into a 3cm thick rectangle.
Fold the dough in half once to create layers.
Cut into 6cm rounds using a plain pastry cutter.
Place scones on the tray and brush tops with egg wash.
Bake for 15-18 minutes until golden brown and risen.
Cool on a wire rack for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Do not overwork the dough to ensure a light, flaky texture.
Ensure butter is very cold before starting the rubbing-in process.
Use a sharp cutter and press straight down without twisting to allow maximum rise.

recipes.recipe_name: Beer-Braised Chicken with Caramelized Onions
recipes.visual_description: The dish features two whole, skin-on chicken thighs with a deep golden-brown, crispy exterior. They rest on a generous bed of soft, mahogany-colored caramelized onions. A rich, glossy amber beer reduction sauce coats the onions and forms a shallow pool around the base of the chicken. Fine shards of freshly grated parmesan cheese are scattered over the meat, beginning to melt from the heat. The arrangement is centered on a clean white porcelain plate, leaving balanced negative space. The setting includes a dark wood table, a neutral linen napkin, and stainless steel flatware. Natural light emphasizes the contrast between the crispy chicken skin and the velvety onion sauce.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a warm, crusty baguette to soak up the beer reduction
Pair with a side of steamed green beans or roasted root vegetables
Serve in a wide, shallow porcelain bowl
instructions: Season chicken thighs generously with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed skillet over medium-high heat.
Place chicken skin-side down in the pan.
Sear for 6 minutes until the skin is golden and crispy.
Flip chicken and sear for 2 minutes. Remove chicken from pan.
Add sliced onions to the remaining fat in the pan.
Cook onions over medium heat for 20 minutes until dark brown and soft.
Pour beer into the pan. Scrape the bottom to release browned bits.
Reduce beer by half over high heat.
Add chicken stock and thyme sprigs. Return chicken to the pan.
Simmer for 15 minutes. Ensure chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken and keep warm.
Whisk butter and 50g of parmesan into the onion sauce until glossy.
Place chicken over the onions. Top with remaining parmesan.
notes: Use a malt-forward beer rather than a bitter IPA to avoid a sharp sauce
Caramelize onions slowly to develop deep sweetness
Always use a meat thermometer to confirm the 75°C internal temperature

recipes.recipe_name: Indian Spiced Chicken and Broccoli Rice Bowl
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl set on a dark rustic wooden table. The base is a fluffy mound of long-grain Basmati rice, pale yellow from turmeric and aromatic spices. Nestled into the rice are succulent, whole chunks of pan-seared chicken thighs, showing a deep reddish-brown spice crust. Vibrant green, tender-crisp broccoli florets are scattered naturally across the surface, providing a sharp color contrast. The dish is topped with a cluster of crispy, dark caramelized onion strips and a sprinkle of bright green chopped cilantro. A small side copper bowl of white yogurt raita and a traditional stainless steel spoon sit beside the plate on a folded grey linen napkin. Natural side-lighting highlights the steam and the moist texture of the chicken.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of cooling cucumber raita
Accompany with lime wedges and raw onion rings
Traditional stainless steel or copper serving vessels enhance authenticity

ingredients.name: Boneless chicken thighs, cut into 4cm chunks

instructions: Mix yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, turmeric, and half the garam masala in a bowl.
Add chicken chunks to the marinade. Coat well. Refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Rinse rice until water runs clear. Soak in cold water for 20 minutes. Drain.
Heat 30ml oil in a heavy-bottomed pot. Add cumin seeds. Let them sizzle.
Add half the sliced onions. Sauté until deep golden brown. Remove and set aside.
Add remaining onions to the pot. Sauté until translucent.
Add marinated chicken. Sear over medium-high heat until browned on all sides.
Stir in drained rice and remaining garam masala. Cook for 2 minutes.
Add 500ml water and salt. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover tightly.
Cook rice and chicken for 12 minutes or until water is absorbed.
Steam broccoli florets separately for 4 minutes until vibrant green and tender-crisp.
Ensure chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Fluff rice with a fork. Fold in steamed broccoli gently.
Garnish with fried onions and fresh cilantro before serving.
notes: Do not over-mix the rice to avoid breaking the long grains.
Ensure the onions for garnish are fried until dark brown but not burnt for the best umami flavor.
Soaking the Basmati rice is essential for the correct elongated texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Sausage and Cheddar Polenta
recipes.visual_description: A wide, shallow white porcelain bowl rests on a dark oak bistro table. A generous portion of creamy, pale gold cheddar polenta forms a fluid, free-flowing base. One large, plump, seared pork sausage sits whole in the center, featuring a taut, deeply browned skin with glistening juices. Thick strips of vibrant roasted red bell peppers and translucent sautéed onions are arranged naturally around the sausage. Fine flecks of bright green flat-leaf parsley are scattered over the dish. A silver fork and a folded white cotton napkin lie to the right. Natural, even lighting highlights the silky texture of the polenta and the charred surface of the meat, with moderate negative space around the bowl edges.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in wide, shallow pasta bowls
Pair with a crisp Italian white wine
Provide crusty sourdough bread to clean the plate
instructions: Bring milk and vegetable stock to a boil in a heavy pot.
Whisk in polenta slowly to avoid lumps.
Reduce heat to low and simmer for 5 minutes, stirring constantly.
Remove from heat and stir in grated cheddar and butter until smooth.
Keep polenta covered and warm.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add whole sausages and sear until browned on all sides.
Continue cooking sausages until the internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove sausages and set aside.
In the same skillet, sauté onion and pepper strips for 8 minutes.
Add garlic and cook for 1 minute more.
Season vegetables with salt and black pepper.
notes: Ensure the polenta remains fluid by adding a splash of warm stock if it thickens too much before serving.
Use aged cheddar for a more pronounced savory profile.

recipes.recipe_name: Mushroom and Chicken Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A shallow white porcelain bowl holds a creamy, fluid risotto cooked all'onda, spreading naturally without being dry. The rice grains are distinct and coated in a glossy emulsion. Distributed throughout are golden-brown seared chicken thigh cubes and earthy cremini mushroom slices. Small pieces of mahogany-colored porcini add visual depth. The dish is garnished with a fine dusting of Parmigiano Reggiano and vibrant green flat-leaf parsley. The setting is a modern bistro with a light oak table surface. A polished silver spoon rests on a folded linen napkin beside the plate. Natural side lighting emphasizes the velvety texture of the rice and the rustic, seared surfaces of the chicken and mushrooms.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in wide, shallow pre-heated bowls
Pair with a crisp Italian white wine like Pinot Grigio or Gavi
Provide extra Parmigiano Reggiano at the table

ingredients.name: Chicken thighs, skinless and boneless, cut into 2cm cubes
Dried porcini mushrooms, rehydrated and chopped
Chicken stock, kept at a simmer

instructions: Heat oil in a heavy-based pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken cubes until golden brown and cooked to 75°C. Remove and set aside.
Add mushrooms to the same pot. Sauté until browned and moisture evaporates. Remove and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add half the butter and shallots. Cook until translucent.
Add rice. Stir for 2 minutes until edges are translucent for tostatura.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed.
Add stock one ladle at a time. Stir constantly. Wait for absorption before adding more.
Return chicken and mushrooms to the pot when rice is al dente.
Remove from heat. Perform mantecatura by vigorously stirring in remaining butter and cheese.
Adjust consistency with a splash of stock until the risotto is fluid and free-flowing.
Season with salt and pepper. Fold in parsley.
Serve immediately on warm plates.
notes: Do not rinse the rice to preserve starch for creaminess
Ensure stock is hot to maintain cooking temperature
The risotto should move like a wave (all'onda) when the plate is tilted

recipes.recipe_name: Beef Lok Lak
recipes.visual_description: Beef Lok Lak is presented on a clean white porcelain plate. A vibrant bed of fresh green watercress and thick-cut red tomato rounds forms the base. Centered atop the greens are glistening 2cm cubes of seared beef. The beef shows a deep caramelized crust from high-heat wok searing. Thin rings of raw red onion are scattered over the beef. To the side sits a small white ceramic ramekin containing a clear lime juice and cracked black Kampot pepper dipping sauce. The arrangement is balanced with moderate negative space. The setting is a light wood bistro table with a folded white cotton napkin and dark wood chopsticks. Natural side lighting highlights the glossy sauce on the meat.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a bowl of steamed jasmine rice
Include a side of sliced cucumbers for cooling
Use a small side dish for the Tuk Meric (lime-pepper sauce)
instructions: Cut beef into 2cm cubes.
Whisk oyster sauce, soy sauces, sugar, and garlic in a bowl.
Add beef cubes and toss to coat.
Marinate for 20 minutes at room temperature.
Mix lime juice, salt, and Kampot pepper in a small dipping bowl.
Arrange watercress and tomato slices on a serving plate.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat until smoking.
Add beef in a single layer.
Sear for 1 minute without moving.
Toss beef quickly for 2 more minutes until caramelized.
Place hot beef over the cold vegetable bed.
Garnish with red onion rings.
Serve immediately with the lime-pepper sauce.
notes: Use high heat to ensure the beef sears quickly without boiling in its juices.
Kampot pepper is essential for the authentic Cambodian flavor profile.
The contrast between hot beef and cold watercress is traditional.

recipes.recipe_name: Sausage and Cheddar Polenta
recipes.visual_description: A wide, shallow white porcelain bowl rests on a dark oak bistro table. A generous portion of creamy, pale gold cheddar polenta forms a fluid, free-flowing base. Thick strips of vibrant roasted red bell peppers and translucent sautéed onions are arranged naturally around the sausage. Fine flecks of bright green flat-leaf parsley are scattered over the dish. A silver fork and a folded white cotton napkin lie to the right. Natural, even lighting highlights the silky texture of the polenta and the charred surface of the meat, with moderate negative space around the bowl edges.

Pair with a crisp Italian white wine
Provide crusty sourdough bread to clean the plate

Season vegetables with salt and black pepper.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Cacciatore with Pappardelle
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of wide, golden pappardelle ribbons is nested in a clean white porcelain pasta bowl. The pasta is coated in a thick, vibrant red San Marzano tomato sauce. A whole, bone-in braised chicken thigh rests centrally on the pasta, showing a rich, caramelized exterior. Small, tender cubes of carrot and celery, along with dark, wrinkled Kalamata olives, are distributed throughout the sauce. Freshly chopped flat-leaf parsley provides a vivid green garnish. The dish is set on a dark wood table with a folded linen napkin and a silver fork. Soft, natural light emphasizes the glossy texture of the sauce and the rustic appeal of the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty ciabatta bread
Pair with a medium-bodied Chianti wine
Offer freshly grated Pecorino Romano at the table
instructions: Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden.
Flip chicken and brown the other side.
Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Add onion, carrot, and celery to the pan.
Sauté vegetables for 5 minutes.
Stir in garlic, rosemary, and thyme. Cook 1 minute.
Pour in wine. Deglaze the pan bottom.
Add tomatoes and olives. Stir well.
Return chicken to the pan. Cover.
Simmer 30 minutes until chicken reaches 75°C.
Boil salted water. Cook pappardelle until al dente.
Drain pasta. Toss with sauce.
Place pasta in bowls. Top with one whole chicken thigh.
notes: Ensure the sauce is thick enough to coat the wide pasta ribbons
Use high-quality San Marzano tomatoes for authentic flavor

recipes.recipe_name: Korean Braised Beef Short Ribs
recipes.visual_description: The dish features large, succulent chunks of dark, glazed beef short ribs piled centrally in a shallow, matte black ceramic bowl. The beef exhibits a deep mahogany sheen from the reduced soy-pear glaze. Interspersed among the meat are ivory-colored daikon radish wedges and vibrant orange carrot chunks, both with edges rounded to prevent breaking. Thick halves of earthy shiitake mushrooms add texture. The arrangement is organic and clean, with a sprinkle of white toasted sesame seeds and bright green scallion rounds. A side of polished white rice in a small stainless steel bowl and a small dish of red kimchi accompany the main bowl on a light oak table. Natural side-lighting highlights the moist, tender texture of the unsliced beef.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a bowl of steamed short-grain white rice
Include a side of traditional napa cabbage kimchi
Present in a heavy ceramic vessel or traditional jjim-gi
instructions: Soak beef short ribs in cold water for 30 minutes.
Drain ribs.
Blanch ribs in boiling water for 5 minutes.
Rinse ribs under cold running water.
Grate the Asian pear into a large bowl.
Add soy sauce, mirin, sugar, minced garlic, and minced ginger to the pear.
Place ribs in a heavy-bottomed pot.
Pour the sauce mixture over the ribs.
Add enough water to just submerge the meat.
Simmer covered for 60 minutes over medium-low heat.
Cut daikon and carrots into 3cm chunks.
Round the sharp edges of the vegetables using a paring knife.
Add daikon, carrots, and halved shiitake mushrooms to the pot.
Simmer for 30 minutes until meat is tender.
Remove the lid.
Increase heat to medium-high.
Reduce the liquid until it becomes a thick, glossy glaze.
Stir in sesame oil.
Garnish with sliced green onions and sesame seeds.
notes: Rounding the edges of the radish and carrots prevents the sauce from becoming cloudy
Asian pear contains enzymes that tenderize the beef naturally
Blanching the meat is essential for a clean and deep flavor profile

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Tikka Masala
recipes.visual_description: The dish features large, charred chunks of succulent chicken submerged in a glossy, vibrant orange-red tomato gravy. The sauce has a thick, velvety texture with visible flecks of ground spices. The chicken chunks show dark, caramelized edges from the high-heat roasting. Plating is in a clean, white porcelain bowl set on a dark wooden table. A single portion is shown with a light swirl of heavy cream on top and a scattering of bright green chopped cilantro. To the side sits a stack of warm, charred garlic naan bread and a small bowl of steamed long-grain basmati rice. Lighting is natural and even, highlighting the rich colors and creamy consistency of the sauce while maintaining professional negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm garlic naan or buttered roti
Accompany with steamed basmati rice
Side of mint-yogurt raita and kachumber salad
Serve in a traditional hammered copper karahi
instructions: Combine yogurt, 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 1 tsp garam masala, 1/2 tsp turmeric, and 1 tsp chili powder.
Toss chicken chunks in marinade. Cover and refrigerate for 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 220°C. Place chicken on a wire rack over a baking sheet.
Roast chicken 15 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Set aside.
Heat oil in a large pan over medium heat. Sauté onions until golden brown.
Add remaining ginger-garlic paste. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in remaining garam masala, turmeric, and chili powder. Toast for 30 seconds.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Simmer 10 minutes until sauce thickens and oil separates.
Stir in butter and heavy cream. Season with salt.
Add roasted chicken chunks to the sauce. Simmer 2 minutes to combine flavors.
Garnish with fresh cilantro.
notes: Kashmiri chili powder provides color without excessive heat.
Ensure the chicken is well-charred for authentic smoky flavor.
Let the sauce simmer until the oil separates to ensure spices are fully cooked.

recipes.recipe_name: Carne Asada with Frijoles Charros
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Carne Asada presented on a matte white porcelain plate. The primary focus is a whole, seared flank steak with distinct charred grill marks and a glistening, juicy surface. Adjacent to the beef, a small, traditional glazed clay bowl contains Frijoles Charros, featuring visible chunks of pink pinto beans, reddish chorizo, and translucent onions in a rich, savory broth. The beans are garnished with bright green chopped cilantro and white crumbled cheese. A charred whole spring onion and a vibrant lime wedge rest on the plate's edge. The scene is set on a dark wooden table with a folded linen napkin and a small basket of warm corn tortillas in the background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Warm corn tortillas
Salsa verde
Grilled spring onions (cebollitas)
Radish slices
instructions: Whisk lime juice, oil, cumin, and half the garlic in a bowl.
Rub marinade onto beef. Refrigerate for 1 hour.
Brown bacon and chorizo in a pot over medium heat.
Add remaining onion and jalapeño. Sauté until soft.
Stir in beans, oregano, and beef stock.
Simmer beans for 15 minutes until liquid thickens.
Preheat grill or cast-iron pan to high heat.
Season beef generously with salt and pepper.
Sear beef for 4-5 minutes per side until internal temperature reaches 54°C.
Rest beef for 10 minutes before serving.
Serve beef whole alongside a bowl of beans.
notes: Ensure the grill is very hot to achieve a deep crust on the beef.
Do not slice the meat before serving to retain internal juices.
Adjust jalapeño quantity to control the heat level of the beans.
