Stir in garlic, ginger, Ras el Hanout, and turmeric. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return chicken to the pot. Add saffron water, chicken stock, half the cilantro, and half the parsley.
Add julienned preserved lemon skins.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 40 minutes.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Add green olives. Simmer uncovered for 5 minutes to reduce sauce slightly.
Garnish with remaining fresh herbs before serving.
notes: Ensure the white pith of the preserved lemon is removed to avoid bitterness.
Adjust salt carefully as preserved lemons and olives are naturally salty.

recipes.recipe_name: Thai Basil Chicken with Jasmine Rice
recipes.visual_description: A steaming mound of fluffy jasmine rice occupies half of a clean white porcelain plate. Beside it, glossy 2cm chunks of golden-brown seared chicken thighs are coated in a dark, savory sauce. Vibrant green Thai basil leaves are wilted throughout the stir-fry. A single fried egg with a lacy, golden-crisp edge and a bright runny yolk rests atop the chicken. The dish is presented on a dark teak wood table with a small side dish of fish sauce containing sliced red chilies. Soft natural lighting highlights the textures of the crispy egg and tender chicken. A traditional Thai stainless steel spoon and fork lie on a white cotton napkin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with Prik Nam Pla (fish sauce with chilies)
Eat with a spoon in the right hand and fork in the left
Provide cucumber slices to cool the palate
instructions: Rinse rice until water runs clear.
Cook rice in 600ml water until fluffy.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a pan over high heat.
Fry eggs until edges are crispy and brown.
Remove eggs and set aside.
Heat remaining oil in a wok.
Sauté garlic and chilies until fragrant.
Add chicken chunks to the wok.
Stir-fry chicken until browned and internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Stir in oyster sauce, soy sauces, and sugar.
Add basil leaves and toss until wilted.
Divide rice into four plates.
Top rice with chicken and a fried egg.
notes: Use Holy Basil for the most authentic flavor if available.
Adjust chili count based on heat preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Chocolate Coconut Brownies
recipes.visual_description: A single, thick, square-cut chocolate brownie sits centrally on a plain white ceramic plate with a slightly uneven rim. The brownie has a crackly, papery top crust and a dense, fudgy interior. A small dusting of fine coconut flour creates a snowy contrast against the dark cocoa surface. A single dollop of softened butter sits on top, melting slightly into the warm crumb. The plate rests on a dark oak kitchen table. A simple stainless steel dessert fork lies to the right. A folded linen napkin is tucked under the plate edge. Warm, soft light from a nearby window highlights the moist, open texture of the brownie's side.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of cold milk
Pair with a scoop of vanilla bean ice cream
Enjoy as a mid-afternoon snack with coffee
instructions: Preheat oven to 175°C.
Grease a 20cm square baking pan.
Melt butter in a large bowl.
Whisk in sugar until combined.
Add eggs and vanilla extract.
Whisk until the mixture is smooth.
Sift in flour, cocoa powder, coconut flour, and salt.
Fold dry ingredients into the wet mixture using a spatula.
Spread batter evenly into the prepared pan.
Bake for 25 minutes until the edges are set.
Cool completely in the pan before slicing.
Cut into 5cm squares.
notes: Do not overbake to ensure a fudgy texture
Use room temperature eggs for a smoother batter
The coconut flour adds a subtle nutty flavor and improves density

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Paprikash
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chicken Paprikash served on a heavy, hand-painted ceramic plate. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs are braised to a deep, glossy orange-red color. They rest on a generous bed of small, irregularly shaped nokedli dumplings. A thick, vibrant paprika gravy coats the meat and flows naturally into the dumplings. A clean dollop of cool white sour cream sits on top of the chicken, slightly melting into the warm sauce. Finely chopped green parsley is scattered across the dish. The plate sits on a weathered wooden table with a side bowl of vinegar-brined cucumber salad. Warm, diffused kitchen light emphasizes the rich, creamy texture of the sauce.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with nokedli (Hungarian dumplings) or wide egg noodles
Include a side of mizeria (cucumber salad) or pickled gherkins
Provide crusty rye bread to soak up the paprika sauce
instructions: Season chicken pieces with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a large deep skillet over medium-high heat.
Brown chicken on all sides. Remove chicken and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add onions to the skillet. Sauté until translucent.
Stir in minced garlic for 1 minute.
Remove skillet from heat. Stir in paprika to avoid burning.
Return chicken to the skillet. Pour in chicken stock.
Simmer covered for 30 minutes. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Whisk sour cream and flour together in a small bowl.
Temper the cream by adding two spoons of hot cooking liquid to it. Mix well.
Stir the cream mixture back into the skillet. Simmer for 5 minutes until sauce thickens.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Removing the pan from heat before adding paprika prevents bitterness.
Tempering the sour cream prevents it from curdling in the hot sauce.
Always use authentic Hungarian sweet paprika for the best flavor profile.

recipes.recipe_name: Filipino Chicken Adobo
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Filipino Chicken Adobo sits in a shallow, rustic ceramic bowl. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs are the focal point, coated in a deep mahogany, glossy sauce that pools slightly at the base. The skin is dark and slightly tacky from the reduction. Scattered over the meat are softened, golden-brown crushed garlic cloves and a few whole black peppercorns. The chicken rests partly on a bed of fluffy, steamed white jasmine rice. The setting is a dark wooden table with a simple spoon and fork placed on a linen napkin. Warm, overhead kitchen lighting highlights the rich textures and the steam rising from the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of atchara (pickled green papaya)
Eat using a spoon and fork, the traditional Filipino way
Pour extra adobo sauce over the rice
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels.
Heat oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken pieces until skin is brown and crisp.
Remove chicken and set aside.
Sauté crushed garlic in the same pot for 1 minute.
Return chicken to the pot.
Add soy sauce, vinegar, water, peppercorns, and bay leaves.
Bring liquid to a boil.
Reduce heat to low and cover.
Simmer for 30 minutes.
Check chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove the lid and increase heat to medium-high.
Simmer until the sauce reduces and thickens into a glossy glaze.
Stir in sugar if using for balance.
Discard bay leaves before serving.
notes: Do not stir the sauce immediately after adding vinegar to allow the raw acidity to cook off.
Use cane vinegar for the most authentic flavor profile.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoked Chicken and Fermented Beet Canapés
recipes.visual_description: Twelve bite-sized canapés arranged on a reclaimed light oak board. Each base is a 3cm circular disc of golden-toasted sourdough. On top sits a single 2cm cube of seared chicken, showing a deep pink outer ring from the beet brine and a caramelized golden crust. The chicken is topped with a delicate cloud of micro-grated white horseradish and a single dark green dill frond. Small flakes of crispy brown chicken skin are scattered precisely on top. The board sits on a grey stone surface next to an undyed beige linen napkin. Soft, natural side-lighting emphasizes the textures of the porous bread and the moist chicken. The entire board is visible with balanced negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve on a hand-carved wooden platter
Pair with a chilled dry cider or light aquavit
Present as part of a seasonal smörgåsbord
instructions: Remove skin from chicken. Reserve skin.
Cut chicken meat into 2cm cubes.
Submerge chicken cubes in fermented beet juice for 45 minutes.
Drain chicken and pat dry with a cloth.
Heat oil in a pan over medium heat.
Fry reserved chicken skin until crisp. Set aside and crush into small flakes.
Sear chicken cubes in the same pan. Cook to an internal temperature of 75°C.
Cut sourdough into 3cm circles using a ring cutter. Save scraps for breadcrumbs.
Toast sourdough circles in the chicken fat until golden.
Place one chicken cube on each sourdough disc.
Grate fresh horseradish finely over the chicken.
Top with crushed skin, smoked salt, and a small dill frond.
notes: Use sourdough scraps to make zero-waste breadcrumbs for future use
The beet brine acts as a natural curing agent and dye
Ensure the chicken reaches exactly 75°C to maintain succulence

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Arroz con Pollo
recipes.visual_description: A wide, shallow white porcelain bowl contains a vibrant mound of golden-hued short-grain rice. Two whole bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs rest atop the rice, featuring a deeply seared, crispy bronze skin. Evenly distributed through the rice are 1cm cubes of charred red bell pepper and finely diced translucent onions. The rice is moist and slightly glossy from the olive oil and tomato reduction. Sprigs of fresh, bright green flat-leaf parsley are scattered over the dish. The plate sits on a rustic light oak table next to a folded white cotton napkin and a polished silver fork. Natural side-lighting highlights the textures of the crispy skin and the individual grains of rice.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in a traditional shallow terracotta dish or paella pan
Accompany with a side of garlic aioli
Pair with a chilled glass of Spanish Albariño
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes until golden.
Flip chicken and sear for 3 minutes. Remove from pan.
Sauté onion and red pepper in the same pan for 5 minutes.
Add garlic and thyme. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in grated tomato. Cook for 4 minutes until liquid evaporates.
Add rice to the pan. Stir for 2 minutes to toast the grains.
Pour in white wine. Scrape the bottom of the pan to deglaze.
Add chicken stock. Bring to a simmer.
Place chicken thighs back into the pan on top of the rice.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 20 minutes.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove from heat. Let rest covered for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Do not stir the rice once the stock is added to allow a crust to form
Grate the tomatoes to remove skins easily while keeping the pulp

recipes.recipe_name: Dark Beer Braised Beef with Asadero
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of 3cm beef chunks glazed in a deep mahogany dark beer reduction. The beef is piled in the center of a clean white porcelain plate. Molten white asadero cheese drapes over the thick beef chunks, showing a stretchy, gooey texture. The dark brown glaze pools slightly around the base of the meat. Bright green jalapeño rounds are placed on top for contrast. The plate sits on a rustic dark wood table. A stack of warm corn tortillas rests in a woven basket to the side. A small bowl of salsa verde and a wedge of lime provide color. Natural, even lighting highlights the glossy finish of the reduction and the creamy texture of the cheese.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas
Accompany with fresh salsa verde
Provide lime wedges for acidity
Serve in a traditional clay cazuela for family style
instructions: Pat beef chunks dry with paper towels.
Season beef with salt and black pepper.
Heat oil in a heavy-based pan over medium-high heat.
Sear beef chunks in batches until browned on all sides.
Remove beef and set aside.
Add onion and garlic to the pan. Sauté for 4 minutes.
Return beef to the pan. Pour in dark beer and Worcestershire sauce.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to medium-low.
Simmer uncovered for 25 minutes until the liquid reduces to a thick glaze.
Distribute shredded asadero cheese evenly over the beef chunks.
Cover the pan for 2 minutes until the cheese is fully melted and gooey.
Garnish with jalapeño rounds and serve immediately.
notes: Use a robust dark beer for a deeper, more savory glaze
Ensure the beef is patted very dry to achieve a deep sear
Monterey Jack can substitute for asadero if unavailable

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Dutch Baby
recipes.visual_description: A large, puffed savory Dutch Baby pancake sits in a well-seasoned black cast iron skillet. The edges are tall, irregular, and deep golden-brown with a crispy, airy texture. The center is slightly sunken and soft, topped with a generous scattering of finely grated parmesan cheese and chopped fresh chives. The pancake is served whole in the skillet, placed on a rustic wooden trivet on a kitchen table. A simple metal server rests beside the pan. The lighting is warm and domestic, highlighting the steam rising from the hot pastry. The background includes a casual stack of ceramic plates and a folded cotton tea towel, creating a lived-in, homestyle atmosphere. The entire skillet is visible on the wooden surface.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve directly from the skillet for a communal experience
Pair with a simple side salad of bitter greens
instructions: Preheat oven to 220°C.
Place a 25cm cast iron skillet in the oven to heat.
Whisk eggs and milk in a bowl until combined.
Whisk in flour, salt, and pepper until the batter is smooth.
Remove the hot skillet from the oven using an oven mitt.
Add butter to the skillet and swirl until melted and foaming.
Pour the batter into the center of the skillet immediately.
Return the skillet to the oven.
Bake for 20 minutes until the pancake is tall and deep brown.
Do not open the oven door during the baking process.
Remove from oven and sprinkle with grated parmesan and chopped chives.
Cut into 4 thick wedges and serve immediately.
notes: Ensure the skillet is very hot before adding butter and batter
Use room temperature eggs and milk for maximum rise

recipes.recipe_name: Provençal Beef Daube
recipes.visual_description: The dish features large 5cm chunks of slow-braised beef chuck, glistening in a deep mahogany-colored wine reduction. The meat remains whole and tender, arranged centrally in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. Bright orange carrot rounds and softened onion wedges are tucked between the beef chunks. Small, wrinkled black Niçoise olives add dark accents throughout the rich sauce. A single strip of fresh orange zest and a sprig of thyme provide a vibrant garnish. The plate sits on a dark oak bistro table next to a torn piece of crusty baguette and a cotton napkin. Natural light from a window creates soft highlights on the glossy sauce and the fibrous texture of the beef.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty baguette slices
Pair with a glass of Côtes du Rhône red wine
Accompany with wide egg noodles or boiled potatoes
Serve in a wide rimmed soup plate
instructions: Cut beef into 5cm chunks.
Season beef with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Brown beef chunks on all sides in batches.
Remove beef and set aside.
Cut onions into thick wedges and carrots into 2cm rounds.
Sauté onions and carrots in the same pot for 5 minutes.
Stir in tomato paste and crushed garlic.
Pour in red wine to deglaze the pot.
Scrape all browned bits from the bottom.
Return beef to the pot with accumulated juices.
Add beef stock, orange peel, thyme, rosemary, and bay leaf.
Bring to a simmer.
Cover tightly and cook on low heat for 3 hours.
Ensure beef reaches an internal temperature of at least 75°C.
Stir in olives and simmer for 10 minutes uncovered.
Remove herb sprigs and orange peel before serving.
notes: For best flavor, cook the dish one day in advance and reheat.
Use a wine you would enjoy drinking for the braise.
Ensure the pot lid is tight to prevent liquid evaporation.

recipes.recipe_name: Southwest Creamy Pasta with Charred Peppers and Black Beans
recipes.visual_description: A wide, shallow white porcelain bowl holds a vibrant mound of al dente penne pasta. The pasta is coated in a glossy, pale-orange cream sauce infused with cumin. Long strips of deeply charred red bell peppers are distributed throughout, showing dark sear marks. Whole, plump black beans and small green flecks of minced pickled jalapeños are visible between the pasta tubes. A scattering of bright green cilantro leaves provides a fresh contrast. The dish is placed on a dark oak table next to a folded linen napkin and a small ceramic dish containing lime wedges. Natural side lighting highlights the creamy texture of the sauce and the charred edges of the peppers.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with fresh lime wedges to balance the richness
Accompany with warm corn tortillas
Provide extra pickled jalapeños on the side for heat

ingredients.name: Canned black beans, drained and rinsed

instructions: Boil pasta in salted water until al dente. Drain and reserve 60ml pasta water.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over high heat.
Add bell pepper strips. Sear until edges are charred. Remove from pan.
Lower heat to medium. Sauté onion and garlic for 4 minutes.
Stir in cumin and minced jalapeños. Cook for 1 minute.
Pour in heavy cream and black beans. Simmer for 5 minutes until thickened.
Return charred peppers to the pan. Add cooked pasta and reserved water.
Toss ingredients until the sauce coats the pasta thoroughly.
Garnish with fresh cilantro and serve with lime wedges.
notes: Use high heat for peppers to ensure a smoky flavor without overcooking
Adjust sauce thickness with reserved pasta water as needed

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Salmon with Lemon-Herb Gremolata
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared salmon is presented on a clean white porcelain plate. The whole salmon fillet features a crisp, golden-brown skin and moist, pink flesh. It rests atop a bed of roasted baby potato halves and whole charred asparagus spears. Blistered red cherry tomatoes and dark Kalamata olives are scattered around the base. A vibrant green gremolata made of finely chopped parsley and yellow lemon zest is spooned over the fish. The setting is a modern bistro with a light oak table and a white cotton napkin. Natural side lighting highlights the textures of the flaky fish and roasted vegetables. The arrangement is organic and professional with balanced negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty sourdough bread
Pair with a crisp dry white wine like Assyrtiko or Vermentino
Offer extra virgin olive oil for drizzling at the table
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Toss halved potatoes with 15ml olive oil and 5g salt.
Spread potatoes on a baking tray.
Roast potatoes for 20 minutes.
Add asparagus and cherry tomatoes to the tray.
Roast for another 10 minutes.
Pat salmon fillets dry with paper towels.
Season salmon with remaining salt and pepper.
Heat 20ml olive oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat.
Place salmon skin-side down in the pan.
Press firmly for 30 seconds to ensure skin contact.
Cook for 4 minutes until skin is crisp.
Flip salmon carefully.
Cook for 2 minutes for medium-rare.
Mix parsley, lemon zest, minced garlic, and 25ml olive oil in a bowl.
Plate roasted vegetables and olives first.
Place one whole salmon fillet on top of vegetables.
Drizzle gremolata and lemon juice over the fish.
notes: Ensure the pan is very hot before adding the fish to prevent sticking.
Do not move the fish during the first 3 minutes of searing for the best skin texture.
Vegetables can be adjusted based on seasonal availability.

recipes.recipe_name: Cantonese Beef and Broccoli Stir-Fry
recipes.visual_description: The dish features 3cm cubes of seared mahogany-colored beef tossed with vibrant green broccoli florets and bright red 2cm bell pepper squares. The ingredients are coated in a glossy, dark brown savory sauce that reflects the light. The beef chunks show a deep sear from the high-heat wok. The arrangement is organic and centered on a clean white porcelain plate with moderate negative space. A few scattered toasted sesame seeds and thinly sliced green scallion rounds provide garnish. The plate sits on a dark wood table next to dark wood chopsticks and a small ceramic bowl of steamed jasmine rice. Natural even lighting highlights the textures of the tender beef and crisp-tender vegetables.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice
Provide chopsticks and a side of chili oil
Serve immediately to maintain 'wok hei' aroma

ingredients.name: Beef flank or sirloin, cut into 3cm chunks
Red bell pepper, cut into 2cm squares

instructions: Toss beef chunks with baking soda and 5g cornstarch.
Marinate beef for 20 minutes.
Blanch broccoli florets in boiling water for 2 minutes.
Drain broccoli and set aside.
Whisk soy sauce, oyster sauce, wine, and remaining cornstarch in a small bowl.
Heat peanut oil in a wok over high heat.
Sear beef chunks until browned on all sides.
Remove beef from wok.
Add ginger, garlic, and bell pepper squares to the wok.
Stir-fry for 1 minute.
Return beef and broccoli to the wok.
Pour in the sauce mixture.
Toss ingredients until the sauce thickens and coats everything evenly.
Drizzle with sesame oil and serve immediately.
notes: Baking soda tenderizes the beef through the velvetting process.
High heat is essential for the traditional smoky flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Wild Mushroom Risotto
recipes.visual_description: The risotto is served on a wide, flat white porcelain plate. The consistency is fluid and free-flowing, spreading naturally across the dish in the traditional all'onda style. The rice grains are plump, glossy, and distinct. Thick, meaty chunks of golden-brown sautéed mushrooms are distributed throughout the rice. The color palette features creamy whites, earthy browns, and soft golds. A light dusting of finely grated Parmigiano Reggiano and tiny green thyme leaves garnish the top. The arrangement is organic and centered with clean margins. Soft natural side lighting emphasizes the creamy emulsion. The background shows a modern bistro setting with a light oak table and a white cotton napkin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve on flat plates to allow the risotto to spread.
Pair with a dry Italian white wine like Gavi or Pinot Grigio.
Provide a high-quality silver spoon for dining.
Serve immediately while the rice maintains its fluid texture.
instructions: Heat vegetable stock in a pot. Keep at a low simmer.
Clean mushrooms. Cut into 2cm chunks.
Sauté mushrooms in olive oil until browned. Season with salt. Remove and set aside.
Finely dice shallots.
Melt 30g butter in a heavy pan. Add shallots. Cook until translucent.
Add rice. Toast for 2 minutes until edges are translucent.
Pour in wine. Stir until liquid evaporates.
Add one ladle of hot stock. Stir constantly.
Add more stock only after the previous ladle is absorbed.
Fold in sautéed mushrooms after 10 minutes of cooking.
Continue adding stock until rice is al dente, approximately 18 minutes total.
Remove from heat. Add remaining butter and Parmigiano Reggiano.
Stir vigorously to create a creamy emulsion. This is mantecatura.
Adjust consistency with a final splash of stock. The risotto must be fluid.
Season with salt and pepper.
notes: Never wash the rice; the surface starch is essential for creaminess.
Ensure the stock is hot to maintain a consistent cooking temperature.
The final texture should be 'all'onda', meaning it moves like a wave when the plate is tilted.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Chicken Pizzaiola with Mozzarella
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spicy Chicken Pizzaiola is served on a clean white porcelain plate. Two whole braised chicken thighs are the centerpiece, covered in a thick layer of melted white mozzarella cheese. The chicken is nestled in a rich, chunky red tomato sauce containing visible diced onions and minced green jalapenos. To the side, several bright green steamed broccoli florets are neatly arranged. The dish is garnished with three whole fresh basil leaves resting on the cheese. The plate sits on a light-colored wooden bistro table with a white cotton napkin and a polished silver fork. Lighting is natural and soft, highlighting the textures of the sauce and the melted cheese.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to soak up the sauce
Pairs well with a crisp Pinot Grigio
instructions: Dice the onion into 5mm pieces.
Mince the pickled jalapeno chilies.
Mince the garlic cloves.
Cut mozzarella into 1cm thick rounds.
Season chicken thighs with salt and oregano.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken for 4 minutes per side until golden.
Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.
Add onion to the same skillet and sauté for 3 minutes.
Stir in garlic and minced jalapenos for 1 minute.
Add crushed tomatoes and simmer for 5 minutes.
Return chicken to the skillet.
Cover and cook for 8 minutes until chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C.
Steam broccoli florets for 5 minutes until tender-crisp.
Place mozzarella rounds on top of chicken pieces.
Cover skillet for 2 minutes to melt the cheese.
Garnish with whole fresh basil leaves before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches 75°C for food safety
Use fresh mozzarella for the best melt and flavor texture

recipes.recipe_name: Tuscan-style Beef and Mushroom Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Tuscan-style beef and mushroom pasta is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The focal point is 3cm chunks of seared, tender beef and quartered, browned cremini mushrooms distributed naturally over wide pappardelle ribbons. The pasta is coated in a thick, savory tomato sauce containing finely diced red bell peppers and onions. The arrangement is organic and fluid, filling the bowl without overcrowding the rim. Light reflects off the glossy sauce and the texture of the meat. A dusting of grated cheese and dried oregano provide contrast. The bowl sits on a dark oak table with a folded cotton napkin and a simple stainless steel fork.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with toasted ciabatta bread
Pair with a glass of Chianti Classico
Accompany with a simple arugula salad
instructions: Cut beef into 3cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat.
Brown beef chunks on all sides in batches. Remove and set aside.
Add diced onion and diced bell pepper to the same pot. Sauté 5 minutes.
Add quartered mushrooms. Cook until browned and moisture evaporates.
Stir in minced garlic and oregano. Cook for 1 minute.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and beef stock. Return beef to the pot.
Simmer on low heat for 45 minutes until beef reaches 75°C and is tender.
Boil pasta in salted water until al dente. Drain well.
Toss pasta with the beef sauce. Serve immediately in warm bowls.
notes: Ensure beef reaches a safe internal temperature of 75°C
Use a heavy-bottomed pot for even heat distribution during braising
Quarter the mushrooms rather than slicing to maintain a meaty texture

recipes.recipe_name: Beer-Braised Chicken with Cayenne and Oregano
recipes.visual_description: The dish features two whole, golden-brown seared chicken thighs as the centerpiece on a clean white porcelain plate. The chicken skin is crispy and coated in a vibrant amber beer reduction. Thick wedges of braised red onion are arranged neatly beside the meat. A layer of melted, bubbly white cheese covers the top of the chicken, showing toasted golden spots from the broiler. Fine particles of dried oregano and chopped fresh cilantro provide a textured green garnish. The plate has ample negative space, highlighting the rich, savory colors of the sauce and poultry. Background elements include a stack of warm corn tortillas wrapped in a cloth and fresh lime wedges.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas
Provide fresh lime wedges for acidity
Accompany with pickled jalapeños

ingredients.name: red onions, cut into thick wedges

instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and cayenne pepper.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes until crispy.
Flip chicken and sear for 4 minutes.
Remove chicken from the skillet and set aside.
Add onion wedges and garlic to the same pan.
Sauté for 5 minutes until onions soften and brown.
Pour in the beer and add dried oregano.
Return chicken to the pan skin-side up.
Simmer over medium heat for 15 minutes.
Verify internal temperature of chicken reaches 75°C.
Top each chicken piece with shredded cheese.
Broil for 2 minutes until cheese is melted and bubbly.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches a safe internal temperature of 75°C
Use a light lager for a crisp flavor profile

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish-Style Pork and White Bean Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spanish-style pork and bean stew is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The dish centers on thick, 3cm chunks of seared pork shoulder and plump, whole white beans. The sauce is a deep, opaque ochre color, thickened by the tomatoes and infused with smoked paprika. Small, translucent bits of diced onion and minced garlic are integrated into the rich liquid. A vibrant garnish of coarsely chopped flat-leaf parsley is scattered over the top. The bowl sits on a clean, light oak table next to a folded gray cotton napkin and a polished silver spoon. Natural side-lighting emphasizes the succulent texture of the pork and the smooth surface of the beans.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty sourdough bread
Pair with a glass of Rioja wine
Offer a side of pickled guindilla peppers
instructions: Pat pork cubes dry with paper towels.
Season pork with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Brown pork cubes on all sides until golden. Remove pork from pot.
Add onion to the same pot. Sauté until translucent.
Add garlic and smoked paprika. Stir for 30 seconds.
Add diced tomatoes. Cook for 5 minutes until softened.
Return pork to the pot. Add chicken stock.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer covered for 75 minutes.
Add white beans to the pot. Simmer uncovered for 15 minutes.
Verify pork internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Garnish with fresh parsley.
notes: Ensure the pork shoulder has some fat marbling for best flavor.
Do not let the paprika burn or it will turn bitter.
The stew is even better if made one day in advance.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Mustard and Oregano Chicken Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of wide noodles coated in a pale yellow, creamy mustard sauce serves as the base. Large, 3cm golden-brown seared chicken chunks are nestled throughout the pasta. Finely diced red chili and chopped fresh oregano provide vibrant flecks of color. The dish is topped with thin shavings of parmesan cheese. The pasta is presented in a shallow white porcelain bowl on a light oak table. A linen napkin and a polished silver fork sit to the right. Natural side lighting highlights the glossy sauce and the texture of the seared chicken. The arrangement is clean with ample negative space around the bowl's rim, reflecting a modern bistro aesthetic.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty sourdough bread
Pair with a crisp dry white wine
Present in wide-rimmed pasta bowls
instructions: Boil 4 liters of salted water. Cook noodles until al dente. Drain and reserve 100 ml pasta water.
Cut chicken into 3 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Dice onion finely. Mince garlic. Deseed and mince chili.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until golden and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pan.
Add onion to the same pan. Sauté 4 minutes until translucent.
Add garlic and chili. Cook for 1 minute.
Stir in Dijon mustard and heavy cream. Simmer for 2 minutes.
Return chicken to the pan. Add chopped oregano.
Toss noodles into the sauce. Add reserved pasta water if needed for consistency.
Stir in half of the grated parmesan. Season with pepper.
Serve immediately topped with remaining parmesan.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches 75°C for safety.
Use fresh oregano for the best aromatic profile.
Adjust chili quantity to control heat levels.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Stuffed Spanish Onions (Cebollas Rellenas)
recipes.visual_description: A single, large braised Spanish onion sits centered in a clean white porcelain shallow bowl. The onion is whole and translucent, showing a deep golden-caramel color from the braising process. The top is open, revealing a savory, dark browned ground beef filling. A rich, glossy, reddish-brown reduction sauce pools at the base of the onion, coating the bottom of the bowl. Fine flecks of bright green chopped parsley are scattered over the top. The setting is a modern bistro with a dark oak table. A side of crusty rustic bread and a simple cotton napkin sit nearby. Lighting is natural and soft, highlighting the moist texture of the onion layers and the sheen of the sauce.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty rustic bread to soak up the braising liquid
Pair with a glass of medium-bodied Spanish Tempranillo
Include a side of simple green olives
instructions: Peel onions and slice off the top 2cm.
Use a spoon to scoop out the onion centers, leaving a 2-layer thick outer shell.
Finely dice the removed onion centers.
Heat olive oil in a pan over medium heat.
Sauté the diced onion and garlic until softened.
Add ground beef to the pan. Brown the meat thoroughly.
Stir in smoked paprika, tomato purée, salt, and pepper.
Stuff the beef mixture tightly into the hollowed onion shells.
Place onions upright in a deep skillet or Dutch oven.
Pour white wine and beef stock into the pan around the onions.
Cover and simmer over low heat for 45 minutes until onions are tender.
Remove onions and boil the remaining liquid until reduced by half.
Spoon the reduced sauce over the onions and garnish with parsley.
notes: Select onions that are uniform in size for even cooking
Ensure the sauce is reduced until it coats the back of a spoon for maximum flavor

recipes.recipe_name: Smoked Paprika Tofu with Romesco Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single portion served on a wide white porcelain plate over a dark wooden bistro table. The foundation is a thick, vibrant orange-red Romesco sauce spread in a natural, free-flowing circle. Centered on the sauce is a single, thick rectangular block of seared silken tofu with a uniform golden-brown crust. Beside the tofu lies a bundle of whole green beans, bright green and showing dark charred spots from the pan. The beans are tossed with translucent, toasted garlic slices. The dish is finished with a scattering of green spring onions cut into thin bias-cut rings and a fresh lemon wedge. Natural window lighting emphasizes the contrast between the smooth sauce and the textured vegetables.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with toasted sourdough or rustic bread
Accompany with a side of Spanish olives
Pair with a crisp Albariño or dry Sherry
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Roast whole peppers and tomatoes for 20 minutes until skins blister.
Place roasted vegetables in a bowl and cover for 10 minutes.
Peel skin and remove seeds from peppers and tomatoes.
Blend roasted vegetables, 2 garlic cloves, smoked paprika, and half the lemon juice until smooth.
Stream in 30ml olive oil while blending to emulsify. Season with salt.
Blanch green beans in boiling salted water for 2 minutes. Drain and pat dry.
Sauté beans with remaining sliced garlic and olive oil in a pan until blistered and charred.
Cut tofu into 4 thick rectangular blocks. Pat thoroughly dry with paper towels.
Sear tofu in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat for 3 minutes per side until golden.
Spoon a generous pool of sauce onto each plate. Place one tofu block in the center.
Arrange a bundle of charred green beans next to the tofu.
Garnish with thinly sliced spring onions and a lemon wedge.
notes: Use the firmest silken tofu available to maintain structural integrity during searing
Ensure the pan is very hot before adding tofu to achieve a crust without overcooking the center
The sauce can be made a day in advance to allow flavors to develop

recipes.recipe_name: Thai Massaman Beef Curry
recipes.visual_description: A single portion served in a deep, hand-painted ceramic Thai bowl. The dish features large, whole chunks of braised beef coated in a thick, glossy, reddish-brown sauce. Whole golden potato cubes and soft, translucent whole shallots are nestled around the beef. The sauce shows a light separation of aromatic oils on the surface. Whole cinnamon sticks and star anise are partially submerged in the curry. A scattering of whole roasted peanuts and fresh cilantro sprigs garnish the top. The bowl sits on a dark teak wood table next to a small bowl of steamed jasmine rice. Natural side lighting emphasizes the rich texture of the sauce and the tender meat fibers.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice
Accompany with Arjad (Thai cucumber relish)
Traditional brass spoon and fork setting
instructions: Heat 100ml coconut milk in a heavy pot over medium heat until oil separates.
Add curry paste to the milk. Fry 3 minutes until fragrant.
Add beef chunks. Stir to coat and brown for 5 minutes.
Pour in remaining coconut milk and beef stock.
Add cinnamon sticks and star anise.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer covered for 90 minutes.
Add potatoes and whole shallots. Simmer 25 minutes until tender.
Stir in palm sugar, fish sauce, and tamarind paste.
Add roasted peanuts. Simmer 5 minutes.
Adjust seasoning for a balance of sweet, salty, and sour flavors.
notes: Ensure the coconut milk 'cracks' to release oil for the most authentic flavor
Do not overcook the potatoes; they should hold their shape
Adjust tamarind levels based on desired acidity

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Arroz con Pollo
recipes.visual_description: A wide, shallow white porcelain bowl contains a vibrant mound of golden-hued short-grain rice. Two whole bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs rest atop the rice, featuring a deeply seared, crispy bronze skin. Evenly distributed through the rice are 1cm cubes of charred red bell pepper and finely diced translucent onions. The rice is moist and slightly glossy from the olive oil and tomato reduction. Sprigs of fresh, bright green flat-leaf parsley are scattered over the dish. The plate sits on a rustic light oak table next to a folded white cotton napkin and a polished silver fork. Natural side-lighting highlights the textures of the crispy skin and the individual grains of rice.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in a traditional shallow terracotta dish or paella pan
Accompany with a side of garlic aioli
Pair with a chilled glass of Spanish Albariño
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes until golden.
Flip chicken and sear for 3 minutes. Remove from pan.
Sauté onion and red pepper in the same pan for 5 minutes.
Add garlic and thyme. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in grated tomato. Cook for 4 minutes until liquid evaporates.
Add rice to the pan. Stir for 2 minutes to toast the grains.
Pour in white wine. Scrape the bottom of the pan to deglaze.
Add chicken stock. Bring to a simmer.
Place chicken thighs back into the pan on top of the rice.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 20 minutes.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove from heat. Let rest covered for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Do not stir the rice once the stock is added to allow a crust to form
Grate the tomatoes to remove skins easily while keeping the pulp

recipes.recipe_name: Turkey and Potato Pasta with Jalapeno-Cottage Cheese Sauce
recipes.visual_description: The dish features rigatoni pasta coated in a smooth, pale cream sauce with visible green jalapeno specks. Golden 1cm potato cubes and rustic seared turkey chunks are scattered throughout the pasta. The turkey is presented in whole, bite-sized pieces, never sliced or fanned. The arrangement is organic and centered on a clean white porcelain plate with ample negative space. Finely chopped fresh parsley provides a vibrant green garnish. The scene is set on a light wooden bistro table under natural, even lighting. A single portion is shown with a cotton napkin and polished silverware nearby. The textures of the ridged pasta and soft potatoes are clearly defined, creating a balanced, professional presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in a wide-rimmed pasta bowl
Pair with a crisp green salad
instructions: Boil 4 liters of salted water.
Cook pasta until al dente. Reserve 120ml pasta water.
Boil potato cubes in a separate pot until tender. Drain.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear turkey chunks until golden and internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Add diced onion and garlic to the skillet. Sauté 3 minutes.
Blend cottage cheese, jalapenos, and reserved water until smooth.
Add cooked pasta and potatoes to the turkey mixture.
Pour in the blended sauce. Toss over low heat for 1 minute.
Season with salt and pepper. Garnish with parsley.
notes: Blending the cottage cheese creates a high-protein, creamy sauce without heavy cream.
Ensure the turkey reaches exactly 75°C to maintain juiciness.

recipes.recipe_name: Rigatoni with Spinach, Sun-dried Tomatoes, and Whipped Ricotta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of rigatoni is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The pasta is coated in a glossy, translucent sauce with bright red julienned sun-dried tomatoes and vibrant green wilted baby spinach leaves. Three distinct, creamy mounds of whipped ricotta are placed on top, showing a soft, airy texture. The pasta is arranged in a natural, free-flowing mound, filling the center of the bowl with moderate negative space at the rim. Tiny flecks of yellow lemon zest and cracked black pepper garnish the ricotta. The setting is a modern bistro with a dark wood table, a silver fork, and a folded white linen napkin. Natural light emphasizes the silky sheen of the pasta.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm ciabatta bread
Pair with a chilled Vermentino or Pinot Grigio
instructions: Boil a large pot of salted water.
Cook rigatoni until al dente.
Reserve 200 ml of pasta cooking water.
Whisk ricotta with lemon zest and a pinch of salt until smooth and light.
Heat olive oil in a wide skillet over medium heat.
Sauté garlic and red pepper flakes for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add julienned sun-dried tomatoes and cook for 2 minutes.
Add spinach to the skillet and toss until just wilted.
Transfer cooked pasta to the skillet.
Add 100 ml of reserved pasta water and Parmigiano-Reggiano.
Toss vigorously to create a fluid, glossy emulsion.
Adjust consistency with more pasta water if needed.
Season with salt and black pepper.
notes: Ensure the ricotta is at room temperature before whipping for maximum fluffiness.
Do not overcook the spinach; it should remain vibrant green.

recipes.recipe_name: Rigatoni with Spinach, Sun-dried Tomatoes, and Whipped Ricotta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of rigatoni is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The pasta is coated in a glossy, translucent sauce with bright red julienned sun-dried tomatoes and vibrant green wilted baby spinach leaves. Three distinct, creamy mounds of whipped ricotta are placed on top, showing a soft, airy texture. The pasta is arranged in a natural, free-flowing mound, filling the center of the bowl with moderate negative space at the rim. Tiny flecks of yellow lemon zest and cracked black pepper garnish the ricotta. The setting is a modern bistro with a dark wood table, a silver fork, and a folded white linen napkin. Natural light emphasizes the silky sheen of the pasta.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm ciabatta bread
Pair with a chilled Vermentino or Pinot Grigio
instructions: Boil a large pot of salted water.
Cook rigatoni until al dente.
Reserve 200 ml of pasta cooking water.
Whisk ricotta with lemon zest and a pinch of salt until smooth and light.
Heat olive oil in a wide skillet over medium heat.
Sauté garlic and red pepper flakes for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add julienned sun-dried tomatoes and cook for 2 minutes.
Add spinach to the skillet and toss until just wilted.
Transfer cooked pasta to the skillet.
Add 100 ml of reserved pasta water and Parmigiano-Reggiano.
Toss vigorously to create a fluid, glossy emulsion.
Adjust consistency with more pasta water if needed.
Season with salt and black pepper.
notes: Ensure the ricotta is at room temperature before whipping for maximum fluffiness.
Do not overcook the spinach; it should remain vibrant green.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Thighs in Savory Mole Poblano
recipes.visual_description: Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs are presented in the center of a wide, matte white porcelain bowl. The chicken is completely enrobed in a thick, glossy, mahogany-colored mole sauce that shows a rich sheen from the butter and chocolate. A generous sprinkling of toasted white sesame seeds provides a bright contrast against the dark sauce. To the side, a neat mound of fluffy Mexican red rice is positioned. The dish is served on a dark wood bistro table with a folded white cotton napkin and a small basket of warm, stacked corn tortillas. The lighting is soft and natural, highlighting the velvety texture of the sauce and the clean edges of the plating.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas
Accompany with Mexican red rice
Garnish with fresh cilantro sprigs
instructions: Toast dried chiles in a dry pan over medium heat for 2 minutes.
Soak toasted chiles in hot water for 15 minutes until soft.
Melt 30g butter in a large pan.
Sear chicken thighs until browned on both sides.
Remove chicken from pan.
Add remaining 30g butter to the same pan.
Sauté onion, garlic, and almonds until golden brown.
Place soaked chiles, onion mixture, cinnamon, and stock in a blender.
Process until completely smooth.
Return sauce to the pan and stir in dark chocolate until melted.
Add chicken thighs back to the sauce.
Simmer on low heat for 25 minutes.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Season with salt to taste.
notes: Ensure the mole sauce does not boil rapidly to prevent the chocolate from scorching.
Use high-quality dark chocolate for the most authentic savory depth.

recipes.recipe_name: Anchovy and Caramelized Onion Crostini
recipes.visual_description: Three rustic slices of toasted sourdough bread sit on a cream-colored ceramic plate. The bread shows golden-brown color and visible grill marks. A mound of translucent, caramelized onions covers each slice. The onions have an amber hue and jam-like texture. A single, whole silver-skinned anchovy fillet lies horizontally on each onion mound. Flecks of bright yellow lemon zest and finely chopped dark green parsley garnish the top. The plate rests on a weathered oak table. A small bowl of extra virgin olive oil sits nearby. Warm, natural light highlights the textures of the crusty bread and glistening oil. The arrangement is casual and asymmetrical. The entire plate is visible.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with chilled Vermentino wine
Present on an individual ceramic plate
Serve as part of a traditional antipasto spread
instructions: Peel and thinly slice onions.
Heat 30 ml olive oil in a skillet.
Add onions.
Sauté over medium-low heat for 20 minutes until amber.
Finely chop 4 anchovy fillets.
Stir chopped anchovies into onions.
Cook 2 minutes.
Remove from heat.
Stir in lemon zest and chopped parsley.
Slice bread into 12 rounds.
Toast bread until golden.
Rub toast with a halved garlic clove.
Drizzle bread with remaining olive oil.
Spread onion mixture on toast.
Place one whole anchovy fillet on each toast.
notes: Use high-quality oil-packed anchovies
Avoid adding salt as anchovies provide sufficient salinity
Serve at room temperature for best flavor

recipes.recipe_name: Japanese Ginger Pork with Onions
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Japanese Ginger Pork is presented on a dark gray ceramic plate. Three thick pork medallions are coated in a glossy brown ginger-soy glaze and arranged in a natural cluster at the center. Softened, golden-brown onion strips are layered over the meat. A precise mound of finely shredded green cabbage is placed to the side. The plate sits on a light oak table next to a small porcelain bowl of steamed white rice. Dark wooden chopsticks rest on a ceramic holder beside the plate. Natural light highlights the glazed texture of the pork and the crisp white cabbage. The arrangement is clean, professional, and follows traditional Japanese plating styles in a minimalist bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of steamed short-grain rice
Accompany with miso soup
Include pickled radish as a palate cleanser
instructions: Cut pork into 2cm thick medallions.
Slice onions into 5mm strips.
Grate ginger finely.
Mix ginger, soy sauce, mirin, and sake in a bowl.
Heat oil in a skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear pork medallions for 3 minutes per side.
Remove pork from the skillet.
Add onions to the same skillet.
Sauté onions for 5 minutes until soft.
Pour the ginger sauce mixture over the onions.
Return pork to the skillet.
Simmer for 2 minutes until the sauce thickens and coats the meat.
Plate the pork and onions immediately.
notes: Use fresh ginger for an authentic pungent flavor.
Do not overcook the pork to ensure it remains tender.
Shred the cabbage as thinly as possible for the correct texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Ceviche de Camarones con Pepino
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of shrimp ceviche served in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The center features a heap of whole, plump pink shrimp mixed with crisp green cucumber half-moons and translucent red onion slivers. The ingredients are bathed in a milky, opaque lime juice 'leche de tigre'. Fine specks of green jalapeno and cilantro are scattered throughout. Two large, orange, skinless sweet potato chunks sit at the edge of the bowl. A small cluster of golden-brown toasted corn kernels is placed opposite the sweet potato. The bowl rests on a light oak table with a white cotton napkin. Natural overhead lighting highlights the glossy texture of the seafood.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of extra leche de tigre in a small glass
Accompany with a cold Peruvian pisco sour
Provide a spoon to enjoy the marinade liquid

ingredients.name: cucumber, deseeded and cut into 5mm half-moons
red onion, thinly sliced into julienne strips
sweet potato, boiled and cut into 3cm chunks

instructions: Bring a pot of salted water to a boil.
Prepare an ice bath in a separate bowl.
Blanch shrimp in boiling water for 2 minutes until just opaque.
Transfer shrimp immediately to the ice bath to stop cooking.
Drain shrimp and pat dry with paper towels.
In a large glass bowl, combine lime juice, garlic paste, salt, and half the jalapenos.
Add the chilled shrimp, cucumber half-moons, and red onion to the lime mixture.
Toss gently to ensure all ingredients are coated.
Let marinate for 5 minutes in the refrigerator.
Fold in the chopped cilantro.
Divide the ceviche into four bowls, ensuring each has plenty of liquid.
Place two chunks of sweet potato on the side of each bowl.
Garnish with toasted corn kernels.
notes: Use very fresh lime juice squeezed just before preparation to avoid bitterness.
Rinse sliced onions in ice water to remove harshness before adding to the dish.
Do not overcook the shrimp; they should remain tender and snappy.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Beef with Charred Corn and Pepper Succotash
recipes.visual_description: The dish features 4cm seared beef chunks as the central focus, glistening with a translucent garlic butter glaze. The meat is arranged in a cluster atop a vibrant bed of charred yellow corn kernels and 1cm diced red bell peppers. The vegetables show dark grill marks against their bright natural colors. Three golden, crispy 3cm tortilla triangles are tucked vertically into the side of the beef. A savory pan sauce pools at the base of the vegetables on a clean white porcelain plate. Finely chopped green parsley is evenly scattered over the dish. The setting is a dark wood table with a white cotton napkin and polished silver fork.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of lime wedges to brighten the savory glaze
Accompany with a small bowl of spicy salsa roja
instructions: Cut beef into 4cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Dice bell peppers into 1cm squares. Mince garlic. Chop parsley finely.
Cut tortillas into small 3cm triangles.
Heat 15ml oil in a large skillet over high heat.
Fry tortilla triangles until crisp. Remove and drain on paper towels.
Add remaining oil to the same skillet. Sear beef chunks 2 minutes per side until browned. Remove beef.
Add corn and peppers to the skillet. Cook 5 minutes until charred.
Add garlic. Sauté 1 minute.
Pour in chicken stock. Scrape bottom of pan. Reduce liquid by half.
Whisk in butter until sauce thickens and glows.
Return beef to the pan. Toss to coat in glaze.
Garnish with chopped parsley.
notes: Ensure the pan is very hot before adding beef to achieve a proper crust
Use fresh corn rather than canned for better texture and charring ability

recipes.recipe_name: Nikujaga
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a deep, earth-toned ceramic Japanese bowl. Large, irregular chunks of soft-simmered potatoes are the focal point, showing slightly rounded edges from cooking. Tender 3cm chunks of beef are nestled between the potatoes, not sliced or fanned. Bright orange carrot chunks, cut in traditional rolling shapes, and translucent onion wedges add variety. The ingredients are partially submerged in a dark, shimmering savory broth. Three blanched green snow peas are placed asymmetrically on top. The bowl sits on a rustic wooden table next to a small bowl of steamed white rice and bamboo chopsticks on a ceramic rest. Warm, soft kitchen lighting highlights the moist textures while leaving natural space around the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a bowl of steamed short-grain white rice
Accompany with miso soup
Provide a small side of seasonal Japanese pickles (tsukemono)
Use chopsticks and a ceramic soup spoon

ingredients.name: Potatoes, peeled and cut into large irregular chunks

instructions: Heat oil in a heavy pot over medium heat.
Sear beef chunks until browned on all sides.
Add onion wedges and carrot pieces. Sauté for 3 minutes.
Add potato chunks. Stir to coat with oil.
Pour in dashi, sake, mirin, and sugar.
Bring to a boil. Skim off any foam from the surface.
Reduce heat to low.
Place a drop lid (otoshibuta) directly on the ingredients.
Simmer for 20 minutes until potatoes are tender.
Stir in soy sauce. Simmer for 5 more minutes.
Remove from heat. Let the dish rest for 10 minutes to absorb flavors.
Garnish with blanched snow peas before serving.
notes: Use Yukon Gold or similar waxy potatoes to prevent them from disintegrating
Resting the dish is essential for the potatoes to soak up the savory broth
An otoshibuta ensures heat circulates evenly without breaking the vegetables

recipes.recipe_name: Sichuan Spicy Poached Beef
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a deep, wide porcelain bowl filled with a vibrant, crimson-red chili broth. Tender, glossy chunks of beef are piled in the center, partially submerged in the aromatic oil. A generous mound of minced white garlic and charred, dark red dried chilies sits atop the meat. Freshly cracked Sichuan peppercorns are scattered across the surface. Bright green chopped scallions provide a sharp color contrast against the deep red liquid. The bowl sits on a rustic dark wood table next to a small bowl of fluffy white rice and dark bamboo chopsticks. Natural, side-lit photography captures the shimmering surface of the oil and the steam rising from the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice
Accompany with cold cucumber salad
Pair with jasmine tea
instructions: Cut beef into 3cm chunks.
Mix beef with cornstarch, soy sauce, and wine.
Marinate for 20 minutes.
Tear cabbage into large pieces.
Blanch cabbage in boiling water for 1 minute.
Place cabbage in a large ceramic bowl.
Heat 30ml oil in a wok.
Fry chili paste, ginger, and half the garlic for 1 minute.
Add stock and sugar. Bring to a boil.
Add beef chunks to the liquid.
Simmer for 2 minutes until just cooked.
Pour beef and broth over the cabbage.
Top with remaining garlic, dried chilies, and peppercorns.
Heat 30ml oil until smoking.
Pour hot oil over the aromatics.
notes: Do not overcook the beef to maintain tenderness.
The oil must be smoking hot to properly toast the garlic.

recipes.recipe_name: Dark Beer Braised Beef with Caramelized Onions
recipes.visual_description: The dish features large, tender chunks of beef braised to a deep mahogany color, nestled in a rich, glossy dark beer sauce. The beef is arranged centrally on a clean white porcelain plate, showing a moist, fibrous texture. Thick ribbons of caramelized onions and small pieces of softened tomato are visible within the sauce. A vibrant garnish of finely chopped flat-leaf parsley provides a fresh green contrast. Beside the plate sits a slice of toasted sourdough bread spread with grainy mustard. The setting is a modern bistro with a light oak table and a neutral cotton napkin. Soft, natural light highlights the glistening sauce and the rustic textures of the meat and bread.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with thick-cut Belgian fries (frites).
Pair with a glass of the same dark beer used in the braise.
Provide extra sourdough bread to soak up the rich sauce.
instructions: Cut beef into 4cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat.
Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef.
Slice onions into 5mm half-moons.
Add onions to the pot. Cook 15 minutes until dark golden.
Stir in tomato paste and diced tomatoes. Cook 2 minutes.
Pour in dark beer to deglaze the pot. Scrape the bottom.
Return beef to pot. Add beef stock, thyme, and bay leaf.
Cover and simmer on low for 2.5 hours until tender.
Stir in brown sugar and mustard. Season to taste.
Garnish with chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Use a beer with low bitterness to avoid a sour sauce.
Ensure onions are deeply caramelized for maximum flavor depth.
Do not trim all the fat from the beef; it adds silkiness to the sauce.

recipes.recipe_name: Traditional Scottish Cranachan
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Cranachan served in a clean, contemporary glass tumbler on a light oak bistro table. The dish features distinct, organic layers of ivory-colored whiskey cream speckled with golden-brown toasted oats and vibrant crimson crushed raspberries. Whole, plump raspberries are nestled within the cream and placed on top. The top is finished with a generous scattering of crunchy oats and a thin, translucent drizzle of amber heather honey. A polished silver dessert spoon rests on a folded white linen napkin beside the glass. The background is a soft-focus modern bistro interior with natural daylight highlighting the textures of the toasted grain and the velvety cream.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in individual glass bowls or tumblers to showcase layers
Accompany with a small glass of the same Scotch whiskey used in the recipe
Traditional shortbread on the side
instructions: Spread oats on a dry baking tray.
Toast oats at 180°C for 8 minutes until golden and fragrant.
Remove oats from oven and cool completely.
Crush half of the raspberries with the caster sugar using a fork.
Whisk double cream in a chilled bowl until soft peaks form.
Fold honey and whiskey into the cream.
Stir two-thirds of the toasted oats into the cream mixture.
Layer the whiskey cream, crushed raspberries, and whole raspberries in four glass bowls.
Top with remaining toasted oats and a drizzle of honey.
notes: Use a peaty whiskey for a smoky flavor profile or a Speyside for sweetness.
Ensure oats are completely cool before adding to cream to prevent melting.
Do not over-whip the cream; it should remain soft and luscious.

recipes.recipe_name: Tagliatelle with Chicken and Wild Mushrooms
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Tagliatelle with Chicken and Wild Mushrooms served on a wide-rimmed white porcelain bowl. The long pasta ribbons are swirled into a loose, organic nest in the center. Large 3cm chunks of golden-seared chicken and thick-sliced sautéed brown mushrooms are distributed naturally throughout the noodles. A light, glossy cream sauce coats the pasta, reflecting soft natural light from a nearby window. Freshly grated parmesan cheese is dusted over the top, accented by finely chopped vibrant green parsley. The dish sits on a rustic dark wood bistro table. A clean white linen napkin and a polished silver fork lie to the side. The arrangement is clean with ample negative space around the bowl's rim.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread
Pair with a crisp Pinot Grigio
instructions: Boil 4 liters of salted water.
Season 3cm chicken chunks with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken until golden and 75°C internally.
Remove chicken from pan.
Melt butter in the same pan.
Add diced onions. Sauté until translucent.
Add sliced mushrooms. Brown for 6 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Sauté for 1 minute.
Add chicken stock. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Boil tagliatelle until al dente.
Stir cream and 50g parmesan into the sauce.
Return chicken to the pan.
Toss pasta with sauce.
Use pasta water to adjust consistency.
Garnish with remaining cheese and parsley.
notes: Ensure pasta is al dente
Use pasta water to adjust sauce consistency

recipes.recipe_name: Beef Puntas with Melted Asadero
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of thick, seared beef chunks and diced green poblano peppers rests in a shallow matte black ceramic bowl. The beef is coated in a glossy, dark brown Worcestershire reduction. A generous layer of melted white asadero cheese drapes over the meat, showing smooth, fluid textures and light steam. Three warm, folded corn tortillas are stacked neatly on the side of the bowl. A garnish of fresh cilantro leaves and a single lime wedge sits on the edge. The bowl is placed on a dark wood table next to a neutral linen napkin. Natural side lighting emphasizes the rich glaze on the beef and the creamy consistency of the melted cheese.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas
Accompany with salsa verde or salsa roja
Provide fresh lime wedges for acidity
instructions: Season beef chunks with salt and black pepper.
Heat oil in a heavy skillet over high heat.
Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Remove meat from pan.
Lower heat to medium. Add onion and poblano peppers to the skillet.
Sauté vegetables for 5 minutes until softened.
Add garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Return beef to the pan. Pour in chicken stock and Worcestershire sauce.
Simmer for 10 minutes until the liquid reduces by half and coats the beef.
Distribute shredded asadero cheese evenly over the beef chunks.
Cover the skillet for 2 minutes until the cheese is completely melted.
Remove from heat and serve immediately.
notes: Ensure the skillet is very hot before searing beef to develop a deep crust.
Do not overcook the beef; aim for medium-rare before adding the cheese.
If asadero is unavailable, Monterey Jack is a suitable substitute.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Tofu with Fresh Tomato and Umami Gravy
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of braised tofu served in a deep, clean white porcelain bowl. The dish features 2cm cubes of firm tofu, seared to a light golden-brown texture, nestled in a vibrant, glossy red tomato gravy. Visible chunks of softened tomato and minced aromatics cling to the tofu. The sauce has a thick, silk-like consistency reflecting natural light. Bright green scallion rings are scattered across the top for contrast. The bowl sits on a dark walnut wood table next to a small ceramic bowl of fluffy, steamed jasmine rice. A pair of dark bamboo chopsticks rests on a small ceramic holder. A simple grey cotton napkin is placed neatly to the side. The lighting is soft and natural.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with individual bowls of steamed jasmine rice
Pair with a side of stir-fried bok choy or gai lan
Provide chopsticks and a short-handled ceramic soup spoon

ingredients.name: Scallions, whites and greens separated and sliced

instructions: Pat tofu cubes dry with paper towels.
Heat neutral oil in a wok over medium-high heat.
Sear tofu cubes until golden on multiple sides. Remove and drain.
Add ginger, garlic, and scallion whites to the wok. Sauté 30 seconds.
Add diced tomatoes. Cook until softened and pulpy.
Stir in soy sauce, mushroom sauce, sugar, and vegetable stock.
Return tofu to the wok. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir cornstarch slurry. Pour into the wok while stirring gently.
Cook until the sauce is thick and glossy.
Remove from heat. Drizzle with sesame oil.
Garnish with scallion greens.
notes: Ensure the tofu is very dry before searing to achieve a crisp exterior
Use highly ripe tomatoes for the best natural sweetness and sauce texture
Adjust sugar based on the acidity of the tomatoes

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo alla Romana with Roasted Peppers and Mozzarella
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pollo alla Romana served on a clean white porcelain plate set on a rustic oak table. The dish features 4cm golden-brown seared chicken chunks nestled among vibrant red and yellow bell pepper batons. Melted white mozzarella chunks drape over the meat, interspersed with a fine dusting of grated parmesan. The arrangement is a natural, flowing mound with moderate negative space around the edges. Fresh green flat-leaf parsley is scattered across the top. The lighting is soft and natural, highlighting the glossy sauce and the charred edges of the peppers. A cotton napkin and a polished silver fork rest beside the plate, creating a contemporary bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty ciabatta bread to soak up the juices
Accompany with a glass of chilled Frascati wine
Present in a shallow ceramic bowl for a rustic family-style feel
instructions: Cut chicken into 4cm thick chunks.
Slice bell peppers into 1cm wide batons.
Mince the garlic cloves.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Season chicken chunks with salt and pepper.
Sear chicken until golden brown on all sides.
Remove chicken from the pan and set aside.
Add peppers to the same pan and sauté for 6 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze the pan with white wine, scraping the bottom.
Return chicken to the pan.
Cover and simmer for 10 minutes.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Stir in grated parmesan cheese.
Tear mozzarella into small chunks and place over the chicken.
Cover for 2 minutes until mozzarella melts.
Garnish with chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Ensure the pan is hot before adding chicken to achieve a deep sear.
Use high-quality buffalo mozzarella for a creamier texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Saffron Arroz con Pollo
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Arroz con Pollo is presented on a clean white porcelain plate. The base is a mound of vibrant, golden-yellow saffron rice, each grain distinct and glistening. Bright green peas and small cubes of soft red pepper are evenly distributed throughout the rice. Two whole, un-sliced chicken thighs with crispy, deep-bronze seared skin sit prominently atop the rice. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of finely chopped emerald-green parsley and a single bright yellow lemon wedge on the side. The plate is set on a light oak wood table with a folded white cotton napkin and a simple silver fork. Natural side-lighting highlights the textures of the crispy chicken skin and the moist rice grains.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in a traditional terracotta cazuela for family style
Accompany with crusty bread to soak up juices
Pair with a crisp Spanish white wine like Albariño
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide, shallow pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until deep golden brown. Flip and cook 2 minutes. Remove chicken.
Add diced onion and red pepper to the pan. Sauté 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in garlic and smoked paprika. Cook 30 seconds.
Add rice. Stir 1 minute to toast and coat in oil.
Crush saffron into warm chicken stock. Pour stock into the pan.
Nestle whole chicken thighs back into the rice.
Simmer uncovered over medium heat for 15 minutes. Do not stir.
Scatter green peas over the surface.
Cover pan. Reduce heat to low. Cook 8 minutes until chicken reaches 75°C and liquid is absorbed.
Remove from heat. Let rest covered for 5 minutes.
Garnish with parsley and lemon wedges.
notes: Use short-grain rice to ensure the correct texture and absorption
Avoid stirring the rice after adding liquid to allow the bottom to develop a slight crust
Always bloom saffron in warm liquid to release maximum color and aroma

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo a la Cerveza con Chipotle
recipes.visual_description: The dish features two whole, golden-brown seared chicken thighs placed atop a generous portion of moist, savory rice. The rice is tinted deep orange from tomatoes and chipotle, punctuated by vibrant green peas and small diced tomato chunks. The chicken skin appears crisp and seasoned. The rice is served in a wide white porcelain bowl, showing a slightly fluid, loose consistency. A scatter of fresh cilantro leaves provides a bright green garnish. The setting includes a light oak table, a crisp white napkin, and a small stack of warm corn tortillas in a cloth-lined basket. Soft, natural side lighting highlights the steam and the rich textures of the braised meat and grains.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas
Accompany with fresh lime wedges
Pair with a cold Mexican lager
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt, pepper, and ground cumin.
Heat oil in a large deep skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden brown. Flip and sear 2 minutes. Remove chicken.
Add onion and garlic to the same pan. Sauté until translucent.
Add rice to the pan. Toast for 3 minutes until slightly opaque.
Stir in tomatoes and minced chipotle chiles.
Pour in beer and chicken stock. Scrape the bottom of the pan to release browned bits.
Return chicken thighs to the pan. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 20 minutes.
Confirm chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Fold in green peas. Cover and rest for 5 minutes off the heat.
Garnish with fresh cilantro before serving.
notes: Ensure the rice is not overcooked to maintain individual grain structure.
The beer adds a slight earthy bitterness that balances the smoky chipotle heat.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Asparagus Involtini with Garlic Parmesan Cream
recipes.visual_description: A single starter portion served on a clean white porcelain plate. Two golden-brown pan-seared chicken involtini sit centrally. Vibrant green blanched asparagus tips protrude from the ends of the chicken rolls. A silky, ivory-colored garlic parmesan cream sauce pools elegantly beneath the meat. The chicken features a crisp, caramelized exterior from searing. The dish is finished with a light dusting of finely micro-planed parmesan and small fresh herb sprigs. The background shows a dark wooden bistro table with a white cotton napkin and polished silver fork. Natural side lighting highlights the moist texture of the chicken and the glossy sheen of the reduction sauce. Clean plating with ample negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as an 'Antipasto' or 'Secondo' starter
Accompany with a crisp Italian white wine like Gavi or Pinot Grigio
Present on warmed porcelain plates
instructions: Cut chicken into 8 small thin medallions.
Pound chicken to 5mm thickness.
Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Trim asparagus to 8cm lengths.
Blanch asparagus in boiling water for 2 minutes.
Shock asparagus in ice water and drain.
Place two asparagus spears on each chicken medallion.
Roll chicken tightly around asparagus.
Secure rolls with kitchen twine.
Heat olive oil in a pan over medium heat.
Sear chicken rolls until golden on all sides.
Cook until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken and let rest.
Mince garlic finely.
Sauté garlic in the same pan for 1 minute.
Add heavy cream and 40g grated parmesan.
Simmer until sauce thickens slightly.
Remove twine from chicken rolls.
Place rolls over a pool of sauce on the plate.
notes: Ensure the pan is not overcrowded to maintain a proper sear
Rest the chicken for 3 minutes before removing twine to retain juices

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Mushroom Fricassée
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of French Chicken Fricassée served in a wide white porcelain bowl. The base is a bed of fluffy, steamed white rice. On top, large, golden-seared chicken chunks are nestled in a velvety, ivory-colored cream sauce. Quartered cremini mushrooms and 2cm vibrant red and yellow bell pepper squares are scattered throughout the sauce, showing distinct textures. The sauce has a glossy finish. A small sprig of fresh thyme sits on top. The plate is set on a light oak bistro table with a folded white cotton napkin and a silver fork. Natural side lighting highlights the cream's sheen and the chicken's seared edges. The arrangement is organic and centered. The background remains a soft-focus restaurant interior.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty baguette to soak up the cream sauce.
Pair with a dry white wine like Chardonnay or Sauvignon Blanc.

ingredients.name: Chicken thighs, boneless, cut into 4cm chunks

instructions: Season chicken chunks with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until golden on all sides. Remove from pan.
Add butter to the same pan. Sauté onion, mushrooms, and bell peppers for 6 minutes.
Add garlic and thyme. Cook for 1 minute.
Pour in 100ml of chicken stock to deglaze. Scrape the bottom of the pan.
Return chicken to the pan. Add remaining stock.
Simmer for 15 minutes. Ensure chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Boil rice in salted water until tender. Drain and keep warm.
Stir cream into the chicken mixture. Simmer for 5 minutes until sauce thickens.
Remove thyme sprigs. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve chicken and sauce over a bed of rice.
notes: Do not boil the sauce rapidly after adding cream to prevent curdling.
Ensure bell peppers retain a slight bite for textural contrast.

recipes.recipe_name: Pappardelle with Braised Beef Short Rib Ragù
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of wide pappardelle ribbons is piled loosely in the center of a shallow white porcelain bowl. The pasta is coated in a deep mahogany-colored ragù. Large, succulent chunks of braised beef short rib are nestled among the pasta folds, showing a tender, fibrous texture. The sauce is glossy and thick, clinging to the wide noodles. Fine shavings of Pecorino Romano and small leaves of fresh rosemary are scattered on top. The plate sits on a rustic dark wood table. A fork rests on a folded linen napkin to the side. The lighting is soft and natural, highlighting the rich textures of the meat and the sheen of the sauce.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty ciabatta bread
Offer extra Pecorino Romano at the table
Pair with a full-bodied red wine like Sangiovese
instructions: Season beef chunks with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat.
Brown beef chunks on all sides.
Remove beef from pot and set aside.
Add onion, carrot, and celery to the pot.
Sauté 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in garlic for 1 minute.
Pour in red wine to deglaze the pot.
Scrape browned bits from the bottom.
Add tomatoes, stock, rosemary, and beef.
Simmer covered on low heat for 2.5 hours.
Remove rosemary sprigs.
Boil salted water in a separate pot.
Cook pappardelle until al dente.
Drain pasta and reserve 100ml pasta water.
Toss pasta with ragù, butter, and reserved water.
Stir until the sauce becomes glossy.
notes: Use a heavy-bottomed Dutch oven for even heat distribution
Do not overcook the pasta to maintain a firm bite
Shred larger meat chunks slightly with a fork if desired before tossing

recipes.recipe_name: Beer-Braised Chicken with Spicy Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Beer-Braised Chicken served in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The foundation is a mound of fluffy, long-grain rice, colored a warm golden-orange by the beer and spice infusion. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs rest prominently on the rice, featuring crispy, deeply caramelized skin with visible seasoning specks. Small, uniform dices of sautéed red bell pepper and softened onions are dispersed throughout the rice grains. The dish is garnished with finely chopped fresh cilantro and a bright green lime wedge placed on the rim. The setting features a rustic wooden tabletop with a neutral cotton napkin and a polished silver fork. Natural light emphasizes the moist texture of the chicken and the individual grains of rice.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Fresh lime wedges
Extra vinegar-based hot sauce
Side of black beans
instructions: Season chicken with salt, pepper, and paprika.
Heat oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 6 minutes.
Flip chicken and sear for 3 minutes.
Remove chicken from the pan.
Sauté onion and bell pepper for 5 minutes in the same pan.
Add garlic and rice.
Stir for 2 minutes to toast the rice.
Deglaze the pan with beer and scrape the bottom.
Stir in chicken stock and hot sauce.
Return chicken to the pan on top of the rice.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 20 minutes.
Confirm chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Use a light lager to avoid bitterness.
Ensure rice is toasted before adding liquid for better texture.
Keep the lid sealed tightly during simmering.

recipes.recipe_name: Pasta with Roasted Corn and Asparagus
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pasta is served in a wide, white porcelain bowl on a rustic wooden bistro table. The pasta is coated in a light, glossy emulsion. Bright yellow corn kernels feature dark charred spots from the sear. Vibrant green asparagus spears and green beans, cut into 3cm batons, are distributed evenly throughout the dish. Translucent diced onions and minced garlic are visible in the sauce. The dish is garnished with large, hand-torn fresh basil leaves and a few drops of hot sauce for color. A subtle drizzle of extra virgin olive oil adds a finishing sheen. The lighting is natural and even, highlighting the crisp textures of the blanched vegetables. A folded white cotton napkin sits beside the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty sourdough bread
Pair with a crisp chilled white wine
instructions: Boil salted water.
Cook pasta al dente.
Reserve 120ml pasta water.
Blanch beans and asparagus for 2 minutes.
Drain and shock in cold water.
Heat 30ml oil in a large pan.
Add corn kernels.
Sear until charred and golden.
Remove corn from pan.
